Cardinals Reveal 'Frustrating' New Jeremiyah Love Injury
full_text:
ARIZONA — Another week, another new injury that pops up for Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love.
Love exited Week 8's win over the Dallas Cowboys with what's now his third different ankle injury of the 2026 season— a specific lower body injury that has haunted the third overall pick since getting his first taste of action in preseason play.
The initial ankle injury in preseason, one that kept him out for the team's final two games, was different than the other ankle injury that hindered him early in the regular season, causing him to miss two consecutive games before returning this past weekend.
And now, as head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Monday, Love's dealing with an entirely different issue.
"This is new, so this is not the left ankle or the right, it's a new portion of the ankle. So I'll keep it at that. I'm going to know more a little bit more tomorrow. And I haven't talked to him yet, so out of respect of not talking to him yet, I'll give you guys more on Wednesday," LaFleur said.
The rookie running back carried the ball nine times for 23 yards before exiting in the first half against Dallas.
When asked if Love was a candidate to hit injured reserve, LaFleur said:
"Just hang with me on that one. I'll talk to you guys Wednesday."
Bam Knight also exited the Cowboys matchup with an injury, leaving just Tyler Allgeier as the lone healthy back in Arizona's backfield. LaFleur said wide receiver Devin Duvernay could have potentially gotten snaps if Allgeier went down.
Love arrived to the desert this offseason as potentially game-changing presence for the Cardinals. However, his abilities and opportunities have been sharply limited as a result of his battles with health issues.
"It's frustrating. It just stinks for him. He wants to be out there and helping his teammates," LaFleur continued on Love.
"This guy loves ball. He just wants to contribute. He's such a team guy. He's such a coachable guy. He's such a likable guy, and so he just wants to be out there helping his guys. For him, just kind of going through what he's going through, it's adversity for sure. But he's going to be stronger because of this."
The Cardinals gave players Monday and Tuesday off with Wednesday serving as their first day back in the building as Week 9 preperation for the Seattle Seahawks begins.

title: Cardinals Suffer Another Season-Ending Blow to WR Room
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are set to lose wide receiver Kendrick Bourne for the rest of the season.
The Cardinals' wideout suffered an ankle injury during Week 8's win over the Dallas Cowboys and did not return. Initial fears from the team suggested it wasn't looking good for the free agent addition after going down with a non-contact injury, and CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz confirmed it today on X:
"Based on initial testing results, #Cardinals wide receiver Kendrick Bourne (ankle) is set to miss the rest of the season, sources tell @CBSSports. Was the fear and he is in fact set to miss the rest of the year. Had ranked second among Arizona wide receivers with 26 catches and had three games this season with 5+ catches."
ESPN's Adam Schefter later added : "Cardinals WR Kendrick Bourne has a fractured tibia that does not require surgery but will sideline him three months and end his season."
#RiseUpRedSea Kendrick Bourne hurt #AzCardinals #AZvsDAL pic.twitter.com/idItog993t
Bourne, an energetic presence in the Cardinals' receiver room, departs after playing just half of a season for Arizona after being signed this past offseason to start as the team's lead slot receiver. After trading Marvin Harrison Jr., Bourne was set to welcome a larger share of the team's passing attack.
Now, the Cardinals are down another wideout after losing Jalen Brooks to injured reserve and Harrison departed via trade. Arizona recently signed Zay Jones, though the team might look for other supplemental help ahead of the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline .
When speaking with reporters today, minutes before Zenitz's report, LaFleur was hesitant to fully deem the injury as season-ending.
"I just talked to KB before, so he is one that I talked to. It's not good, so we'll see," he said.
"There's different doctors and stuff that all these guys know each other in the medical [world] and you're sending it to different people, getting different people's opinions. Kendrick might be doing some stuff on the side with maybe his team. Who knows? So there's a lot of opinions in terms of where that's at. But it's not looking good. Not saying it's the season, but it might be."
The Cardinals are 3-5 and had seemed to find a groove with Gardner Minshew in at quarterback, who was named as the starter moving forward.
Bourne's familiarity with LaFleur made him a strong fit for the Cardinals' offense, especially his usage as a in-line blocker in motion to explode through the A or B gap and create some mismatches and confusion in the interior.
The Cardinals are likely to officially place Bourne on injured reserve soon, though all indications suggest he's done for the 2026 season.

title: Cardinals Reveal Drastic Quarterback Shakeup
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have made their quarterback change official.
Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur confirmed to reporters that Gardner Minshew would be the team's new starting quarterback after Week 8's impressive comeback victory against the Dallas Cowboys.
The change was expected, as Minshew replaced the struggling Jacoby Brissett in the third quarter and helped Arizona overcome a two-score deficit in the fourth quarter to get their third win of the season in dramatic overtime fashion.
"I think he kind of showed all of us in terms of him going out there being the competitor that he is. Doesn't shock me, obviously. I mean, the production was pretty wild in terms of the amount of points and just moving up and down the field. But he's a competitor, and he's always prepared," LaFleur said of making the change to Minshew.
However, that's not the only change LaFleur announced. Rookie third-round pick Carson Beck is now the team's No. 2 quarterback, leaving Brissett as the emergency passer on gamedays. That's massive in terms of Beck's development, who has been inactive for every game this season as Arizona's QB3.
"Just think that's the right thing to do," LaFleur added on moving Beck to backup status. "Continue his development in terms of getting a little bit more reps with the scout team and all that. He's week-to-week in terms of [his health], he's feeling really good right now. So thought that was the best thing to do."
It's a massive shift in the Cardinals' quarterback room ahead of their Week 9 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, one that makes Brissett's haggling with Arizona over the summer a bit more eye-opening after the lackluster production he gave the Cardinals to start the season.
"That's not easy. It's not a fun phone call. There's no book for that," LaFleur said on telling Brissett the news. Arizona also told other position players today so they weren't caught off guard by the change.
"Obviously there's a human element to it. I have a lot of respect for Jacoby the person. I have a lot of respect for Jacoby the player. Like I told you guys yesterday, that was not all on him. This was collective. But the position that those guys sign up for, we know the deal. We needed a spark, and obviously Gardner gave us one."
However you slice it, it's a new era for the Cardinals.

title: Insider Sets The Record Straight on Cardinals, Budda Baker Trade Noise
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have some massive decisions to make in the coming days, and star safety Budda Baker could be at the helm of those discussions.
The long-time safety and Cardinals team captain once again finds himself in trade noise ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline, which has seemingly emerged into a tradition at this point due to Baker's talent level and Arizona's typical lack of success.
The Cardinals just emerged to 3-5 on the season with Baker still carrying a lion's share of production — what's the latest on potential trade scenarios?
ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter doesn't foresee a deal happening.
"Budda Baker? That guy's been such a stud. I don't know if Budda Baker's going to be traded, I don't think Arizona wants to move on from a guy who has meant so much to that franchise, who is such a baller," he said on The Pat McAfee Show .
"I don't think Arizona wants to move on from Budda Baker.. He's meant so much to that franchise and he's such a baller" ~ @AdamSchefter #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/OZSjpcBo0k
Baker, to this point, has tallied 51 tackles with 3.5 sacks, four passes defensed, one interception and one forced fumble. The face of the franchise is currently in his tenth season — all with Arizona — and has survived plenty of front office and coaching changes.
Baker's meant a lot to the Cardinals' fan base, sticking through thick and thin with the organization despite its massive amount of lows since he entered the league.
However, that doesn't stop trade interest from other teams — which is something not new to Baker. Speaking with ESPN's Josh Weinfuss last week, Baker said he understands it's a business but very much wants to stick around.
"I'm here. I want to win. I want to be here," he said. "And I'm just controlling what I can control, just taking it one week at a time, and hopefully when the deadline ends, I'll still be here. If not, I mean, it's a business. I understand at the end of the day and that's it."
Baker, an eight-time Pro Bowl player, is set to be a free agent after the 2027 season. Spotrac shows the Cardinals have an out on his contract after this season, where they can part ways with the veteran for only $3 million in dead cap space.
The Cardinals are heavily expected to be active around the deadline in terms of selling players. After moving off of Marvin Harrison Jr., Arizona could also see faces such as Josh Sweat and Jacoby Brissett dealt as well.

title: Cardinals, Ravens Are Suddenly Perfect Trade Partners
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals move into their next week of football with a vastly different outlook at quarterback.
Minshew Mania has officially infiltrated the desert after Arizona's comeback win against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8, marked by the switch from Jacoby Brissett to Gardner Minshew in the third quarter.
Minshew injected a new sense of life into Arizona's offense, one the Cardinals will likely depend on moving forward. The organization is likely going to continue rolling with Minshew for the foreseeable future.
That places the veteran Brissett in a precarious spot, especially with third-round pick Carson Beck in the wings. Arizona, with the trade deadline over a week away, could very well move on from Brissett.
And the perfect team emerged on Sunday.
The Baltimore Ravens, sitting at 4-4 and desperately trying to maximize their playoff window, are now down Lamar Jackson for likely the season while backup Tyler "Snoop" Huntley is also sidelined with an injury.
The Ravens need a quarterback, one who is cheap and full of veteran experience to immediately be plugged and played in Baltimore.
That quarterback could very well be Brissett.
Brissett's on the final year of his contract and surely won't be returning to Arizona at the end of the year. The Cardinals likely wouldn't be looking to squeeze teams out for maximum draft capital, likely settling for a Day 3 pick if interested teams indeed call on Brissett.
NFL insider Jason La Confora says one NFL person believes Brissett is a fit for the Ravens:
Brissett's time in the desert is likely coming to an end, and as the league's Nov. 10 trade deadline crawls closer, Arizona will see an uptick in calls on various veterans across the roster — Brissett included.
Now, there's no incentive to keep Brissett in a Cardinals uniform, which should make for an easy exit. He's a cheap and experienced option for the Ravens to target, and urgency is as high as ever to turn things around in Baltimore.
Brissett could very well end up in a Ravens uniform. Soon.

title: How Cardinals Completed Improbable Comeback to Stun Cowboys
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals erased a 14-point deficit to take down the Dallas Cowboys 33-30 in Week 8.
"I don't know if there's any words that I can express about this team right now other than they're resilient and they just keep fighting," head coach Mike LaFleur said postgame.
"They're always in the fight. That was a total team effort right there."
Here's how they got it done.
With Arizona trailing Dallas 17-3 late in the third quarter, Mike LaFleur decided to bench quarterback Jacoby Brissett.
The Cardinals turned to journeyman quarterback Gardner Minshew II, who hadn't appeared in a regular-season game since December of last season.
Minshew showed no signs of rust, leading the Cardinals' offense to four straight touchdown-scoring drives to end regulation. Notably, Minshew went a perfect 3-for-3 inside the red zone — an area where the Cardinals have struggled in recent weeks.
"He did a good job. Obviously, extended a few plays, stuff like that," LaFleur said postgame. "I thought his timing was great. He's had a lot of success in this league, and he's about as resilient as they come."
On the day,Minshew completed 17-of-23 passes for 188 yards and three scores.
The Arizona Cardinals were down to just one running back Sunday against Dallas after Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (concussion) both left the game with injuries. Tyler Allgeier was the last man standing.
Despite nursing a toe injury himself, Allgeier flourished as the team's lead back, producing a career-high 191 scrimmage yards and two total touchdowns.
"Shoot, we had to dig deep," Tyler Allgeier told J.P. Shadrick and A.Q. Shipley on the Cardinals Locker Room Show. "It was just me playing for Bam and J.Love, and I feel like I had them on my back, pushing my way into that end zone."
Per Next Gen Stats, Tyler Allgeier gained +96 rushing yards over expected, the most by a Cardinals rusher since 2018.
"He couldn't come out, and he knew that. He put his cape on and became Superman for us," head coach Mike LaFleur said. "I'm proud of him cause he's a resilient dude. He's exactly what you want."
The Cardinals held the Cowboys' potent offense to a season-low 3.6 yards per play and 2.4 yards per carry. Arizona also recorded four sacks, the most Dallas has allowed in a single game this season.
Coach LaFleur credits the defense's success to their playstyle.
"I thought Nick [Rallis] had a really good game plan. I thought they had a great week. They got men on that defensive side. They're grown-ass men, and they're always excited about the opportunity to be 1-0 every week. They just kept battling today."

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly: Cardinals Rally To Upset Cowboys
full_text:
There was some doubt, but in the end the Arizona Cardinals continued to reign supreme against the Dallas Cowboys.
Led by a second-half surge, Arizona backup quarterback Gardner Minshew and running back Tyler Allgeier led the Cardinals to a 33-30 overtime win over the Cowboys Sunday afternoon. Since 2008, the Cardinals are 9-1 against the Cowboys and have a perfect 5-0 record at AT&T Stadium in Arlington.
Here is the good, the bad, and the ugly from the Cardinals' historic upset against their old NFC East foes, the Cowboys:
Arizona was dead in the water in the first half, leaving points on the board after a big defensive stop in plus territory on its second offensive drive. The Cowboys ballooned the lead to 17-3 in the middle of the third quarter as the game trended toward a Dallas victory.
The Cardinals somehow rallied in the final 17 minutes, starting with a massive 63-yard touchdown run for Tyler Allgeier to close out the third quarter.
With running backs Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight out due to injury, Allgeier was the heart and soul of the Arizona rushing attack to close out the afternoon. Gardner Minshew , who came in for starter Jacoby Brissett, was impeccable through the air.
Allgeier rushed for two explosive runs — his second came on a 52-yard rush up the left side to put Arizona in positive territory. The Cardinals' backup quarterback threw for 17 of 23 for 188 yards and three touchdowns, all in the final quarter, to spark the late-game rally.
Kicker Chad Ryland missed the game-winning extra-point attempt, but made up for it in crunch time by booting a 42-yard field goal to win the game in overtime, staking a claim to yet another victory in Dallas.
Arizona may have gotten the win today, but the defense still remains the biggest issue so far this season. That doesn't mean the Cardinals didn’t have positive moments.  Mack Wilson Sr. made a big-time stop on the first defensive drive, and the unit held the Cowboys to two late field goals.
CeeDee Lamb led the Cowboys with seven receptions for 58 yards, his longest catch on the day being  27 yards. George Pickens burned the secondary for a massive 37-yard gain, and Ryan Flournoy scored Dallas' only passing touchdown with an impressive red-zone catch.
On the ground, Javonte Williams had a decent day, logging 24 carries for 56 yards, while Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott scored his first rushing touchdown of the season to open the fourth quarter.
The Cardinals might be the most banged-up team in the entire NFL this season -- more bodies were sent to the tent this afternoon against Dallas. The offensive line alone has taken its fair share already this season.
Love left the game early with a right ankle injury in the first half. It was particularly frustrating for the rookie running back, who slammed his helmet on the sideline before going into the blue tent. He returned to the sideline but was ruled out mid-game. His timetable to return to full health is unknown at this time.
Knight was taken out of the game after he suffered a concussion, colliding head-to-head with Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown. It forced Allgeier to take the brunt of the touches in the second half.
Arizona's receiver room took a big hit this afternoon. Kendrick Bourne suffered an ankle injury in the first half. Depth piece Reggie Virgil was carted off in the fourth quarter after colliding with the goalpost, and No. 1 receiver Mack Wilson revealed he played the game with two broken ribs.

title: Cardinals Fans React to Stunning Win vs Cowboys in Week 8
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals pulled off an incredible upset over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8, erasing a two-possession deficit late in the fourth quarter before eventually winning in overtime.
The Cardinals' win at AT&T Stadium pushed their record to 3-5 on the season, and guaging the reaction of Arizona fans on social media, the talk of the town is quite obvious.
We asked for your reactions, and you delivered. The hottest talking point was Gardner Minshew, who usurped Jacoby Brissett in the third quarter and marched the Cardinals to an impressive comeback victory.
This offense looks completely different with Menshew. Suddenly the redzone woes went away. pic.twitter.com/RiHRf6ollw
"I think the Brissett experience is officially over. Has to be," said Jen.
J Love Era added, "Brissett can pack his bags tomorrow and Minshew mania is running wild."
Running wild indeed, at least for now. Minshew completed 17-of-23 passes for three touchdowns, marching Arizona on four straight touchdown drives immediately after coming in for Brissett in the second half.
Every1 stepped up after the QB change. It was literally next man up for every position that took a hit. The defense played with nothing but ❤️. There is nothing wrong with the character of our PLAYERS. Changes should have happened weeks ago. (Also, it's Dallas and they suck).
"Everybody get on the magic Minshew bus," Paul said.
What makes this victory even sweeter for the Cardinals is beating Dallas. Arizona has had the Cowboys' number in recent meetings, and today are officially winners of their last nine-of-ten against Dallas, who have not beaten the Cardinals since 2017.
ALWAYS great to beat Dallas. I remember when Plummer beat DAL at the buzzer (19-17 in 99???). That was a gargantuan upset. Love giving them an L.
"As a Cardinal fan from back in the day, anytime we beat the Cowboys is the Super Bowl for me," said Desmond.
Entering today, LaFleur didn't have a ton of good graces with the fan base. Despite it being his rookie season, that's understandable with having just two wins ahead of today.
However, Week 8's win over Dallas did pave the path for some praise.
Graham said, "Feel like we have a reason to watch games again. And fair play to LaFleur for doing it as it would of been easy to wait till end of the game."
Was starting to doubt Mike a little bit but after minshew coming in and see it was on brisket
And it's pretty safe to say all Cardinals fans are feeling like this after walking out of AT&T Stadium with a dub:

title: Cardinals WR Michael Wilson Reveals Brutal Injury He Played Through vs Cowboys
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals pulled off an incredible, come-from-behind upset in their 33-30 victory over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8.
The Cardinals' efforts weren't propelled with a full squad, as plenty of talented players ranging from Jeremiyah Love to Kendrick Bourne were forced out of action due to injury through points of the afternoon at AT&T Stadium.
For a moment in time, Arizona lost Michael Wilson before the freshly paid receiver returned after halftime. It wasn't known exactly what Wilson was dealing with, though he was in obvious pain throughout the stages of the Cardinals' comeback.
As it turns out, Wilson was playing through two broken ribs.
Michael Wilson just told me and @joshweinfuss that he has two broken ribs. Says he’s playing through “a lot” of pain. “This organization’s paying me a lot of money. So if I can muster up the strength to go play, even at 60%, I’m going to.”
"Pain is temporary, glory is forever. I'll take the rib pain for a win for the Arizona Cardinals," he added (h/t Zach Gershman of AZCardinals.com).
Wilson likely did so when diving for a go-ball early in action, hitting the ground hard and coming up empty-handed in the second quarter. He went to the blue medical tent after wincing in pain getting off the ground.
Wilson gutted it out for the Cardinals in a big way, finishing the day with eight receptions for 111 yards and a game-tying touchdown with six seconds remaining. He also added a 17-yard rush in overtime to help put Arizona in position to kick a game-winning field goal.
"He's a stud. He's everything you want," LaFleur said of Wilson post-game. "... but if you guys knew how much pain that Mike was in, and to go out there and do what he did and just continue to battle and have that big run on the third-and-one, proud of him."
Wilson has faced plenty of scrutiny in recent weeks for a lack of performance, especially after the Cardinals dealt Marvin Harrison Jr., though the Stanford product rose to the occasion in Week 8's upset victory.
"Making huge plays. Like when we needed it, he was our guy. Just absolutely playing through it," Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew said of Wilson after the win.
"Like he's so tough. Like especially for a guy from Stanford, he's so tough. I tell him that. But no, I'm super happy for Mike and man, that was awesome. I was fortunate to have a lot of reps this offseason with him, knowing how he fights for the ball, knowing how he can win at the top of routes. Knowing he's going to be in the right place. You feel good every time you have a one-on-one to him."

title: 4 Big Instant Reactions After Cardinals' Stunning Comeback vs Cowboys
full_text:
That was a game no Arizona Cardinals fan will forget anytime soon.
The Cardinals won an absolute thriller in Dallas against the Cowboys, 33 to 30. This game had so many "wow" moments that it went to overtime, where Arizona completed their comeback with a walk-off field goal.
So, after a huge game like this, what are the main takeaways for the Cardinals?
The Cardinals' offense struggled early in the game under quarterback Jacoby Brissett , putting up only three points. Late in the third quarter, the Cardinals brought in Gardner Minshew at quarterback and benched Brissett. The move worked out, as Minshew helped the Cardinals put up 30 points and ultimately a win in Dallas.
In the victory, the eighth-year veteran threw for 188 yards and three touchdowns, while completing 17 of 23 passes. Minshew threw many great passes, showing his quick release and decisive decision-making.
Minshew's best play came with the game on the line, throwing an absolute dime to wideout Michael Wilson in the end zone with six seconds left. Minshew’s touchdown pass knotted it up at 30-30 with Dallas, and while the Cardinals missed the point-after, Minshew's clutch throw forced overtime and led to the eventual win.
Like Brissett, Minshew's ability to extend the play out of structure is very limited, so Cardinals fans should not expect any Josh Allen- or Patrick Mahomes-like plays from Minshew. However, unlike Brissett, Minshew did a great job distributing the ball out and running the Cardinals offense smoothly.
At the end of the 2025 season, Michael Wilson was putting up some of the best numbers at wide receiver. During the last 8 games of 2025, Wilson had at least 80 yards in at least five of those games, and 100-plus yards in three.
However, before this game, Wilson was off to a quieter start in 2026. He only had two games above 80 yards and none above 100. However, Wilson put on a show against the Cowboys' defense.
Wilson had 8 catches for 111 yards and one touchdown. Many of those catches were outside the numbers, which is a hard part of the field to catch passes in because there is little room for error. While the Cowboys' defense has plenty of issues, their defensive backs are one of the better position groups, with players like Joey Porter Jr. and Caleb Downs.
Minshew and Wilson's connection looked great and could be something very special.
The offensive line was very good, helping former Atlanta Falcons running back Tyler Allgeier have a huge game. Allgeier ran for 147 yards on 11 carries, averaging a remarkable 13.4 yards per carry.
On the defensive line, they played very well. They got four sacks on Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott. While that isn't a huge amount of sacks, for a Cardinals defensive line that has been pretty bad at getting sacks, it was a solid outing against a good Cowboys offensive line.
One player who flashed was defensive tackle Roy Lopez. Lopez's stats weren't insane, as he got two tackles, but he showed great energy during certain moments in the game, making an impact far beyond the box score.
In any win, there are still things that a team can do better, and that could not be truer for Arizona in this game. They struggled in the red zone early on, especially running back Jeremiyah Love. Before he exited the gam e due to injury, Love wasn't the best, as he only ran for 23 yards.
The Cardinals also committed nine penalties for 77 yards. While yes, this is head coach Mike LaFleur's first year, this is Week 8 of the NFL season, so a lot of these mistakes should be ironed out by now. Unfortunately, they are still happening a lot.
Another staple of the LaFleur Cardinals has been slow starts, and today was no different. While this was a very fun comeback for the Cardinals, it is not a consistent winning formula in the league.
Overall, this game perfectly sums up this Cardinals team. They are a fun young squad, which means they will have some lows and also a lot of highs.
Can the Cardinals build off it? Next week, the Cardinals travel to Seattle to take on the defending champion Seahawks.

title: Falcons Get James Pearce Jr. Back, Release 2 Defenders
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are getting a key piece of their pass rush back while making adjustments to their defensive personnel ahead of Sunday’s Week 9 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain.
Falcons edge rusher James Pearce Jr. has officially been reinstated by the NFL on Monday, making him eligible to return following his eight-game suspension .
Pearce’s reinstatement comes alongside two defensive roster moves. Atlanta waived defensive lineman Jared Ivey and released defensive end Drake Jackson, opening two spots on its 53-man roster as the team prepares for its international matchup, one of which will be filled by Pearce.
Pearce’s return could provide a significant boost to a Falcons defense looking to turn things around after Sunday’s disappointing 16-0 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
The rookie led Atlanta with 10.5 sacks last season and emerged as one of the team’s most productive pass rushers. His ability to generate pressure could be particularly important as the Falcons look to improve their defensive production heading into the second half of the season against a team like the Bengals, who have an explosive passing game.
Ivey appeared in seven games for Atlanta this season after joining the organization through waivers following the NFL’s initial roster cutdowns in August. He recorded eight combined tackles, one sack, two tackles for loss, and two quarterback hits.
Jackson joined Atlanta’s practice squad in September before being signed to the active roster on Oct. 24. He appeared in two games for the Falcons this season.
Although both defenders are now off the active roster, their time in Atlanta may not necessarily be over. Ivey and Jackson could potentially return to the Falcons’ practice squad if they clear waivers and the organization elects to bring them back.
The timing of the moves is notable, with Pearce officially back in the fold. Atlanta now has additional flexibility to adjust its defensive personnel while making room for the return of one of its most important pass-rushing contributors.
The Falcons enter Week 9 with a 3-5 record and will look to get back on track against Cincinnati. The Bengals are coming off a 43-36 overtime win over 1-7 Tennessee Titans.  Sunday’s matchup in Madrid will provide an opportunity for Atlanta to get its defense back on track, with Pearce eligible to return.

title: Falcons Lose Two Key Contributors Ahead of Game in Spain
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons will be without two important players when they travel to Madrid, Spain, to face the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday.
Head coach Kevin Stefanski announced Monday that defensive end Samson Ebukam and rookie wide receiver Zachariah Branch are dealing with hamstring injuries that will keep both players out of the Week 9 matchup.
“Samson Ebukam, Zachariah Branch have hamstring injuries,” Stefanski said to open his Monday press conference. “That’s going to keep them out of this game. Not sure, long term, how many games those types of injuries will be, but we’ll obviously treat those and then see how it goes over the next couple of weeks.”
The injuries leave Atlanta without contributors on both sides of the football as the team begins preparations for its international matchup against Cincinnati.
Ebukam has been a consistent presence in Atlanta’s defensive line rotation throughout his first season with the organization.
The veteran defensive end joined the Falcons this offseason after spending the previous two seasons with the Indianapolis Colts. His arrival also reunited him with defensive line coach Nate Ollie, whom he previously worked with in Indianapolis.
Through the first eight weeks of the season, Ebukam has recorded 2.5 sacks and 15 quarterback pressures, according to Next Gen Stats. His pressure total ranks fifth among Falcons defenders.
His absence creates another challenge for Atlanta’s pass rush, which will need additional production from the remaining defensive line rotation against a Cincinnati offense led by quarterback Joe Burrow.
The Falcons will likely need other defensive ends to take on expanded responsibilities while Ebukam recovers.
Branch’s absence will also be felt, particularly in Atlanta’s return game.
The Falcons selected the former USC wide receiver in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft to add another explosive element to their receiving corps while providing versatility as a return specialist.
Although Branch has primarily served as a complementary option in the passing game, recording 10 receptions for 64 yards, his contributions on special teams have been more substantial.
He has returned eight punts for 83 yards and 14 kickoffs for 360 yards this season.
Branch exited Sunday’s loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers early after returning a kickoff and did not return to the game. The hamstring injury will now sideline him against Cincinnati.
Losing Branch takes away an option who has provided Atlanta with opportunities to generate field position through the return game.
Atlanta will have to adjust its personnel heading into a matchup that carries importance as the team looks to get back on track following its loss to Tampa Bay.
The Falcons will face a Cincinnati team featuring one of the NFL’s most talented quarterback and wide receiver combinations. Having their defensive line depth and special teams personnel tested will make the upcoming matchup even more challenging.
Stefanski did not provide a definitive timetable for either player’s return, leaving open the possibility that their absences could extend beyond Sunday’s international game.
Atlanta will release its first official injury report Wednesday as preparations continue for the Week 9 matchup in Madrid.
For now, the Falcons know they will have to find answers without Ebukam and Branch as they attempt to get back into the win column against the Bengals.

title: What’s Going On With the Falcons’ Run Defense?
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have a serious problem defending the run, and Sunday’s loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers exposed just how much the unit has regressed over the past month.
Atlanta entered Week 8 with one of the NFL’s top rushing defenses, ranked fourth in the league and allowing just 88.9 rushing yards per game. However, the Buccaneers completely dismantled that reputation, rushing for a franchise record 324 yards in a 16-0 victory at Raymond James Stadium.
The performance was particularly alarming because Tampa Bay completely abandoned its passing game. Baker Mayfield finished 0-for-3 passing, but the Buccaneers still controlled the afternoon by repeatedly attacking Atlanta on the ground.
Bucky Irving rushed for 170 yards and a touchdown on 27 carries, while Kenneth Gainwell added 140 yards on 25 carries. Both running backs established career highs , and Tampa Bay averaged 5.8 yards per carry.
For a Falcons defense that had been one of the team’s biggest strengths early in the season, Sunday’s performance raised serious questions about what has changed.
The Buccaneers’ performance was not an isolated incident. Atlanta’s struggles defending the run have been building since its Week 5 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.
The Falcons allowed 208 rushing yards to Baltimore, followed by 98 against Chicago and 123 against San Francisco. Tampa Bay then took things to another level with 324.
That is 753 rushing yards allowed across four games, an average of 188.3 per contest. The Dallas Cowboys are last in the NFL in rush defense at 152.8 yards-per-game.
The contrast with Atlanta’s early-season performance is significant. The Falcons entered their Week 8 matchup ranked fourth in rushing defense. Their season average now sits around 118 rushing yards allowed per game.
The numbers suggest Atlanta has gone from a defensive strength to a potential liability in a matter of weeks.
The most concerning part is that opponents have found success using similar concepts. Baltimore, Chicago, San Francisco and Tampa Bay have all been able to generate production on the ground, putting increased pressure on Atlanta’s defensive front and linebackers.
Following Sunday’s loss, safety Jessie Bates III acknowledged that Atlanta has to do a better job recognizing and defending the running schemes opposing offenses are using.
“We’re gonna see these same runs. We’re gonna see these same gap schemes. People are going to load the box. They feel like that’s going to be the answer to beat us,” Bates said.
The veteran safety also pushed back against the idea that Atlanta’s defense was completely ineffective.
“I thought we did a good job up until the fourth quarter. I think the first three quarters, I really thought we contained them.”
However, that containment eventually disappeared.
Bates acknowledged that Tampa Bay’s limited passing attack made the defensive assignment straightforward. The Falcons knew the Buccaneers wanted to run the football.
“You gotta bring your hard hat and be able to stop the run, and like I said, we didn’t do that,” Bates said.
This shows a larger issue with Atlanta’s defensive execution. Knowing what an opponent wants to do is one thing. Having the personnel and discipline to stop it is another.
The Falcons have an opportunity to respond when they travel to Madrid to face the Cincinnati Bengals.
However, the upcoming matchup presents another challenge for a defense that has struggled to contain opposing rushing attacks.
Bates believes the solution starts with preparation and execution.
“We just gotta be able to come in next week and be more prepared to stop the run and run the ball better,” Bates said.
Atlanta cannot afford to continue allowing opposing offenses to dictate the game through their ground attacks.
The Falcons entered the season with expectations of having a physical defense capable of controlling the line of scrimmage. Their early-season rushing defense suggested they were moving in that direction.
Now, four consecutive games of significant rushing production from opponents have changed the conversation.
The Buccaneers provided the clearest example of what happens when Atlanta cannot stop the run. Tampa Bay completed zero passes, scored 16 points and still won comfortably.
That should be a major wake-up call.
The Falcons need answers from their defensive front, better gap discipline from their linebackers and more consistent tackling from the entire unit.
Otherwise, opposing offenses will continue following the blueprint Tampa Bay just established.

title: Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. Leaves Tampa with Something to Prove
full_text:
After his worst NFL performance, and arguably in his entire football career, Michael Penix Jr. vows to be better moving forward as the Atlanta Falcons quarterback.
“I’m going to shake back,” he said. “I promise you I will.”
In a monsoon-like road NFC South clash, Penix tossed four interceptions against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during Sunday’s 16-0 shutout Week 8 loss for Atlanta (3-5) . Penix finished completing a measly 8 of 24 passes for 125 yards.
Underthrows and Tampa (3-5) defenders jumping passes led to interceptions. Linebacker Alex Anzalone caught two, and cornerbacks Zyon McCollum and Jacob Parrish had one apiece.
Penix admitted that the football’s dampness was the main challenge behind the disastrous afternoon . But he isn’t using that as a crutch.
“The conditions are what the conditions are,” Penix told reporters after the game. “Both teams had to play in it.”
The interception-laced game followed Penix playing some of his best football – two straight three-touchdown games against legitimate Super Bowl contenders, the Chicago Bears, and the San Francisco 49ers.
“I do not,” head coach Kevin Stefanski said when asked if he had concerns about Penix’s oxymoronic performance compared to the previous weeks. “Obviously, we can do a better job. Mike can do a better job. I can do a better job.”
Much hype surrounded Penix entering the Bucs game, as he had just been named the NFC Offensive Player of the Week after leading the Falcons to a win over the formerly undefeated Niners . Also, it was his first time in the NFL or college that Penix played near his hometown of Dade City, less than an hour from Tampa’s Raymond James Stadium.
“I had a lot of family in the stands,” Penix said. “For them to see that performance, a performance I never had in life, it kind of sucked.”
He added that Bucs head coach and defensive playcaller Todd Bowles “didn’t do anything special,” and that Tampa Bay played coverage instead of showing many blitz looks, its usual calling card.
The Bucs still only mustered 16 points despite nabbing four picks for Penix, which he said was the first time that had ever happened to him.
Additionally, the Bucs never completed a pass on Sunday in their three attempts; the first time an NFL team has won a game with that stat since 1974 .
That’s right, they didn’t complete a pass. And didn’t have to.
Penix’s interceptions put the Falcons defense in short-field situations, allowing three field goals and the game’s lone touchdown, a four-yard rush by running back Bucky Irving.
So the Falcons’ third-year signal caller is rightfully shouldering the blame for Sunday’s embarrassment.
“As a quarterback, the leader, I got to protect the ball,” Penix said. “That’s the only way that we’re going to be able to win these games, and I did a poor job of that today.”
The Falcons next face the Cincinnati Bengals for the NFL’s Week 9 Madrid game next Sunday, Nov. 8. Kickoff is at 9:30 a.m. on the NFL Network.

title: Falcons Make NFL History for All the Wrong Reasons in Loss to Buccaneers
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons had an opportunity to take control of the NFC South on Sunday. Instead, they became part of one of the strangest performances in NFL history.
Atlanta suffered a humiliating 16-0 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium, allowing its division rival to accomplish something that had not happened in more than 52 years. Baker Mayfield completed zero passes, yet Tampa Bay still managed to win by two scores.
According to the FOX broadcast, the last NFL team to win a game without completing a single pass was the 1974 Buffalo Bills, who defeated the New York Jets 16-12. Tampa Bay became the first team since Buffalo to accomplish the unusual feat.
For Atlanta, the historical significance only added to an afternoon filled with missed opportunities and costly mistakes.
The Falcons entered Sunday with a chance to move into first place in the NFC South but struggled to generate anything offensively. Michael Penix Jr. completed just eight of 24 passes for 125 yards and threw four interceptions, including three in the first half.
Atlanta’s running game offered little help, either. Bijan Robinson finished with 76 rushing yards on 19 carries, while the Falcons totaled just 99 yards on the ground.
Meanwhile, Tampa Bay ran for a franchise-record 324 yards on 56 carries. Bucky Irving led the way with 170 yards and a touchdown, while Kenneth Gainwell added 140 yards, both career highs.
The Buccaneers essentially abandoned the passing game because of the relentless rain and wind. Mayfield finished 0-for-3, but Tampa Bay’s rushing attack proved more than enough.
For Atlanta, watching an opponent win without completing a pass was particularly frustrating for a defense that entered the afternoon looking to establish itself against the run.
Falcons running back Bijan Robinson acknowledged the difficult conditions following the loss.
“I haven’t played a game like that before. I played in the snow, but not a rain game like that,” Robinson said.
He also recognized that Atlanta failed to execute its own offensive identity.
“We pride ourselves on running the football. We just can’t turn the ball over.”
Penix accepted responsibility for his four interceptions, emphasizing that protecting the football was especially important in the conditions.
“Knowing that the conditions are like that, as a quarterback, the leader, I got to protect the ball. That’s the only way we’re gonna be able to win these games,” Penix said.
Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski also acknowledged that Tampa Bay simply outperformed Atlanta.
“You got to play the game that’s in front of you,” Stefanski said. “We didn’t do a good enough job as a team. So that’s a credit to them, credit to their players, credit to their coaches. They did a better job than we did.”
On the other sideline, Mayfield wasn’t particularly concerned about the historical implications of his performance.
“It’s winning. That’s what I think about it. We won,” Mayfield said.
Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles explained that the weather ultimately dictated the offensive approach.
“We didn’t say we were not going to throw the ball; the conditions told [offensive coordinator Zac Robinson] that,” Bowles said.
The defeat drops Atlanta to 3-5, leaving the Falcons one game out of first place in the loss column in the NFC South. They will have little time to dwell on the disappointing performance, with a trip to Madrid to face the Cincinnati Bengals coming next week.
For a team with legitimate division aspirations, Sunday’s performance was a significant step backward. The Falcons not only failed to capitalize on an opportunity to take control of the division, but also allowed the Buccaneers to pull ahead of them in the division without completing a pass.

title: Winners and Losers: Falcons Struggle in Rain-Soaked Loss to Buccaneers
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons had an opportunity to build momentum against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but a difficult afternoon in the rain exposed several problems on both sides of the football.
Michael Penix Jr. struggled to protect the football, the running game failed to consistently establish itself, and Atlanta’s run defense continued to show signs of regression. However, there were a few bright spots, particularly on the defensive side, where Jessie Bates III continued to make game-changing plays.
The Falcons were shut out 16-0 despite Baker Mayfield failing to complete a single pass. Here are the winners and losers from Atlanta’s disappointing matchup against Tampa Bay.
There is no getting around it. Michael Penix Jr. had a disastrous afternoon against Tampa Bay.
Penix finished 8-of-24 for 125 yards with four interceptions and no touchdowns. Three of those interceptions came in the first half, putting Atlanta in difficult situations throughout the game.
The weather conditions certainly played a factor, with heavy rain making it difficult for both quarterbacks to find their footing. However, Penix’s decision-making and accuracy were major concerns. Several of his throws were off target, and the interceptions repeatedly stalled Atlanta’s offensive possessions.
The Falcons could not afford to give Tampa Bay extra opportunities, especially in a divisional matchup with significant implications. Instead, Penix put the offense behind the eight ball and made it nearly impossible for Atlanta to establish any consistency.
Perhaps the most frustrating part of the performance was that Tampa Bay did not complete a single pass all afternoon. Baker Mayfield finished 0-of-3 for zero passing yards, yet the Buccaneers still managed to shut out Atlanta.
Penix entered the game having thrown just one interception all season. He left Tampa Bay with four more on his season total.
It was a disappointing performance for a quarterback who had shown considerable improvement in recent weeks. The conditions deserve some consideration, but four interceptions are simply unacceptable.
Atlanta’s run defense has taken a significant step backward since its Week 5 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.
Before that contest, the Falcons were among the league’s best run defenses. They had allowed just 193 rushing yards combined through their first four games, an average of 48.3 yards per contest.
The Ravens ran for 208 yards on 35 carries, averaging 5.9 yards per attempt. Things have not gotten much better since.
The Chicago Bears followed with 98 rushing yards, while the San Francisco 49ers rushed for 123 yards the following week. That meant Atlanta surrendered 429 rushing yards over those three games, averaging 143 yards per contest.
Sunday was an entirely different level of disappointment.
In a game where Baker Mayfield attempted just three passes and finished with zero passing yards, Tampa Bay did not need to throw the football to control the game.
Bucky Irving rushed for 170 yards on 27 carries, while Kenneth Gainwell added 140 yards on 25 carries. Both running backs reached career highs in rushing yards, and Tampa Bay finished with 324 rushing yards as a team.
That was a franchise record for the Buccaneers, surpassing their previous mark of 283 yards against Philadelphia in 2015.
The performance was particularly concerning because Tampa Bay was essentially telling Atlanta what it wanted to do on every possession. The Falcons simply could not stop it.
Atlanta has gone from having one of the NFL’s most reliable run defenses to an area opposing offenses can consistently attack. Whether it is missed tackles, poor gap discipline or difficulty getting off blocks, the Falcons need to find answers quickly.
Nick Folk’s struggles continued against Tampa Bay, raising additional questions about Atlanta’s kicking situation.
Folk missed a 53-yard field goal wide left in the first quarter, an opportunity to put points on the board in a game where scoring opportunities were going to be limited.
The weather deserves consideration. Kicking in heavy rain is never easy, and the conditions at Raymond James Stadium created challenges for both teams.
However, watching Tampa Bay kicker Chase McLaughlin convert all three of his field goal attempts only made Folk’s miss more noticeable.
Folk entered the game having converted 12 of his 16 field goal attempts this season, a 75 percent success rate. After Sunday’s miss, he dropped to 12-of-17, or 70.6 percent.
That is a concerning number for a veteran kicker who has built his reputation on consistency.
Special teams coordinator Craig Aukerman expressed confidence in Folk earlier this week, emphasizing the importance of supporting the veteran kicker through difficult stretches.
“My biggest thing is I just want to support him, make sure that he knows that I’m there,” Aukerman said Thursday.
Aukerman’s comments showed that the coaching staff is not ready to give up on Folk. However, Sunday’s performance only adds to the pressure.
Atlanta cannot afford to leave points on the field, particularly in games where offensive production is already difficult to find.
Atlanta’s problems establishing the running game continued against Tampa Bay.
While the Falcons’ run defense has struggled, their own rushing attack has not consistently provided the offense with the physical identity it needs.
Bijan Robinson entered Sunday’s matchup with 704 rushing yards on 131 carries, averaging 5.4 yards per attempt through seven games. He had also recorded four rushing touchdowns.
However, his recent production had been less consistent. Robinson rushed for 86 yards against Baltimore, 61 against Chicago and 63 against San Francisco in the three games leading into Sunday’s matchup.
That stretch continued against Tampa Bay.
Robinson finished with 19 carries for 76 yards, averaging four yards per attempt. The Falcons totaled just 99 rushing yards on 28 attempts, averaging 3.5 yards per carry.
The heavy rain made establishing the ground game even more important. Instead, Atlanta struggled to generate consistent offensive momentum.
Robinson remains one of the most talented running backs in the NFL, but the Falcons need to do a better job creating opportunities for him.
Whether it is improved blocking, better play calling or finding ways to create more space at the line of scrimmage, Atlanta must get its running game back on track.
The Falcons cannot continue relying on Penix to carry the offense, particularly when weather conditions make throwing the football increasingly difficult.
Even with Atlanta’s struggles defensively, Jessie Bates III continued to demonstrate why he remains one of the most important players on the Falcons’ defense.
The Falcons struggled to contain Tampa Bay’s rushing attack, but the defense did enough to prevent explosive plays from completely taking over the game. Bates was once again at the center of a crucial turnover.
One of the biggest moments came when Baker Mayfield fumbled the snap before scrambling and flipping the football to Bucky Irving. Irving appeared to have an opportunity to score before Bates delivered another outstanding punchout, knocking the football loose in the end zone.
The result was a touchback and possession for Atlanta.
It was another example of Bates’ ability to create game changing moments when his team needs them most.
Bates has now forced a fumble in each of his last three games. According to the Falcons, the last time an Atlanta player forced a fumble in three consecutive games was Jessie Tuggle in 1990.
Entering Sunday’s matchup, Bates had recorded 40 combined tackles, one interception and two forced fumbles this season. His latest forced fumble continued a remarkable stretch of play.
His impact goes beyond the traditional statistics. Bates consistently finds ways to put the football on the ground and give his offense additional opportunities.
Atlanta has had plenty of defensive problems recently, but Bates continues to be a reliable…

title: What We Learned from Falcons 16-0 Loss to Tampa Bay Buccaneers
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons arrived in Tampa with a chance to take over first place in the NFC South. Instead, there will be some more soul-searching about who this team is.
The Buccaneers bludgeoned the Falcons in the trenches with not one, but two running backs running for career highs. The Falcons were supposed to have a good run offense and a good run defense. They still might, but the Buccaneers were better at both.
The conditions were atrocious, but that can't explain away every mistake Michael Penix made. The Falcons drop to 3-5, even with Tampa, a half-game behind the 3-4 Panthers, and the Falcons have lost to both teams.
The first-quarter woes for the Atlanta Falcons continue. Michael Penix has the worst EPA in the NFL in the first quarter, and it got worse today with two interceptions. He was top 10 in the NFL overall in EPA, despite his dreadful starts to games.
The Falcons tried to change it up by taking the ball when they won the opening coin toss, but that still didn’t help.
Despite the two turnovers, the Falcons' defense held the Bucs to two field goals and escaped the first quarter only down 6-0.
It was supposed to be a happy homecoming for Penix , but this is a game he'd like to forget.
Penix threw four interceptions. Some of that could be attributed to the weather, but his fourth interception came after it had stopped raining and was just a poor read.
The Buccaneers dominated the Falcons in the trenches across the course of the game, so they could afford to get literally less than nothing from their passing game.
The Falcons fell behind and needed Penix to throw the ball. It wasn’t his day. A 77-yard catch-and-run by Jahan Dotson helped make the box score look a little better, but Penix finished 8/24 passing for 125 yards with four interceptions. And frankly, there could have been at least two more.
Penix threw his third interception just 17 minutes into the game. Baker Mayfield only threw the ball three times in the entire game, all in the first half.
Tampa built a 9-0 lead on 128 rushing yards and three field goals off of three Penix INTs. They finished with a franchise-record 322 yards, with both Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell getting career highs of 170 and 140 yards, respectively.
Penix missed the end of last season and the beginning of this season with an ACL tear. He’s looked completely recovered, but if there was ever an indication that he’s 100%, it was this: QB sneaks. The Falcons have been loathe to run quarterback sneaks with Penix. He ran three sneaks, including on back-to-back plays.
There were no worries about his knee coming out of this game. Unfortunately, his performance is going to lead to several more questions.
The Atlanta Falcons get James Pearce Jr. back next week ahead of their trip to Madrid to face the Bengals. However, if they don’t find a way to seal the edge off left tackle better, he’s not going to make much of a difference.
The Buccaneers had two huge plays in the third quarter at left tackle that set up their first touchdown to make the score 16-0.
Pearce will help the pass rush, but at the time of the score, with about four minutes left in the third quarter, the Buccaneers had -2, yes, minus two yards passing.
The Falcons head to Madrid next week to take on a very different Bengals team. Cincinnati will stress the Falcons through the air and not in the trenches the way the Buccaneers did.
Atlanta isn't out of it in a weak NFC South, but the game next Sunday in Spain has become must-win.

title: How Falcons Safety Jessie Bates III Perfected the NFL’s 'Peanut Punch'
full_text:
The “Peanut Punch,” made famous by former All-Pro cornerback Charles Tillman, is surging across the NFL.
Defenders are increasingly targeting the football with a closed fist, trying to punch it out of the ball carriers’ hands. The technique is making an impact across the NFL, with forced fumbles up 39% compared to the 2025 season, according to Jomboy Media.
In Atlanta, there is someone who’s perfected the “Peanut Punch,” in safety Jessie Bates III . It was on full display last Sunday, Oct. 25, when he punched the ball out of tight end George Kittle’s hands to preserve a 29-20 Falcons win to knock off the undefeated San Francisco 49ers .
🚨 ¡La D de Atlanta con el fumble! 😱 Jessie Bates III le sacó el balón a George Kittle y ¡Terminó con el invicto de los San Francisco 49ers! 🤯 #NFLMX 📺💻 @somos_FOX pic.twitter.com/u4kNujehak
“There are people doing it around the league,” Bates told reporters Monday. “It’s not like I’m reinventing the wheel.”
Bates also caught a toe-tap interception from Niners quarterback Brock Purdy. The pick and forced fumble moved his total to six games with both, only behind Rod Woodson (seven), a fellow Fort Wayne, Indiana native and Snider High School alumnus.
The ninth-year NFL veteran Bates says the talent comes from his time, when he starred as a three-sport letterman athlete on Snider’s football, basketball, and baseball teams before starring on the gridiron at Wake Forest.
“You go back to my high school tapes. I’m punching at the ball, I’m picking the ball off,” Bates said.
“I definitely encourage guys to play multiple sports because it does translate. The same way I pick a pocket in basketball is the same way I can punch the ball out on a football play. Baseball, coming off a bat, is the same thing as a quarterback throwing the ball.”
Since arriving in Atlanta in 2023, Bates’ forced fumbles are almost on par with his interception total. Through 58 games with the franchise, he has 10 forced fumbles compared to 14 interceptions.
His season-high forced fumbles are four, set in 2024. He’s already halfway towards that total through the Falcons’ first seven games, at two.
Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich called Bates “the best in football” at the “Peanut Punch.”
“It’s no surprise to us,” Ulbrich said. “If you just watch any one of our practices, you see how intentional Jessie is about hitting the ball. And it’s not just the random haymakers on the ball. It’s really the precision, trying to find the leather, and then ultimately trying to find the air behind the ball. He’s got an amazing feel for that. We’ve always got to keep the ball at the forefront of our minds, and having a guy like Jessie leading the charge, I feel fortunate in that way.”
Bates’ mastery of “Peanut Punch” has spread to the entire team – even on offense. It forces a heightened sense of ball security for players like running back Bijan Robinson , who’s known not to fumble often.
“Those things don’t just happen on Sunday,” Bates explained. “Our whole defense does a good job of doing that in practice. When you’re punching at the ball on Bijan, it makes him better as well. Makes our football team better.”
Bates returns to action when Atlanta (3-4) heads to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (2-5) for a Week 8 NFC South clash . Kickoff is at 1 p.m. from Raymond James Stadium and will be televised on FOX.
Gerald Thomas, III, is a national award-winning reporter contributing to Atlanta Falcons On SI. He has several years of writing and editorial experience, including covering college athletics under the USA TODAY umbrella.

title: Atlanta Falcons vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers Weather Update: It Could Get Ugly
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. is headed back to play in his hometown of Tampa, Fla. for the first time since as a professional, but the conditions could be less than ideal.
Playing in a dome for home games and three road games in the NFC South, the weather isn't something the Falcons typically have to worry too much about, except for the random trip to Buffalo or anywhere in the AFC East late in the season.
However, that's not the case in Tampa today.
The Falcons are scheduled to kick off against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at 1:00 p.m. on Sunday afternoon, and the weather conditions could play a huge role in the game and the viewing experience, even for the television audience.
The Weather Channel predicts scattered thunderstorms beginning at 10:00 a.m. in Tampa, and then it gets ugly.
They predict a 100% chance of heavy thunderstorms starting at Noon and lasting until 3:00 p.m., when they start to dissipate. Even then, they predict scattered thunderstorms until 5:00 p.m. EST.
Raymond James Stadium doesn't allow umbrellas , so if you made the trip to Tampa, leave those in the car. There's no doubt that fans at the game are going to get wet. The biggest concern in the heavy thunderstorms will be the lightning.
The NFL will play through a downpour, but they'll clear the stadium in the event of lightning in close proximity, and that appears to be inevitable this afternoon. We'll keep you updated on delays if they occur through the afternoon.
The Buccaneers and Falcons are both good running teams, and they're both good at stopping the run. Tampa has the NFL's No. 3 rushing offense at 146.4 yards per game, and the Falcons come in at No. 6 at 139.9.
The Buccaneers also edge Atlanta on run defense with the league's No. 2 rush defense, allowing just 77.3 yards per game, and the Falcons are No. 4 at 88.9 yards per game.
Tampa holds a slight edge in both categories and would welcome a sloppy game that helps negate the Falcons' advantage in the air.
Both teams have had their struggles at quarterback at various times this season. But despite starting two games with Cooper Rush under center, Atlanta still has the No. 4 passing offense at 255.6 yards per game.
Tampa was without Baker Mayfield for three games this season, and even when he came back last week, he needed just 64 yards in the Buccaneers' blowout of Carolina. Tampa is averaging 217.4 yards per game through the air, 19th in the NFL.
Adding to their desire to keep this a battle in the trenches, star wide receiver Emeka Egbuka has been ruled out with a concussion.
The kicking game will also be affected. Falcons kicker Nick Folk has struggled beyond 50 yards so far this season, and Atlanta may scrap the idea of kicking from distance all together today.
We'll hope for no lightning delays. There's little hope that fans will stay dry. A sloppy game in the elements favors the home team. Will it be enough? We'll find out on Sunday afternoon.

title: FalconsSI Staff Split on Falcons vs. Buccaneers Week 8 Predictions
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have an opportunity to make a major statement in Week 8 when they travel to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Coming off an impressive victory over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers, Atlanta has a chance to carry that momentum into a divisional matchup with significant NFC South implications.
The Buccaneers are coming off a blowout victory over the Carolina Panthers, but their 2-5 record leaves them needing a win to keep their divisional hopes alive. Meanwhile, a Falcons victory would give Atlanta sole possession of first place in the NFC South.
Here is how the FalconsSI staff sees Sunday’s matchup playing out.
This is the ultimate Lucy and Charlie Brown game for Falcons fans. Atlanta is coming off an impressive home victory against the San Francisco 49ers, while Tampa Bay remains just 2-5 despite a blowout win over Carolina.
The opportunity is there for the Falcons to take sole possession of first place in the NFC South and potentially put the Buccaneers’ divisional hopes on life support.
This is exactly the kind of game Atlanta should win. Unfortunately, it is also the type of game the Falcons have dropped year after frustrating year.
However, looking beyond the history of disappointment, Atlanta is playing better football than Tampa Bay right now. The Falcons and Buccaneers can both run and stop the run, but Atlanta is getting better quarterback play and has a better set of (healthy) weapons on offense.  Bucky Irvin is a great back, but Bijan Robinson is an elite player.
The rainy weather might keep the score down in this one, and it could help negate the Falcon's advantage through the air.
Surely, Lucy keeps the football in place for Charlie Brown this time.
Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 16
Falcons-Buccaneers matchups always deliver compelling storylines, and Sunday’s meeting is no exception.
There is Kevin Stefanski facing Baker Mayfield, Michael Penix Jr. making his long-awaited return to Tampa and Zac Robinson now serving as Atlanta’s offensive coordinator.
Both teams enter the matchup following statement victories. Atlanta knocked off the previously undefeated 49ers, while Tampa Bay dominated the Panthers.
A win would give the Falcons an opportunity to take over the top spot in the NFC South and continue building on their recent success.
Prediction: Falcons 27, Buccaneers 17
99% of Falcons fans have deep-seated trauma, and games like this are exactly why. The Falcons are fresh off a win against arguably the best team in football and are facing a team that’s struggling. These are exactly the games the Falcons have inexplicably lost in recent years.
That said, this is not a one-sided matchup. The Buccaneers are much better than their record suggests. They have a really good defense and have been excellent in the trenches on both sides of the ball. On top of that, all of the Buccaneers’ losses have been one-score games against teams above .500.
I think this game will come down to how the Falcons’ o-line fares against the Bucs’ d-line. Michael Penix Jr. is an above-average quarterback when he’s playing ahead of the sticks and has a clean pocket. The other question is whether this o-line can create running lanes against one of the best run-defending d-lines in the league.
I’m much more confident in how the Falcons’ defense stacks up against the Bucs’ offense. The defensive line has been playing great, and the Bucs’ banged-up receiving corps is overmatched against the Falcons' secondary.
Ultimately, I have the Falcons winning this, but I think it will be a closer matchup than most expect.
Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 20
I expect a tough, physical divisional battle with the weather playing a major factor in Sunday’s outcome. The Falcons should lean heavily on their running game to control the clock, establish the pace and keep Tampa Bay’s offense off the field.
Atlanta cannot afford to get away from what worked against San Francisco. Establishing the run will help take pressure off Penix while creating opportunities for the offense to control the game.
Defensively, the Falcons need to make enough key stops and force the Buccaneers into difficult situations. Tampa Bay is capable of making plays offensively, but Atlanta has shown improvements on that side of the ball.
Coming off last week’s momentum-building victory over the 49ers, I like the Falcons to carry that confidence into Tampa.
It won’t be easy, but Atlanta does enough on both sides of the ball to earn a hard-fought divisional victory, take over first place in the NFC South, and leave Tampa Bay with a win.
Prediction: Falcons 24, Buccaneers 17
The Falcons are fresh off their biggest win of the season, but they have to take the show on the road on Sunday. They've had a lot of success in Tampa over the last few years, and this team will enter with a lot of confidence with how Michael Penix has been playing. This will be a tight game that I expect will come down to the final drive.
The Buccaneer defense is solid, and it will be a difficult test on the road for an offense that hasn't shown it can consistently be a steady unit.
Atlanta has a chance to take over the top spot in the NFC South on Sunday, but it won't happen just yet.
Prediction: Buccaneers 20, Falcons 17
