title: Ravens GM Eric DeCosta Should be Fired For Sunday's Offensive Line Atrocity
full_text:
The reasons for firing Ravens failing general manager Eric DeCosta go far beyond the reasons for keeping him.
A clear-eyed billionaire who wanted to win badly would have dismissed him when he fired former head coach John Harbaugh in January, but that’s not what we get in Baltimore. There were a litany of reasons to accept that the entire culture in Owings Mills was warped as the 2025 campaign came undone, but Steve Bisciotti chose sides instead and absolved DeCosta of blame and absurdly claimed he “bats .800” on the job and is some kind of a savant; that’s farcical given his pathetic record in the draft, free agency, the trade market and, worst of all, in negotiating contracts including the one with Lamar Jackson that trumps all else.
Everybody in the NFL sees it – boy does Eagles GM Howie Roseman who just undressed him in the Cam Jurgens trade – but unfortunately, the only person that matters can’t bring himself to do the hard work of rebooting an entire front office that has been living off the regulation of genius Ozzie Newsome for nearly a decade now. But that Jurgens trade – a second round pick in 2028 that could end up in the top 40 overall selections – while making an terrible line demonstrably worse as he replaced rookie Vega Ioane at center, that should be the end.
The case for ending this charade regime, led by the most overhyped and under-delivering GM in recent NFL history – the kind who inherits Jackson on a rookie deal on the cusp of his first MVP season (he should have three) and wastes his 20s - is deep. Leave it to DeCosta to make the pass protection demonstrably worse year after year, while failing to get the QB signed in a reasonable manner year after year.
If for no other reason than this dynamic, DeCosta would be fired on the spot if there was actual accountability and if this owner really cared, with the 2026 season already worse than last year and the team getting DeCosta-ed (blowing a double-digit lead in the second half to lose) or blown out every week.
Three quarterbacks getting hurt in one half doesn’t happen in professional football, for whatever reason, and the lack of adjustments from a scheme-and-personnel standpoint were staggering to NFL execs who watched the film. Lamar Jackson being lost likely for the season and back-up Snoop Huntley being immediately jumped behind the line and abused on the blitz was ugly;trying to have undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, with no reps since preseason, drop back repeatedly against that was far below grade.
“That can’t happen,” one GM said. “What the (heck) was the OC doing? They didn’t do nearly enough to help that kid. They threw him to the wolves ... That was hard to watch, man.”
Another GM said: "I don't know what the hell they were thinking. That's karma when you do what they did to Maxx," referring to DeCosta's cowardly act pulling out of a trade for star Maxx Crosby in March.
With a coaching staff full of novices getting outclassed after halftime every week, that’s all on DeCosta. He wanted puppets. Boy, did he get them.
Ravens QBs dropped back 17 times in the first half; they were hit nine times and sacked four times and hurried four times. Both tackles – Ronnie Stanley and Roger Rosengarten - proved they were no match for Greg Rousseau (that’s what a real passer rusher looks like, DeCosta, but he’s no Oweh!). But they didn’t get nearly enough help from the backs and tight ends. Somehow rookie coordinator Declan “Genius” Doyle thought this was a good day to run 11 personnel nearly 66% of the time (three receivers and one back) while his quarterbacks got dismembered.
Happy Halloween! Trick or Treat!
The Bills had an astonishing pressure rate of 64.5%, and a sack rate of 13.3%. Simple twists and stunts were totally befuddling to this offensive line. They had complete and utter disrespect for Doyle and this line (and by default the failure GM behind them both) as well they should – how about blitzing on two of every three plays for the entire game?
Yeah, that happened. Ravens QBs completed nine passes on 20 dropbacks against the blitz for 69 yards. Overmatched rookie head coach Jesse Minter almost tried to laugh off the atrocity after the game, pretending he’d have to look at the film first, and even Monday he failed to speak stringently enough to the extent of the problem (of course this team is walking all over him, and it's time to sell at the deadline).
“There’s a lot of things we still need to improve on,” Minter said, “in particular with the offensive line - pass protection, the run game. We’re chasing improvement and we’re chasing continuity, which we haven’t quite had.”
Of course, trying to squeeze a few more years out of Ronnie Stanley, who thought his career was over years ago with chronic ankle/lower leg issues , was always silly. When he came back to DeCosta at the combine a few years on a soft market, that was the time to walk away not extend (we said repeatedly on the radio at the time). Right tackle Roger Rosengarten is a replacement level guy at best far more comfortable running than trying to hold up against a real pass rusher.
The interior OL has been a cruel joke on any and all Ravens QBs just waiting to land since DeCosta chose a fringy edge defender with limited pass rush in the second round (Zion Young, a profile he has misevaluated with staggering consistency ) instead of any center in the draft after letting Tyler Linderbaum be among his massive exodus of young talent in March. Pretending Danny Pinter or Jovaughn Gwyn could play was cute (our guy Brian Baldinger and a legion of execs said it had no chance ).
They couldn’t even realize that rookie Vega Ioane was the solution at center despite him faring quite well, and Jurgens has led the team to two of its worst yards before contract games for Baltimore running backs (0.75 and 0.30) in recent history since coming out of concussion protocol to move back to a position he hadn’t been playing in Philly …. where he was about to get benched. DeCosta lit $10M on fire giving it to John Simpson.
It’s the stuff that ends a charade of a GM career in places serious about winning. But Bisciotti couldn’t be bothered to take part in almost all of his own head coaching search; DeCosta has sucked up to him for years, Bisciotti speaks about him like David Rubenstein speaks about baseball fraud Mike Elias) so don’t hold your breath waiting for anything to change in Owings Mills. The press conference hyping DeCosta when they fired Harbaugh was shameful in realtime and looks like a weak Vaudeville routine now with the passing of just a few months.
The Castle and The Warehouse are one in the same: Reality doesn’t matter, accountability only extends to coaches/managers and the joke’s always on the paying customer.
Thursday night should be a doozie. Wonder if DeCosta will break out the sunglasses at night in primetime again? In a real organization, he'd be reading his termination papers through them by now.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The Ravens Will Have A New Starting QB and Kicker Thursday Night. They Just Don't Know Which Ones
full_text:
The Ravens do not know who will start at quarterback on Thursday night in a must-win game against the Jaguars, according to head coach Jesse Minter, while second-year kicker Tyler Loop could be heading to Injured Reserve..
In an atrocious combination of roster-construction failure and misevaluation by their crack front office – and gross negligence by rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle – the Ravens got three quarterbacks hurt behind the line of scrimmage in Sunday’s, 36-10 debacle in Buffalo. They ran 11 personnel – three receivers, not heavy packages designed for max protection – over 65% of the time, they didn’t do enough to help failing tackles and called way too many pass plays in a game that was basically done by halftime, behind failure GM Eric DeCosta’s greatest offensive line malfeasance yet (set Derrick Henry free from this mess before the deadline, like a real org).
Superstar Lamar Jackson was lost, likely for the season , with a mostly free runner smashing his hand on the first dropback of the game in his first game back from a three-week, high-ankle sprain. Backup Snoop Huntley (toe) was quickly ambushed behind this line himself, and he will not be able to play Thursday, according to Minter, and undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano was beat up and getting treatment on his foot and ankle throughout the game.
“I think we’ll figure that out in the next day or two,” Minter said of his starter. At 4-4, losing three straight games, scoring three points in the second half total in those games and allowing the most points in the NFL in the second half with the worst scoring differential, it probably doesn’t really matter at this point.
Baltimore has two AFC wins (Colts and Jaguars) and its playoff hopes are nil without Jackson. Whether it’s Fagnano trying to gut it out – “To Joe’s credit he’s kind of fighting through some things … we expect him to have a chance on Thursday,” Minter offered – or Austin Reed who was just brought back to the practice squad this week after a brief cameo in the preseason, this is going to be rough. The Ravens are trying to acquire a veteran with ties to this system – Chicago’s Tyson Bagent was the top objective, league sources said, but won’t come cheaply if at all – and are expected to make a play for former Arizona starter Jacoby Brissett.
Mintner said the team could have more clarity on the timetable for Jackson later this week – he was scheduled for a procedure the coach said Sunday – but the reality is the Ravens are virtually certain to be out of the mix whenever Jackson could come back, and with a fake contract for 2027 that essentially cedes all leverage to him , playing him would be ridiculous even by DeCosta’s standards.
As for Loop, he sent the opening kickoff out of bounds and missed another chip-shot field goal and Minter and DeCosta have had him on notice for weeks. Minter was nebulous about the nature of the injury and when exactly it occurred (“He was dealing with something small that kind of became something more,” is what we’re going with here). Whatever it is, he could be bound for IR and Jake Moody will be elevated from the practice squad for Thursday’s game.
The Ravens are going to raise eyebrows with Loop having "something" going on - we didn't get a lower-body or upp-er-body cop out here, and the nebulous timetime given he has never shown up on any injury report, but has struggled with consistency. Hmm.
Moody has kicked for three teams previously and is yet to establish himself after being a second-round pick of the 49ers. Loop was drafted in 2025 to replace scorned and despised former kicker Justin Tucker, who accepted a lengthy suspension from the NFL for sweeping and credible accusations of predatory sexual behavior from throughout his tenure in Baltimore. He was never condemned in any way by anyone in this organization, even when finally terminated, and mostly praised even on the way out.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The Overwhelming Case For The Ravens Trading Derrick Henry At The NFL Deadline
full_text:
The Ravens need to get real about the Frankenstein roster that feckless general manager Eric DeCosta constructed yet again.
They need to get real – as they scramble to find second-and-third-string QBs (we have the names) to prop up another lost season after getting three quarterbacks hurt Sunday (a 36-10 defeat that frankly flatters DeCosta and wannabe head coach Jesse Minter ). It's time to acknowledge what a nightmare front office they are and what a pathetic offensive line they have constructed, again. Having blown years of opportunities to get two-time MVP Lamar Jackson extended and instead ending up with him in a potential walk year,  and now on Injured Reserve and potentially having played his last snap as a Raven (the only one he completed Sunday; ambushed immediately by DeCosta's OL and "genius" Delan Doyle's playbook), it’s time to get real.
Checked-out billionaire Steve Bisciotti is running a $370M waste of payroll with DeCosta and team president Sashi Brown doling out ridiculous contracts to their buddies and building a roster with no heart, no soul, no leadership and precious few blue-chip performers. He already gave away a 2028 second-round pick that could end up in the top 10 of that round for a concussed and soon-to-be-benched offensive lineman. DeCosta needs to do right by some of these players and do right by the fanbase and start playing youngsters and eradicating some of the problems that are standing in their way.
Problem is, they aren’t getting anything in return for DeCosta’s guys – astonishingly overpaid vets like Mark Andrews, Marlon Humphrey, Roquan Smith, Trey Hendrickson, John Simpson – and they would have to include draft capital with them to incentivize any contending team with a teal GM to take them on. They are broken; they are done and the league already knew (they couldn't get anything for Andrews after the 2024 season(.
However, first-ballot Hall of Famer Derrick Henry, in a running back market that is already getting heated up for Jonathan Taylor (Colts) and Tony Pollard (Titans), could bring back decent return now and with so few other options, the rebuild should begin with him. Maybe they get a half decent pick for struggling left tackle Ronnie Stanley and they could get a lil something for 40-year-old defensive lineman Calais Campbell, who could help a good defense in their rotation but is wasting the likely final season of his Hall of Fame career here, too.
Let’s be clear, the Ravens trying desperately to get Bears back-up Tyson Bagent or demoted Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett isn’t to save the season … it is literally to just be able to field a team with two QBs for a stretch of time. The Ravens will not have quality QB play this season, and if Jackson leaves, who knows when they will ever again (somebody ask DeCosta about Kyle Boller if you can find him; he’s cowering behind Sashi last I heard).
The only way, at age 32, with a terrible offensive line, this was going to have a chance to work was if Jackson was performing like the best player in football and drawing loads of attention from the defense with his legs and opening up space for Henry to get a head of steam before contact. DeCosta trade fail Cam Jurgens has made the run blocking worse (0.30 yards before contact for RBs in his first start; 0.75 in his second), Jackson is on IR and we are looking at having a backup QB from outside the building potentially start Thursday, or undrafted, beat-up rookie Joe Fagnano.
It’s over for Henry here. It has no shot to be even slightly below functional, let alone league average.
Doyle, the rookie offensive coordinator, is horribly out of his depth without the real genius, Jackson, on the field. And they are wasting what’s left of Henry's remarkable career, at the age where virtually all RB careers die ( we told you in the spring ). Yet  Doyle is running Henry more than any back in the NFL and it's not getting better .
He is getting crushed at or behind the line of scrimmage, there is no under-center rush attack without Vega Ioane at center (he was out with a knee injury and they pushed him back to guard after the desperate ploy for Jurgens ). Henry leads the NFL with 158 carries  - this is ridiculous; a winning team with a team with a real offense could get way more out of him with less load – and ranks 29th at 4.0 yards per carry.
The last five weeks Henry is 33rd in the NFL at 3.6 yards/carry. That's the reality without Jackson.
For the season, Henry is 36th in the NFL at 0.87 yards before contact – that ain’t gonna work and it will get worse as Jurgens, a major medical red flag, gets beatdown in the  second half of the season and with Simpson a waste of $10M and with the tackles getting exposed, too. How can I be 100% sure this will be an unmitigated disaster run game without Jackson? Here’s the breakdown for Henry:
With Jackson : 75 rush – 340 yards – 7 TDs (4.5/carry); 20 1st Downs, 1.12 Yds B4Contact
16% rushes 0 or Neg Yards, 42.7% Success Rate, 6.7% Explosive Rate
Without Jackson : 83 – 292 – 1 (3.5/carry); 12 1st Downs, 0.65 Yds B4Contract
23% rushes 0 or Neg Yds, 33.7% Success, 2.4% Explosive Rate
Check please. Let the selfish GM who is never at fault and always shuns accountability do right by this man and move the remaining $6M of his deal and get back some picks.
He doesn’t want to leave. For whatever reason, he is dead against it.
He doesn’t owe them anything, this isn’t what DeCosta sold him and running him into the ground with below-grade QBs and a failure offensive line serves no one. Give rookie “Joker” Adam Randall carries , run Wild Cat with Justice Hill. Empty out that playbook from the genius OC you hired when he was 29 years old (who comes from a coaching family tree of almost nothing but acute play-calling failures) .
How about this for the mooks in the front office who haven’t worked hard in years and operate like made men who have jobs for life and peacock around like they’ve accomplished something:
FIND A REAL FOOTBALL PLAYER ON WAIVERS. GET OFF YOUR ASS ON A TUESDAY AND STEAL SOMEONE OFF A PRACTICE SQUAD LIKE THE RAIDERS STOLE DARREN WALLER FROM YOU. BACK UP FOR YOUR BS FOR JUST ONCE. PLEASE. SHOW HOW SMART YOU ARE AND FIND A DECENT BACK TO PLAY OUT THE STRING.
They are losers and have managed to be losers, even with Jackson producing what should have been three MVP seasons. And they are fat and lazy and entitled, because the owner always fired assistant coaches and never asked real questions of personnel (him claiming DeCosta essentially "hits on 80% of his transactions" back in January told you how little Mostly Silent Steve pays attention anymore ).
I’ve known it forever, the league has known it for years and despite getting most of the Baltimore corporate media sucking from their thumb, the fans see DeCosta and Brown for the frauds they are now, too.  (And longtime Ravens coordinator Wink Martindale breaks it down below).
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Ravens Have Initiated Trade Talks For This QB With Lamar Jackson Possibly Out For The Season
full_text:
The Ravens are in a dire situation with the quarterback position, getting three passers injured in an ugly loss to Buffalo Sunday including losing Lamar Jackson, possibly for the year, with a serious thumb injury. And they are trying desperately to line up a quarterback to be in uniform ahead of Thursday’s game against Jacksonville, according to league sources.
Jackson was hurt on his first dropback of the game in what became a third-straight ugly defeat (36-10, this time), getting hit in the hand by pass rusher Greg Rousseau, who destroyed Baltimore’s pathetic offensive line all game. Jackson is headed to Injured Reserve and rookie head coach Jesse Minter acknowledged after the game it could be season-ending, With the way this season is going, even a four-week absence would probably end the season as Jackson doesn’t have a viable contract for 2027 and has GM Eric DeCosta by the throat in contract leverage and could want out next season; he won’t be playing in garbage games or quasi-garbage games.
Backup Snoop Huntley left the game with a toe injury that will likely keep him from being able to start Thursday and possibly to play at all. And rookie emergency QB Joe Fagnano, an undrafted rookie forced into action, was getting treatment on his ankle/foot throughout the second half and his status for Week 9 is in question as well with such a quick turnaround.
“We'll do everything in our power to keep rolling, to keep this thing going, to get it back on the right side,” Minter said after the game, alluding to the QB issue. “Again, with whatever that looks like, and whoever that's playing. If it's Joe, we have a lot of belief in Joe, whoever it is. But that's what we'll do."
The Ravens had to begin reaching out to other front offices, immediately Sunday, as relying on free agency to fly someone in, work them out, make sure they can pass a physical and get them signed in time to play Thursday is a stretch. A trade would be ideal and while there are few options in that vein who already have an understanding of the system rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle is operating.
The Ravens top pursuit is Bears back-up quarterback Tyson Bagent, according to multiple high-ranking NFL personnel execs. They have reached out to Chicago, but are in a desperate position, DeCosta already got fleeced trading a second-round pick for a concussed and suspect offensive lineman . Multiple league sources told me through the summer that the Bears were rebuffing all overtures for Badgent (who makes $4M this year and $4M next year), who they believe can be a valuable back-up in Ben Johnson’s system.
“Chicago doesn’t have to trade him,” one NFL GM told me. “They like him … Wonder how hard they squeeze DeCosta?”
The Bears signed Bagent to a contract extension in part because of that upside; he has great athleticism and the ability to run option plays and try to generate something for a Baltimore run game that is going nowhere (32-year-old back Derrick Henry is getting swallowed up at the line of scrimmage in the traditional run game).
Bagent, 26, was signed as an un-drafted free agent in 2023 out of tiny Shepherd College and was rushed into starting duty. When Johnson arrived last year (with Doyle on staff) they took a liking to him. Bagent played in three games this season with Caleb Williams was out, completing 66% of his passes for 6.4 yards/attempt and a 63.9 rating. The Bears play at Seattle on Monday night, which also complicates things.
He is well-versed in the offense, his legs can help sustain things but he is not one to push the ball downfield. The Bears are carrying three QBs, including veteran Case Keenum. Broncos third QB Sam Ehlinger – the Broncos offense is similar to Baltimore’s with Denver coach Sean Payton Doyle’s primary mentor, could be another option. Ehlinger was inactive for Denver's game Sunday.
A high-ranking official from another NFLclub also suggested Jacoby Brissett as a viable option for the Ravens. "That's the other name I heard they are interested in, besides the back-up in Chicago," he told me. It's unclear at this point if the Ravens have contacted the Cardinals but this would also make sense.
Brissett had a career year in 2026, but carries a very manageable $1.5M base salary and the Cardinals want to get a look at rookie Carson Beck, and the rebuilding team benched Brissett for journeyman Gardner Minshew Sunday in a comeback win over Dallas. Execs around the NFL expect the Cardinals, in a rebuild, to move veterans before the trade deadline.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Major Lamar Jackson Injury Update And 4 Key Takeaways From Ravens Third Straight Defeat
full_text:
It’s November, the Ravens have two AFC victories, their feckless general manager has been exposed for the utter failure that he is once again, and his offensive line is truly a remarkable disaster which can’t stop getting quarterbacks hurt.
Welcome to the midpoint of the 2026 season; it’s even worse than 2025.
When you fire a future Hall of Fane head coach and over-empower Eric DeCosta, the huckster who can’t evaluate players or negotiate contracts with a modicum of acumen or professionalism, you can torpedo a season almost before it starts. This qualifies - another year of Lamar Jackson missing more time than he plays and more unsightly football in all three phases and Sunday’s 36-10 debacle at Buffalo may just have been the last truly meaningful game this fading team (4-4) plays.
Jackson was smashed in the hand by Bills edge rusher Greg Rousseau on his first snap back from a high-ankle sprain that Ravens overmatched rookie coach Jesse Minter insisted was day-to-day for nearly three weeks (allegedly Ravens $30M “closer” Trey Hendrickson was active for this game; another DeCosta scam gone wrong ). Backup Snoop Huntley was immediately under assault and he was gone before the midpoint of the second quarter with a toe injury and so undrafted rookie Joe Faganao took the rest of this beating in his NFL debut behind a line that was shameful in its approach and execution (Fagnano was receiving regular medical attention by the third quarter).
Minter said Jackson will head to Injured Reserve and when asked if it could be season-enning he said, "potentially." It's also potentially his final game as a Raven, in that case. Even a four-week absence means garbage time in the season for Baltimore and with no real contract moving forward, it would be stupid - even by DeCosta standards (super low bar) - for Jackson to play again. Baltimore has no tie-breaking hope as it's two conference wins are against teams a combined 3-11 (Colts and Titans).
"Things happen," Minter offered, "but it's how you respond."
DeCosta better get real about an always-necessary rebuild that should have started with his firing in January. And with the trade deadline now nine days away and his roster overloaded with horrible contracts for bad football players, a loss to the Jaguars should trigger a natural resetting of this organization that will beg major questions of the owner, Steve Bisciotti, and DeCosta for charting this path in the first place.
The fools in charge of this franchise better get another QB (or two) in here, but good luck finding one who had much experience with a coaching staff full of novices. This is dire, and it could definitely get worse. They face a stout Jacksonville team at home Thursday and the only other QB who was around them this summer for any period of time, Skyler Thompson, was put on IR before Fagnano for his chance to make the team.
A toe problem for Huntley can be a very big deal, and certainly more than enough to keep him from playing on a short week after being unable to play a half of football with the injury. Executing a trade and getting a player in Baltimore in time to know the offense and be able to serve even as a back-up with only one real day of practice this week is impossible. Will have to be a free agent or someone off a practice squad I figure, but either way this is quite a bleak scenario for the first few days of November. Fagnano will clearly be ailing after all the huge shots he took, and he too could miss what little practice time there is this week.
"We have to make sure Joe came through the game okay," Minter said, acknowledging more transactions might come with Huntley under review, too.
Jackson can call his shot next season given how he took DeCosta to school on his contract and why would want to sign on for more of this, you have to start to wonder. Miami will make a push, among others.
I don’t want to hear about injuries to centers who aren’t even starting centers and were never going to be starting centers. Danny Pinter and Jovaughn Gwyn were silly vanity plays by a loser GM, he always needed a real center and the desperate, panic overpay for Cam Jurgens – very likely about to be benched in Philly – has already backfired, badly.
Jurgens missed two games with a concussion, offered nothing in the ground game in Week 7 and was totally exposed in Week 8. Somehow first-round pick Vega Ioane is the only competent lineman on this team, and he was hurt. Jurgens got abused on simple stints, the interior got abused and Baltimore had 52 yards in the first – even on three QBs that’s a joke. They were destroyed at the line of scrimmage. Rousseau undressed right tackle Roger Rosengarten whenever he wanted, or Ronnie Stanley on the other side.
Buffalo blitzed with abandon, and produced 9 QB hits, four hurries and four sacks on 17 dropbacks in the first half. Stanley is not a starting-caliber left tackle, DeCosta lit $10M on fire signing John Simpson and they continued to commit crushing penalties when they did move the ball, with Stanley’s hold negating Derrick Henry’s TD on the opening drive of the second half (Baltimore settled for a field goal).
"It's honestly a tough eval (evaluation) right now," Minter said, deferring to a tape study that is going to be ugly for all involved.
And while Mark Andrews is not an OL, he must be mentioned for being a total no show yet again. He is there to help the linemen, and it is beyond ridiculous how little he has to offer as a football player and how unthinkable it is that DeCosta is paying his buddy $13.5M a year to do nothing while letting Iasiah Likely walk.
But hey, "genius" coordinator Declan Doyle didn't get shutout for the third straight week after halftime. He put up a field goal.
All the tough talk about kicker Tyler Loop, now’s the time to make the move to Jake Moody. Full disclosure – this team is no good, the GM is a mega fraud and they should be selling everyone they can before the deadline and playing the kids. But given the talking points DeCosta has been giving his puppet coach about this kicker – I believe this is it and Moody will get his shot (careful what you ask for).
Loop’s opening kickoff went out of bounds, setting up the Bills with great field position on what became a scoring drive. With the QBs under duress, every point would matter, and Loop missed a 27-yard field goal on a perfect day that would have tied the game at 10; Buffalo scored off what amounted to that turnover and the Ravens wouldn’t get any closer.
DeCosta is desperate for scapegoats and his greatest (only) strength as an NFL exec is convincing the glazed over billionaire he works for that it’s always someone else’s fault. The kid kicker will pay for this.
Stop me if you’ve heard this before – the defense was awesome in the first half and then gave up a 50-yard explosive and a TD on the first drive of the second half and showed their true colors after the half? Yeah, that’s who they have been under DeCosta for years, and the half-field shot to DJ Moore, beating Marlon Humphrey, after Buffalo just missed on one late in the first half, told you all you need to know.
Good on the defense for bowing up after a terrible first drive and they showed some badly-missing determination and gumption on repeated short-yardage situations to stay in the game into the second half despite the QB injuries, but you knew the levy would start to break in the second half.
While Buffalo couldn’t finish drives and Josh Allen was off in the first half, they ran 44 plays in the first 30 minutes and the volume was going to catch up to this awful defense as the game went on,, when Minter gets utterly thrashed week after week as a head coach and play caller.
And Minter got destroyed in the second half again. He is worse than Zach Orr, folks. Allen produced 20 points in the second half, rolling up 219 yards on a ridiculous 7.5 yards/play before he made way for the back-up. Minter stinks at being a head coach and coordinator at the same time and…

title: Lamar Jackson Suffers Potentially Significant Thumb Injury At Buffalo
full_text:
Lamar Jackson came back to the Ravens from a three-week absence and suffered what appeared to be a significant thumb injury on his first snap, casting further doubt on a season already on the brink.
Jackson dropped back to pass under immediate pressure, with Bills EDGE Greg Rousseau following through on a pass rush and hitting Jackson’s right hand with some velocity as he released an incomplete pass. Jackson immediately grabbed his hand, began moving to the sidelines with great pace and was whisked back to the locker room for immediate medical attention. The CBS cameras picked up a shot of the hand in which there was clearly damage around the thumb and Jackson appeared to be in great pain.
The Ravens ruled out Jackson for the rest of the game before the first quarter had concluded. Backup Snoop Huntley suffered a foot injury shortly after entering the game and undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano made his NFL debut midway through the second quarter and he has to play the rest of the game (running back Justice Hill would replace Fagnano if he got hurt). Jackson came back to the field in the second half with a large cast/splint on his right hand.; by the end of the third quarter Fagnano was receiving attention on his foot and ankle.
Thumb injuries on a quarterback’s throwing hand tend to be very difficult to navigate, and will beg questions about the position not just with a quick turnaround against Jacksonville on Thursday, but llikely beyond that.
A former NFL head coach was I was texting with during the game immediately commented that it looked serious to him, he has seen multiple quarterbacks take hits like that and it tends to be problematic with the tendons and ligaments around the thumb and all the torque needed to deliver the ball with velocity and accuracy
Back-up quarterback Snoop Huntley was thrust back into the game after successive games in which he and the offense failed to score a point in the second half with rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle calling plays for the first time this year. The Ravens were hopeful that Jackson could reignite their failing run game with Derrick Henry looking his age at 32 behind a bad offensive line, but Huntley has not activated his legs and he cannot push the ball downfield.
The Ravens win 70% of their regular season games that Jackson starts and are 7-14 without him, with general manger Eric DeCosta a fraudulent roster builder and talent evaluator. Decosta has also repeatedly failed to extend Jackson like a normal front office would, putting themselves in  a massive hole now, with Jackson a de-facto free agent in 2027 , with a no-trade clause and no-franchise tag clause and $85M cap hit, and Baltimore a team in serious decline liking having to gut the roster next year with a $370M payroll heavy on bloated contracts and short on blue chip players.
There is a growing drumbeat in NFL personnel circles that the Miami Dolphins will make a serious push for Jackson, who is a native of that area and spends his offseasons there. The Ravens maintained Jackson was “day-to-day” while missing three weeks with the high-ankle sprain, during which time he could barely run or practice for the most part. DeCosta made Jackson play out his entire rookie deal, and endure a potential collusion case while on a non-exclusive tag to get a fair-market deal the first time; all highly unusual but that's how this suspect front office operates.
As for the game, Huntley was getting attention on the sidelines after the Ravens cut the deficit to 10-7 early on, and Fagnano (UCONN) soon entered as the emergency third QB. The Ravens came into Buffalo with just one AFC win, and losses to the Bills and Jaguars in the span of five days would effectively end their season and perhaps prompt selling veterans at the trade deadline.

title: Four Pivotal Ravens Matchups to Watch vs. Bills
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens' Week 8 bout against the Buffalo Bills could ultimately be decided by battles between specific position groups or individual players outperforming their counterparts on the other side of the ball.
In the team's first game with two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson back under center after he missed the last three games with an ankle sprain, they're entering this matchup as slight road underdogs.
If the Ravens prevail, they will improve to 5-3 and will likely still be in last place in the AFC North standings since they're the only team without a division win, and even if the other three lose on Sunday, they'd all be tied with the same number of losses. Here are the four matchups that can either make or break this game:
The Ravens' two-time Pro Bowl wideout ranks seventh in the league in receiving yards with a team-leading 608 yards and is one of only two pass catchers averaging over 100 receiving yards per game with his 101.3, trailing only the reigning Offensive Player of the Year, Jaxon Smith-Njigba. An area where Flowers has feasted the most this year, no matter who has been under center, is over the middle of the field.
First-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has consistently found ways to get him matched up against off-ball linebackers in space, which is a mismatch in favor of the Ravens every time. With Jackson back in the lineup, Flowers can get back to stretching the field vertically, as the two of them were routinely linking up for 20-plus yard plays through the air to begin the season before injuries interrupted their lethal connection.
With Buffalo's elite blocking unit at full strength in this game, Baltimore is going to need to play to its full potential in the trenches both along the interior and on the edge. In order to slow down James Cook and a Bills' rushing attack, which ranks fifth in the league in yards, second in yards per attempt (5.1) and first in expected points added by the ground game (31.71), they'll need to win at the point of attack and own the line of scrimmage. With a quarterback like Josh Allen who can plow his way for a first down in just about any short-to-medium yardage situation, limiting their gains on early downs will be paramount, as will maintaining rush-lane integrity to limit and prevent scrambles.
Some specific individual matchups to keep an eye on will be the Ravens' four-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Trey Hendrickson against Bills' left tackle Dion Dawkins, two-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike against guards O'Cyrus Torrence and Alec Anderson and outside linebacker Mike Green against backup right tackle Tylan Grable, who is filling in for injured veteran Spencer Brown .
On the flip side, the Ravens also need to dictate terms in the trenches on offense against a talented Buffalo front in order to have success in Jackson's long-awaited return to the lineup. It won't be easy along the interior, especially without stud first-round rookie Vega Ioane, who is out with a knee injury . It means that they'll have to face the defensive tackle duo of veteran Ed Oliver and second-year breakout Deone Walker with yet another different configuration, as this will mark the second game for two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens since being acquired via trade and the second start of the season for Andrew Vorhees.
On the edge, the only player who's been consistently generating pressure for the Bills is defensive end Gregory Rousseau. He leads the team with six sacks but hasn't recorded one in their last three games, and since he lines up on the defense's left side, he'll be seeing a lot of Ravens right tackle Roger Rosengarten, who has had a nice bounce-back campaign as one of the team's most consistent offensive linemen.
The Ravens have struggled to limit the impact of the opposing team's wideouts for all four quarters this season, and their corners are the primary culprits, allowing the third-most receiving yards to the receiver position with 1,271. While the Bills haven't gotten much prolific production from their wideouts, with none over 300 receiving yards entering this game, they tend to make key plays in high-leverage moments, and veteran D.J. Moore will be back in action for the first time since Week 4. After horrendous showings in last week's loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, Baltimore will need a big bounce-back game from their starting outside duo of Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins in this one if they hope to avoid getting in a shootout.

title: Ravens Week 8 Inactives, With Lamar Jackson Returning
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens may be a few more AFC losses from being out of contending more and into player-development mode with another season in the balance, but they are leaning into their experience Sunday at Buffalo.
With the return of Lamar Jackson from a three-week absence with a high-ankle sprain, Baltimore badly needs to beat the Bills to turn the tide after blowing double-digit leads in the second half two straight weeks in losses to the division rival Bengals and Browns. With that in mind, general manager Eric DeCosta is leaning into his highest-paid players at Buffalo – despite their historic struggles – and the inactives for this game speak to that dynamic.
The Ravens also knew their top pick, guard Vega Ioane (14th overall and the best center on the team as well) was out with a knee injury. Perhaps he can get back for Thursday’s game bit this is obviously a short week. Rookie receiver Elijah Sarratt (fourth round) was also inactive and the Baltimore native has yet to find his way in this offense.
Rookie slot corner Chandler Rivers (fifth-round) has strong instincts attack the ball on screens in front of him but has been picked on badly in coverage – Baltimore’s slot defense has been atrocious - and has plenty to do with them getting DeCosta-ed week after week – and he is not playing in this game, either.
Young guard Emery Jones has been battling injury which means a sixth new offensive line combination in eight games, with struggling Andrew Vorhees likely thrust back into that role. Aeneas Peebles – the only defensive tackle DeCosta took in a historically significant 2025 DT draft despite it being a big need – still cannot see the field and he was scratched again. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano is again the emergency third QB.
Starting safety Jaylinn Hawkins was ruled out with injury on Friday.
Jackson’s return gives this team a chance to reverse the course of its season, but it carries almost identical warts and serious personnel concerns as the pathetic product DeCosta fielded in 2025, when he won a power struggle with potential Hall of Fame head coach John Harbaugh, gutting that staff that included offensive coordinator Todd Monken, now head coach of the Browns and a top midseason candidate for NFL Coach of the Year, along with Harbaugh (Giants).
DeCosta and team president Sashi Brown branded this a Super Bowl contender when they hired novice head coach Jesse Minter and built one of only two staffs in the entire NFL without a former NFL head coach on the roster . Yet about 20 percent of the Week 1 roster was compromised of players without an NFL snap, while at the same time the bulk of the team-record $370M payroll was going to veterans decidedly on the decline with ridiculously bloated contracts (Roquan Smith, Marlon Humphrey, Mark Andrews, John Simpson).
The coming weeks will be critical to determining how much longer they can afford to prop up some of them, as we discussed recently with longtime NFL GM Marty Hurney on "The Daily Flock."

title: Bills' Week 9 Injury Outlook: What We Know About DJ Moore, James Cook, Spencer Brown
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills ' offense was already without one starter in Week 8.
After the Bills took the field without starting right tackle Spencer Brown against the Baltimore Ravens on November 1, four more key offensive players wound up needing medical attention at some point.
Although none of the four injuries appear overly concerning, they certainly warrant monitoring closely as the new week unfolds.
Being that their Week 9 game is next Monday, the Bills will benefit from one extra day of rest and recovery prior to visiting the Minnesota Vikings on November 9.
As is becoming customary, Bills' first-year coach Joe Brady offered no injury information during his Monday press conference .
Here are outlooks for Brown and the four other offensive players, including running back James Cook and wide receiver DJ Moore, who made fans hold their collective breath at different points during Sunday's 36-10 win.
Brown missed the first two practices due to back issues coming out of the bye week. He managed to participate in a limited capacity on Friday before being ruled questionable for the game.
"I told Spencer I was going to give him all the way up until game time," said Brady after the win. "We were able to make the decision last night because he wasn't feeling like he could be the best version of himself, but he was close."
Brown left the October 12 victory in Los Angeles after 16 snaps as a result of a flare-up. Only six days later, he returned to the lineup and played the entirety of the October 18 win in Las Vegas.
If all goes according to plan , Brown will be back at right tackle on Monday Night Football against the Vikings.
"It's just making sure I'm fully physically ready to go, and make this push for the next five weeks, and get a little mini bye again, and make the push at the end of the season," said Brown on October 28.
Bills RT Spencer Brown is inactive today vs Ravens pic.twitter.com/c8jGoAAZ2L
After getting folded up on a fourth-quarter carry up the middle, Cook was officially evaluated for a head injury.
The scare happened on the second snap of the fourth quarter. The reigning NFL rushing champion gained five yards on 2nd-and-4 run before getting crunched in a pile. Cook stayed down for a minute before popping up and leaving the field without help.
Initially ruled as questionable to return, Cook reentered with 9:31 remaining and proceeded to gain four yards on his final touch of the day. With Buffalo in control, there was no need to push the envelope with the RB1.
Moore encountered a potential knee issue midway through the fourth quarter. He caught a four-yard pass to convert a 4th-and-1, and potentially hyped-extended his knee while being tackled.
Gingerly walking off to the sideline , Moore made a visit to the blue evaluation tent where he apparently received good news. Returning to the sideline following the possession, quarterback Josh Allen went to check on his wide receiver. The two met as Moore emerged from the tent, apparently reassuring the quarterback that serious injury has been avoided.
Josh Allen: "Is he in here?" *DJ Moore walks out of the blue tent* *Josh Allen smiles* #BillsMafia @BuffaloPlus pic.twitter.com/1uKDwF15H9
Moore gave an on-field interview to NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe after the game. Subsequently addressing reporters in the locker room, he did not sound worried.
"Like 90 percent, I feel good. Football, you always gonna have some nicks and bruises and probably got those. I don't feel them right now, but I probably feel them like in 15 minutes," said Moore, who finished with 82 receiving yards and one touchdown.
It appears that the Bills could be without Palmer for multiple weeks depending upon the severity of his hamstring injury that happened in the first quarter against the Ravens.
With 2:29 remaining in the opening period, Allen took a deep shot downfield to a streaking Palmer, who pulled up lame in the middle of the route. The Bills initially tabbed Palmer as doubtful to return before downgrading the wide receiver to out in the third quarter.
Palmer, who was plagued by injury for much of the 2025 campaign , could be on his way to Injured Reserve, especially with the Bills needing a roster spot for wide receiver Tyrell Shavers when he comes off the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list.
Anderson was banged up on the game's first possession, but missed only six total snaps.
On a play where Khalil Shakir scored a touchdown that was taken off the scoreboard following a review, Anderson appeared to injure his right leg. He went into the blue tent while Austin Corbett replaced him for the remainder of the scoring drive.
Anderson spoke to reporters following the game , and he did not give any indication of a potentially lingering injury.

title: Bills' Chances of Landing Budda Baker Take Hit With Trade Rumor From Adam Schefter
full_text:
One of the positions the Buffalo Bills need to address before the NFL trade deadline passes on Nov. 10 is safety.
The Bills haven't gotten great play out of their starters in 2026, Cole Bishop and C.J. Gardner-Johnson, and that's especially true with Gardner-Johnson, who is also a candidate to self-destruct and get himself cut at any minute.
Buffalo doesn't have great options behind those two, either, with Damar Hamlin being extremely limited and Jalon Kilgore being unproven as a rookie.
At the very least, the Bills need more depth, but we'd love to see general manager Brandon Beane swing for the fences and get a proven starter who can make a big impact in a Bills defense surrendering the third-most passing yards per game.
Unfortunately for the Bills, one of the best potential options to fill their need at safety, Arizona Cardinals defensive back Budda Baker, might not be available at the trade deadline.
This comes from ESPN's Adam Schefter, who noted on "The Pat McAfee Show" that Arizona may not be keen on trading him.
"That guy has been such a stud I don't know that Budda Baker is gonna be traded," Schefter said . "I don't think Arizona wants to move on from a guy that has meant so much to that franchise. (Baker) is such a baller)."
There's no doubt that Baker means a lot to a team he has spent his entire career with. In fact, you could even call the eight-time Pro Bowler and four-time All-Pro a franchise great at this point.
However, it just doesn't make sense for the rebuilding Cardinals to hold on to him.
After all, Arizona is at least a few years away from being able to compete for anything significant and Baker is going to turn 31 in January and could be well into his decline before that happens.
The timelines just don't match up here, and with the Cardinals' need for more draft capital to accelerate their rebuild, they must seriously consider trading the veteran defensive back.
Baker would be a massive upgrade for the Bills' secondary.
The veteran defensive back is a difference-maker as a box safety who can both improve Buffalo's run defense and pass-rush with his ability to get after the quarterback when asked to blitz.
He doesn't offer much in coverage, but the Bills can deploy Bishop back deep. Adding Baker would also move Gardner-Johnson down the depth chart and improve the safety room's depth.
It's also worth noting that Baker's contract runs through 2027 , so he won't be a short-term rental for Buffalo. He also has a clear out in that deal, so the Bills can cut ties if things don't pan out.
When it comes to draft compensation, a fourth-round pick may be enough to get it done. The Bills can easily afford that with the team having its fourth-round selections in each of the next three years, and Spotrac projects the Bills will have a fourth-round comp pick next year, also.
If Beane and the Bills can find a way to get something done, there's no question Buffalo should pull the trigger.

title: Buffalo Bills Highest And Lowest Graded Players from Week 8 Victory
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills took care of business in Week 8, handing the Baltimore Ravens a 36-10 defeat .
Buffalo was fresh off their bye week, but they weren't exactly sharp to begin the game. Despite the Ravens losing Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley in the first half, Buffalo had a lead of just 16-10 roughly halfway through the third quarter.
They were able to kick things into gear at that point, finishing with 17 unanswered points as they cruised to a record of 6-1. It was their most lopsided victory of the season, and that should have been the case given the injuries Baltimore sustained.
What was most encouraging was seeing signs of life from the defense, which included two unexpected players, Geno Stone and Te'Cory Couch , stepping up and performing well.
Let's dive into the Pro Football Focus scores to see who were among the best, as well as who fell short for Buffalo in Week 8.
Kaleb Elarms-Orr was able to shine in this one, although he did play just 14 snaps. He seems to do his best work when he's not asked to carry a heavy load and continues to show promise.
Stone broke up a pass which was then intercepted by Davison Igbinosun.  Stone was able to get the best of his former team in Week 8. The final defender was Couch, who played primarily in the nickel and was far better than expected with a 79.9.
Offensively, Dalton Kincaid was their top-rated player with an 82.9 . He finished with 86 yards and a touchdown in four receptions.
Josh Allen was their other offensive player in the top five, earning an 82.3. Allen had three total touchdowns and would have had an even higher grade if not for his one interception.
DeWayne Carter and Jackson Hawes each finished under 30 points, which is unfortunate. Carter was a stud early in the year but has cooled off as of late. Hawes has been in a sophomore slump, and even had a pass go off his hands get intercepted on Sunday.
Michael Hoecht and T.J. Parker fell at No. 3 and No. 4 on this list, although Parker did record a sack. Dawson Knox rounded out the bottom five as every tight end not named Dalton Schultz had a rough outing.
Overall, Buffalo played well but they will need more from their role players in Week 9 as they take on the Minnesota Vikings, who are looking for some revenge after suffering their first loss of the season.

title: Buffalo Bills Are No Longer the Last Team to Accomplish Unthinkable Feat
full_text:
Back in 1974, the Buffalo Bills accomplished a feat that does not happen very often.
In a game against the New York Jets that season, the Bills failed to complete a single pass on two attempts in the contest against Gang Green yet they still managed to win, 16-12.
Since then, no other team had accomplished that feat in the NFL before it was done on Sunday in Week 8.
It was the Tampa Bay Buccaneers who snapped the 52-year streak after they defeated the Atlanta Falcons, 16-0, without completing any passes, which is unthinkable, especially in this day and age when throwing the football is as prominent as ever.
The Bucs attempted just three passes in the entire game and actually finished with -2 passing yards officially because quarterback Baker Mayfield got sacked once.
The reason behind the Bucs' lack of passing had to do with the inclement weather conditions that brought heavy rain. Instead, Tampa Bay decided to run the football a whopping 56 times, gaining 324 yards in all.
Seven of Tampa Bay's points came on a rushing touchdown, and the other nine came from three field goals made by Bucs kicker Chase McLaughlin, who made kicks from 46, 34 and 42 yards.
"We knew it was going to be a nasty day and what type of conditions it was going to be," head coach Todd Bowles said . "We were worried about ball security, and we took care of it other than the fumble in the end zone. We didn't say we were not going to throw the ball; the conditions told [Offensive Coordinator Zac Robinson] that. You could see, with the downpour and the wind blowing, you can kind of see that ball wasn't going anywhere."
Unlike the Bucs, the Falcons did attempt to throw the football, but that did not yield positive results. Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. threw four picks and completed just 8-of-24 passes for 125 scoreless yards.
Before the Bills and the Bucs, there were eight other instances of a team winning a game without completing a pass, but none of those occurred after 1950.
Here's a look at those instances:
The Bucs' accomplishing that feat is especially shocking because of the amount of passes that are thrown in the modern era. It was considered unfathomable to think a team could win the way the Bucs did on Sunday, but here we are.
In the Bills' aforementioned victory over the Jets, Joe Ferguson was Buffalo's quarterback .
While he didn't complete a pass on two attempts, he did rush for 14 yards and a touchdown on 10 carries. O.J. Simpson and Jim Braxton were responsible for most of the offensive output, with Simpson totaling 31 carries for 117 yards and Braxton finishing with 84 yards and a score on 17 totes.
The Jets didn't do much throwing, either, as Joe Namath was only able to complete two passes on 18 attempts, totaling 33 yards. Namath tossed three interceptions, also.

title: Why Bills' Defensive Performance vs. Ravens Feels Like Fool's Gold
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills had several question marks surrounding them coming out of the bye week.
Whether it be the continued sloppy, yet somehow effective play of the offense or the lackluster defensive displays, first-year head coach Joe Brady and new Bills’ defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard had a lot to figure out despite the hot start to the season in the win column.
And Leonhard, specifically, seemed to have a target on his back from the fanbase for a unit that ranked in the bottom fourth of the league in just about every important category on that side of the ball entering Week 8.
On Sunday, however, that same struggling unit dominated the Baltimore Ravens at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, holding the AFC North squad to just 10 points: the lowest output they’ve held an opposing team to all season.
Undoubtedly, it was a great sight to see, and one that was desperately needed.
But, was it really all that impressive? Should Bills Mafia believe that a defensive turnaround is on the horizon for the remainder of the season?
It’s certainly a pleasant thought . . . though, it might be more of a pipe dream.
Given the unique circumstances surrounding the outcome on Sunday, what everyone witnessed this past weekend from Buffalo’s defense might be more of a mirage than some sort of miraculous flip of the script.
Not only did Baltimore get just one snap from franchise quarterback Lamar Jackson before he had to leave the game due to a thumb injury, but backup Tyler Huntley—who had started the team’s previous three games—lasted just five snaps before he exited with a foot ailment.
From there on, it was undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano who finished out the game in their collective absence.
It was Fagnano’s first regular-season action in the National Football League, and he finished the game with 91 passing yards and one interception after completing a mere 47.6% of his passes for the game.
He was also sacked three times and lost one fumble.
So, just by looking at the numbers, some might find it hard to find any fault in the outing. And, for the most part, they’d be right.
However, what transpired is exactly the type of performance that a defense should put forth against a rookie emergency third-string quarterback who is unexpectedly playing his first professional game—on the road—in the NFL.
To be quite frank, nobody should be patting Leonhard or his players on the back.
The goal, in the end, should be for the defense to put blinders on the rest of the way. The unit’s performances through the first six games of the 2026 campaign were so bad that it’s going to take a cornucopia full of solid performances before any praise is deserved or thanks is given.
Ultimately, the first real test for the defense might not come until—fittingly—Thanksgiving night when the Kansas City Chiefs come to Western New York for a primetime holiday showdown.
Well, the offenses of Buffalo’s next three opponents—the Minnesota Vikings ( 20 PPG ), New York Jets ( 21.3 PPG ), and Miami Dolphins ( 16.7 PPG )—have collectively been held to below 20 points 13 times so far this fall.
Comparatively speaking, the Chiefs and quarterback Patrick Mahomes have been unable to break that threshold just once this season while averaging 23.9 points per contest and topping the 30-point mark three times.
For that reason, fans should probably pump the brakes a little on believing there is a defensive resurgence happening during the second half of the season before Buffalo goes up against a solid offensive counterpart later in November.
The Bills’ banged-up secondary did limit the AFC’s leading receiver entering Week 8, Zay Flowers, to zero yards and zero catches on five targets in the matchup on Sunday, while also limiting perennial All-Pro running back Derrick Henry to only 60 total yards ( 53 yards rushing, 7 yards receiving ) and just one touchdown on 13 touches ( 11 carries, 2 receptions ), so there are certainly areas to build upon.
However, how much of that was the product of the incredibly unusual occurrences that unfolded on Sunday?
That will seemingly be the million-dollar question moving forward . . . and Leonhard’s defensive unit must continue to answer the call.
A repeat performance on Monday Night Football in Minneapolis next week against the Vikings , who just dropped their first game of the season after scoring just 15 points against the Detroit Lions, would be a great place to start.

title: Four Winners & One Loser From Bills Lopsided Win Against Ravens in Week 8
full_text:
Once again, the Buffalo Bills proved to be one of the top teams in the league after a bye week as they defeated the Baltimore Ravens easily in Week 8.
It might not have been the prettiest game throughout, but Buffalo still won 36-10, thanks in large part to the Ravens dealing with multiple injuries at quarterback . Lamar Jackson was lost to a thumb injury on the first play of the game, and not long after that, backup Tyler Huntley went down with a foot injury.
Undrafted free agent Joe Fagnano was no match for Josh Allen and the Bills, who remain the top team in the AFC East. With this one in the books, let's see who stood out as both winners and losers for the Bills this weekend.
Nursing a 10-7 lead, the Bills needed a play from their defense in the second quarter, and Cole Bishop delivered. The safety went after Tyler Huntley on a blitz and lit him up, forcing a fumble in the process. The loose ball was recovered by linebacker Kaleb Elarms-Orr, and even though Buffalo was kept out of the end zone, Bishop set them up close enough that Tyler Bass knocked in a field goal to make it a 13-7 lead for the Bills.
2025 third-round pick Landon Jackson recorded his first career sack on Sunday, and did so at a great time. Baltimore had to turn to emergency third-quarterback Joe Fagnano, and he completed a couple of passes to move the Ravens to the Buffalo seven.
That's when Jackson broke free and sacked the rookie for a nine-yard loss. A couple of plays later, Tyler Loop missed a 34-yard field goal as things fell off the rails for Baltimore following Jackson's play.
Geno Stone was given a chance to prove himself on Sunday and was facing his old team. He stepped up near the end of the first half after DJ Moore fumbled the ball away. Baltimore was attempting to cut the lead going into the half, but Stone broke up a pass from quarterback Joe Fagnano.
He was unable to come up with the pick himself, but he batted the ball in the air, and rookie Davison Igbinosun ended up corraling it for his first career interception. That set up the Bills for a late field goal, sending them into the half with a nine-point lead.
Buffalo was up 10-0, but allowed the Ravens some life late in the first quarter with a costly turnover. Josh Allen threw the ball to Jackson Hawes, and while it was slightly behind the second-year tight end, Hawes had both hands on the ball.
He was unable to bring it in, however, and the ball bounced into the arms of Broderick Washington Jr. Baltimore responded with a Derrick Henry touchdown as Hawes' sophomore slump continues.
Josh Allen wasn't sharp throughout, but he threw for 289 yards with two touchdown passes and a touchdown run. His two passes put him atop the franchise leaderboard as he surpassed Jim Kelly for the most touchdown passes in team history.
Josh Allen becomes the Bills all-time leader in TD passes (259) with Jim Kelly in attendance 👏 BALvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/k62VFqausS
Allen and the Bills' offense continue to rack up points, and they just improved to 6-1 this season. Now, they turn their attention to the Minnesota Vikings, whom they will face on Monday Night Football in Week 9.

title: Josh Allen Leaps Bills Hall of Famer, Sets Another Team Record vs. Ravens
full_text:
Josh Allen may go down as the greatest Buffalo Bills player of all time. And the team record he just set will be a major addition to his resume.
The Bills took care of business off of their bye week, handling the Baltimore Ravens , 36-10, after the team lost both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injury in the game.
Allen looked like he had become the franchise's all-time passing-touchdown leader (including the playoffs) when he found Khalil Shakir on a first-quarter throw in the red zone. That only set up his first touchdown of the day: a 1-yard quarterback sneak, pushing his rushing TD total for the year to nine.
But it was D.J. Moore who hauled in the record-setting pass. Which was fitting, as Buffalo's new No. 1 wide receiver returned to the lineup for the first time since Week 4 . Shout-out to the CBS camera crew too for immediately cutting to Jim Kelly, the previous Bills' record-holder.
Adding in is connection with Dalton Kincaid in the fourth quarter, Allen is now up to 260 TD passes in his career.
Josh Allen becomes the Bills all-time leader in TD passes (259) with Jim Kelly in attendance 👏 BALvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/k62VFqausS
Allen has become the franchise's leader in several categories, including rushing touchdowns and total touchdowns scored. Next on his radar could be regular-season TD passes (237), passing yards  (35,467), and wins by a QB (101), all held by Kelly.
Kelly and Allen's mutual admiration has been shared over the years. The Hall of Fame QB joined Good Morning Football in June to discuss Allen being named the NFL's top QB in a poll run by ESPN specificallly with coaches and executives throughout the league.
"Josh is Josh. That's what he does. He runs, he makes the big plays with his legs," said Kelly in an iterview with WWE star Seth Rollins. "And yeah, you want him to protect himself a little bit more, because he does take chances. But the thing is, that's him. That's the way he plays football, and I love it."
With Allen's league-leading ninth rushing TD of the year coming in the win over Baltimore, he extended his career rushing scores to 88. He and Cam Newton are the only players in NFL history to lead their respective franchises in both passing and rushing TDs.
It is hard to quantify how diverse Allen's dual-threat skills are. Once he gets to 90 rushing TDs, he'll be tied for 14th all-time with Eric Dickerson and Curtis Martin, two Hall of Fame running backs.
That's what makes what he does through the air even more impressive. It will only be a matter of time before Allen's name is attached to more of Buffalo's all-time passing ranks when it's all said and done.
Josh Allen. Dalton Kincaid. All Buffalo in this one. BALvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/StHo4EOPvC

title: Biggest Takeaways From Buffalo Bills Week 8 Win Against Ravens
full_text:
Leading up to the showdown between the Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens, there was a lot of news surrounding the health of Lamar Jackson . He had been dealing with a high ankle sprain, which kept him out for three games, but he was back in action in Week 8 . At least for one play.
Jackson was injured on the first snap of the game when his hand hit Greg Rousseau's while attempting a pass to Zay Flowers. Jackson was quickly taken to the locker room , and Tyler Huntley took over under center. Huntley couldn't finish the first half either, as he suffered a toe injury. Baltimore turned to undrafted rookie free agent Joe Fagnano, who was the emergency third quarterback.
Despite being down to their third quarterback, the Ravens hung with the Bills much longer than expected. Eventually, the Bills pulled out in front, winning 36-10. Considering they were coming off a bye week, it was a rather sloppy performance from Buffalo, as they had far too many penalties and left points on the board.
Still, they're 6-1 and looking ahead to their big showdown with the Minnesota Vikings next week. Before we turn our attention to that game, let's look back at their latest win with the biggest takeaways from Week 8.
The Bills have one of the top offenses in the NFL, and part of that is due to Joe Brady's aggressiveness. That was on display on Sunday as he attempted four fourth-down conversions in the first quarter.
His first was a fourth-and-goal, which ended in a touchdown run from Josh Allen. They failed to convert on a fourth-and-four in the second quarter, but made up for it on fourth-and-one from the 11 on the next drive. Allen pitched the ball to James Cook, who extended the ball and converted the first down, although they needed the assistance of replay.
Brady and the Bills should have been able to score another touchdown there, but a questionable third-down run led to a loss of yards, forcing them to settle for a field goal from Tyler Bass. His final fourth-down attempt in the first half was a short pass to Ty Johnson, which moved the ball to the Baltimore 18 at the two-minute warning.
Even with the Ravens going to their third quarterback by the second quarter, this game was closer than it should have been for much of the first half. That wasn't necessarily due to the Ravens, but more so to the continued sloppy play from Buffalo.
There was a first-half interception from Josh Allen, which went off the hands of backup tight end Jackson Hawes. Shortly after the two-minute warning, there was another turnover; this time, DJ Moore fumbled it away after catching a pass at the Baltimore 20. That ended an impressive six-play, 61-yard drive and took points off the board for the home team.
An interception allowed Buffalo to score right before the half, giving them a 16-7 lead, but this game should have been a blowout going into the break.
After recording six sacks over the first three games of the season, Greg Rousseau was getting plenty of attention as a potential Defensive Player of the Year candidate . Since then, he's been quiet . That changed against the Ravens, as Rousseau impacted the game on the opening play.
While no one wants to see an opponent injured, it was a good play from Rousseau to get a hand in the way and force an incomplete pass from Jackson. He continued to create pressure and picked up his seventh sack of the season. In all, Buffalo had four sacks on the day, including the first of Landon Jackson's career.
Penalties have been a concern throughout the season, and that was the case once again in Week 8. Buffalo was flagged 10 times for 87 yards, giving the Ravens far too many free yards in the process.
They take on one of the elite defenses in Week 9 in the Minnesota Vikings. It will be a tough contest on the road and the Bills are going to have a tough time coming out with a win if they don't clean up the discipline issues.
Congratulations are in order for Josh Allen, who hit DJ Moore for a touchdown early in the fourth quarter, which was the 259th of his career. That moved him ahead of Jim Kelly for the most in franchise history.
Josh Allen becomes the Bills all-time leader in TD passes (259) with Jim Kelly in attendance 👏 BALvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/k62VFqausS
He threw another one to Dalton Kincaid shortly afterward, putting the game away in the process.

title: James Cook Injury Update: Buffalo Bills RB Status Following Scary Hit
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens are playing in a game full of injuries .
Most have been on the Ravens' side, but the Bills might have just been dealt a major blow. While driving for a score early in the fourth quarter, running back James Cook ran for a first down but landed awkwardly while being tackled.
Cook's head hit the turf , and his upper body seemed to roll over the top of him. It was scary enough that left guard Alec Anderson was seen waving the training staff onto the field to check on the star running back.
After lying on the ground for a moment, Cook was able to pop up, which was an excellent sign. He then entered the blue medical tent for further evaluation.
Cook was evaluated for a head injury and has been cleared to play . He returned to the sideline with his teammates and will be able to get back on the field.
Before going to the sideline, Cook had been a huge part of the offense. He had 20 rushing attempts for 76 yards with a touchdown. He also had two receptions for 21 yards, helping Buffalo take a commanding lead into the final quarter.
With the Bills up by multiple touchdowns, it would probably be wise to allow Cook to rest for the remainder of this game and focus on their big showdown in Week 9 as the Bills will visit the Minnesota Vikings on Monday Night Football. Minnesota boasts one of the league's elite defenses and Buffalo will need Cook as close to 100 percent as possible to pull off a win.
Baltimore lost their starting quarterback on the opening drive, with Lamar Jackson suffering a thumb injury when his hand hit Greg Rousseau's arm. His backup, Tyler Huntley, also went down as he suffered a foot injury.
For Jackson, it was a frustrating turn of events after he missed the previous three games with a high ankle sprain. He was excited to return to action against the Bills, but finished just 0-1 passing.
Huntley was also sidelined after suffering a foot injury, leaving the Ravens with their emergency quarterback Joe Fagnano. The undrafted rookie out of UConn was also banged up during the game, suffering an ankle injury. He stayed in the game, but this has been a tough one for both sides of the ball.

title: Dolphins Standout Could Be Answer to Carolina Panthers' Prayers
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have seemingly hit rock bottom on one side of the ball . For two straight weeks, Carolina has underperformed defensively, and while injuries play a major role, the production is still alarmingly bad.
The Panthers' secondary is decimated ; Carolina currently has four corners injured, leaving third-stringers on the field. That area of struggle is understandable; what's egregious is Carolina's inability to stop the run.
Through seven games, the Panthers rank among the bottom three rushing defenses in the NFL, surrendering just over 140 rushing yards per game. Even more alarming, the Panthers allow 198.3 rushing yards at home, second-to-last in the NFL behind the Dallas Cowboys.
It's safe to assume the lack of run defense was a contributing factor in defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero getting fired. Carolina has two home games in which it allowed over 258 yards on the ground.
The NFL trade deadline is in 6 days, taking place on November 10th at 4 PM ET. With that said, Carolina can add some help to a struggling run defense.
Bleacher Report's Kristopher Knox dropped his trade candidate big board entering Week 8 . On that list, shocking the potential fit, Carolina was mentioned, but it didn't have to do with the secondary.
While the secondary is injured, the defensive line has been relatively healthy throughout the season, and it's still been abysmal at stopping the run. Sieler is an established veteran in the NFL, and earned a three-year extension, worth up to $67 million.
The Miami Dolphins are a prime seller candidate for the trade deadline. The playoffs aren't a realistic goal, so trading an instant contributor like Sieler to a playoff hopeful makes sense. Knox also noted that Sieler could be a potential cap casualty.
Releasing or getting Sieler off the roster would save the Dolphins roughly $13.8 million for next year, Even more reason to ship him to a contender now.
The best part: Sieler won't command too much  as far as what the Panthers would have to return. Knox slotted Sieler's trade value as a conditional fifth-round pick.
Right now, Carolina doesn't own any fifth-rounders, but the Panthers do own two fourth-rounders, so they could give the Dolphins either one of those picks, whether it's the Vikings' fourth-rounder or Carolina's own, that's more than a fair price for a team that is 1-7 on the season and needs to load up on draft picks.
The deal seems like a no-brainer. Sieler has 2 sacks so far. Against the run, Sieler is very good, with excellent technique and great hand placement once a play has started. Carolina has to figure this out at some point, because they've already taken the most extreme measure, and another offensive coordinator won't be fired again.

title: The Carolina Panthers Are Officially On Fraud Watch
full_text:
I think it's time to have an uncomfortable conversation about the Carolina Panthers.
At 3-4, I could probably talk myself into feeling OK about where they are. That Detroit win still looks pretty good. The problem is I started looking at the other two wins, and that's where this gets interesting.
Carolina beat Atlanta 34-3 with Cooper Rush starting at quarterback . They beat Philadelphia 25-14 with Tanner McKee starting in place of Jalen Hurts . The Lions are the only team the Panthers have beaten this season with its regular starting quarterback on the field.
So yeah, I'm starting to wonder if this team is actually any good.
I keep coming back to Detroit because that's the game that makes me hesitate to completely write Carolina off. The Panthers were good that night. They put up 32 points and beat a Lions team that I thought would give them all they could handle.
But what have we seen since then? Carolina beat an Eagles team playing without Jalen Hurts, then got blown out at home by Tampa Bay and lost at Green Bay . That's not exactly helping the argument that Detroit was the start of something.
Maybe the Panthers really are somewhere in the middle. I'm just not ready to give them the benefit of the doubt anymore.
The good thing about putting Carolina on fraud watch is they can get themselves off it. Denver comes to Charlotte next , and that's another chance for the Panthers to show me Detroit wasn't just one really good night.
I have no idea what to expect from them anymore. I thought I had a pretty good feel for this team after Detroit. I definitely don't now. That's what makes Denver interesting to me. I want to see which Panthers team shows up.
The one that beat Detroit can win that game. The one I've watched the last two weeks probably isn't going to. Maybe I'll feel completely different about them next week.
