title: Eagles and Chargers CBs Among Those Projected as Ideal Panthers Additions
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers ' biggest needs became apparent on Thursday Night Football. Losing to the Green Bay Packers , Carolina was once again embarrassed, especially on defense, so badly that defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero was fired .
Now losing two straight, both performances alarmingly bad for different reasons, Carolina should be a buyer come trade deadline time. The deadline is just eight days away, taking place on November 10th at 4:00 PM ET.
As for where the Panthers would look, one position is clearly the top concern on the roster: cornerback. By the second half of the TNF loss to Green Bay, Carolina was trotting out third-string corners and leaving them on islands with stud WR Matthew Golden.
The secondary is riddled with injuries. Both starters, Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn, are still on IR after suffering major injuries earlier this season. Akayleb Evans was placed on IR prior to the Packers game with knee and triceps injuries.
Rookie corner Will Lee III was the best starter, but he hurt his hamstring on Thursday night. The severity is still to be confirmed by Carolina.
With that room now decimated, Carolina needs to add some depth . Here are two ideal trade options as the deadline approaches.
ESPN's Matt Bowen and Jeremy Fowler dropped their top 25 trade candidates, and included which teams would be good fits for each player. For the Panthers, two players in the top 15 of their list had the Panthers listed as a good fit.
The first was Riq Woolen. A Super Bowl champion in 2025 with the Seattle Seahawks, Woolen signed with the Eagles in free agency, and has a base salary of $1.86 million; Carolina can certainly afford that.
Woolen has failed to find an interception thus far in 2026, but is top 30 in passes defended with 6. Low interception numbers aren't the end of the world. Outside of his rookie year, when he totaled 6 interceptions, Woolen has posted 3 or fewer each year, but has notched double-digit passes defended every season.
Woolen's long frame and downfield speed are tools that Carolina could use, especially in man coverage, as Bowen noted. If Carolina made this move, Woolen would warrant a fourth-round pick.
The other corner touted as a potential fit for Carolina already has experience in the building. Donte Jackson was traded to the Pittsburgh Steelers in 2024 after spending six seasons with the franchise.
Jackson is currently on the Los Angeles Chargers, and while Carolina doesn't look like a juggernaut, it's certainly better than what the Chargers are doing. Once again, the Chargers lost and remain the NFL's lone winless team, at 0-7.
Jackson is in the final year of his contract and is 29. Carolina wouldn't have to give up more than a sixth- or seventh-round pick to reunite.
Woolen is the more enticing option, being slightly younger and having a longer frame, but either would be an instant upgrade with how depleted this Carolina secondary is.

title: What Will Actually Change With Todd Wash Running the Panthers Defense?
full_text:
The Panthers didn't fire Ejiro Evero in the middle of the season just to keep doing everything the same way. That's what I'm interested in seeing now that Todd Wash is running the defense. Carolina isn't going to throw out an entire defensive system seven games into the season. There isn't enough time for that.
But Dave Canales has already talked about finding different ways to use the players he has, and Wash has been around long enough to know exactly what he's working with. So I'm not expecting a completely different defense against Denver. I am expecting to notice some differences.
This is probably the first thing I'll be watching for. I've gotten used to seeing the Panthers line up in Evero's 3-4 over the last few years. That's one thing that could look a little different with Wash. NFL.com reported that we'll probably see more four-man fronts now that he's calling the defense.
I'm curious to see what that looks like. I'm not expecting the 3-4 to disappear because you can't just change everything in the middle of a season. But this defense hasn't stopped the run very well, and Canales brought that up when he talked about the change. At this point, why not see if a different look up front helps?
If there's one player I'm most interested in seeing under Wash, it's Derrick Brown. The two already have some history together, and it was a pretty good history the first time around. Wash was Brown's defensive line coach when Brown made the Pro Bowl in 2023 and set an NFL record for tackles by a defensive lineman. Canales even brought up Wash's history of getting production out of Brown when he explained why he chose him to take over the defense.
This season hasn't gone nearly as well. Brown didn't record his first tackle for loss until Thursday night against Green Bay, and he's still looking for his first sack. For a player as talented as Brown, that's hard to ignore. If Wash can get him going again, that alone would make this defense look different.
This is another part of the change that interests me. Wash has been coaching defensive linemen for a long time, so I'm curious to see how much that shows up now that he's calling the defense. The Panthers have some guys who can get after the quarterback. I'd like to see them turned loose a little more.
Jaelan Phillips is the first guy I think about. When he's healthy, I don't need to see him trying to do five different things. He can rush the passer, and Carolina needs more of that right now. I'd make it pretty simple with him. Go get the quarterback.
Sometimes the easiest answer is letting your best players do what they're best at.
Changing coordinators isn't going to matter much if Carolina keeps getting pushed around on the ground. That's been one of the biggest problems with this defense, and it's one Canales brought up when he explained why he made the coaching change. This has probably been the most frustrating part of watching this defense for me. There have been games where teams didn't have to do much besides keep handing the ball off.
Tampa Bay ran for 258 yards, and that's just not something you can survive very often in the NFL. Green Bay was much better. The Panthers only gave up 66 yards on the ground in that one, which is a pretty big difference four days later. Now I want to see which one was closer to what this defense really is.
Wash has been working with this defensive line for a while, so he knows what he has up front. If he's going to change anything right away, I'd start there.
I'm not sure what this defense is going to look like against Denver. That's probably why I'm looking forward to seeing it. Wash isn't walking into a new situation. He's been standing on that sideline and working with these guys for the last few years. He knows what's gone wrong, and I'm sure he has his own ideas about what he'd do differently.
Well, now he gets to do it.
I'm not expecting everything to suddenly be fixed. I just want to see something that makes me say, OK, that's different. Maybe we see it with Brown. Maybe it's the way they line up or how they use Phillips. We'll find out against Denver.

title: Panthers Mock Draft: Trenches, Trenches, and More Trenches
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are still in first place, but based on the last few weeks of football, it's hard to predict that they'll stay there. The competent, capable team that beat the Detroit Lions is seemingly nowhere to be found now.
Regardless of whether they can stay afloat in a bad division, they should have eyes on the future. There are still way too many holes on this roster, and we suspect plenty of current starters or key contributors won't be around next year.
So, without further ado, here's our first mock draft of the season.
Note: Draft order changes constantly with virtually every single game played.
The offensive line has to be a priority, and ironically, the Panthers have good options at tackle moving forward. They don't have good options on the interior. The jury's out on center Sam Hecht, Luke Fortner won't stick around, Robert Hunt has been bad, and Damien Lewis is hurt. Enter Iowa interior lineman Kade Pieper, who can play guard and center.
The other side of the line isn't in good shape, either. Tershawn Wharton has been bad and could be cut, and aside from Derrick Brown, not much is working to stop the run. Kentucky defensive lineman Tavion Gadson would provide the Panthers with a much-needed body up front to help fix the defense's biggest issue.
The Panthers still can't really rush the passer. Nic Scourton will be back and Jaelan Phillips will hopefully be healthier, but the Panthers are likely to lose Pat Jones. Since Phillips has sadly been underwhelming, EDGE isn't a spot the Panthers can totally ignore in the draft.
Apparently, you can't actually have too many cornerbacks. Mike Jackson may or may not be on the team, and relying on Jaycee Horn and Will Lee to play 17 games each is a risk. The position has to be addressed again, and going back to the fourth-round CB well here with Jalen Mayo is smart.
It's true that tackle is in a better spot (assuming Ikem Ekwonu gets re-signed and can play again), but it's still not good. Who knows what Taylor Moton's future looks like? Rasheed Walker should honestly never play a down for the Panthers after his contract is up, and Monroe Freeling, at best, is very raw right now. The Panthers can add some developmental depth in Niki Prongos.
At this point, the Panthers should be more than happy loading up on the trenches. That is clearly the weakness of this team despite the investments, so the need is still there. Adding Santana Hopper gives the Panthers another shot at someone up front being able to stop the run.
Sure, a seventh-rounder faces long odds of ever even playing in the NFL, but if the Panthers are taking a swing, it should be at a position they need depth at, and this year has revealed exactly where that is. Adding cornerback Dezz Ricks gives them one more bullet in the chamber.
The same logic above applies. On offense, the position that's been crushed the hardest is tackle, so adding more players there makes the most sense. They need better blocking, so why not take a chance on Tyree Adams?

title: Panthers Urged to Swap Bryce Young for Lamar Jackson in Ill-Fated Proposal
full_text:
Could the Carolina Panthers move on from Bryce Young? It's possible, although it seems like they're smart enough to understand that what's gone wrong over the last two weeks has less to do with Young and more to do with his surroundings.
Jason McIntyre and Colin Cowherd of FOX Sports, however, don't agree with that assessment. They're wrong, and their proposal for how the Panthers should proceed at the quarterback position is not a good one.
McIntyre said that this makes "back-to-back weeks" that Young "did not look like a starting quarterback," which is immediately a misinformed take on what's been going on with the Panthers.
Cowherd interjected that he simply couldn't extend Young if he were the Panthers based on these last two weeks. McIntyre added that during the offseason, head coach Dave Canales said Young was the franchise player "for now."
Because the door was technically left open with that comment (nevermind the fact that Young has played the best football of his NFL career, last two weeks included, this season), McIntyre and Cowherd began to speculate on who the Panthers could get, and a two-time MVP came up.
"Lamar Jackson wanted a contract, has not gotten it," McIntyre said. "Does he want to head south, perhaps? Is there a world where Carolina makes a move on Lamar Jackson? I'm just speculating because Bryce Young just does not look like the guy."
Cowherd added that Young is "too good to be a backup," calling him a high-level bridge quarterback. It's as if these two haven't watched a snap of the Panthers this year. Young has faced the highest pressure rate in the NFL and has been dealing with a knee injury since Week 3 that has sapped his mobility.
Those are untenable circumstances for virtually all NFL quarterbacks. The protection has fallen off a cliff (and it was bad to begin with), and Young isn't healthy enough to offset it at the moment. But enough about Young being way better than these two understand.
Jackson is obviously an upgrade. He's a two-time MVP, and when he's playing, there are one or two quarterbacks better than him. He is nearly unrivaled, and his prime is still going on. So yes, the reductive take that Jackson improves the Panthers is true, but it's not that simple.
The Panthers are on the hook for Young's fifth-year option regardless of an extension. That complicates an addition. The cost to acquire Jackson would be astronomical. If they were to pull off a trade, it would cost them a boatload of valuable picks.
That's before signing Jackson to a long-term deal. Now, Jackson is significantly better than Young, but it's probably not worth skipping a potential $40 million salary for Young to add a $60 million salary for Jackson.
Plus, say what you want about Young, but he is durable. Jackson, lately, has not been. Is there any hope that a different, more injury-prone slender QB would hold up better behind this porous offensive line?
Young might not be Jackson, but simply swapping them out just doesn't make sense for the Panthers in any way, shape, or form.

title: Eagles Defender Pitched as Panthers Trade Acquisition & It Makes Too Much Sense
full_text:
I wasn't really looking for Riq Woolen's name when I started checking out some of the trade talk around the Panthers. I knew Carolina needed another corner, but I figured most of the names being thrown around would either cost too much or wouldn't be much better than what the Panthers already have.
Woolen made me stop for a minute. I remember him from Seattle more than anything, especially his rookie year when he had six interceptions and made the Pro Bowl. He's 6-foot-4, can run and has 12 interceptions in his career. Now he's in Philadelphia on a one-year deal and his name is starting to come up with the trade deadline getting closer.
I wouldn't mind seeing Carolina take a chance on him.
I already thought the Panthers were thin at corner before the Green Bay game. Then I watched Will Lee III leave with a hamstring injury and started wondering who Carolina had left.
It wasn't a long list. Chau Smith-Wade and Marco Wilson were out there, and Malcolm DeWalt IV ended up playing in his first NFL game just days after joining the Panthers. Akayleb Evans had already gone on injured reserve, while Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson weren't available.
I don't know when all of those guys are coming back. Maybe Horn and Jackson return soon and things start looking a lot better. After watching Thursday night, I'd rather not wait around and find out.
That's why Woolen makes more sense to me now than he probably would've a couple of weeks ago. Carolina doesn't need him to come in and be its No. 1 corner. The Panthers need another guy who has actually played a lot of NFL football.
Woolen isn't playing like the guy I remember from Seattle right now. He had a rough game against Dallas on Monday, and I'm not going to ignore that just because I like the idea of Carolina trading for him.
But I do remember what he looked like early in his career. Six interceptions as a rookie will get your attention , and he followed that with two more the next year and three in 2024. He's had 12 in four-plus seasons, which is more than enough for me to wonder if there's still something there.
Maybe there isn't. Philadelphia signed him for one year, and if everything was going great I doubt we'd be talking about whether the Eagles might trade him a few months later.
I still think I'd take the chance if the price wasn't much.
I've seen Woolen mentioned in several trade ideas lately, and Carolina keeps coming up as a possible fit. That isn't surprising after watching what has happened to the Panthers at corner over the last month.
I wouldn't give Philadelphia anything close to a premium pick. If the conversation starts getting into the first three rounds, I'm out. Carolina has too many other needs and I'm not giving away an important draft pick for a player who could leave after the season.
If we're talking about a late-round pick, I'm listening.
Maybe Horn and Jackson both come back and a month from now Carolina suddenly has plenty of corners. I'd be fine with that problem. It sounds a lot better than what I watched Thursday night, when the Panthers were trying to finish a game at Lambeau Field with three healthy guys left at the position.
I don't know what Philadelphia would actually want for Woolen or whether Dan Morgan has any interest in him. I just know this is one of the trade ideas I've seen where I wouldn't need much convincing.

title: Panthers Not Trading for Quenton Nelson Aged Like Milk Within Days
full_text:
I saw the Quenton Nelson trade Tuesday and immediately thought about the Panthers. A few days ago I wouldn't have said that. Nelson was available and Carolina apparently wasn't interested, and I didn't have much of a problem with it. He's 30, his contract is almost up and I wasn't interested in seeing the Panthers give away a bunch of draft picks for a guard.
Then I saw Seattle got him for a third-round pick in 2027 and a fifth in 2028 . That wasn't nearly as much as I thought Indianapolis would get for him, especially considering the kind of player we're talking about. Throw in everything that's happened with Carolina's offensive line over the last few days and I started looking at it differently.
I probably would've made that trade.
I wasn't thinking much about Nelson when the Panthers played Tampa Bay. I was thinking about Taylor Moton finally being back and hoping Carolina could get through a game without something else happening up front. Instead, Moton broke his fibula and now he's done for the year . That's a pretty lousy way for his season to end after he had just gotten back.
That's also when the Nelson stuff started bothering me more. Ikem Ekwonu hasn't played yet, and now Carolina is going back to Monroe Freeling at right tackle. Rasheed Walker has been handling the other side, so this isn't exactly an offensive line where I'd look around and say they're good enough and don't need anybody else.
I know Nelson wouldn't have taken Moton's spot. If Carolina traded for him, he was going to play guard and Moton's injury still would've been a problem. But I would've felt a whole lot better about the line with Nelson somewhere in the middle of it, especially once I found out Seattle didn't have to give Indianapolis a first or second-round pick to get him.
Maybe I wouldn't be thinking this way if Moton hadn't gotten hurt. That's why I didn't care much when the Panthers weren't involved with Nelson in the first place. A week later I'm looking at who's available up front and what Seattle paid, and it doesn't sound like such a bad idea anymore.
A future third and fifth isn't nothing, but those aren't picks that would've scared me away. Carolina would've kept its first and second-round picks, and the third wouldn't have been until 2027. When I first heard Nelson's name around the deadline, I figured Indianapolis would want considerably more than that.
Maybe the Colts would've asked Carolina for something different. I have no idea what those conversations would've looked like, or if the Panthers even called. All I can go by is what Nelson actually cost Seattle, and I would've been comfortable with Carolina paying that price.
The contract would've been the part I'd worry about. Nelson is going to want to get paid, and I understand not wanting to spend a ton of money on a guard in his 30s. But that's something Carolina could've figured out later, and I think I'd rather have that decision to make with Nelson already on the roster.
If you asked me about Nelson before Moton got hurt, I probably would've told you to keep the picks. I didn't think this was the kind of move Carolina needed to make, and I definitely didn't want to see them overpay for an older player. A lot changed once Moton went down and I saw what Seattle actually gave up.
I don't know if Nelson would've changed much about this season. The Panthers are 3-4, they've lost two straight and putting one great guard on the offensive line isn't fixing everything we've watched go wrong. I can understand why Carolina might've looked at the age, contract and draft picks and decided it wasn't worth it.
I'm just not sure I agree anymore.
A 2027 third and a 2028 fifth for Quenton Nelson is a deal I would've made.

title: The Panthers Aren't Playing Sunday, But There's One Team They Need to Win
full_text:
I'm not used to the Panthers already being done for the week when Sunday gets here. After watching them lose to Green Bay on Thursday night , I guess the good part is I can sit back today and watch everybody else.
There is one game I'll be paying attention to more than the others.
Atlanta plays Tampa Bay, and as much as I hate to say it, I'm pulling for the Falcons.
I probably wouldn't care much about this game if Tampa hadn't just embarrassed Carolina. The Bucs came into Charlotte with one win and left with a 43-13 win . I didn't see that coming at all.
What bothers me now is Tampa is sitting at 2-5 and still isn't buried. That's crazy when you think about it. Carolina and Atlanta only have one more win, and New Orleans is sitting there with two as well .
So I'm looking at Tampa a little differently than I was a week ago. I thought the Panthers would beat them. Instead, Tampa beat Carolina by 30 and now gets another NFC South game at home.
Let Atlanta handle them today.
I'm not thrilled about the Falcons getting to four wins either. I just don't care about that as much today.
Carolina gets Atlanta again later this season . If that game matters when we get there, the Panthers can do something about it themselves. Right now I'd rather see Tampa take another loss.
Maybe I'm putting too much into what happened last week. A 30-point loss will do that to you. I just watched Tampa look a whole lot better than its record against Carolina, and I'm not interested in seeing whether it can start putting a few wins together.
The Panthers can't do anything about their 3-4 record today. They already played their game this week and lost it. All they can do now is watch the rest of the division play out.
If Tampa loses, I'll take it. The Bucs stay at two wins, Carolina gets a few extra days to get itself together and we move on to next week.
It might feel strange pulling for Atlanta for three hours.

title: Panthers Given Mandate to Make 1 Crucial Trade to Salvage Season
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have to make a trade. After another debacle , this time on national television, Thursday night, the Panthers clearly don't have the guns to keep up with actual NFC contenders. They may not have the guns to keep up with NFC South contenders.
Injuries are probably the main reason why. It is hard to say this team wouldn't be pretty good if at least some of Xavier Legette, Taylor Moton, Damien Lewis, Ikem Ekwonu, Will Lee III, Nic Scourton, Chris Brazzell, Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson, Jonathon Brooks, and Jaelan Phillips were out on the field.
The Panthers have to do something if they really want to try to contend this year, and their offseason spending spree suggests that they do. And if that's the case, FOX Sports' Greg Auman has a clear target in mind.
The last two weeks (or five days) have been absolutely brutal to the Panthers. Not only did more injuries pop up, but every facet of this team came crashing back down to earth as the Panthers slipped from 3-2 to 3-4. It has been ugly.
Bad performance has played a part, but a complete lack of healthy players has, too. And that is nowhere felt more than at cornerback. It's been weeks since Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson went on IR, and Dan Morgan has sat idly by. The injuries at corner haven't gotten better.
Akayleb Evans, who was outmatched as a starting corner, is on IR now. Will Lee III went down on Thursday, and it doesn't look good. They're trotting practice squad players out and running out of options at the same time.
A trade just has to happen, and according to Greg Auman of FOX Sports, it needs to be Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen.
"There’s so much of a Seattle presence in Carolina between head coach Dave Canales and general manager Dan Morgan, both longtime Seahawks guys and where Tariq Woolen began his career," he wrote, highlighting the obvious connection.
"Backups aren’t likely going to get them a repeat division title, so upgrading the secondary would be a priority if they were to be active at the trade deadline," Auman concluded.
The Panthers can't survive with the corner situation as it is. They also can't survive the offensive line situation, but Woolen is available, and starting-caliber offensive linemen just aren't. Cornerbacks are also cheaper.
The Panthers may or may not make a move, but this is one that has to be on the radar. We simply cannot go on like this unless Carolina is content struggling all year.

title: Reviewing Jeffery Simmons' Debut vs. Seahawks and Postgame Quotes From Bears DT
full_text:
We can confidently say that new Chicago Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons had a successful debut in the Week 8 victory against the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night.
Simmons finished the game tied with a team-high six tackles and notched one sack, a bunch of pressures and two tackles for loss. Simmons also made an impact in run defense, securing a team-high three run stops, per Pro Football Focus .
The former first-round pick wasted no time getting involved in the pass-rush, with Simmons recording his first Bears sack on the second defensive series of the game for Chicago.
He made Seahawks second-year guard Grey Zabel look silly.
Jeffery Simmons wasted NO time making an impact for the Bears' defense pic.twitter.com/Kedlt9Dxop
And that was the beginning of things to come for Simmons versus the Seahawks. The four-time Pro Bowler was getting penetration throughout the contest and routinely made Sam Darnold uncomfortable, which helped thwart the passing attack.
Even when he wasn't getting through to pressure Darnold, Big Jeff was drawing so much attention that he freed up his teammates to make plays.
Two examples of that were the sacks from Montez Sweat and Devin Bush. In both instances, Simmons took on a double team and that impacted Seattle's ability to account for the two Bears defenders, who got through unblocked and took Darnold down.
Jeffery Simmons being double-teamed gave Devin Bush the opportunity to go and get the sack pic.twitter.com/Ukd329JpZ2
Another clear benefit we're seeing with Simmons early on is the fact that the Bears are having success rushing just four and that allows Dennis Allen to drop more into coverage, which is huge because Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson continue to amount to huge liabilities, as we saw on Monday night.
When it comes to Simmons' playing time, the All-Pro D-tackle was on the field for 55 of the 63 snaps, per PFF which is about 88% of the plays, so he was pretty much full go in his debut.
Bears head coach Ben Johnson said it best when he simply stated that Simmons' "impact was profound," according to the team's official website .
Simmons didn't look like a guy who was in his first game in a new defense and that's because he went right to work learning the playbook as soon as he arrived in Chicago.
"I was in the building 'til almost 10 o'clock Thursday night just trying to get the game plan and catch up," Simmons said. "Getting the game plan early in the morning Friday. Just spending the extra time. Then when I ran out of the tunnel, I kept telling myself, 'It's just football. Go out there and be me. Play by play, just stay in the moment.'
"That's always my goal - just embrace the moment. That's what happened tonight. It was like a lift [off my shoulders] once I ran out there. Thank God they got the ball first as well. To be able to run out there and get my first snaps as a Chicago Bear, it was a lot of emotions. I'm grateful to be here, and today was a great start."
In his postgame interview with ESPN's Laura Rutledge, Simmons said he's "excited to be a Chicago Bear" and "it means a lot to me to be able to play meaningful football," something he didn't do much of in recent years in Tennessee.
We talked about the impact Simmons had when it comes to the attention he draws and how that frees up the guys around him, and T.J. Edwards and Daniel Hardy said they certainly saw that.
Montez Sweat sack. Look at him and Jeffery Simmons. pic.twitter.com/YPSGE270Tx
"I think he's just — I don't know — you can feel his presence," Edwards said. "Especially me, I'm right behind him, so I can kind of just feel how they're trying to block him. I feel like [the defense] was just flying today. They made our job a whole lot easier. But he definitely helps, for sure. He's just himself. His play speaks for [itself]."
"Phenomenal player," Hardy said. "Really charged up the locker room. Definitely boosted up the DL. He took a ton of reps tonight and made them all count.  You gotta account for him. Give him a 1-on-1, it's not gonna end well. He frees stuff up for everybody just because he draws so much attention to him. So appreciate it, and we're all happy with the production."
Montez Sweat was also one of the beneficiaries of Simmons' mere presence upfront and admitted he was seeing more one-on-ones because of the new Bears defensive tackle.
"I definitely got my opportunities," Sweat said. "I definitely got some 1-on-1s. I was looking forward to taking advantage of that, and I'm looking forward to doing that the rest of the year.
"[Simmons has] definitely upped his game and his IQ. He's always had a real love for the game, and that affects you across the whole line and the whole team."
Simmons was everything the Bears could have hoped for and then some. It's scary to think he could get even better once he has a better grasp of the defense and, potentially, even more help if Chicago acquires Khalil Mack or another edge rusher.

title: Game Balls in Bears' Statement Primetime Victory vs Seahawks
full_text:
Buckle up, ladies and gentlemen. The 2026 Chicago Bears are officially Super Bowl contenders. One week after a sensational primetime win over the New England Patriots , the Bears just took down the defending champion Seattle Seahawks in their own home, and they did it in dominant fashion. For those counting at home, that gives the Bears a win over each of last year's Super Bowl teams.
On top of proving themselves as legit title contenders, the Bears also secured what could be a valuable tiebreaker for a potential Wild Card spot. If neither the Bears nor Seahawks win their division, this game could be the deciding factor on which team gets to keep dancing while the other starts their offseason early, and the Bears now have that win in their pocket.
But we're still a ways away from playoff seeding. For now, the Bears and their fans can celebrate an impressive upset win played on the national stage. With that in mind, let's hand out some game balls.
He may have missed three games, but Caleb Williams is undeniably an MVP candidate . He gave Seattle's defense absolute fits all night, becoming the first quarterback to put up 200 passing yards against Seattle this season. But he didn't stop there. Williams finished his night with 247 yards while completing 24 of 34 pass attempts. He only threw one touchdown, but he didn't give the ball away and only took one sack.
After giving the best defense in the league more than they could handle, this first ball goes to Williams.
Welcome to Chicago, Mr. Simmons! The Bears' blockbuster trade for Simmons paid dividends immediately as big No. 99 practically lived in Seattle's backfield. He frequently lined up against second-year guard Gray Zabel who was making his first start at right guard, exploiting an unexpected advantage after the Seahawks' Quenton Nelson trade .
Simmons finished his debut as a Bear and earns his first game ball with a sack, a quarterback hit, a pass deflection, and a pair of tackles for loss.
Through most of tonight's game, I didn't believe Swift had done enough to earn a game ball despite his two touchdowns. He averaged less than three yards per carry in a game where the Bears could have really used some explosive gains on the ground, after all.
But his third touchdown of the night, which came with five minutes remaining and proved to be the dagger, was too much to ignore. Swift didn't play his best game, but he showed up when it mattered the most, and that's what counts. For that, Swift gets this last game ball, his first since that Week 1 thriller against the Carolina Panthers .
Honorable Mention: James Lynch, for securing his first career interception off a tipped pass by Austin Booker. His pick gave the Bears the ball inside Seattle's 10-yard line with a 10-point lead and just six minutes left in the game. The rest is history.

title: Jeffery Simmons' Electric Debut and More Takeaways From Bears' Statement Win vs. Seahawks
full_text:
We considered the Chicago Bears' Week 8 contest against the Seattle Seahawks a good old measuring stick game to see just how legit the Bears are in 2026.
Well, we can say the Bears more than measured up after emerging victorious over the reigning Super Bowl champions by a score of 34-17.
The Bears jumped out to a lead after a touchdown on their first drive of the game and didn't relinquish it the rest of the way thanks to fantastic play on both sides of the ball that was led by Jeffery Simmons on defense and Caleb Williams on offense.
Now, let's dive a bit deeper into the details by taking a look at the biggest takeaways from the Bears' decisive Week 8 win over the Seahawks.
Sometimes it takes a player time to start making an impact with his new team but that was not the case with Simmons.
Big Jeff made an instant impact with his first sack in the first quarter, and that was just the beginning of his contribution.
Simmons was collapsing the pocket all night long and made Sam Darnold extremely uncomfortable as he racked up a bunch of pressures. He also made his presence felt in the run game.
Jeffery Simmons wasted NO time making an impact for the Bears' defense pic.twitter.com/Kedlt9Dxop
Even when Simmons wasn't getting pressures, the extra attention he was drawing freed up the guys around him to make plays, as we saw on the sacks by Montez Sweat and Devin Bush. It's also clear Chicago won't have to blitz as much with all the pressure a four-man rush can bring with Simmons.
When it comes to how Dennis Allen deployed him, we saw the new Bears defensive tackle lineup inside and out.
When it was all said and done, Simmons finished with a team-high six tackles, one sack, two tackles for loss and one QB hit in what was nothing short of an electric debut.
Williams faced his toughest challenge of the 2026 season against the league's best defense and he passed the test with flying colors.
Williams' command of the offense, poise in the pocket and accuracy continues to be impressive to watch. He has very much made the leap to becoming an elite quarterback in his third season and his showing on Monday night cemented that.
The former No. 1 overall pick finished 24-of-34 for 247 yards and one touchdown. He is the first quarterback to finish north of 200 passing yards against the Seahawks this season.
In the first half, it looked like it was going to be a long night for the Bears' secondary with Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
JSN ripped off four catches for 92 yards and a touchdown over the first two quarters, with the score coming on a 43-yard catch that saw him shake Tyrique Stevenson out of his shoes with a double move.
But it was a different story in the second half for JSN, who posted just two catches for 26 yards. Once JSN stopped producing, the Seahawks had a much tougher time moving the football without any assistance from the rushing attack.
Kudos to Dennis Allen for pressing the right button to significantly limit the league's best wide receiver over the final two quarters.
It's one thing to beat the reigning Super Bowl champs who were coming off an impressive win over the Kansas City Chiefs last week, but it's even more impressive that the Bears beat the Seahawks on their home turf in primetime.
This was nothing short of a statement win for the Bears and if there was any doubt left about Chicago's status as a true contender before this game, that can be put to bed now.
Speaking of making a statement, how about head coach Ben Johnson soundly winning the battle over Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald, who is one of the elite defensive minds.

title: Watch Jeffery Simmons Record First Bears Sack in Debut vs. Seahawks
full_text:
Superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons is making his debut with the Chicago Bears in the Week 8 game against the Seattle Seahawks and he wasted no time making an impact.
In the first quarter on the Seahawks' second drive of the contest, Simmons broke through Seattle's offensive line to record his first sack with the Bears.
Simmons beat Seahawks right guard Grey Zabel on the play. Zabel moved over to the right side of the line after Seattle acquired Quenton Nelson last week.
Check out Simmons' sack below.
Jeffery Simmons wasted NO time making an impact for the Bears' defense pic.twitter.com/Kedlt9Dxop
Unfortunately, fellow defensive lineman Grady Jarrett was called for a facemask penalty on the same play, so the loss of yardage was negated.
However, Simmons was still credited with the sack and the Bears were able to overcome the flag and force a Seahawks punt on the drive.
With that sack, Simmons now has five on the season and he has already matched the total amount of sacks Bears interior defenders had over the first seven games.
Through two drives, Simmons recorded two tackles, one sack and one tackle for loss. He's already showing why the Bears acquired him.
When the Chicago Bears pulled off the trade for Jeffery Simmons, the team made NFL history .
The Bears unloaded two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick to the Tennessee Titans for Simmons and a fifth-rounder.
With Chicago giving up the two first-round picks, it was the first time in the common draft era (since 1967) that a team traded multiple first-round picks for a defensive tackle.
When the Bears traded Gervon Dexter to the Atlanta Falcons prior to Week 1, Chicago subtracted its best interior pass-rusher.
The hope was that guys like Kentavius Street and Jordan van den Berg could step up to fill the void, but neither player has been able to do that and Bears interior defenders have tallied just one sack combined through seven games.
The Bears sported a top-five run defense entering Week 8, but they have also faced the fewest rushing attempts in the league and have given up the 10th-most rushing yards per attempt.
Simmons, who is a four-time Pro Bowler, three-time All-Pro and one of the very best defensive tackles in the NFL, provides a boost on both fronts for Chicago.
His four sacks and 24 pressures rank seventh and fifth at the position, and Simmons is first with 20 stops, according to Pro Football Focus .
Simmons ranks seventh in pass-rush grade, 17th in run defense grade and ninth in overall grade.

title: Caleb Williams Cleats Controversy, Explained: Why Bears QB, NFL Are at Odds Over Footwear
full_text:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams and the NFL are currently at odds over cleats. Yes, cleats.
Upon his return from injury, Williams decided to change his cleats to a pair made by a company called Caddix, but that has resulted in fines from the NFL.
Williams has had an opportunity to avoid those fines, but he has remained defiant despite the continued punishment from the league.
Here's more information on why the NFL is fining Williams, and why he continues to accept those fines despite having the option to avoid them.
The Caddix cleats are relatively new on the scene and Williams is wearing them because they utilize "SmartStuds" technology that supposedly reduces rotational torque and lowers the risk of injury.
"Our SmartStuds flex and release under load. Instead of locking the foot in place, SmartStuds deform slightly during pivoting and cutting, allowing for quicker stud release from the playing surface," the compant writes on its website. "This reduces rotational torque on the knees and ankles without sacrificing the traction athletes need for acceleration and cutting. By targeting safe rotational stiffness ranges identified in biomechanical research, Caddix cleats strike the balance between performance and protection."
Williams suffered a hamstring injury in Week 2 that forced him to miss three games, so it's safe to assume that's what spurred on his decision to switch to Caddix cleats. He is not an investor in Caddix.
The NFL is levying fines on Williams because the cleats break a rule that prohibits non-approved logos on cleats. Players are allowed to display logos on cleats made by Adidas, Nike and Under Armour, but that's it.
If Williams wants, he can avoid fines by simply covering up the logo on the Caddix cleats, but he refuses to.
"Caddix isn't in a position to tell players how to wear our products, especially when players purchased them themselves," Caddix CEO Jack Rasmussen said.
"I certainly can't explain why he won't tape over them either," Rasmussen added.
According to ESPN's Ian Rapoport , Williams' decision to not cover the logo is "a matter of principle" and the Bears quarterback wants to help spread the word about the cleats.
So far, both Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Flacco, who is an investor in the company, and Caddix have offered to pay the fines the league continues to hit Williams with. In Week 6, Williams was fined $11,941, and then that fine was doubled in Week 7 to a whopping $23,822.
There has been a belief that Williams might eventually be forced to cover the logo or he won't be allowed to play. When asked about that, head coach Ben Johnson was confident Williams wouldn't hurt his team if it came to that.
"He's all about the team, and I know he's not going to hurt the team," Johnson responded.
Now, it'll be interesting to see if Williams decides to cover up the logo in the Week 8 game against the Seattle Seahawks or if he'll continue to thumb his nose at the NFL. Doing the latter will continue to be a costly proposition.

title: Chicago Bears vs. Seattle Seahawks Inactives: Who's in, Who's Out for Week 8
full_text:
The Chicago Bears and Seattle Seahawks have released their list of inactives ahead of the Week 8 game on Monday night.
Seattle and Chicago both made a huge trade in the week leading up to this game, with the Seahawks acquiring guard Quenton Nelson and the Bears trading for Jeffery Simmons . Both are officially active, as expected.
Ahead of the contest, the Seahawks ruled out left tackle Charles Cross, running back Velus Jones Jr. and wide receiver Rashid Shaheed. Meanwhile, linebacker Uchenna Nwosua, who was doubtful, is inactive.
Seattle also had four players listed as questionable in guard Anthony Bradford, quarterback Drew Lock, linebacker Patrick O'Connell and defensive tackle Brandon Pili. Lock and Pili are officially inactive.
For Chicago, we already knew running back Kyle Monangai was going to miss his fourth consecutive game , but we didn't have clarity on the statuses of cornerback Malik Muhammad and linebacker D'Marco Jackson.
But upon the Bears releasing their inactives before kickoff, we learned that Muhammad is inactive and Jackson is active.
Now, a look at the full list of inactives for both teams.
Bears inactives: RB Kyle Monangai, QB Case Keenum, OL Jordan McFadden, DB Malik Muhammad, DL Jordan van den Berg, DL Jayden Loving
Seahawks inactives: LT Charles Cross, RB Velus Jones Jr., LB Uchenna Nwosu, WR Rashid Shaheed, QB Drew Lock, DT Brandon Pili, G Beau Stephens
The Seahawks are officially welcoming back running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price. This will be Charbonnet's 2026 debut after he spent the first seven weeks on the PUP list as he recovered from his torn ACL. Price had been on injured reserve since Week 3 with a chest issue.
With Monangai inactive once again, the Bears will be depending on Roschon Johnson to pick up the slack behind D'Andre Swift, and Zavier Scott will once again serve as the No. 3 back.
Muhammad's absence is a huge blow to the Bears' defense, as he has been Chicago's best cornerback. That will push the struggling Tyrique Stevenson back into a starting role opposite the equally disappointing Jaylon Johnson.
While Simmons is going to play for the Bears, it remains to be seen just how many snaps he'll see. Head coach Ben Johnson hinted Simmons will likely be limited .
“He might not be quite that high Week 1 for us, but he certainly has shown the ability to carry a load,” he said of Simmons' expected workload in his first game with the Bears.
One of the Bears' starters on the interior, Grady Jarrett, has played 72% of the snaps this season, so look for Simmons to be somewhere around 40-50%.
With the addition of Simmons, the odd man out upfront is rookie Jordan van den Berg, who had been struggling over the first seven games. The sixth-round pick is now going to have to scratch and claw for a chance at work moving forward.

title: Bears Reportedly in the Market for Secondary Help as Trade Deadline Approaches
full_text:
The Chicago Bears' interest in adding an edge rusher to its injured group has been well-established with the Khalil Mack trade rumors .
But while NFL insider Jordan Schultz confirmed the Bears front office's pursuit of Mack, which will come from competition from the San Francisco 49ers, Schultz also shared intel on Chicago's interest to bolster the secondary.
"San Francisco and Chicago, those were two teams I thought would be really active," Schultz said. "I don't think either team is done. ... The Bears want another pass-rusher and secondary help. I wouldn't rule out another move for either team. There's a lot of Khalil Mack buzz for both clubs."
The Bears have issues with their secondary all season, due to both injuries and inconsistency.
Safety Coby Bryant has been out all year with a knee injury, while nickelback Kyler Gordon missed the first five games of the season with a calf injury. Cornerback Malik Muhammad has a toe injury, while Tyrique Stevenson had a hip injury that cost him the Atlanta Falcons matchup. Safety Cam Lewis has had various injuries since the offseason.
Meanwhile, Stevenson and fellow cornerback Jaylon Johnson have struggled out wide. Chicago's defense has given up 8.7 yards per pass attempt this season, which is the worst in the NFL.
A trade makes sense to stop the bleeding. Is it feasible to pull off a trade for an EDGE and the secondary, though?
If it comes down to it, what do the Bears need more?
Chicago's defense breads its butter by stopping the run. It's probably more important to keep the defensive front stocked with depth than the secondary. A strong pass rush can keep quarterbacks away from chances to do damage against the third level anyway.
While the team has largely survived Dayo Odeyingbo going down with a quad injury and being put on the IR , it can't bank on losing anymore depth along the edge. A Montez Sweat injury would be a doomsday event.
Mack makes all the sense in the world as a target, though one hopes the Niners wouldn't drive his price up too high. The Los Angeles Chargers have been stubborn on the trademark, but are still winless. Reality will hit that franchise sooner rather than later.
If Bears fans had their druthers, Ryan Poles and Co. would fork up enough draft picks to fill every hole on the defense. Caleb Williams and Co. have inspired enough hope on the other side of the ball.
We'll see how Chicago handles the next eight days.

title: Bears and Ravens Connected as Possible Trade Partners By Ian Rapoport
full_text:
All of the talk surrounding the Chicago Bears ahead of the NFL trade deadline pertains to Chicago being a buyer.
The Bears have already cemented themselves as that with the trade for Jeffery Simmons , and reports suggest they are also looking around for an edge rusher .
But is there a scenario in which the Bears could sell off a piece? That has become a possibility thanks to the Baltimore Ravens' injury woes at quarterback.
After losing both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injuries in Week 8, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport suggested Bears signal-caller Tyson Bagent as a potential trade target for the Ravens.
"Tyson Bagent, the Chicago Bears backup quarterback who's been on again off again, obviously played with (Ravens offensive coordinator) Declan Doyle, (the Bears') offensive coordinator last year, would be a potential name to consider (for the Ravens)," Rapoport said.
Not only did the Ravens lose both quarterbacks, but Jackson is going to miss at least four games because he needs surgery on his injured thumb and will be placed on injured reserve. There is even a chance Jackson misses the rest of the 2026 season.
As for Huntley, he's dealing with what is believed to be turf toe , and as we've seen with Bears running back Kyle Monangai, that could lead to a multi-week absence.
As long as those two are on the shelf, the Ravens are forced to roll with rookie Joe Fagnano, who showed why he isn't a good option during the loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday.
Rapoport isn't the first insider to link Bagent and the Bears to the Ravens when it comes to a potential trade.
Ravens On SI's Jason La Canfora reported on Sunday night that Bagent is Baltimore's No. 1 target and the Ravens have already called Chicago about a possible trade .
"The Ravens top pursuit is Bears back-up quarterback Tyson Bagent, according to multiple high-ranking NFL personnel execs," La Canfora, who added that the Ravens "have reached out to Chicago," said.
The Ravens-Bagent connection is a logical one, and not just because of the Ravens' dire situation.
After all, Bagent has played under Doyle in the past when he was the Bears' offensive coordinator in 2025, so there's a natural fit there.
Chicago is also carrying three quarterbacks, with Caleb Williams, Bagent and Case Keenum, so they have the depth to be able to trade one of Bagent or Keenum.
But we also know that the Bears are high on Bagent, with head coach Ben Johnson saying during the offseason that he believes Bagent might be one of the best 32 quarterbacks in the NFL.
Bagent didn't exactly show that in relief of an injured Williams in Week 5, when the Shepherd product struggled mightily before getting benched in favor of Keenum, who struggled in that contest, also, but played great football in Week 3.
At the end of the day, the Ravens are going to have to come with an overpay offer for the Bears to even consider trading Bagent.
A late-round pick isn't going to do much for a win-now team like Chicago and certainly won't be worth the Bears subtracting from their quarterbacks room during a season in which they have lost Williams to injury for multiple games.

title: Stat Predictions for Bears vs Seahawks Includes Up-and-Down Day for Caleb Williams
full_text:
Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season saw some crazy finishes and a handful of blowouts, but Monday Night Football should provide a thrilling conclusion to this week's slate of games. The Chicago Bears are set to face the Seattle Seahawks on the road in a game that both teams need in a bad way. The Seahawks are looking to avoid a 4-4 start while the Bears need a win to avoid plummeting to last place in the NFC North.
Before the season started, this game looked like a lock for the Bears to lose. However, the Seahawks have struggled somewhat to start the season while the Bears sit at 5-2 and just swung a blockbuster trade for superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons last week. Now this Monday night matchup has all the looks of a preview of the NFC Championship game in January.
With that in mind, let's get to some stat predictions for this contest of contenders, starting with the quarterback.
In my Week 8 keys to victory for the Bears , I said that Williams would have to put up another 300-yard passing game in order to beat the Seahawks, but I don't believe he's going to get close to that number. Seattle's defense is arguably the toughest unit he's going to face all year, and he likely can't expect much help from the run game since Kyle Monangai has been ruled out again .
Williams will still make some plays, and his final stat line should be better than any other quarterback who's faced the Seahawks this year, but it won't be anything worth writing home about. Expect him to be under fire quite a bit which will result in one interception and a few close calls that will define an up-and-down performance for No. 18.
Similar to my prediction for Williams, I expect Swift to put up underwhelming numbers. Monangai's absence will be sorely felt in this one as his hard-charging style of running is exactly what the Bears could use against this dominant defensive front. Instead, Swift will have to try to beat defenders around the edges, and that's a significantly harder task.
Swift won't have his worst day at the office on Monday, but it won't be pretty, either.
In the Bears' Week 6 win over the Atlanta Falcons , Chicago managed to stop superstar running back Bijan Robinson, and they did that by keeping him off the field. The offense controlled the clock, raced out to an early lead, and that removed Atlanta's run game from the equation. Don't expect that same tactic to work against the Seattle Seahawks and superstar receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
For one thing, even if the Bears get a big lead early on, that's only going to create more opportunities for Smith-Njigba. And second, the Bears simply do no not have any defensive backs capable of keeping up with the reigning Offensive Player of the Year. He's going to get open early and often and put on a dominating performance against Chicago.
While it hasn't been officially confirmed yet whether Jeffery Simmons will play in Week 8 , general manager Ryan Poles assumes he will and it's almost unfathomable to imagine that he won't. Simmons is too good to keep on the sidelines of such a pivotal game, even though he's only been a member of the team for five days.
With that in mind, I expect him to give Chicago a solid R.O.I. right from the jump, and that includes two sacks and four tackles-for-loss. He'll give Seattle's offensive line absolute fits all night, especially with the unexpected advantage that Seattle's Quentin Nelson trade gives the Bears.

title: Will Jeffery Simmons Play Tonight? Workload Expectations for New Bears DT vs. Seahawks
full_text:
The Chicago Bears made a massive addition — both literally and figuratively — to their defense this past week when they acquired Jeffery Simmons in a trade with the Tennessee Titans.
General manager Ryan Poles showed he's really going for it this season after giving up two first-round picks and a fourth-round selection in exchange for Simmons and a fifth-rounder.
The blockbuster deal marked the first time in the common draft era that a team has traded multiple first-rounders for a defensive tackle, so that goes to show you how serious Poles is about 2026.
But with that trade going down just days ago and Simmons having such a short time to get acclimated and ready to play in a new defense, many are wondering if he will make his debut versus Seattle.
The expectation is that Simmons will indeed suit up for his Bears debut on Monday night against the Seahawks.
First, Poles said he believed that Simmons would go , although he did say the ultimate decision will rest on the coaching staff.
Then, when he first addressed the media on Friday, Big Jeff told reporters that he's ready to go.
"At this point, I'm still trying to catch up with the playbook, get this game plan down and just trust the process, especially with this first week" he said . "But at the same time, I'm ready to roll. I'm ready to help this team win football games."
Head coach Ben Johnson also made it sound like Simmons will play.
“He’s played a lot of football, he’s been in a few different defensive schemes, and I think (Dennis Allen) is going to be able to find a spot to do what he does best,” Johnson said . “We don’t want him thinking out there, and that’s what you’re conscious of coming into a new team, but he’s a smart guy and we’ve been encouraged by what we’ve seen so far.”
As far as how much Simmons will play, we can't say for sure. One would assume he probably won't see a full workload in his first game with the Bears, which is something Johnson said would likely be the case.
“He might not be quite that high Week 1 for us, but he certainly has shown the ability to carry a load,” he said of Simmons' expected workload in his first game with the Bears.
The only real roadblock is how much of the defense Simmons can grasp in such a short time. It's not like he's coming off the couch to play, so conditioning isn't an issue at all.
One of the Bears' starters along the interior of the defensive line, Grady Jarrett, has been playing 72% of snaps this season. We could see Simmons playing around 50% in Week 8.

title: Bengals Could Take a Chance on Unproven Running Back at Trade Deadline
full_text:
Calls for the Bengals to make a running back trade are at an all-time high, with two stars rumored to be available in Jonathan Taylor and Saquon Barkley.
While the team should absolutely show interest in both, it may make sense to pivot to a cheaper option in Tennessee's Tyjae Spears, who could be an ascending player.
The Athletic's Daniel Popper recently labeled Spears a fit for the Bengals, citing his abilities as a pass-catcher and pass blocker.
"Spears, a 2023 third-round pick, is in the final year of his rookie deal, he has only 18 carries in six games this season (he was limited to 11 snaps in Week 6 because of a knee injury), Like most of the Titans' skill players, there is upside in a better situation," Popper said. "He has good hands and can line up in multiple spots in the pass game, Spears is also a physical pass protector, especially when chipping on the edge, He can provide some explosiveness, especially as a pass catcher, He had a 35-yard screen reception in Week 6 against the Texans, Spears has 142 career receptions."
Spears has flashed upside during his young career as both a runner and a receiver. However, the Titans' struggles since his arrival have kept him from reaching his ceiling. He has 1,114 rushing yards at 4.1 yards per carry and eight touchdowns, plus 147 receptions for 948 receiving yards and two touchdowns.
For comparison, Chase Brown has 2,473 rushing yards at 4.2 YPC and 14 touchdowns, plus 165 catches for 1,096 yards and 10 touchdowns. It is clear that Brown is the superior back, but acquiring Spears could give more flexibility to the Bengals offense as both players have similar skillsets.
The deterrent for a trade may stem from Spears' injury history. He has missed ten games in his career due to sporadic injuries; the most concerning ones came in college. At Tulane, Spears suffered two ACL injuries that left him with severe arthritis in his right knee and left him without an ACL.
This alone could cause the Bengals not to consider trading for Spears. With him also in a contract year, they might have to negotiate a new deal with a player whose future is murky should he perform well.
With everything considered, the Bengals' best trade target at running back from the Titans is likely Tony Pollard. He has proven he can still provide a solid running back floor, with the potential to have a big game at any time, as shown by his 155-yard, three-touchdown performance last week.

title: Bengals 'Aggressively' Pursuing Jonathan Taylor Ahead of 2026 NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Bengals continue to be tied to Jonathan Taylor trade talks ahead of the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline next Tuesday. NFL insider Jordan Schultz appeared on The Pivot podcast this week and noted Cincinnati is among a group of teams in "hot pursuit" of Jonathan Taylor.
The Colts star running back is on a sinking ship in Indianapolis right now, and Schultz laid out the potential price tag below.
"My understanding is that five to six teams have been aggressively pursuing him: Giants, Packers, Broncos, Seahawks, Bengals, Vikings," Schultz said about Taylor . "I believe he also would be open to a fresh start, and I think it'll take at least a second-round pick plus. Call it plus additional compensation to get it done. And I actually do expect that to happen."
Schultz also broke down what a player like wide receiver Josh Downs could go for at the deadline.
Either weapon could be a nice way to supercharge Cincinnati's offense. It ranks sixth in EPA/play this season among NFL attacks and second in success rate.
Taylor or Downs would likely round out the best overall offense in the NFL.
"Then you have Josh Downs. Now the Colts want a third-round pick for him, but I think ultimately they'll probably get a fourth. He's very valuable in the receiving game.I would say keep an eye on the Steelers, Chiefs, and Commanders, among others, and then don't be surprised if other teams that we haven't even considered yet, because he's valuable and he's set to become a free agent," Schultz noted about Downs. "But you have the Colts, really, big picture-wise. They have officially entered a full-on rebuild, and when you talk about stockpiling draft picks, clearing cap space, reducing financial commitments to give their GM really maximum flexibility."
If the Titans game is any indication , Cincinnati needs to get help at cornerback, linebacker, or safety ahead of the deadline. Why not multiple trades? The team has eight draft picks next year and a clear runway to the No. 1 seed in the conference given the schedule difficulty.
Taylor's price right now may not make much sense to build strength on strength.
The time is now to make a move, and Cincinnati is clearly interested. Taylor is posting 4.1 yards per carry this season (26th among RBs), with eight touchdowns (second).

title: How Bengals QB Joe Burrow's Hot 7-Game Start Ranks Against Best QB Seasons in NFL History
full_text:
Joe Burrow’s 20 passing touchdowns are the most through seven games in Cincinnati Bengals history, and they are the sixth most in NFL annals.
The 20 TDs put Burrow on pace to surpass the 50-touchdown milestone he called “doable” back in May.
Burrow already owns the top three touchdown totals in franchise history, with 43 in 2024, 35 in 2022 and 34 in 2021. And he has the top three passing yards marks with 4,918 in 2024, 4,611 in 2021 and 4,475 in 2022.
At his current pace, Burrow would finish with 53 touchdowns and 5,136 passing yards to shatter his franchise records.
The pace for 53 touchdowns puts him in the conversation for breaking Peyton Manning’s NFL record of 55 in 2013, although Manning was on an even more scorching pace through seven games that season than Burrow is this year.
In leading the Broncos to a 6-1 record in 2013, Manning threw 25 touchdowns with just three interceptions.
Burrow has six picks offsetting his 20 TDs.
Some other key seven-game numbers for Manning in that Super Bowl season (with Burrow’s current numbers).
8.9 yards per attempt (7.9)
71.6 completion percentage (73.0)
There are two other 50-touchdown seasons in NFL history, with Tom Brady (2007) and Patrick Mahomes (2018) hitting the number on the nose.
And it's worth noting that all three previous 50-TD seasons were accomplished in 16 games, whereas Burrow will have a chance to play 17.
Here is where their numbers stood through the first seven games of their 50-touchdown seasons.
27 TDS (most in NFL history)
73.8 completion percentage
64.9 completion percentage
The previous Bengals record for most touchdown passes through the first seven games was 17, set by Boomer Esiason in 1988 and tied by Burrow in 2021. Both led to Super Bowl appearances.
There have been four other seasons with 15 TD passes through seven games – Jeff Blake (1995), Andy Dalton (2015), Dalton (2018) and Burrow (2022).
Burrow has 13 touchdowns in his last three games, throwing for four each against the Miami Dolphins and Baltimore Ravens before tossing five in Sunday's 43-36 overtime win against the Tennessee Titans.
His three consecutive games with at least four touchdown passes also is a franchise record. No other player in Bengals history has ever thrown four touchdowns in back-to-back games.
Burrow had back-to-back four-TD games in 2021 (four vs. Ravens and four vs. Chiefs in Weeks 16-17) and 2024 (five vs. Raiders and four at Ravens in Weeks 9-10).

title: Ja’Marr Chase Clearly Frustrated After Bengals' Sloppy Win: 'Ask Zac'
full_text:
The Bengals beat the Titans 43-36 in overtime on Sunday at Paycor Stadium. It was an emotionally charged game for star wideout Ja’Marr Chase. Despite another poor start, the offense failed to meet his high standards. Chase finished with 11 catches on 16 targets, accumulating 141 yards and scoring a touchdown.
Chase quickly said Tennessee couldn't cover both him and Tee Higgins, who also finished with over 100 receiving yards.
“They couldn’t cover us the whole game,” Chase said. He expressed his dissatisfaction and hunger to improve, acknowledging he was "not satisfied" with his performance.
Why do the Bengals continue to get off to slow starts?
“I’m not sure about that; you should ask Zac (Taylor)," Chase said. "It’s not my responsibility. Ask Zac.”
Chase remained silent when asked whether he felt disgusted in the second quarter after catching a 30-yard touchdown reception. "No comment." He was visibly frustrated throughout the postgame locker room interview and didn't seem interested.
The frustrated Chase voiced his frustration to his teammates and Taylor on the sideline after Mike Gesicki's 25-yard touchdown gave the Bengals a 29-28 lead in the fourth quarter.
"Ja'Marr is a leader for us, and we're gonna follow," Gesicki said on Monday . "There's a lot of urgency in this locker room, and I've felt that from really since the start of OTAs. And our leaders have been vocal about it. And Ja’Marr is one of the best players in the world, so I think we should follow his lead. He has every right to express himself, and I think especially when he doesn't allow that to affect his play, like he goes out there and still makes plays, and it's all coming from good intentions. So he just wants us to reach our potential and maximize what we have in this locker room."
Taylor made it clear that he's OK with Chase being frustrated during the game.
“That’s just part of the game. It’s a tight game; it’s an emotional game," Taylor said on Sunday. "We’ll work through it. He had a big day for us and came up really big at the end in overtime. That’s just one of those things that happens in a football game.”
Despite the apparent frustration, Chase and Taylor share one objective: winning. Chase’s exceptional performance, even during high-pressure situations, sets the stage for the Bengals to refine their execution and build momentum as they prepare for next week’s matchup in Madrid against the Atlanta Falcons.

title: Zac Taylor Details Injuries to DJ Turner II, Cashius Howell Following Win Over Titans
full_text:
Bengals head coach Zac Taylor spoke to the media on Monday and updated where things stand with injuries to Cedric Johnson (ankle), Cashius Howell (wrist), and DJ Turner (heel).
Howell is already in a cast after getting surgery on the wrist, and Taylor confirmed he is likely going on injured reserve, while Turner and Johnson are day-to-day and will travel to Spain with a chance to play this week.
Cincinnati is hitting the skies for their Sunday morning game in Madrid against the Falcons.
"I'm not going to say that yet, but probably trending in that direction," Taylor said about Howell going on injured reserve. Both Turner and Johnson have much less serious injuries.
The defensive end depth is murkier than it's ever been this season as Cincinnati tries to keep up its great production along that part of the defense.  Shemar Stewart is the only healthy backup DE behind Myles Murphy and Boye Mafe.
The whole unit got embarrassed a bit across the Titans' 36-point showing on Sunday, but they made enough plays to pull out the win.
"Absolutely. I think any time you win, that's a big box to check," Taylor said about the team still having momentum this season. "I know we have the guys in there that are happy we won, but they're not satisfied with our overall performance. Each position group will go through that and find things we have to be better at. That's just part of it. Obviously it's better to do after a win, but that doesn't mean you can dismiss some of the things we know we have to clean up."
Cincinnati is going through a sped-up week, with all of the main parts of their workweek happening in the morning hours of Eastern Standard Time while they live in Central European Time.
"It speeds up the earlier part of your week, so that we can travel on Tuesday night," Taylor noted. "It changes your days a little bit. For the players, it doesn't make it more taxing. It's a little more taxing on the coaches. But it's like playing on a Monday night and having to turn around on a short week. Nothing we haven't had to do before — nothing to complain about. It just changes the structure of how you'll meet."
Cincinnati is trying to get to 6-2 overall this weekend.

title: Bengals' Offensive Shootout Victory Over Titans Made Franchise History
full_text:
Not many people predicted the Cincinnati Bengals to get in an offensive slugfest with the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. If anything, the majority of folks following both teams probably felt the Bengals should handle the 1-6 Titans fairly easily.
Instead of the Bengals having a smooth outing before their trip to Spain, the team had to go to overtime to take down the Titans 43-36. There were struggles on both sides of the ball, which included Joe Burrow throwing three interceptions.
Still, allowing 36 points is normally the recipe for a loss. Taking a closer look at the Bengals' history, it's really a miracle they won on Sunday.
John Sheeran of AtoZ Sports shared a stat that almost sounds made up. The Bengals' win on Sunday was the first time in franchise history that the team has won a game while allowing 36 points and turning the ball over at least four times.
Coming into Sunday, the Bengals were 0-20 in such cases.
What can be said about Burrow's performance? The three interceptions were obviously brutal, yet the Bengals quarterback accounted for six touchdowns on the day, which included five through the air and one rushing touchdown.
Burrow finished the game with a passer rating of 115.5, and the Bengals quarterback is not taking this win for granted in his postgame press conference.
"We lose that game the last three years," Burrow said . "Like I said, it's hard to win. Obviously you want to be great, snap in and snap out. It's not the reality of it. All we can do is keep working hard and try to get better."
No one should ever feel sorry for winning a game in the NFL. Sunday's game against the Titans proved that winning is hard in this league. One could look around the rest of the league and see that from the results on Sunday.
This is a game that can be put in the rearview quickly and move the focus to the next week. Next week will be a tricky matchup with the Atlanta Falcons, given the nature of the crazy travel. A fast turnaround may be what this team needs to keep their momentum.

title: Joe Burrow WOWS With Elite Titans Pro Football Focus Grade Despite Turnovers
full_text:
The Bengals didn't play a clean game by any means in Sunday's 43-36 win over the Tennessee Titans, but they still tallied some stellar Pro Football Focus grades from the outing.
The team posted a season-high 87.6 grade overall and had two players grade out at 93 or higher, starting with Joe Burrow on offense (93.1 overall).
The league's highest-graded passer this season continued playing elite football with 450-plus total yards, six touchdowns and three interceptions on Sunday. He committed three turnover-worthy plays on Sunday after entering the game with four total, but he was so clutch and sound on the other 71 snaps to wash it all away.
According to ESPN, Burrow is the second QB in NFL history with 450 passing yards, five pass TDs, and one rushing TD in a single game, and first in 75 years. The other was Norm Van Brocklin in 1951, who set the NFL record with 554 passing yards in that game.
Following Burrow, Tee Higgins (90.8) continued his career-best season with another 90-plus outing after leading all Bengals with a 91.6 mark last week. The rest of the top-five on offense went in this order: Dalton Risner (80), Ja'Marr Chase (78), and Amarius Mims (75.3).
The bottom-five offensive grades went in this order (min. 15 snaps): Drew Sample (49.6), Chase Brown (57.1), Colbie Young (61.1), Mike Gesicki (64.9), and Samaje Perine (68.9). It was a very strong day for the offense with low-end grades this high.
On defense, Cincinnati is really hoping to not have DJ Turner II (93.3) on the mend for long. The fourth-year corner is playing the best football of his career and peaking at the right time for a major payday in one way or another this offseason.
He got ruled out with a lower-body injury after posting the best grade of the game across 58 snaps. Turner has a career-best 74.3 PFF grade this season. Four other Bengals graded 67 or better on Cincinnati's defense: B.J. Hill (91.8), Jordan Battle (76), Dexter Lawrence (70.6), and Myles Murphy (67.9).
The bottom-five on defense went in this order (min. 15 snaps): Josh Newton (39.6), Bryan Cook (40.6), Dax Hill (44.9), Demetrius Knight Jr. (47.7), Barrett Carter (54.4). The middle of the Bengals defense struggled in a big way at the second and third levels.
They have to get that cleaned up before facing the Falcons in Spain on Sunday morning.

title: 7 Winners and 3 Losers From Bengals' Wild OT Win Over Titans
full_text:
In nail-biting fashion, the Bengals emerged victorious in Paycor Stadium on Sunday 43-36 over Tennessee.
Here are seven winners and three losers from Sunday's win.
Higgins just continues to add to his career-best campaign. He consistently beat his coverage and created easy options for Joe Burrow in the middle of the field and on the boundary. His best grab happened on the offense's first play following a Boye Mafe strip-sack turnover where he and Burrow connected for a 17-yard touchdown. Burrow then found Higgins later for the game-tying touchdown at the end of the fourth quarter.
Higgins has continuosly exceeded expectations this season, and is comfortably on pace for his first 1,500 yard receiving season. He finished Sunday with 10 catches for 155 yards and two touchdowns.
Both Demetrius Knight Jr. and Barrett Carter continue to miss tackles, and this time it played a large part in Tony Pollard gashing the defense for a 41-yard score. They were not alone however as Jordan Battle, Bryan Cook, and D.J. Turner failed to bring Pollard down as well.
To make matters worse, there is absolutely no awareness when it comes to covering tight ends. The Titans have failed to generate production from their tight ends all season, yet on Sunday both Gunnar Helm and Daniel Bellinger combined for eight catches, 112 yards and a touchdown. The lack of performing a basic task on defense is inexcusable at this point.
That is another reason you trade for Dexter Lawrence. Lawrence showed up on the stat sheet with seven total tackles, a sack, and a fumble recovery that he almost scored on. He saved his best play for the most dire moment however.
Cam Ward and the Titans needed to gain only 12 yards to setup a possible game-winning field goal with 32 seconds left. Lawrence then took matters into his own hands, and on 3rd and 3 chased down Ward for a crucial 13-yard sack to force overtime. He is the star that this Bengals defense has missed on the interior of the D-line.
Holding penalties are now officially a problem for Fairchild at this point. He committed a terrible holding penalty on a play where Burrow found Chase Brown in the end zone. He also jumped early for a false start penalty at the end of the third quarter.
Fairchild has maintained a solid level of play at left guard all season, but he has to clean up the penalties.
Mafe showed more dominance on Sunday and added another sack to his total with 5.5 sacks now on the year. It did not stop at the sack however as Mafe knocked the ball out of Cam Ward's hands as well for a fumble that Dexter Lawrence recovered. He has proven himself as one of the best playmakers on the team.
On a day where the defense seeming did all that it could to keep the Titans in the game, one drive stood out more than the rest. The defense committed three different penalties while up 21-13 in the third quarter to extend the Titans drive where they ultimately tied the game.
Josh Newton committed the first of two pass-interference penalties against Gunnar Helm for a thirteen yard penalty.
After a Cashius Howell offsides call, Bryan Cook got to Helm too early at the goal line for a four-yard penalty that placed the ball at the one-yard line. Tony Pollard scored his second touchdown of the day on the next play. These undisciplined mistakes have plagued the defense all year, and cannot continue if they hope to make a deep playoff run.
Chase finished with eleven catches for 141 yards, but his best grab happened on a third down where he and Burrow connected deep over the middle for a touchdown.
That play essentially woke the Bengals offense up for the rest of the game, and like Higgins he showed up on outside as a consistent option for Burrow.
The argument is there for Burrow to not make the winners list after he tossed three interceptions to Amani Hooker. However, the way Burrow continued to launch accurate passes afterwards is the main reason the Bengals avoided an upset in their stadium.
Burrow proved all of the doubters wrong when it comes to his ability as a clutch quarterback. After having an even ratio of three touchdowns to three interceptions, he threw two more touchdowns and ran for the game-winning score in overtime. He could have thrown five interceptions, and he would still make the winners list this week as he set a career high in total touchdowns in a game with six.
Burrow finished Sunday with a statline of 38 for 48 passing, for 472 total yards, and six total touchdowns.
Gesicki has finally become involved in the offense outside of the red zone and still kept his touchdown streak intact.
He finished the day with four catches for 76 yards and a 25-yard touchdown.
Burrow found two of his tight ends for touchdowns today, with Jack Endries hauling in one for what also was his first NFL reception. This is the best first impression Endries could have possibly had after the team placed Erick All Jr. on Injured Reserve with another torn ACL.
Endries should continue to see his role within the offense develop.
