title: Bengals Narrow Betting Favorites in Spain Battle Against Falcons
full_text:
Cincinnati is headed to Europe as betting favorites over the Atlanta Falcons this week. The team opened as three-point favorites Monday morning on DraftKings Sportsbook with a point total set at 51.5 points overall.
Both teams are struggling to beat the number this season as Cincinnati failed to cover as 13.5-point favorites on Sunday. They sit at 3-4 against the spread in 2026, while Atlanta is 3-5.
The Bengals just beat the Titans 43-36 to get to 5-2 on the 2026 season.
"We found a way to win. We talked all week about playing a complete game. We talked about all those things. That's obviously our intent," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said on Sunday. "Today didn't go that way for us, but I'm not going to lose sight of the fact that our guys stepped up at the end of the game, kept it together, and believed we were going to find a way to win. I don't care what their (the Titans') record is. They have been in a lot of games this year.
"So, our guys, in all phases, stepped up and found a way to walk off a winner. I get the chance after a win to clean things up. We need to clean up, go on the road to Spain, and find a way to get another one."
Cincinnati has won its past three games against the Falcons, last losing to them in the 2010 season, 39-32.
The Bengals have played two international games in their history, both in London last decade. In their last trip across the pond, Cincinnati took on a 24-10 loss to the Rams at Wembley Stadium during Taylor's first season in 2019.
"It's an unbelievable opportunity to grow the game internationally. That's an important part of what we do," Taylor said this past offseason about the contest. "I think it's awesome the brand of the Bengals gets extended internationally. We've got a lot of great players on the team that the world will get to watch on center stage."
Cincinnati kicks off against Atlanta at 9:30 AM ET on Sunday.

title: Cashius Howell Posts Video of Injured Wrist Following Bengals Win Over Titans
full_text:
The Bengals look like they won't have Cashius Howell for a while.
Cincinnati's 2026 second-round pick suffered a wrist injury in the 43-36 win over Tennessee. He posted a video from the hospital on his Instagram showing a big cast on his arm.
We will learn more from Zac Taylor this week. If he is put on injured reserve, expect the Bengals to add a name to its practice squad before leaving for Spain this week.
"Cashius, we'll see. I think it was his wrist. He (trainer) just told me about DJ Turner, and I forgot. I'll get you an update tomorrow or Wednesday," Taylor said on Sunday.
Howell has six tackles and one sack in seven games played this season.
Cincinnati won a wild game that was much closer than expected.
Joe Burrow had to pull off two clutch touchdown drives in the fourth quarter and overtime.
"We won. I want a complete game, and I want to start the first quarter faster — those are things we are going to continue to talk about," Taylor noted. "But there is something to finding a way to win. You guys have watched us play the last two years, and some of these games have gone the other direction. So for our guys, particularly late in the fourth quarter and overtime, to step up and seal the game, I'm not going to dismiss that. I'm proud of the guys for fighting through the whole time and finding ways for each guy to step up and make some plays so we could walk out a winner — to get to 5-2 and now go on the road, and reset and go do it again."
Taylor was impressed with how Tennessee kept so much pressure on his team.
"Those guys fought. They had a great plan. They attacked us," Taylor noted. "I give Tennessee a lot of credit. We'll watch the tape to see the things we need to clean up. There are certainly a lot of things. How many turnovers did we have? Four? Four turnovers are going to keep a team in the game. There are just things we're going to watch and clean up, but I am proud of the guys for finding a way to win the game."
Cincinnati travels to Spain early this week.

title: Todd Monken Sends Blunt Message to Browns During Monday Press Conference
full_text:
The Browns entered the AFC North showdown with an opportunity to improve to 6-2 and remain unbeaten in division play. Instead, Cleveland struggled offensively , surrendered eight sacks and committed several costly penalties in a game that quickly got away.
While Monken addressed many of those shortcomings immediately after the loss, his comments Monday provided a more detailed assessment of what went wrong and how they need to show more discipline against New Orleans.
“ We weren’t very poised and we didn’t keep our composure ,” Monken said when asked about three unnecessary penalties. “And you are how you play, not how you talk.”
Monken made it clear that his message to the team wasn’t limited to one disappointing performance.
The Browns also struggled to protect quarterback Deshaun Watson, allowing eight sacks against Pittsburgh’s aggressive defensive front. Rather than placing the blame on one player or position group, Monken emphasized that the responsibility belongs to everyone.
“Ultimately eight sacks is below the line,” Monken said. “When you get anywhere near that number, we all got to take a big bite of it and say it’s not good enough.”
He pointed to several contributing factors, including protection breakdowns, play calling and Watson’s ability to get rid of the football.
“It’s not one individual person. It’s a collective thing that we’ve got to continue to fight to get better at.”
“We got behind. We didn’t really get into a rhythm and we didn’t get any auxiliary yards,” Monken said.
He also acknowledged that the coaching staff must improve its approach.
“Certainly got to scheme it better and got to coach it better and execute better...We weren’t at our best the last couple weeks in stopping the run. All right. Now what? What are we going to do to stop the run?”
Despite those concerns, Monken isn’t ready to let one disappointing afternoon define Cleveland’s season.
The Browns are 5-3 through eight games, and their head coach believes they have considerable room for improvement.
“We haven’t really even scratched the surface yet of where we can be,” the head coach said proudly.
He believes the disappointment following Pittsburgh reflects how much the Browns expect of themselves.
“This is a good spot to be in, right? To be disappointed that you’re not 6-2 and that you didn’t find a way to win the game on the road and be 3-0 in the division.”
Monken stressed that the Browns have earned their five victories, just as they must accept responsibility for Sunday’s performance.
“We also earned the way we played yesterday and we weren’t poised and we weren’t composed and we earned that.”
Now the challenge is turning those words into a better performance.
“We’re going to circle the wagons. We’re going to figure out what we can fix. Get after it on Wednesday. Flush it today. Get after it Wednesday and take another step forward.”

title: Eight Sacks, One Major Concern: Browns Must To Make This Change Before It's Too Late
full_text:
Some things can be ignored, others can't.
The Cleveland Browns' offensive line struggles fall into the latter.
On Sunday, Nov. 1, the Browns lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers, 27-6, with the offense failing to score a touchdown. Across the first three drives, Cleveland managed to fumble twice and punt once, with quarterback Deshaun Watson being pressured over and over again.
While the early blunders set the team up for failure, the surplus of bodies in the backfield all day long did as well.
Watson ended up being sacked eight times and was pressured on a whopping 65% of his dropbacks in the first half alone. He did complete 27 passes for 324 yards, averaging 8.3 yards per attempt, but he wasn't able to get the offense moving until the final few drives, when the game was too far gone.
Watson took the blame postgame, but it was obvious that he wasn't given enough time to make anything happen.
“I’m always going to put the sacks on me. … I’m always going to take responsibility for those," he said.
But it is hard to keep putting the blame on him, as sacks have been a recurring issue all season long. He has taken 33 total sacks , 16 of which have come from the Steelers game and the loss to the New York Jets a few weeks back.
While the issue can't fall solely on one player, but right tackle Tytus Howard has been having a tough time this season.
He is routinely called for penalties up front and has allowed too much pressure in the backfield for Watson and the running back room. In run blocking, he ranks 51st out of 69 individuals with a mark of 56.9, while his passing grade helps him out a bit at 75.2. That is good enough to rank him 21st out of 69 individuals.
However, when combined, he is graded as the 45th-ranked offensive tackle out of 69, placing him towards the bottom of the list.
And honestly, such a ranking makes sense. He just hasn't played well. In total, he has allowed 17 pressures, two sacks and five quarterback hits, all while being flagged seven times.
He doesn't just have to clean up multiple areas of his game, but pretty much everything.
If the Browns want to continue elevating the play up front around rookies Austin Barber and Spencer Fano, they may need to make a move as the NFL Trade Deadline approaches. Whether it is signing a player from free agency or even just making a subtle trade that might not break headlines, Cleveland needs to round out the offensive line.
And that might mean cutting ties with the 30-year-old Howard if things don't start getting better.

title: Browns' Embarrassing Loss to Steelers Exposes a Major Problem Todd Monken Can No Longer Ignore
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns talked the talk last week , but tripped over their own feet when it came to walking the walk against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Nothing went the Browns’ way in Sunday’s matchup and they fell out of first place in the AFC North. From the defense’s inability to stop the run to the offensive line’s inability to provide any breathing room, there was plenty of blame to go around for the loss in Pittsburgh.
Todd Monken’s offense has not been able to run the ball, and Deshaun Watson was sacked eight times in a game for the second time this season. The offense turned the ball over on the first two drives, and the Browns fell behind early in the game.
In all five of their wins, the Browns have relied on game-winning drives and fourth-quarter magic. They consistently get behind in games, and the offense struggles to score in the first half. Their opponents have used big runs to get into scoring position in the first quarter.
Monken can no longer ignore the slow starts as the schedule flips to November and each game matters more and more.
The Browns were down 20-6 heading into halftime. They came back from a 14-point deficit in the prior game, but that was against a lowly Tennessee Titans team. Coming back in a game for the division lead, in a stadium where they have not won a regular-season game since 2003, was too much to ask from an inexperienced team.
The offense had two first-half drives that started promising, but ultimately led to field goals. The Steelers got the ball with under a minute left and drove down the length of the field with little resistance for a touchdown right before halftime. Monken has to find a way to win games starting in the first half.
There is a lot to fix all the way around and they have to play like a more complete team to get out to early leads. The offense has looked lost to start games, which should be the opposite, as the first 15 or so plays are scripted. The offensive line has given Watson no time to throw, and when he does get time, he holds on to the ball too long and ends up bailing out of the pocket.
The first series or two should have an emphasis on getting the ball out on time to the correct read. The lack of a running game has also hurt the line’s ability to protect Watson. There were few running lanes for Quinshon Judkins and when he did have room to run, he was leg-tackled by a single defender. The running game has to be established early to make life easier for Watson and the passing game.
The defense has started games slow and their tackling has been suspect. Jaylen Warren had over 100 rushing yards in the first half alone. Aaron Rodgers was hitting wide open receivers in the middle of the field against zone coverage and they did not put the offense in the best position to succeed.
They are dealing with injuries on the defensive front, but the guys who are playing need to step up to get the offense the ball with a tie or a lead. Too often, the Browns have been down before fans even get settled into their seats.
The trend of starting the game slowly was one that was in the back of the mind as the Browns were winning. The team is young, and Monken is still trying to install his offense with all the new players. However, halfway through the season, the problem is becoming too big to ignore, and Monken has to address their first-half performances.
The Browns sit at 5-3 with a light schedule in the back half of the season. If they want to make the playoffs, Monken can no longer rely on game-winning drives.

title: Jared Verse’s Struggles Raise a Costly Question for the Browns
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are facing a decision that looked like a foregone conclusion just months ago. Does it make sense to exercise Jared Verse’s fifth-year option, or should the Browns reconsider a major commitment to a centerpiece of the Myles Garrett trade?
On Monday, June 1, the Cleveland Browns traded franchise cornerstone Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in exchange for a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick, a 2029 third-round pick, and 25-year-old edge rusher Jared Verse.
Verse came to Cleveland with high expectations; Browns GM Andrew Berry went as far as to say, “He’s a perfect DNA match for our attacking front.”
Browns GM Andrew Berry on the trade of Myles Garrett: “It wasn’t something that we anticipated certainly coming into this year or coming into the spring or quite honestly coming out of the draft.” pic.twitter.com/3ITBfea5kn
The praise Verse received was well deserved, as he had already won the AP NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year award in 2024 and recorded 12 sacks across his first two seasons. Before the 2026 season, Verse seemed to be an ascending star in the league.
Verse came to Cleveland with energy, expressing confidence in the team’s work ethic and winning potential during his introductory press conference:
#Browns edge Jared Verse says “that’s not a losing team out there” pic.twitter.com/rnw3JYF7Uu
Despite the optimism surrounding his arrival , Verse has struggled to deliver the expected pass-rush production. Verse has yet to record a sack during the 2026 season and only has 13 total pressures on the season, according to PFF , putting him well behind the pace of his 80-pressure season in 2025.
That decline raises an important question: should the Browns pick up Verse’s fifth-year option on his rookie deal?
A fifth-year option allows a team to extend a first-round draft pick’s four-year rookie contract by one season at a salary determined by league rules that account for position, playing time, and Pro Bowl selections. Teams make that decision after the player’s third season, and the option salary becomes fully guaranteed once exercised.
In Verse’s case, his fifth-year option is projected at approximately $28 million for the 2028 season, according to Over the Cap , because of his two original-ballot Pro Bowl selections.
Cleveland must decide in spring 2027 whether his production justifies that commitment. Declining the option would still leave Verse under contract for the 2027 season. A strong finish would give the Browns more reason to make that substantial financial commitment.
The Browns felt comfortable moving on from Myles Garrett due to the timeline fit Verse provided, as his age is in line with the team's many young stars. Verse still has nine regular-season games to show that he belongs in Cleveland’s long-term plans. His past success earned him the opportunity, but his remaining performances must justify the price.

title: Steelers Players Clap Back At Browns' Jared Verse Following Disappointing Performance
full_text:
Things can't get much worse for the Cleveland Browns right now.
On Sunday, Nov. 1, the Browns lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers on the road from Acrisure Stadium in an abysmal 27- 6 showing. Not only did the offense fail to score a touchdown, but the defense was getting beat left and right as running backs Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle combined for nearly 200 yards on the deck with two touchdowns.
Leading up to the game, just weeks after beating the Steelers at home, Browns defensive end Jared Verse spoke up about how he had been waiting for the rematch. He said the Steelers' antics in the first meeting were "garbage" and "dirty."
Browns vs. Steelers recently Jared Verse: "I don’t got no respect for anybody that plays too dirty, and that does too much extra shit after the game. ... I can’t wait to get my hands on them again." Cam Heyward: "The AFC North is on fire and I’m glad I’m in the kitchen because…
Well, unfortunately, not only were the Browns not able to back him up, but his play wasn't able to either.
The 25-year-old finished the game with practically nothing on the stat sheet, posting just a single assisted tackle.
Following the win, Steelers defensive back Jaquan Brisker clapped back at Verse, saying he should have kept quiet.
“He should have kept his mouth shut," Brisker said. "All that talk, and then to come out with 0 tackles? You didn't stand on business. He gotta look at himself in the mirror and get better."
#Steelers S Jaquan Brisker calls out Jared Verse: “He should have kept his mouth shut. All that talk, and then to come out with 0 tackles? You didn't stand on business. He gotta look at himself in the mirror and get better." (📽️ @AshleyWenskTV ) pic.twitter.com/0dA7tduHdQ https://t.co/8eKpqrPMSr
Verse's time in the Orange and Brown hasn't been too hot, with Sunday's performance just adding fuel to the fire that is the narrative that he has lost his touch.
Through the first eight games of the year, he has a whopping 10 solo tackles and eight assisted tackles for 18 total . He also has zero sacks, forced fumbles, fumble recoveries and pass deflections, all areas he at least recorded a single statistic in previous years.
Following in Brisker's words, Steelers offensive lineman Max Iheanachor also shot a diss in Verse's direction.
On X, he posted, "Like I said, Talk is cheap," followed by a talking emoji.
Like I said, Talk is cheap 🗣️
Verse didn't just have a tough time in the stat column either on Sunday, as he was seen being ragdoll-tossed down to the ground by Steelers offensive guard Mason McCormick on a field goal attempt. Verse went crashing down to the ground, landing right on his head.
The circumstances warranted a 15-yard penalty.
After the game, Verse spoke out and said that he doesn't have any respect for McCormick's moves on the play.
In response, McCormick said that he had no idea it was even Verse jumping towards him on the play, seemingly downplaying the situation.
I asked #Steelers G Mason McCormick on dumping #Browns DE Jared Verse during a PAT — you’ve probably seen it by now, I don’t really need to explain: pic.twitter.com/PaeBLlXtxP
Either way, Verse has dove head first into the Browns-Steelers rivalry, getting a front row seat to just how crazy it can get.
While antics, lackluster performances and postgame quotes are going to steal the show, that could have all been avoided if the Browns had won on Sunday.
But for the third time this season, Cleveland ended up on the bad end of a result.
If Verse and the Browns want to chat back and forth with the opposition leading up to a Sunday showdown, next time, they better be able to back it up.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Steelers Expose Browns' Biggest Weakness in Frustrating Cleveland Loss
full_text:
There was plenty of back-and-forth between the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers throughout the past week.
The latter ended up being the team to live up to all the talk.
The Steelers took an early 10-0 lead that proved to be insurmountable as Deshaun Watson and the Browns offense failed to reach the end zone on Sunday.
Cleveland's first two drives ended in fumbles, setting the tone for an ugly Sunday in Pittsburgh.
The Browns couldn't do much of anything right in the loss. A quick glimpse at the box score shows how the Browns finished with 34 rushing yards, while the Steelers had 200. Jaylen Warren led the way with a dominant 17 carries for 143 yards.
The Browns defense had no answer for Warren and company, while the Browns offense struggled for each and every yard on the ground. That made passing the focus and resulted in Watson taking eight sacks, as he was under constant pressure with every single dropback.
#Browns DE Jared Verse has been talking plenty of trash about the #Steelers .... Well, Steelers G Mason McCormick just did this to him.  😳😳 pic.twitter.com/OP1iknS4JP
The score may have been even worse if the Steelers capped off two early drives with touchdowns instead of field goals, and if DK Metcalf didn't bobble a potential big catch right into the arms of Denzel Ward.
Watson and the Browns have been comeback specialists in 2026, with the latest coming last week against the Tennessee Titans. Yet the Steelers are on an entirely different level, improving to 6-2 with the win.
Sunday's game also involved a rare Shedeur Sanders sighting in 2026. He came on for a series and completed two short passes while Watson was getting checked out on the sideline and ultimately cleared to return.
Fans seeking a positive from the loss can look to the big day from Harold Fannin Jr. The tight end finished with 10 catches for 154 yards, representing a new career-best in yards. Yes, some of the yardage did come near the end of the game. But there's still no denying his game-changing abilities when properly involved in the offense.
Next up is a road game against the 2-5 New Orleans Saints, currently resting up on a bye week. That is a team with a total of 602 rushing yards through seven games, so all eyes will be on the Browns defense to see if the unit can end this current trend of getting destroyed in the running game.
This loss was an ugly one, however, the Browns do get the split with the Steelers in 2026. Winning in Pittsburgh has been nearly impossible for the post-1999 Browns, so Sunday's loss was nothing too surprising.
Steve is a lifelong Cleveland sports fan who proudly wears his Guardians, Browns, and Cavs gear in his current home of Santa Barbara. He has covered Cleveland sports online for the past decade and is still waiting for the Browns to draft a QB who signs a second contract in town.

title: 3 Biggest Takeaways From Browns Week 8 Loss to Rival Pittsburgh Steelers
full_text:
Well, the Cleveland Browns just embarrassed themselves.
After talking big all week leading up to the final regular season meeting with the Pittsburgh Steelers this year, the Browns took the field at Acrisure Stadium and put up a disappointing performance.
On Sunday, Nov. 1, the Browns lost to the Steelers, 27-6, with multiple glaring issues leading to the team's downfall. From a lackluster start to the game from the offense to countless penalties and issues with self-control, the Browns suffered loss No. 3 of the season.
Fortunately, there is still plenty of season left to make corrections, but this one stung a bit.
Here are the three biggest takeaways from the Browns' Week 8 loss to the Steelers on the road:
Yet again, the offense looked slow out of the gates.
Across the first three drives of the game, the Deshaun Watson-led offense managed to muster a whopping 14 yards off of 11 players. The Browns would leave each with zero points, as two fumbles and a punt stole the show.
Watson was responsible with one fumble, with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. being the other.
The Browns would finish the first quarter trailing by seven points, before two field goals helped to lessen the blow in the second. By the time the opening half concluded, Cleveland was down by 14 points, 20-6.
While Watson did end up finishing the game with 27 completions for 324 yards passing , his lackluster start to the game set the tone.
Deshaun Watson may have finished with 27 completions for 324 yards... but the slow start to Sunday's game set the tone for the Browns' offense... They have to stop turning it on so late. Final: 27-6. #DawgPound
If the Browns want to start putting themselves in more favorable positions to win, getting on the board within the first drive or two is going to have to become a priority.
The Browns hurt themselves... a lot.
By the end of Sunday's game, penalties had taken away 80 yards from them. For a team already going up against a loud fanbase at Acrisure Stadium, putting yourself in increasingly difficult situations with self-inflicted penalties makes things much worse.
Heading into Week 8, the Browns had a whopping 63 penalties across seven games, bringing them to an average of nine per game. While pre-snap issues have been a big part, the offense has just been all-around sloppy.
Head coach Todd Monken will likely harp on the team's penalty issues behind closed doors, which is the correct thing to do, but things have got to start changing.
The Browns just can't keep beating themselves.
Among the 80 yards of penalties on Sunday were a few taunting calls, something that seemed shocking considering they came with Cleveland trailing by multiple scores.
If the Browns are going to talk the talk, they better be able to walk the walk.
On Sunday, they just simply didn't.
Two takeaways: 1) how are you taunting down 21 points? 2) how are you throwing flags like that in a rivalry game? Either way, gotta keep your emotions in check… #DawgPound
Before they started to lose control of their emotions later in the game, the Browns looked asleep. From start to finish, the entire game felt all over the place in the emotional department. Jared Verse, one of the Browns' leaders on the defensive side of the ball, yet again fell short after a week of talking smack to the Steelers.
It's always nice to see players hype up an outing, especially when the rivalry runs so deep, but if you are going to, you have to back it up.
Looking to put Week 8 behind them, the Browns return to the gridiron on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1:00 p.m. EST from Caesars Superdome in New Orleans to take on the Saints.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Week 8 Browns vs. Steelers: What To Expect, Injury Report, How To Watch and More
full_text:
It's another rendition of a rivalry that runs deep.
Following a 27-24 victory at Huntington Bank Field for the Cleveland Browns just a few weeks ago, the Pittsburgh Steelers will be searching for revenge in the second meeting of the 2026 NFL regular season.
On Sunday, Nov. 1, the Browns and Steelers will face one another at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh for a Week 8 showdown. The two sides will renew the storied rivalry in the 151st all-time meeting. This time around, though, the narrative is centered on the Steelers' long winning streak at home and the Browns' opportunity to sweep the Steelers for the first time since 1988.
The Browns last won in Pittsburgh on Oct. 5, 2003, when then-quarterback Tim Couch threw for over 200 yards and two touchdowns, while the defense forced two interceptions in a 33-13 victory.
Looking to repeat such efforts, the Browns will need to come locked in and ready to go against an experienced, veteran-led Steelers squad.
From the jump, Sunday's game is going to be a fiery one.
Throughout the week, the two sides had been throwing little jabs at one another, with defensive linemen Jared Verse and Cam Heyward being at the center of the attention.
"I'm not worried about Cam [Heyward]," Verse said earlier in the week. "I'm not worried about their O-line. I'm not worried about nobody they got on their team. We out there to go dominate."
He went on to say that he has been waiting for the rematch, and that last time's meeting left a bad taste in his mouth due to some "dirty" plays.
In response, Heyward clapped back at Verse, pretty much calling him a baby.
"Double-teaming, sliding, chipping, are those not allowed in our game? Yeah, I got the bruises to prove it," Heyward said. "But we don’t whine about it, baby. It’s part of the game. And so, I’m looking forward to this game. It’s gonna be a fun game..."
But this isn't something unexpected.
In seasons past, the rivalry has run deep, with tensions never really running low. However, that isn't necessarily a bad thing, as a blood-boiling rivalry makes things entertaining for everyone involved.
Fortunately, things are looking clear for Sunday's meeting.
From 1pm through 5 pm, the temperature is expected to sit between 67 degrees and 69 degrees, with somewhat cloudy skies. The precipitation is at 10%, while the Humidity comes in at 53%. There are no expected storms.
While Browns Stadium always sees a good amount of wind, Acrisure will not.
The air quality is a strong 44, with the wind coming in at just three miles per hour. If there are any gusts, they are expected to be roughly eight miles per hour.
Date and Time: Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026 at 1:00 p.m. EST
The game can be watched on television on CBS, with streaming options such as YouTube TV, Fubo, DirecTV and Paramount+ available as well.
The last time the Browns and Steelers clashed, multiple players went down with injuries.
For the Browns, the two standouts were defensive tackles Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr., who left the game at different points with lower-body injuries. Although Hall Jr. ended up finishing the game, both he and Graham would miss future games.
Heading into Sunday, both players are healthy.
Here is the rest of the injury reports as of the early morning hours on Sunday:
CB Echols (Hamstring) - Out LB Highsmith (Groin) - Cleared CB Ramsey (Wrist) - Cleared WR Skowronek (Calf) - Questionable DB Slaughter (Hamstring) - Out
S Delpit (Neck) - Cleared DT Graham (Ankle) - Cleared DT Hall Jr. (Ankle) - Cleared CB Harden (Hamstring) - Questionable OT Howard (Concussion) - Cleared LB Schwesinger (Ankle) - Cleared DE Verse (Knee) - Cleared DB Thomas (Ankle) - Questionable
Kickoff between the two sides is set for 1:00 p.m. EST, with the winner taking the top spot in the AFC North in a crucial part of the season.

title: Can the Browns Beat the Steelers? Traveling to Pittsburgh is No Easy Task
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have already weathered the storm that is the Pittsburgh Steelers once this season.
But that doesn't mean the second meeting is going to be any easier.
On Sunday, Nov. 1, the Browns will travel to Acrisure Stadium to take on the Steelers for the second matchup between the two sides during the 2026 NFL regular season. The Browns won the first meeting, 27-24, but since then, the Steelers have made many changes and improvements.
They head into Sunday's outing with a three-game winning streak in hand, a mark the Browns sit just a game behind.
When these two sides meet, though, records and successes that season are thrown out the window.
It is simply a good ol' fashioned rivalry, and anything can happen.
What is going to make the biggest difference on the first day of November will likely be confidence, especially in the way of the Browns.
As a young squad, they won't just face one of the league's most experienced, veteran-led teams, but also a team that has called their number time and time again in Pittsburgh. The Steelers have held onto a narrative for 22 straight regular-season games: not losing at home to the Browns.
The Browns have lost 22 straight regular-season games in Pittsburgh, and have not won a regular-season game there since Oct. 5, 2003 -- 8,248 days ago. They are one loss today shy of tying the NFL record for most consecutive road regular-season losses vs. a team in NFL history… pic.twitter.com/10avzSmShS
The Browns have not won a game in Pittsburgh since Oct. 5, 2003.
At that time, Tim Couch was the Browns' signal caller, throwing for two touchdowns and one interception in a 33-13 victory. The Browns would go on to win just five games that season, losing 11, but as the rivalry has shown in the past, sometimes that is one of the most important games on the schedule.
Browns defensive end Jared Verse sparked the fire up a bit earlier in the week, putting more weight on a good performance from Cleveland on Sunday.
"I'm not worried about Cam [Heyward]," he began. "I'm not worried about their o-line, I'm not worried about nobody they've got on their team. We're out there to go dominate."
Verse has yet to record a sack this season, but that doesn't mean he hasn't been impactful. On film review, the 25-year-old has been seen taking assignments away from other offensive linemen, freeing up his teammates to get into the backfield and go to work.
As a defense, the Browns rank 12th in points allowed this season, while the line itself ranks fifth in pressure rate. Even with Verse not putting any sacks on the board, the group is finding a way to disrupt opposing quarterbacks.
But in front of the Steelers faithful, Verse and the rest of the defense will certainly get an earful. They will have to show they can cut out the fans and trash talk and put veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers on his backside.
Browns head coach Todd Monken understands that the rivalry runs deep, but he is making it known that this new group of players has nothing to do with the long-winded losing streak.
Instead, he has been trying to set the stage for a new opportunity for the current squad to show the rest of the league how good they are, as a win against the Steelers would put them in sole control of the AFC North.
"Whether it's where we're at record-wise, comparing the past or the history against the Steelers—it's a divisional game," Monken said. "Fastest way to get in the playoffs is win your division. That's the fastest way to get in the playoffs. I mean, you're guaranteed in the tournament and we're a long ways away from that.
"That's not what I'm saying. That's why the game is what it is. And rivalries are made up of good teams playing each other and we're fighting like hell to be a really good team."
The Browns will look to snap a losing streak that has lasted longer than many players on the active roster have been alive.
Even with that, though, rookie wideout Denzel Boston understands just how important a win would be.
"We know coming into this game it’s going to be chippy considering what happened last game," he said. "...I had a conversation yesterday with people [about the losing streak]... which we aren't paying attention to any of those stats going into the game, but I can tell it is huge for the city of Cleveland."
Sunday will be the 151st installment of such a storied rivalry, with the two sides set to square away at 1:00 p.m. EST.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Eye-Opening Stat Shows What the Browns Need WR Jerry Jeudy to Rediscover
full_text:
A season where the Cleveland Browns won just three games and lost a whopping 14.
But although there were many, and I mean many, negatives following that season, one big-time positive was the breakout of wide receiver Jerry Jeudy.
The then-25-year-old went out and led the offense with 90 receptions, 1,229 yards and four touchdowns . He averaged 13.7 yards per reception and 72.3 yards per game. That type of productivity gave a glimpse into Jeudy's true potential.
Posted on X by Gridiron Stats and Info on Saturday, Oct. 31, the last time the Browns had a 150-yard receiver was Jeudy, back during the 2024 season. In a late-season Dec. 2 matchup with the Denver Broncos, he hauled in nine of 13 targets for 235 yards and one touchdown.
Last time each NFL team had a 150-yard receiver pic.twitter.com/gOIl3DRSHK
Even with such production, somehow, someway, the Browns would lose 42-31. But Jeudy still put a positive light on the game as he joined the record books, becoming the fourth player in franchise history to surpass 200 receiving yards in a game, trailing just Josh Gordon and Amari Cooper for the top spots.
However, just a few years later, now at age 27, Jeudy has seemingly fallen completely out of the Browns' offensive plans.
And looking back at 2024 and comparing his play to that of 2026 begs the question: can he ever return to that form?
Just three seasons ago, Jeudy was catching passes from a combination of Jameis Winston, Deshaun Watson, Dorian Thompson-Robinson and Bailey Zappe.
Now, in 2026, he has Watson as his starting signal caller.
Building chemistry has been difficult, especially with Watson missing the last two seasons. When Jeudy joined the Browns from the Denver Broncos, the controversial quarterback was already dealing with off-field issues and injuries, limiting the time they could spend developing a connection.
As long as Watson can stay healthy this season, the bond will gradually form.
Since getting just five targets for two catches and 26 yards across the first three weeks of the season, his involvement in the offense has shot up tremendously over the last four weeks. From Week 4 through Week 7, he has made 14 catches on 18 targets for 145 yards.
While at times he doesn't get the rock thrown his way until late, Watson has turned to him in critical moments, where Jeudy has then delivered.
The Browns know it, Watson knows it and Jeudy knows it: when the Browns need a play, they go his way. He has the experience and the resume to prove that he can be an elite weapon, especially downfield; that connection just needs a chance to fully grow.
I asked #Browns WR Jerry Jeudy about Cleveland’s fourth-quarter grit and ability to find a way to win: "We're just motivated. We're determined to win each and every week. We come with the mindset to win the game, no matter what the score is. We focus on each play." pic.twitter.com/d7mPzimahA
And fortunately, it seems that he will have every opportunity to make up for lost time.
Over the course of the last few weeks, rumors have swirled about whether or not the Browns' front office would start shopping him. While the Browns will at least listen to an offer if it is substantial enoug h, which makes total sense, they do not plan to actively look to move him elsewhere.
It seems that the 27-year-old will have a chance to remain in Cleveland and form a deeper bond with the young offense.
"With Cleveland in the postseason mix and Jeudy maintaining a good attitude despite the emergence of rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston at wide receiver, sources say his chances of being traded is viewed as less likely," Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter recently wrote. "The Browns aren't shopping Jeudy at all, and the price is high. It would take a premium deal to get Cleveland to move on -- even if general manager Andrew Berry is open to discussing any deal.
"But as of right now, a Jeudy deal seems unlikely."
It sounds like Jerry Jeudy is locked into the Browns roster unless a team comes with a wild offer (which isn’t happening). Ian Rapoport ( @RapSheet ) and Adam Schefter ( @AdamSchefter ) reporting the Browns aren’t shopping the veteran receiver and "the price is too high." Browns… pic.twitter.com/qV98g4Ce6b
Jeudy's next opportunity to slowly start regaining that dominant form he displayed in 2024 will be this weekend on Sunday, Nov. 1, when the Browns travel to Pittsburgh to take on the Steelers.
The two sides will matchup at 1:00 p.m. EST at Acrisure Stadium for the second meeting of the season.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: George Pickens Trade Buzz Heating Up With NFL Insider's Report After Cowboys Loss
full_text:
With the Dallas Cowboys now sitting at 3-5 following a devastating loss to the Arizona Cardinals in Week 8, many are starting to wonder if the team should trade George Pickens.
It's not hard to see why. Pickens isn't making the same impact he did last season, and the impact he is making is doing nothing to change the Cowboys' fortunes this season.
We're also seeing a potential deterioration of the relationship between Pickens and the Cowboys in recent weeks. First, head caoch Brian Schottenheimer called him out for his lackluster run-blocking, and then we saw Pickens waste no team leaving the field after the Cardinals loss, which might be a sign he's checked out.
Adding to all of that, the Cowboys are also heading for a contract showdown with him in 2027, as Pickens is set to be a free agent and tagging him could lead to a holdout.
According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz , some around the league are beginning to wonder if Pickens could be moved at the trade deadline.
"But the biggest name people around the league are really starting to get curious about is George Pickens in Dallas," Schultz said on The Pivot .
"He's playing on the franchise tag, he has not been utilized the same way as last year. You're talking about, in my opinion, Ryan, one of the four or five most talented receivers in football and the Cowboys' season is, honestly, unraveling, especially defensively."
Schultz then goes on to say that those same people wondering if owner Jerry Jones could use Pickens as a trade chip to improve another area of the team, like the defense, for example.
"The question becomes, and this is the question that several teams have asked me: would Jerry Jones consider having a little ace up his sleeve, if you will?" Schultz asked. "And Dallas, would they consider using Pickens as a trade chip to improve another area of the roster? I'm not saying it'll happen, but given where the Cowboys are right now, and given the demand for a talent like George Pickens, that is one I'm certainly watching."
There is nothing illogical about what Schultz is saying here. At this point, there seems to be no benefit to holding on to Pickens any longer.
It would be more worth it for the Cowboys to flip him for defensive help, or even just draft capital given how much the team's stable of picks has dwindled because of recent trades.
And that's something The Athletic's Jonathan Jones touched on over the weekend.
Jones' sources believe the Cowboys will have a tough time trading another pick because of their lackluster stable and that led Jones to wonder if the Cowboys might make a player-for-player deal instead.
"Jerry Jones is always down to make a deal, but sources there think a pick-for-player trade would be difficult considering what Dallas has left. Player-for-player trades have always been rare in the league, but if Dallas acquires help, maybe that’s their method," Jones wrote.
Pickens is the most valuable trade chip the Cowboys could afford to part ways with, so it makes sense to consider him a candidate to be moved in a player-for-player deal that brings in an impact defender.
If the Cowboys are in a position where they can improve the defense by sending Pickens away in a deal, it's something they should at least consider. It might also make sense to unload Pickens if a team offers a Day 2 pick.

title: Cowboys Defense Takes Major Hit With Two Rookie Starters Injured
full_text:
Losing is bad enough, especially when you blow a 14-point lead in the fourth quarter as the Dallas Cowboys did this weekend against the Arizona Cardinals . It's even worse when a team suffers injuries during such a defeat, which also happened to the Cowboys.
Dallas was playing well on defense for the first 45 minutes, but then cornerback Joey Porter Jr. and rookie safety Caleb Downs left with injuries and things fell apart. On Monday, there was an update on injuries and it doesn't look great for the Dallas defense.
They're waiting for tests on Porter, so there's not a lot to update there. For Downs, however, he's in concussion protocol , leaving his status for Week 9 in doubt.
What's worse is that fellow first round pick Malachi Lawrence also suffered an injury against the Cardinals and his update was the most concerning. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer admitted the injury suffered by Lawrence was worse than they initially thought, adding that he could miss multiple weeks.
Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said rookie OLB Malachi Lawrence could be out a few weeks with an ankle injury. TE Jake Ferguson has a chance to play Sunday despite his ankle injury. Rookie DB Caleb Downs is in concussion protocol.
Lawrence was selected 23rd overall out of UCF and had recently moved into the starting lineup. He has 13 tackles and one sack on the season in eight games.
In addition to the rookies being injured, the Cowboys announced that P.J. Locke is also in concussion protocol. Jake Ferguson, who injured his ankle in Week 8, has a chance to play this weekend, according to Schottenheimer.
Downs, who was selected 11th overall out of Ohio State, has 52 tackles, one sack, and two forced fumbles in eight games. He's been a central piece to the Dallas defense, but could miss a game that he's had marked on the calendar since the schedule was released.
In Week 9, the Cowboys will face the Indianapolis Colts on the road. Downs was interested in this game since his older brother, Josh Downs, is a wide receiver for Indianapolis. The elder Downs enters Week 9 with 30 receptions for 330 yards and a touchdown.
Interestingly enough, Josh Downs recently requested a trade from Indianapolis. The Colts are currently 2-6, but have been open for business as they look toward the future. They fired general manager Chris Ballard and have traded guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner.
Rumors have them potentially moving on from running back Jonathan Taylor as well, but for now, the Cowboys are set to face Taylor as well as Josh Downs. Unfortunately, they might be short-handed on defense when they do so.

title: Ex-NFL QB Hearing Cowboys Could Be Done With Dak Prescott After 2026
full_text:
Former NFL quarterback Chris Simms has dropped an interesting little nugget about the Dallas Cowboys and quarterback Dak Prescott on Monday.
In the wake of the Cowboys suffering a brutal defeat at the hands of the Arizona Cardinals in Week 8, Simms said on the "Chris Simms Unbuttoned" podcast that there's been some chatter about the Cowboys "being at the end of their rope" with the veteran quarterback.
And, because of that, the talk is that there's a chance that Prescott won't be the Cowboys' quarterback in 2027 if things don't turn around this year.
“There’s been some murmurs that, in Dallas, that they’re a little bit like at the end of their rope with Dak Prescott," Simms said . "Like, it’s like things better turn around or he ain’t gonna be the quarterback there next year. We'lll see. We'll see.”
Simms didn't offer up more details than that, but we would take this with the smallest grain of salt possible.
We're not buying what Simms is putting out there.
The biggest reason is Prescott's contract. The Cowboys have no wiggle room to get out of it, with the deal having astronomical dead cap hits, even with a post-June 1 cut or trade.
We also know Dallas isn't simply going to bench Prescott when he's making all that money. Just look at Dallas' insistence on playing DaRon Bland despite his struggles.
According to Over the Cap , Dallas would take on a dead-cap hit of $131 million or $76 million in 2027 depending on if they cut Prescott before or after June 1, and the dead money figures for a trade settle in at $86 million and $31 million pre- and post-June 1.
Bear in mind, those are just the dead money figures for next year. Dallas would be taking on dead-cap hits through 2030 because of void years on Prescott's deal.
Unless the Cowboys plan on blowing it up and rebuilding (there is no way Jerry Jones will do that), the chances of Dallas taking on those dead-cap hits are extremely slim. And, even if Dallas was able to find a trade partner, no team is taking on Prescott's deal, so Dallas will be eating a large chunk of it.
If anything, the Cowboys might have to extend the veteran signal-caller or at least restructure his deal with Prescott set to account for a massive $76 million cap hit in 2027. Both of those avenues will kick the can down the road further.
All of that and we haven't even mentioned that the Cowboys have to find a replacement. Signing a veteran would be expensive and add more financial burden on top of all of that dead money, and drafting a quarterback offers no guarantees.
We also find it hard to believe the Cowboys blame Prescott as much as Simms' report suggests.
Sure, Prescott has fallen short of expectations overall during his career and has only delivered two playoff wins, but the struggles the Cowboys have experienced in his tenure haven't been all his fault.
Take this season and the last two years, for example.
The Cowboys have sported the worst defense in the NFL in that span and that has stacked the deck against Dallas' ability to have any semblance of success. Prescott and the offense have been the only shred of hope this franchise has had since 2024.
Dallas also struck out badly with the hires of head coach Brian Schottenheimer and defensive coordinator Christian Parker to further hinder the team.
The bottom line is this: Prescott's contract is an albatross and that in and of itself makes it highly unlikely a divorce from the Cowboys is coming as early as 2027.

title: Dallas Cowboys Highest & Lowest Graded Players in Crushing Week 8 Loss
full_text:
It was a tale of two halves for the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8. During the first 30 minutes, they were in full control and well on their way to defeating the Arizona Cardinals for the first time since 2017.
For the final 30 minutes, they looked as though they forgot what sport they were playing .
Dallas suddenly couldn’t stop the run or the pass and the offense completely flat-lined at the end. It was a frustrating loss that dropped them to 3-5 on the season and has head coach Brian Schottenheimer feeling the heat . As for the play on the field, let’s check out which players performed well and which ones fell short, at least according to the grades from Pro Football Focus.
Markquese Bell technically had the highest grade at 86.2, but since he played just three snaps, we skip to Quinnen Williams as the top-rated player with an 82.4. Williams had two sacks and has now recorded at least one in each of the past three games. He’s joined at the top by fellow defensive tackle Kenny Clark, although neither could make a huge play at the end to save their team. Malik Hooker was fourth with a 75.9 and in all honesty, it’s shocking to see three defenders in this list after that performance.
Two offensive players made the top five with George Pickens leading the way with an 80.0. Dak Prescott was fifth overall with a 75.8. Pickens’ grade makes it even more infuriating that he was targeted just four times and had a mere two catches for 48 yards. It also explains why he was so quick to leave the field after the loss.
Alijah Clark has been earning more playing time as of late, but Sunday wasn’t his best showing. He comes in as the lowest-rated player with a 38.1, although DaRon Bland’s 40.1 wasn’t much better. Otito Ogbonnia has been their best run defender, but he fell in the lowest-rated category following an excellent game from the Cardinals’ rushing attack.
Offensively, their lowest-graded players were all along the offensive line. Cooper Beebe and Tyler Guyton were the fourth and fifth lowest-graded players, but they weren’t alone. Tyler Smith was given a 45.9 and Terence Steele earned a 48.2. Only Tyler Booker (73.3) had a good grade on the O-line, which sums up their problems at the end of the game.

title: Former NFL Head Coaches Eviscerate Cowboys After Historically Bad Loss to Cardinals
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are getting it from all angles following their total collapse in the Week 8 loss to the Arizona Cardinals.
The Cowboys deserve every bit of the tongue-lashings they are getting from the NFL world after they managed to cough up a game in which they were in total control of.
Dallas had a 14-point lead going into the fourth quarter, and they were up by 10 with just 3:54 remaining. However, that just wasn't enough to exorcise the demon that has been the Cardinals , who have beaten Dallas in nine of the last 10 meetings between the two franchises.
On Sunday night, former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin questioned the Cowboys' effort and killer instinct on "Football Night In America."
“Watching the end of that game," he said, "I didn’t see individuals or particular units that wanted to grab the bull by the horns and win the game."
“I see a team that doesn’t have anybody that wants to be the unit to secure victory," Tomlin added.
When it comes to fixing those issues, Tomlin said the Cowboys have to identify "who wants it" and lean on those players more.
“You gotta figure out who wants it, and you gotta shift your division of labor to those that want it,” Tomlin said. “And so knowledge of your team is a major component. But also, you got to challenge those guys individually and collectively. Tell them you’re looking for that guy who wants to be it.”
Former New York Jets coach Rex Ryan went in on the Cowboys for what he called "one of the all-time choke jobs in the history of football."
“One of the all-time choke jobs in the history of football," Ryan said on ESPN's Get Up . "You gotta be kidding me here."
"This is atrocious," Ryan added. "They stink... how in the hell do you not win this division... you stink on defense. Stop!"
It's hard to argue with what Ryan is saying in any regard, and that's especially true with Ryan pointing to this as a historic loss.
The 14-point fourth-quarter lead the Cowboys blew on Sunday was tied for the largest in franchise history . Prior to the Cardinals loss, the Cowboys were 342-2-1 when leading by 14 points or more in the fourth quarter.
Taking it a step further, the Cowboys had never blown a 14-point fourth-quarter lead at home in franchise history, according to CBS Sports' Doug Clawson .
Ryan's note about the division makes what the Cowboys are doing this season even more jarring.
A division has never been more ripe for the taking than the NFC East this season. The Washington Commanders and Philadelphia Eagles both stink and are going nowhere, and the New York Giants are fortunate to have the number of wins they do and aren't good, either.
The Cowboys should be running away with the division. Instead, Dallas is as bad as their division mates and is sitting in second place in the NFC East and trail the Giants by three in the loss column going into Week 9.
And, lest we forget, the Giants currently have the head-to-head tie-breaker advantage after beating Dallas in Week 1, so the deficit is even bigger until the Cowboys even that out.
At this point, winning the division means nothing. That will only serve to delay the inevitable.

title: Stephen A. Smith Unloads on Dak Prescott, Cowboys Following Week 8 Loss
full_text:
Week 8 brought us another loss for the Dallas Cowboys as they fell to the Arizona Cardinals 33-30 in overtime.
Sadly, the late-game collapse feels all too normal at this point, but so do the press conferences that follow. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer is again saying he needs to get to work and be better while Dak Prescott is preaching patience while defending the coaching staff .
Another thing else that feels normal these days is seeing Stephen A. Smith lose his mind while railing on the Cowboys. That was the case again on Monday as he called the team "pathetic" on ESPN's First Take. Naturally, he took aim at the defense, but also said Dak Prescott isn't handling things correctly by the way he's defending his teammates and coaches.
"I'm really sick and tired of that damn Dak Prescott saying all the right things after a post-game conference. I understand the defense is trash. I understand they're horrible against rushing. I understand they gave up," Smith said.
He went on to say that while Prescott is technically saying the right thing, it's actually leaving the team without the leadership they need. Smith claims the accountability is gone in Dallas and said Prescott should take a page out of the book of many other star quarterbacks who might not have been so nice seeing a 14-point lead evaporate.
"Could you imagine if some of the superstars that you've seen play defensively throughout the years of Aaron Rodgers and Tom Brady and Drew Brees and the list goes. Could you imagine how they would have been on the sidelines? Could you imagine how they would be in a post-game conference if you asking them about a team's putrid performance like that?"
“They are trash. They are horrible. They are pathetic!” @stephenasmith goes OFF on the Dallas Cowboys after their loss to the Arizona Cardinals 😬 pic.twitter.com/58g5c1WPr2
It's not just Prescott who makes everyone feel secure in Dallas, according to Smith. He says the coaching staff doesn't hold players accountable, which is why he believes Jerry Jones messed up by not hiring Rex Ryan when he was looking for his new defensive coordinator this offseason. Unlike Parker, Ryan is known for being overly aggressive and Smith believes that fire is what this defense lacks.
"Jerry Jones made a mistake by not going and getting Rex Ryan to be his defensive coordinator. You need somebody fiery. You need somebody that's going to hold cats accountable. You need somebody that's in Dallas that's going to make people recognize that their jobs are on the line if they don't go out there and produce," Smith said. "Because individually as talent, they seem to have it. But you know what? The losses don't hurt enough because life is real comfortable in Big D."
Ryan hasn't coached in the NFL since 2016 when he was the head coach of the Buffalo Bills. He doesn't feel like a real candidate at this point, but that doesn't mean Smith's argument is wrong.
There's definitely a lack of leadership in Dallas, which is why this team is so prone to mental mistakes and late-game collapses. That falls on Brian Schottenheimer more so than anyone . Sure, Parker has not lived up to expectations, but this team was just as bad in 2025 without Parker. The one common denominator is Schottenheimer and his seat needs to be hotter than anyone's in Dallas right now.

title: Dak Prescott Misses the Mark in Attempt to Deflect Blame off Schottenheimer Amid Cowboys' Woes
full_text:
When a team is struggling as badly as the Dallas Cowboys are this season, it's only natural to blame the head coach.
And that's especially true when it comes to Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer, who hasn't done a good job, both in a lead role and as the offensive play-caller.
After the Cowboys' latest debacle against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 8, quarterback Dak Prescott tried to deflect the mountain of blame that has come Schottenheimer's way.
He said placing all of the blame on Schottenheimer for the Cowboys' struggles is "cowardice."
“It’s all of us,” Prescott said, per the team’s website . “Don’t put the blame on one person. Simple as that. I think that’s weak. I think that’s cowardice."
"This game is about all 11 that touch the field and every person that has a part in it coaches and support staff. It’s never just one person’s fault," Prescott added. "Even if I go out there and throw a bunch of interceptions, it’s never just truly one person’s fault. And so, don’t take the easy and cheap way out. This is about us and it’s about us backing him up and backing one another up and we’ll have to show it.”
The problem with what Dak is saying is that nobody is placing all of the blame on Schottenheimer's shoulders. There is plenty to go around for the players and for defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who is simply inadequate , at best, at his job.
But the buck stops with Schottenheimer, who has failed miserably at leading this team and calling the offense.
We saw another example of Schotty's poor decision-making at the end of the first half on Sunday, when, with one timeout in his pocket, he decided to call a run play with 11 seconds left rather than throwing a pass to get Brandon Aubrey closer.
The result was a four-yard gain and a 61-yard attempt for Aubrey that the Cowboys kicker missed. Had Aubrey made the field goal, Dallas would have won the game, plain and simple. Now, it never should have come to that, but the point stands.
There may also be a culture issue in Dallas, and if so, that's yet another stain on Schottenheimer's tenure.
Multiple former Cowboys have questioned the players' effort , and even Schottenheimer has called out George Pickens for not doing enough as a run-blocker, for example.
Effort problems equal culture problems and it's Schottenheimer who is responsible for setting the tone in that department. He's clearly not doing a good enough job on that front.
There are no two ways about it. The Cowboys don't have the right man for the job and no amount of support from Prescott is going to convince us otherwise. Until Schottenheimer is let go, there's zero hope for Dallas.
Unfortunately, owner Jerry Jones continues to show no desire to make a much-needed change , whether that's at head coach or defensive coordinator.

title: Cowboys Insider Believes Brian Schottenheimer’s Ego Holding Him Back
full_text:
Despite going 7-9-1 during his first season as the head coach of the Dallas Cowboys, there was still a lot of positive energy around Brian Schottenheimer entering the new year.
His offense was among the best in the league and the Cowboys spent the offseason working to improve their defense . Now after a 3-5 start and yet another fourth-quarter meltdown, Schottenheimer is feeling the heat . The calls for his job are growing and every week, he says he’s going to put in the work to get things fixed.
Schottenheimer has done his best to remain confident, but one insider thinks the way he sees himself might be the problem. Following the loss to the Arizona Cardinals, Bryan Broaddus said that Schottenheimer’s ego is getting in the way as he’s trying too hard to be something he’s not.
"Schotty called himself an elite play caller. And you know what I think Schotty's biggest issue is? I think Schotty wants to be compared to (Sean) McVay, and I think he wants to be compared to (Kyle) Shanahan, or Ben Johnson. I think he wants to be compared to those guys,” Broaddus said.
“And I think his ego doesn't allow him to just be Brian Schottenheimer. Just to go and call a game where it's for the best of what he's got on the field that day. I think his ego doesn't allow him to be that way. I think he wants to be recognized as McVay and all those top play callers right now. You know, (Liam) Coen. But you don't have the creativity of those guys. You don't have the way that they have – The forward thinking."
@BryanBroaddus says Schotty’s EGO is what’s holding him back @1053thefan @ZachWolchuk pic.twitter.com/REYLarNeFp
Broaddus also discussed how those elite play-callers he mentioned have plays ready to go for certain situations. He said they know what to do with a four-minute offense and how to move the ball when they need to, where as Schottenheimer falls flat when it’s time to rely on scheme and game management.
Nothing summarizes that better than an unbelievable stat shared by Bobby Belt of 105.3 The Fan. Belt pointed out that the Cowboys had 34 yards of offense on their final 27 plays. During that same span, Arizona had 267 yards on 31 plays.
Dallas gained 34 yards of offense on its final 27 plays from scrimmage. The Cardinals picked up 267 yards on its final 31 plays in that same time frame.
Schottenheimer had the better players, there’s no denying that. But even with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, and Javonte Williams, the Cowboys were unable to move the ball. Yet the Cardinals did whatever they wanted with Gardner Minshew, Michael Wilson, Trey McBride, and Tyler Allgeier.
That comes down to coaching and once again, the better coach won.

title: Checked Out George Pickens Wasted No Time Leaving Field After Cowboys' Week 8 Loss
full_text:
George Pickens looks like he's checked out after the Dallas Cowboys' Week 8 loss to the Arizona Cardinals .
Well, maybe we should say he was checked out before the Cowboys' Week 8 loss because Pickens appeared to be quite convinced that Arizona kicker Chad Ryland's game-winning field goal in overtime would go through before it actually did.
Thanks to video shared by FOX Sports via WFAA's Mike Leslie, Pickens was seen running through the tunnel and to the locker room just seconds after Ryland's field goal went through.
It would appear that Pickens had already made his way to the back while the ball was in the air, at the latest. He clearly had no desire for postgame handshakes.
How did he get there so fast? (via @MikeLeslieWFAA ) pic.twitter.com/gUZKSxzM5q
Pickens got there so fast, it's like he hopped in a time machine. If that doesn't show a player who is checked out, we don't know what does.
Pickens' early exit from the field came after a game in which he was targeted just four times and reeled in two catches for 48 yards. Pickens also played 42 snaps, which was fewer than CeeDee Lamb (56) and Ryan Flournoy (50).
The Cowboys wideout isn't having a terrible season, but he also isn't putting up the numbers he did in 2025, which isn't totally surprising because Lamb has stayed healthy.
Let's be realistic here: Dallas isn't going anywhere in 2026 and it's time to seriously consider trading Pickens at the deadline, when teams will be most desperate to add to their rosters.
There is just no future for Pickens in Dallas. We've been hit with another stark reminder that having two great receivers doesn't mean anything if a team can't play defense at a competent level, something the Cowboys have been incapable of all season.
Dallas cannot extend Pickens under any circumstances because of the hinderance that would have on the Cowboys' ability to improve the rest of the roster, and especially the defense.
The same rule applies with franchise-tagging Pickens in 2027, and there is also a good chance he won't fall in line with that again like he did this year, which could lead to a holdout.
Furthermore, we're seeing the relationship between Pickens and the Cowboys deteriorate in real time. It started with head coach Brian Schottenheimer calling Pickens out for his lackluster run blocking, and his rapid exit from the Week 8 game was another shining example of how things are moving in a bad direction.
The Cowboys could certainly use a replenishment of draft capital after trading away so much of it in recent years. Dallas is sitting with just 10 picks in the next two drafts, including only four in 2027.
Pickens can get the Cowboys at least one pick back, and maybe two if there is enough competition to acquire his services.
It's more worth it to do that than to hold on to him in what is looking like another lost season for the Cowboys.

title: Cowboys Injury Updates After Week 8 Loss: Joey Porter Jr., Jake Ferguson, Caleb Downs
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys saw three key players deal with injuries during the Week 8 loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday afternoon.
First, tight end Jake Ferguson suffered an ankle injury in the first quarter, and while he did get back into the game after that, Ferguson exited again later on and did not return.
On the defensive side of the ball, safety Caleb Downs suffered a concussion that forced his early exit and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was in and out of the game throughout with an ankle issue.
Here's what we know about all three players following the game on Sunday.
According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , Ferguson suffered a low-ankle sprain.
"Cowboys TE Jake Ferguson suffered a low ankle sprain Sunday in Arizona, per source," Fowler reported.
That's obviously better than the high-ankle variety, but Ferguson could still miss time depending on the severity. That's not an ideal situation for a Cowboys team that already has an injury at the position with Luke Schoonmaker, who didn't play in Week 8 .
James Mitchell replaced the injured Schoonmaker on Sunday and he now has a chance to see more action next week. If both players are ruled out, we could see highly-touted rookie Michael Trigg get his first game action of 2026.
We don't know the severity of Porter's ankle issue yet, but we do know it's something he has been battling since he joined the Cowboys.
Porter spoke on the injury after the game.
""It's been going on since I got here in the first game against Houston," he said . "It's very frustrating. Today, I just wasn't on a good leg. It's very frustrating to not be able to move how I want to."
Despite his ankle injury, Porter continues to be very effective in coverage after giving up just one reception on two targets for nine yards, per Pro Football Focus . He was limited to just 36 snaps.
There was no update on Downs' concussion after the game.
He'll now begin this coming week in the concussion protocol and that leaves his status up in the air for Week 9.
It goes without saying the Cowboys can ill-afford to lose a player who has been one of the best on the defense this season. If he doesn't play, we might see Cobie Durant in the slot next week.

title: How Broncos' Huge Win Over Chiefs Changed Their NFL Trade Deadline Outlook
full_text:
Jonah Coleman has been a revelation over the past two weeks.
But in the face of J.K. Dobbins's continued regression, has Coleman's emergence been enough to move the Denver Broncos away from trading for a running back ahead of the November 10 deadline?
That's the question. The Broncos are riding high after stunning the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday , erasing an 11-point fourth-quarter lead to win 28-24 at Mile High.
Coleman was a big part of that fourth-quarter resurgence , with some explosive running, a massive 51-yard catch-and-run, and the go-ahead touchdown. Dobbins was again relegated to the bench in the second half on the heels of his impotent 13 yards rushing on seven carries.
Obviously, the Broncos didn't expect Dobbins to be this slow in getting up to speed after recovering from the Lisfranc foot injury that ended his 2025 campaign in Week 10, or else they wouldn't have given him the two-year, $16 million deal he signed in March. If Denver had a crystal ball, it would have let him depart to Jacksonville and let his recovering be the Jaguars' problem.
Alas, nobody can see the future, but the past can often serve as a reliable predictor. After Dobbins was lost for the season, the Broncos' ground game was reduced to a rookie RJ Harvey late last year, complemented occasionally by a Jaleel McLaughlin or Tyler Badie carry.
Harvey was nowhere near up to the task of carrying a playoff team's run game, though he did have a few shining moments. Sitting at 6-2 now, with a half-game lead over the Chiefs in the AFC West, the Broncos have to decide whether they're willing to roll the dice on the possibility of Coleman being the only reliable playmaker in the backfield behind Bo Nix.
It doesn't appear that Dobbins is going to suddenly turn the ship around, despite his recent comments , and Harvey is on injured reserve for at least three more games, after suffering a knee injury during practice last week. Meanwhile, the trade deadline is a week away, and the Broncos have a full complement of 2027 draft picks.
Jonathan Taylor sure looks attractive , although the Indianapolis Colts have already received an offer of a second-round pick for the talented back. Taylor is the same age as Dobbins (almost 28), but he's rapidly approaching the 2,000-carry milestone, which is often when a running back will begin to decline, sometimes precipitously.
Taylor has 1,699 NFL carries, plus 208 receptions since entering the league in 2020. That's a lot of wear and tear on his tires. Unlike Dobbins, Taylor has managed to avoid major injury as a pro, but because of that, there's a lot of mileage on his odometer.
Taylor is also averaging a career-low 4.1 yards per carry and his explosive play rate has declined this season. Whether that's due to the Colts' offensive line or the vagaries of Father Time is anyone's guess, but those are the facts.
The good news is that, about the time Taylor hits the 2,000-carry milestone, his contract will be much closer to expiring, so that could offer the Broncos a bit more peace of mind. He's under contract for $15 million in 2027 and $9.6 million in 2028, so he's not overly expensive — it's more about the draft capital the Colts will want in exchange for him.
There are other backs the Broncos could consider, like Tennessee's Tony Pollard, who has just 15 fewer rush yards than Taylor's 610 yards this season, and would come at a fraction of the cost. Another option would be Breece Hall, whom the New York Jets are obviously protecting ahead of the deadline, holding him out of Sunday's game.
Hall is having a terrible season, having appeared in only three games, with 163 rushing yards and a touchdown on 51 carries (3.2 avg.). Perhaps a change of scenery could do him wonders, but he has an injury history and ball security issues, at times.
The Broncos have been linked to Hall in the recent past , so it's possible they could reach out to the Jets and talk to GM Darren Mougey, who served as GM George Paton's top lieutenant for years. Who knows? Perhaps Mougey would cut Paton a deal for Hall.
I held out hope that Dobbins would eventually snap out of his funk, and turn things around. I attributed his struggles to the brutality of Denver's inital schedule, but he's just not improving.
And when Coleman hits the field, and finds plenty of yards and plays to be had behind the same Broncos offensive line that was getting pilloried for not opening things up for Dobbins, it's much harder to give the veteran the benefit of the doubt. Perhaps the third major injury of Dobbins's NFL career was the straw that broke the camel's back and he may never return to form.
The Broncos are paying him moderately well to perform, though. And Sean Payton has nine more games to prepare for, and if the Broncos achieve their goal of winning the division, a playoff run to anticipate.
Denver will need a reliable ground attack to go the distance. Coleman has been an exciting revelation, but as a rookie, I'm not sure the Broncos would be wise to rely on him to carry the load when things get tough in late December and January.
Despite Coleman's huge day against the Chiefs, because Dobbins was so terrible yet again, the Broncos have to stay in the trade conversations taking place across the league. Pollard or Hall could be an asset to the Broncos' ground attack, but Taylor would be an immediate difference-maker capable of elevating the offense to another level, especially with Coleman as part of a one-two punch.
Harvey will eventually return from IR, but he's more of a 'joker' receiving option than a ball carrier the Broncos could lean on. This team has Nix on a rookie contract for only two more seasons, so if there's a big move to be made to get the Broncos over the hump, now's the time to swing.
