title: Broncos Grades After 28-24 Win Over Chiefs: Bo Nix Returning to Pre-Injury Form
full_text:
The Denver Broncos now sit atop the AFC West with a 64% chance of winning the division after yet another fourth-quarter comeback victory, this time against the Kansas City Chiefs .
Had the Broncos lost this one, their chances of winning the division would have dropped to 30%, so this game was a must-win, even if Sean Payton stopped short of calling it that last week. His boldness and aggression against the Chiefs reflected the importance of the game, as the Broncos came out on top 28-24 and Payton earned the 200th victory of his career, reaching that impressive milestone the sixth-fastest in NFL history.
While the Broncos' defense allowed some explosive plays, the unit actually played well overall, and so did the offense, except in the third quarter. There were a lot of high grades this week, though a few players still ended up below the starting grade of 50.
With that said, let's dive into Week 8's player grades.
Bolles played a great game and didn't allow a single pressure. That makes three games this year where he hasn't given up any pressure, and makes him the only left tackle to have achieved that so far this year.
Bolles continues to play at an All-Pro level and was a key part of the Broncos' offensive line producing its best game by far, with the lowest-graded blocker being right guard Quinn Meinerz (64.4).
Surtain was back after missing a few weeks and was only targeted twice, allowing one catch for eight yards. He was a shutdown corner in the truest form.
Surtain also played a great game against the run and helped shut down a few attempts for minimal gains.
This was a solid game from Nix , though there were a lot of yards left on the field due to some serious ball placement issues. However, he wasn't afraid to push the ball, was quick and decisive with his throws, and didn't bail on a clean pocket.
Nix looks like he is getting back to his late-season form before his injury, which could push Denver back into the Super Bowl conversation.
Waddle didn't have a huge game with three catches for 39 yards, but his 35-yard reception was a big play for the offense. He also showed how much of a difference he makes even when he isn't being targeted, based on how the Chiefs were covering him.
There's a reason why Payton has plans for Waddle's role to continue growing as the season marches ahead.
Robinson has been excellent for Denver and picked up three pressures while doing great against the run. There is a good chance he becomes a quality starter in the future due to his explosive athleticism.
Teams try to pick on Moss, but the Chiefs mostly avoided him with four targets his way. He only allowed two catches for 10 yards, and he broke on one ball, forcing the receiver to break it up to avoid an interception. His tackling and run defense were sound as well.
Jones has continued to show his value as an interior pass rusher, but his run defense has been a question. He not only did well against the run this week, but his high grade was because of his run defense rather than his play as a pass rusher.
This was the first time Jones looked like he could be a starter or the fourth player on the unit, instead of the fifth or sixth.
Not only did Powers do well in the run game — he was great — and he held up well in pass protection. Powers didn't allow a single pressure against the Chiefs and put together one of the best games of his Broncos career, by far.
Whenever Adkins has been on the field, he's been consistent and reliable, both as a receiver and as a blocker. He's not a tell when he's on the field, thanks to his versatility, which the Broncos have exploited well this season.
The only question is why Adkins isn't seeing the field more, as he has been far and away the Broncos' best tight end.
With Talanoa Hufanga out again, the Broncos signed Rapp to the 53-man roster ahead of this game, using him and Devon Key to replace Hufanga. Alas, Rapp really struggled against the Chiefs and was at fault for more than one explosive play.
Strnad has been playing at a high level for most of the season, but the Chiefs had his number on a couple of big plays. On one such play, he got stiff-armed into the turf, while on another explosive run, he struggled to wrap up with good technique.
Bonitto struggled against the run and failed to generate much pressure (only two). He also got caught in a broken-coverage situation that resulted in a 73-yard touchdown by Emmett Johnson. It was a rough game all around for the pass rusher.
With two targets and zero catches, Engram had another quiet day. He has not lived up to expectations as the ‘joker’ tight end for Payton, and his blocking remains a liability. It's time to limit his snaps even more.
Mims's effort was once again questionable whenever the play wasn't designed to get him the ball, especially as a route-runner. Sure, he can generate explosives for the offense, as evidenced by his 14-yard run, but he needs to show consistent effort to get more utilization.
If Mims doesn't run every route with 100% effort, it eliminates a potential target from the passing equation, making it harder on Nix to move the chains.
Trautman's blocking wasn't all bad, but he only had two good blocks on 14 run-block snaps. Adkins only had 13 run-block snaps, but nine of his blocks were positively graded.
What saves Trautman’s grade was his one long catch, though it wasn't really a great play by him. Again, it's time to give Adkins an increased role, and it should be at Trautman's expense.

title: Film Room: How Broncos Erased 11-Point Deficit to Stun Chiefs
full_text:
Here we go again with the “Heart-Attack Horsies."
It’s inexplicable how the Denver Broncos win close games nearly every week, yet here we are. This team, led by quarterback Bo Nix , somehow pulls a rabbit out of its hat when the chips are down.
Once again, the Broncos erased an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit in miraculous fashion, beating the Kansas City Chiefs 28-24 . It took a pair of touchdown drives and a last-second sack to pull it off, but the Broncos are officially in first place in the division, once again.
Everyone says this isn’t a sustainable way to win football games, but the Broncos have won 15 consecutive one-score games. Eventually, it has to become the expectation that they’re going to pull it off.
This week was crazy, though. Let’s break down the fourth quarter by the offense in this week’s film room.
Jonah Coleman's vision is awesome on this play. Franklin is doing such a great job as a blocker, too. pic.twitter.com/kA3Wvx0J9N
The Broncos hadn't gotten the ground game rolling for most of the game. J.K. Dobbins was a non-factor in the second half , and the Broncos leaned into the explosiveness of Jonah Coleman when the game was on the line.
To open the Broncos' first scoring possession of the fourth quarter, Coleman showed off his vision on an inside zone run for 10 yards. Watch wide receiver Troy Franklin and tight end Adam Trautman at the point of attack.
Franklin has developed his blocking incredibly well over the course of the season. Denver slices him across the formation as a kick-out blocker on the cornerback, and he does a good job up front. Trautman, who actually gets run into by Coleman, digs out the linebacker at the second level and helps pave the way.
This is a great run by Coleman. There really isn’t a lot there to begin with because center Luke Wattenburg gets beaten at the line of scrimmage, forcing the rookie to cut it back to the outside. Once he hits Trautman in the back, he bounces it outside and buries his head to finish the run with good power.
Wattenburg gets dumped in Bo's lap, but he escapes and hits Sutton camped out in the zone on a stop route. pic.twitter.com/cyQZ7HoOqa
I wanted to highlight this play because it shows how much differently Nix is playing while throwing on the run.
Wattenburg loses immediately to the bull rush and gets dumped directly into Nix’s lap, making the quarterback roll to his right. The Chiefs are in zone coverage, and wide receiver Courtland Sutton sits down in the soft spot to pick up eight yards and keep the drive rolling.
This isn’t a spectacular play, but we haven’t seen this very much over the course of the season. Nix would escape pressure and roll to his right, but he wouldn’t keep his eyes downfield and would usually throw the ball away. Keeping the offense on track is critical when you’re down 11 points in the fourth quarter.
This is a ridiculous catch by Trautman. Watch Bo pull it back when he sees Dobbins is covered underneath. Bolton actually fell down, which allowed Trautman to make this catch. Tack on 15 for roughness at the end. pic.twitter.com/sfLT86S1tg
This play was absolutely insane for a handful of reasons. It was raining at this point in the game, further accentuating how insane this play is.
The Broncos are trying to take a shot on first down near midfield, but nothing is there. Nix gets antsy in the pocket and goes into creation mode.
Watch as Nix looks to Dobbins underneath on the checkdown. He has to eat the football because Dobbins has a defender draped all over him. Nix resets his feet and fires a dart to Trautman, who makes a ridiculous catch in front of Chiefs linebacker Nick Bolton — who slipped on the wet field — and scampers upfield for an explosive gain.
The fact that Nix held onto a wet football on the pump fake is nothing short of incredible. That easily could have been a fumble, but he kept the play alive and took a chance to hit Trautman in a tight window. Bolton could have broken that pass up if he didn’t fall.
The Broncos also got 15 yards added to the result of the play thanks to an unnecessary roughness penalty by Chiefs safety Alohi Gilman, setting the offense up in the red zone.
This is really cool. Denver scored 2 times in the flat. Watch Tranquill closely on the 2 point conversion. He crashes to the flat to cover Engram and leaves a massive window for Waddle on the crossing route. That was schemed up to perfection. pic.twitter.com/W7gi4BA2vF
A few plays later, on 4th-and-Goal, Nix hit tight end Nate Adkins for his second touchdown pass of the game, which was followed by a great play design for a two-point conversion to cut the deficit to three points.
I’m splicing the first touchdown of the game into this to show how they schemed the two-point conversion open, and how great a play call it was.
On the first touchdown, the Broncos run Franklin across the formation into a bunch formation. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle runs a quick out route to the flat, with Franklin and Sutton muddying up the defense at the release. We’ve seen this look before when Peyton Manning was in Denver, and it’s a great design to get an easy throw for points.
On the second touchdown, Adkins runs an arrow route to the flat from an attached wing alignment, and Sutton draws a pair of defenders upfield to open the flat.
Watch Chiefs linebacker Drue Tranquill closely on this play. He gets his eyes inside and bites on the play-action fake while Adkins sprints to the flat. Tranquill isn’t responsible for the flat on this play, but keep this in mind.
On the two-point conversion, Denver runs a 'sail' concept right in front of Tranquill, who dashes to the flat to cover tight end Evan Engram’s out route. That opened up a massive throwing window to Waddle, who finishes in the end zone for the second time.
Nix takes his time letting Waddle clear Bolton, and puts a good ball into his target's chest plate. This was a great way to take advantage of Tranquill’s aggressiveness in coverage.
Perfect play call against an overload blitz. Bolton gets caught inside and lets Coleman get a free release to the flat. Franklin doing yeoman's work as a blocker down field once again. pic.twitter.com/LvvuunTASh
After Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal, the Broncos are set up with great field position, plenty of time, and a pair of timeouts.
Sean Payton dials up a halfback “dash” play, running Coleman across the formation and into the opposite flat. Denver catches the Chiefs in an overload blitz to the left side, and Coleman gets a free release through the line of scrimmage, running wide open.
Bolton gets caught inside and doesn’t touch Coleman in the hole, then rushes upfield to try to pressure Nix. That simple mistake was all it took to break this play open.
Watch Franklin as a blocker downfield. He draws his defender across the field, then blasts Gilman into the boundary, opening a cutback lane for Coleman to gain more yards.
You don’t get explosive plays without receivers doing their jobs downfield, and this is the second week in a row where Franklin has done a fantastic job as a blocker on an explosive play.
Coleman's 2nd career TD. His vision is so freaking good. pic.twitter.com/wEcUD9TPcK
On the next play, the Broncos run wide zone inside the 5-yard line. Coleman’s vision on this play is incredible.
Left guard Ben Powers gets blown into the backfield at the point of attack, forcing Coleman to cut it back. Coleman puts his foot in the ground and gets north in a hurry, squeezing behind wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr., who does a good job at the second level to seal the lane to the end zone and help the Broncos take the lead.
You can watch these plays a hundred times, and it still won’t explain how the Broncos managed to turn it on so intensely when the game is on the line. They got some luck, some help from key penalties, great schemes and play designs, and cleaned up some execution errors.
But it doesn’t explain why . There’s something about this team that is supernatural. It’s Mile…

title: Why Sean Payton Expects Broncos WR Jaylen Waddle's Role to Expand
full_text:
Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle delivered his first official "Penguin" celebration during Sunday's comeback victory over the Kansas City Chiefs.
And there might be more where that came from.
Speaking Monday, Broncos head coach Sean Payton said he expects Waddle's role—and therefore his production—to continue to expand as the division-leading club enters the stretch run toward the postseason.
“Absolutely, let’s keep going," Payton said via conference call with reporters. "It’s something that’s going to be important for us. He’s dynamic, he’s quick. Each week as we gameplan, it was a little bit more challenging last week because Wednesday he didn’t go and there’s that uncertainty. We’re going to need his plays down the stretch.”
Indeed, Waddle entered the Week 8 contest as questionable with a chest injury he re-aggravated the game prior. The Broncos' top receiver looked no worse for wear, catching three of his team-high six targets for 39 yards and a touchdown, after which he hit the aforementioned move.
HE HIT THE PENGUIN DANCE pic.twitter.com/3mJ0u48DVl
Perhaps most notably, Waddle was featured prominently over the middle of the field, highlighted by a 35-yard snag on a rope from quarterback Bo Nix, who went 20-of-32 for 222 yards, two scores, and zero interceptions amid the 28-24 conquest — his NFL-leading 15th game-winning drive since 2024.
“It means a lot," Nix said in his postgame press conference. "That’s a big divisional win for us, obviously—one of our toughest opponents in the division, one of our rivals. They played us really well again, and we just responded this time. That’s just a good football team, and they’re going to give us their best every time, and so we just have to respond well.”
Sunday's game marked the seventh time this season that Waddle recorded at least five targets in a game. However, it was also the seventh time that he failed to eclipse 50 receiving yards; that lone occasion came in Week 2, when he hung 138 yards across 10 catches on the Jacksonville Jaguars.
For the Broncos' passing offense to take the next step — especially important in January and beyond — they must continue finding ways to get the ball in the hands of the threat for whom they surrendered a first-round pick to acquire.
Denver has one last matchup prior to its Week 10 bye, facing a hapless Carolina Panthers defense that just fired their defensive coordinator. If there's ever going to be a week for Waddle to replicate the success he had against Jacksonville, and for Payton to make good on his intentions, this is it.

title: Sean Payton Reveals Broncos Loved Two Other RBs in Draft Besides Jonah Coleman
full_text:
Jonah Coleman has arrived.
The Denver Broncos' rookie running back has only been active for four games this season. He's actually touched the ball in three of those contests and in each one, he's been a difference-maker.
In his second game since returning from injured reserve, Coleman posted a season-high 104 yards from scrimmage and scored the Broncos' go-ahead touchdown to vanquish the Kansas City Chiefs 28-24. Once again, the rookie out-earned J.K. Dobbins in snap share and touches.
Coleman has momentum, and the spark he has provided the Broncos' offense has been palpable. One play before his touchdown, late in the fourth quarter, the rookie caught a Bo Nix pass and rumbled 51 yards downfield to set the Broncos up on the 5-yard line.
JONAH COLEMAN DOWN TO THE 4 KCvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/nRd1e0xIhC
It was a huge, explosive play that electrified the Mile High faithful at Empower Field. Suffice it to say, Broncos Country loves its rookie running back.
On the other side of the field, Kansas City's rookie running back also had himself a day, totaling north of 100 scrimmage yards, almost all of which came as a receiver. Johnson scored a 73-yard touchdown on a play where Patrick Mahomes beat the Broncos' blitz, lofting the ball over everyone's heads and into the rookie's hands, who then turned on the jets and rumbled to the house.
With a running back like Kenneth Walker III at the top of the depth chart, Johnson doesn't get many carries, but the Chiefs find creative ways to utilize him. The Broncos met with Johnson as a prospect, but ultimately chose to draft Coleman about a round-and-a-half before Kansas City selected the former Nebraska star.
The Broncos' interest in Johnson during draft season was public, but Payton confirmed it after Sunday's game, complimenting the running back class in the 2026 draft.
“Yes, that’s right... Emmett was one [of the running backs Denver liked]," Payton said post-game. "We just didn’t like two [running backs], but we loved Emmett."
Payton said the Broncos also liked Indiana's Kaelon Black, whom the San Francisco 49ers drafted late in the third round.
"The 49ers drafted one (Black) that we really liked," Payton said. "We felt this was a good running back draft, and I’m not even talking about those guys that went early. The kid from Indiana (Black), the player that Kansas City took, all of those guys have good tape and [are] different type runners, right? Exciting backs that are going to play a long time in this league.”
For what it's worth, Coleman has rushed for 134 yards and two touchdowns in the four games he's been active, with nine receptions for 97 yards. Black has touched the ball in all seven of San Francisco's games, and with the 49ers on bye, he's sitting with 233 rushing yards and one touchdown, with three receptions for four yards.
Johnson has touched the ball in all seven of Kansas City's games, totaling 77 rushing yards, with 14 receptions for 237 yards and one touchdown. Coleman is on pace to obliterate the numbers of Black and Johnson, but both of those rookies are playing behind two of the best running backs in the NFL.
What's so exciting about what the future of Coleman's rookie campaign could hold is that he's become the de facto No. 1 running back in Denver. There's always the chance that Dobbins could wrest back the RB1 duties because Payton likes to ride the hot hand, but the arrow is pointing straight up for Coleman.
Coleman's football IQ and make-up are very unique for a rookie. Crediting his offensive line and teammates for helping to spur his big day and secure a tough win over the Chiefs is only the latest example of the intangible traits that drew the Broncos to him.
Coleman has already caught the clutch-time bug. He's been part of two big fourth-quarter comebacks and without his contributions in those games, including Sunday vs. the Chiefs, the Broncos don't come back to win.
From the locker room after the final gun, Coleman showed his appreciation to Broncos Country and talked about the team's mindset that head coach Sean Payton helped cultivate this past week.
“Coach [Payton] said it was going to be a fourth-quarter game and it’s hard to play at [Empower Field at] Mile High when they got the crowd rocking like how they [were]," Coleman said. "Broncos Country showed up today. It helped us get that win."
Of course, without the Broncos' defense stopping Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs from racing down the field and scoring a touchdown in the closing 1:48 of the game, this one would have shaken out differently. It was another complementary win for the now 6-2 Broncos, and Coleman was thrilled to contribute to it in such a big way .
"It was good to just go out there and punch in the game winner and rely on the defense and allow them to dominate like they’ve been doing all year," Coleman said.
The rookie garnered rave reviews from his head coach and veteran teammates, including Nix. Like Payton, Nix complimented Coleman's explosiveness, burst, and ability to create big plays for a Broncos offense that's — let's face it — still finding its way.
“Jonah played great, ran the ball really tough. He’s explosive when he gets the football," Nix said. "He runs hard, hard to tackle, very quick to the hole and through it. I thought he did a really good job of... He just made the plays that were there. He didn’t let the moment get too big."
The rookie was even doing his part to motivate his veteran teammates and keep their eye on the prize as the fourth quarter approached.
"I just got to give a shoutout to my O-line and my teammates for keeping the confidence up the whole game," Coleman said. "The game didn’t go our way the whole entire game until the fourth quarter. I went up to all the O-linemen and the receivers and the defense [saying],  ‘It’s going to be a four-quarter game,’ like Coach [Payton] said, just to remind them it’s not over. So when the fourth quarter hit, that’s when the spark just lit up in the whole team.”
With how well this kid is playing, it makes you wonder how serious the latest rumors are of Denver's interest in the running back market ahead of the NFL trade deadline, especially Jonathan Taylor in Indy. If the Broncos traded for a player like Taylor, Coleman would take a back seat, and it might affect his development.
For this reason and many others, when it comes to the rumors of Denver's interest in Taylor and other backs on the trade block, I'll believe a move when I see it. The NFL trade deadline is November 10, and the Broncos have one more game until then — a road trip next week to face the Carolina Panthers.

title: Broncos QB Bo Nix Makes NFL History in Week 8 Win Over Chiefs
full_text:
Despite trailing by 11 points in the fourth quarter... despite quarterbacking an offense that converted just 2-of-11 third-down attempts, Nix led the Denver Broncos to a massive 28-24 comeback victory over the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday that shifted the balance of power in the AFC West.
Few Broncos quarterbacks have been able to conjure Mile High Magic with the potency that Nix does. With each week that passes , another record falls, and it was no different in the Broncos' win over the Chiefs that gave them sole possession of first place in the AFC West.
In Sunday's win over the Chiefs, Nix completed his 15th game-winning drive and his 12th fourth-quarter comeback since entering the league in 2024. Both stats lead the NFL over that span.
Nix's 15 game-winning drives and 12 fourth-quarter comebacks are tied for the most by any quarterback in his first three seasons in NFL history. And if the best predictor of future outcomes is past outcomes, he's likely to get at least one more of each before this season is over, pulling into sole possession of those records.
Since Week 7, Nix's confidence has seemingly returned. The Broncos' offense was frustratingly inefficient at times against the Chiefs, but he totaled four explosive passing plays, all to different receivers.
Again, it wasn't always pretty, but Nix did a good job of walking the razor's edge of pushing the ball when there were opportunities while also avoiding turnovers. Against the Chiefs, he went 20-of-32 for 222 yards and two touchdowns.
Nix has been criticized as being too conservative this season, but he has begun to loosen up over the past two weeks. Despite the Broncos' offensive inconsistencies, they've been able to hang in games due to excellent, timely defensive play, and Nix's discretion as a passer.
This was Nix's fifth straight game without an interception. What makes it more impressive, though, is that he's attempted at least 20 passes in each of those games without being picked off.
Now, given how often he passes the ball horizontally or behind the line of scrimmage, we shouldn't be too surprised, but he has been pushing the ball downfield more over the past two weeks. Five straight games without a pick is tied for the second-longest streak in team history, and it's the longest since Case Keenum back in 2018.
Nix has now attempted 164 consecutive passes without being picked off. It's the sixth-longest streak in Broncos history, and it's the second time in his career he's recorded a passing streak of more than 160 straight attempts without an interception.
Overall, Nix is more than satisfied with the win, given how hard they are to come by in the NFL, especially against the Chiefs, but he knows there's plenty of room for improvement.
“I thought the first two quarters were pretty good," Nix said post-game. "We hung in there; we got three scoring drives. Then the third quarter, where we had three three-and-outs, we just didn’t do too well on first and second down. We had too many third downs."
The better the Broncos can start doing on first down, the more proficient they'll become on third down. As rookie running back Jonah Coleman continues to build momentum, perhaps that worm will soon turn; otherwise, it wouldn't be a shock to see the Broncos swing for the fences and trade for a running back — like Jonathan Taylor — they could rely on to create on his own on first and second down.
The most important thing was getting the win, though, especially with the magnitude of Sunday's stakes. The Broncos dethroned the Chiefs as AFC West champions last year, and they're now in the driver's seat when it comes to repeating.
“It means a lot," Nix said of the victory. "That’s a big divisional win for us, obviously—one of our toughest opponents in the division, one of our rivals. They played us really well again, and we just responded this time. That’s just a good football team, and they’re going to give us their best every time, and so we just have to respond well.”

title: Broncos Had Some Big Winners & Losers in 28-24 Victory Over Chiefs
full_text:
Sean Payton and Bo Nix are undefeated at home against the Kansas City Chiefs, after the Denver Broncos stormed back in the fourth quarter to vanquish their rival and avenge their Week 1 loss.
The Broncos were down 24-13 in the fourth quarter, but once again, they were able to conjure some Mile High Magic and prevail 28-24.
The 6-2 Broncos now take the lead in the AFC West, and their schedule opens up for the next several weeks. The Chiefs still have a couple of not-so-tough games coming out of Week 8, but then they’ll face the worst of their schedule.
The Broncos are poised to run away with the division and repeat as AFC West champions, if they can keep the pedal to the metal from here on out. There’s still a lot of football left to be played this season.
As we romp through the aftermath of this huge divisional victory, let’s break down the Broncos’ biggest winners and losers.
Once again, Nix didn’t play all that well through the first three quarters, but as is his way, he turned it on when it mattered most and came through with some big plays when the chips were down.
Nix fed his playmakers in the fourth quarter, and the Broncos galvanized around him, with several players contributing to this team’s fourth fourth-quarter comeback of the season. Fans can get frustrated with the conservative play and relative inconsistencies, but Nix has now won 20 of his last 23 games.
Does it matter how the sausage gets made, so long as it does? After Nix took some big steps forward last week against the Arizona Cardinals, he played with much-improved confidence against the Chiefs — rising to the occasion given the stakes — and delivered another signature win.
Nix finished 20-of-32 for 222 passing yards and two touchdowns. He also converted a two-point attempt with his arm, connecting with Jaylen Waddle, and rushed three times, though it was for just four yards.
Now that the Broncos are truly through the worst of their hellish first-half-of-the-season gauntlet, look for Nix to take his game to the next level. It’s time to start padding the stats along with the wins in the standings.
Comeback complete for Bo Nix and the @Broncos pic.twitter.com/C0Vc6UtMtW
After returning last week from injured reserve to ignite the Broncos’ ground attack , Coleman once again served as this offense’s spark plug. He didn’t have the most efficient day rushing against the Chiefs’ tough front seven, toting it nine times for 41 yards, but like his quarterback, the rookie saved his best play for when it mattered most.
In the fourth quarter, the Chiefs failed to extend their lead to six points with 2:36 left in the game when Harrison Butker missed a 53-yard field-goal attempt. On the ensuing play, Nix hit Coleman underneath, and the rookie turned on the jets, rumbling 51 yards to the Chiefs’ 5-yard line.
JONAH COLEMAN DOWN TO THE 4 KCvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/nRd1e0xIhC
Coleman punched it on the next play for the Broncos’ go-ahead touchdown. The rookie just gives the Broncos’ offense an element that J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey haven’t been able to provide.
Coleman’s burst is palpable, as are his want-to and intensity. Coach Payton is going to continue riding the hot hand.
Now, it wasn’t all great, as Coleman did get stuffed several times on the goal line on two different possessions that forced the Broncos to go for it on 4th-&-Goal, but they were the collective plays of the offense and the line, and Nix punched it in with his arm both times.
With the NFL trade deadline coming up on November 10, the Broncos don’t need to make a move for Jonathan Taylor . However, it would be nice to have another weapon in the backfield who can create on his own.
This was only the third game of Coleman’s career in which he touched the ball, and he’s just gaining a head of steam. For that reason and others, I have my doubts that Denver will make a move.
It’s obvious, given what I just wrote and what we all witnessed on Sunday, but Dobbins comes out of this game as a big loser. He said last week that he cares most about winning, but the Broncos signaled a lack of trust in him to make plays and move the chains against the Chiefs.
Dobbins finished with just seven carries for 13 yards, and although he was already being usurped by Coleman before it happened, we didn’t see the veteran much after his brutal eight-yard loss in the second quarter, where he ran backward and paid the price. That cost the Broncos, killing a drive.
With RJ Harvey out on injured reserve for at least the next three games, the Broncos are going to need Dobbins for their running back committee, but Coleman is clearly the guy Payton and company are now counting on to spark the offense. Dobbins simply hasn’t looked the same since returning from his season-ending foot injury last year.
So long as Dobbins can keep his cool and not cause problems as his snap and touch share erode in the face of Coleman’s rise, the Broncos could opt to hold onto the valuable draft capital required to land the likes of Taylor, even though they’ve been linked to him in the rumor mill. I’ll put it this way: I’ll believe a Taylor-to-Denver trade when I see it.
Surtain returned to the field for the first time since Week 4, and boy was it good to see him out there. He finished with eight tackles (seven solo), tied for the second-most on the team, and he defended four passes, allowing three completions for just 20 yards.
Surtain saved a touchdown with an absolutely beautiful diving pass break-up. It would have been nice to see him come away with the near-interception he was close to nabbing, but given that he hasn’t played football for a month, it was a strong return performance.
Outside of a couple of explosive completions to running back Emmett Johnson out of the backfield, the Chiefs’ passing offense was lackluster. Take away Johnson’s 119 receiving yards on three catches, and Patric Mahomes would have passed for just 193 yards.
I don’t know what it is or why, but Engram can’t seem to get on the same page with Nix. The veteran tight end was targeted three times on Sunday, but he was held without a catch.
Engram has kept a strong attitude, focused on all the winning he’s done since joining the Broncos last year, but he’s certainly disappointed with his lack of statistical production. The Broncos have involved him much more in the run game as a blocker, so he’s making his contributions, but the receiving stats aren’t there.
Usually, they’re not there for any other tight end, but against the Chiefs, Nix connected with Adam Trautman for a big 22-yard gain and Nate Adkins for a one-yard touchdown. That’s got to be tough for Engram, but hey, the Broncos won the game, and if he wants it to change, he’s got to step his game up.
Waddle played this game hurt. He’s dealt with a chest injury for several weeks and aggravated it last Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, but he was a trooper and dressed against the Chiefs .
Waddle was Nix’s most-targeted receiver once again, earning six. He caught three of them for 39 yards and a touchdown, the bulk of which came on a big 35-yard strike over the middle.
Bo Nix scrambles and finds Jaylen Waddle for 35 yards! KCvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/twsyio2RAC
Nix missed a wide-open Waddle in the third quarter, throwing the ball in the dirt at his feet, just a bit short. But Waddle saw plenty of action, scored a touchdown, and caught a two-point conversion.
Props to the veteran wideout for battling through a painful chest injury to help the Broncos knock the Chiefs down a peg or two and take the divisional lead.

title: 3 Wild Takeaways From Broncos' 28-24 Comeback Win Over Chiefs
full_text:
You simply cannot make this up.
In a thrilling game, the Denver Broncos outlasted the Kansas City Chiefs in the most improbable fashion. Down by 11 points to start the fourth quarter, Bo Nix and the Broncos' offense scored two touchdowns, and the defense came away with a massive sack of Patrick Mahomes on fourth down to seal a 28-24 victory and take sole possession of first place in the AFC West.
My heart is still pounding. My blood pressure is through the roof. And I still cannot believe what we just witnessed.
What did we learn, though? Let's break down this week's key takeaways.
It was frustrating in the second half. Denver's offense went three-and-out on three consecutive drives as the Chiefs started to pull away. But as quickly as the weather changed to start the fourth quarter, so did Bo and the offense.
Nix's performance in the fourth quarter over the course of his career has been nothing but magical. The throw he made to Adam Trautman on the first scoring drive in crunch time was absolutely insane.
This might be the second-best fourth-quarter comeback of Nix's career, behind only the 33-point display he had against the New York Giants last year. The stakes in this Broncos-Chiefs game meant so much more, making it one of the best finishes I have personally witnessed.
Nix finished the game 20-of-32 for 222 yards and a pair of 4th-&-Goal touchdown passes from the 1-yard line.
You may doubt the guy. But don't ever count him out.
The ending of that game was made even more insane due to a couple of explosive gains following the game-winning touchdown run by Jonah Coleman.
But those explosive gains weren't the only ones.
Chiefs rookie running back Emmett Johnson absolutely destroyed the Broncos on Sunday. He had a 73-yard touchdown catch and run on a blown coverage, as well as another 38-yard reception in the second quarter, where he slipped a Justin Strnad tackle.
Johnson was also responsible for the 44-yard kickoff return that set the Chiefs on the last drive of the game.
It wasn't just Johnson. Known Bronco assassin Travis Kelce had a 27-yard reception on the final drive as well.
Denver's defense did a much better job in the tackling department this week against Kenneth Walker III and company, but they nearly lost the game by allowing as many explosives as they did.
Overall, the Broncos' defensive performance was rather impressive. Kansas City finished with 399 total yards, but over 100 of those yards came on two Johnson explosives. The Chiefs only ran the ball for 90 yards as a team, which was a triumph given what they did to Denver in Week 1.
Rumors have been swirling about the Broncos looking to make a move at the running back position heading into the November 10 trade deadline, and it's not hard to see the shift in focus in the running back room as it stands.
Dobbins lost his starting job to Coleman, and it's blatantly obvious. Dobbins only ran the ball seven times for a paltry 13 yards and rarely saw the field in the second half.
Coleman out-carried Dobbins by four totes, looked more explosive in doing so, and the rookie's 51-yard reception to set up his second career rushing touchdown was incredible.
Given the remaining schedule and being in first place in the West, this is the time to make a move. Adding an explosive playmaker who can create for himself should be a key focus this week, and there are more than a few options on the table with Jonathan Taylor , Tony Pollard, and Breece Hall reportedly on the trade block.

title: Broncos vs. Chiefs: 5 Bold Predictions for AFC West Showdown
full_text:
In a day's time, the Denver Broncos could be sitting atop the AFC West . To do that, the Broncos have to beat the Kansas City Chiefs .
If my bold predictions this week are realized, pulling ahead of the Chiefs in the division race is a given. These predictions won't be easy, some more than others, but they're bold for a reason.
Let's grab the crystal ball and dive in.
Nix has only broken 200 yards passing three times this season, and he's thrown for two touchdowns in just one game. He's yet to break 200 yards and throw for more than one touchdown in a single game this season.
Nix gets over that hump against the Chiefs by pushing the ball and hitting some explosive plays . He gets picked off once, early in the game, but bounces back instead of retreating into his safe shell.
Coleman has only played in three games, but he only saw three snaps and no touches in one of them, so it's only really been two games. In both games, the Broncos' coaches trusted the rookie to run out the clock, finishing with 69 yards and 58 yards from scrimmage.
In Coleman's third game of real action, he continues his takeover of the top running back spot and breaks 100 yards from scrimmage.
Patrick Mahomes is currently the least-sacked quarterback in the NFL this season, with only seven. The Chiefs are surrendering the seventh-lowest pressure rate on Mahomes.
He's difficult to sack because of how he moves the pocket and escapes, and quickly gets rid of the ball. Now, Jacoby Brissett was hard to sack for the same reasons, and Denver walked out with three sacks, and his time to throw was faster than Mahomes.
However, at Mile High, Bonitto, Allen, and Roach combine for five sacks on Mahomes, keeping the streak alive.
In his first game back from injury, Surtain nets an interception. I'm not predicting he takes it to the house, but given how he plays, it's possible.
Surtain is due for an interception, and it comes in a huge game with the division lead at stake.
Vance Joseph should start every defensive meeting with 29.8%, as that was the Broncos' missed-tackle rate in the season opener at Arrowhead Stadium. The Broncos had eight players with at least two missed tackles, and both starting linebackers combined for nine.
Suffice it to say, the Broncos' tackling won't be that bad again. They vastly improve it with the home crowd at their back.

title: Potential Fallout of Broncos Placing RB RJ Harvey on Injured Reserve
full_text:
The curious case of Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey has reached its climax.
Harvey, who reportedly suffered a knee injury during Thursday's practice, has been placed on short-term injured reserve and will miss at least the next four games, the team announced Saturday .
The second-year back had already been ruled out for Week 8 against the Kansas CIty Chiefs.
In corresponding transactions, the Broncos promoted safety Taylor Rapp from the practice squad to the active roster, while also elevating running back Cody Schrader and offensive lineman Gavin Ortega from the taxi squad.
As mentioned, Harvey popped up on the injury report earlier this week with a knee issue; he was limited in practice on Thursday and did not practice Friday. The injury is not considered to be abnormally long-term or season-ending, though severe enough to warrant placement on IR.
Speaking Friday, Broncos head coach Sean Payton failed to disclose an update on Harvey's outlook, saying only, "No status now."
First, the obvious: this further thins out a running back room that previously lost RB Tyler Badie to short-term IR -- a room now presumably led by rookie Jonah Coleman, with fading veteran J.K. Dobbins also slated for a significant workload.
Coleman and Dobbins (and, to a much lesser extent, Schrader) must pick up the slack after Harvey rushed for 87 yards and a touchdown while ranking second on the team in receiving with 25 catches for 217 yards and another score across six games thus far.
“I think I’ve been a broken record just relative to a lot of things offensively and us improving," Payton said Wednesday concerning the run game. "There was obviously a step last week. We have to continue to build on it, different type [of] defense in this game. I think it’s shifting the focus to the technique of where these ends play, the type of front we see. It’s different than the last couple of games.”
Second, there were conspiracy-level theories floating around social media that Harvey wasn't really injured and instead was being kept healthy as part of a pending trade for Colts RB Jonathan Taylor. Those ... can be put to rest.
The Broncos continue to be linked to a blockbuster Taylor acquisition, though if Indianapolis insists on a back being included in the deal, they'll need to settle for Dobbins or Coleman, provided the latter is made available.

title: Three Linebackers Lions Could Trade For After Recent Injuries
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will have to navigate some injuries at the linebacker position.
Both Jack Campbell and Jimmy Rolder suffered significant injuries , which saps the team of its depth at the position. Rolder will miss the rest of the season, while Campbell's injury has had fewer updates as fans outpour their support after the scary moment that led to his exit from Sunday's game.
With the stretch run approaching and the NFL trade deadline one week from Tuesday, general manager Brad Holmes and company could see fit to add talent through a trade to the linebacker room.
Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez and Trevor Nowaske all have starting experience and will be looked at to contribute, but Amen Ogbongbemiga is the only other healthy option currently on the active roster. It should be noted that Detroit could also elevate veteran Joe Bachie to the active roster, as Bachie began the year on the active roster before being released and re-signed on the practice squad.
Here are three possible trade targets the Lions could look to add at the linebacker position.
Henley was an intriguing player coming out of the draft in 2023, and is now entering the final year of his rookie deal. A rangy athlete, Henley is a weakside linebacker who could help some of the Lions' issues in coverage.
He has three career interceptions, and has also flashed some pass-rush potential with five career sacks. With the Chargers now sitting at 0-7, Henley could be expendable as the team evaluates whether or not to extend him.
For Detroit , Henley fits an ideal mold and would give them another athletic option within their linebacking corps.
Gay is a veteran option who is in his second year with the Dolphins. He is a middle linebacker, so he would be slated to fill the role that Campbell's vacating at this point. He has been a reliable tackler up to this point, with a miniscule 8.7 missed tackle rate through his first six games.
The Lions could get an up-close look at the linebacker this week, as the Lions are set to travel to Miami to take on the Dolphins on Sunday. Miami is currently 1-6 under first-year coach Jeff Hafley, and Gay could be a player who nets them some valuable draft capital.
Like the previous two names, Barton is currently a leader on a struggling AFC team. The veteran is on his fourth NFL team in eight seasons, and has had at least 80 combined tackles in each of the last four campaigns.
Barton is another middle linebacker option, and has had a missed tackle rate under 10 percent in each of his NFL seasons. This year, the number is currently a touch higher at 10.8 percent through eight games, but solid performances would likely get that number back below double digits.
The Lions could use another veteran option amidst their linebacking corps after the injuries, and Barton fits that mold. He's another affordable option, and still has one year of control beyond this year.

title: Lions Sign Veteran LB Off Patriots Practice Squad: Will He Help?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are making an addition to their linebacking corps.
On Monday, reports indicated that the Lions will be signing linebacker K.J. Britt to their active roster off of the New England Patriots' practice squad. Britt, 27, is in his sixth NFL season and has played one game for the Patriots as an elevation this year.
NFL insider Adam Schefter was the first to report the news, and no corresponding move has been reported as of publication. The Lions could place one of their two injured linebackers on injured reserve to clear a spot on the 53-man roster.
This signing continues a trend that general manager Brad Holmes has developed in his tenure, which has been to seek out replacements for injuries on practice squads. Earlier this year, the Lions signed undrafted rookie safety Bishop Fitzgerald off the Pittsburgh Steelers' practice squad after Avonte Maddox suffered a season-ending injury.
Britt has appeared in 77 games with 16 starts throughout his career. He was drafted in the fifth-round of the 2021 NFL Draft by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and spent four years with the Buccaneers in a rotational role.
Last year, Britt inked a one-year pact with the Miami Dolphins and appeared in all 17 games. He was not retained by the Dolphins in the offseason, and competed for a roster spot with the Patriots during training camp before being cut and re-signed to the practice squad.
He was active for the Patriots against the Las Vegas Raiders on Oct. 11, but did not log a defensive snap while playing 14 special teams snaps.
In his career, Britt has recorded 162 combined tackles, four tackles for loss and a half-sack. He has logged 994 career defensive snaps in his six seasons, and 1,303 special teams snaps. He figures to be a rotational contributor for Detroit while also adding another option for their special teams units.
The Lions are looking to offset the losses of a pair of players who suffered injuries in their Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings. Jimmy Rolder, their rookie fourth-round pick out of Michigan, suffered a hamstring injury that is expected to end his season.
Meanwhile, defensive captain and All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell suffered what appeared to be a serious injury on the same play as Rolder. Campbell was immobilized and carted off the field in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game, and fans have shown an outpouring of support amidst updates from the organization.

title: Detroit Lions Injury Updates: Rolder, Reed, Mays, Wonnum, Branch
full_text:
The Detroit Lions came away from the game against the Minnesota Vikings with several players dealing with a myriad of injuries.
Head coach Dan Campbell, speaking to local reporters on Monday afternoon, provided a series of injury updates on key players that departed the Week 8 contest at Ford Field.
Unfortunately for rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder, an injury-plagued first NFL season has ended prematurely, as he suffered a hamstring injury against Minnesota.
The injury could potentially require surgery. The fourth-round pick was seen angrily hitting the ground prior to leaving the game in the second half.
Campbell expressed he will be meeting with general manager Brad Holmes to review all the potential options at the linebacker position, including the possibility of an external signing or move.
When asked, he expressed each linebacker has the capability of being the green dot captain, but the decision has yet to be made for the Dolphins game. Derrick Barnes was relaying the defensive signals when Jack Campbell left the game.
Defensive end D.J. Wonnum and Brian Branch are currently in concussion protocol.
Center Cade Mays is reportedly dealing with a low ankle sprain, cornerback D.J. Reed is battling a hip injury and running back Jacob Saylors is also dealing with a neck injury. Each are not expected to practice on Wednesday at the teams Allen Park Performance Center.
Detroit's sixth-year head man shared he saw Campbell at the hospital last evening, expressing, "It was good, it was positiv. Got to see his parents and talk to his wife. Everybody's in good spirits."
The scene was disturbing at Ford Field due to Campbell being carted off the field and not being able to give a thumbs up to supporters.
Campbell is among the most popular players in the locker room and among the coaching staff.
"I don't even know if I can put into words. You get voted captain, that says a ton," said Campbell. "He's a guy that's trustworthy, he's dependable. He'd give you the shirt off his back. He's just all heart, man. All effort and just an unbelievable person."

title: Update: Preliminary Indications Are Positive For Jack Campbell
full_text:
The Detroit Lions suffered a devastating injury loss Sunday in their win over the Minnesota Vikings, as linebacker Jack Campbell appeared to suffer a serious injury in the fourth quarter.
Campbell remained down on the Ford Field turf for several minutes while being worked on by medical personnel after a tackle attempt. Eventually, he was placed on a backboard and carted off the field. He was taken to a local hospital in Detroit for further evaluation, and remained hospitalized overnight.
The team released another brief statement on Monday afternoon.
"Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital. Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time."
Campbell's injury was a devastating blow for the defense, as he is a captain for the unit and a player that many within the organization look to as both a leader and a tone-setter. Campbell had an All-Pro season last year, and earned a four-year contract extension worth up to $81 million.
The injury caused a big reaction on Sunday, with many teammates voicing their support and well-wishes for the beloved Iowa product after the injury. Wide receiver Jameson Williams noted that the team felt extra motivation to defeat the Vikings after that moment.
"That was pretty hurtful. He's a captain of this team, he's a big leader to this team. We're praying for him a lot. It just motivated us a lot more," Williams said. "We got a third-down, fourth-down stop. After that, the crowd was into it, offense went to go score after that. I guess we just turned it up a notch for our brother. He goes out there and puts it on the line every single play for us. That's why he's got that C on his chest. We're praying for him, hoping everything goes okay and he gets better."
Williams had multiple big moments in Sunday's win, including the game-winning touchdown with under five minutes to go. He finished with four catches for 70 yards.
Detroit's linebacker room has already had to deal with multiple injuries, with Damone Clark suffering a season-ending injury in training camp and Devin White suffering a forearm injury that has sent him to injured reserve.
In addition to Campbell, rookie lineabcker Jimmy Rolder was injured on the same play and exited the game with a hamstring ailment.
Detroit also lost a number of other players to injury in Sunday's game, with Brian Branch, DJ Wonnum, D.J. Reed, Cade Mays and Jacob Saylors all departing due to different injuries.

title: Grades: Battered Lions Outlast Vikings Defense, Earn Gritty Win
full_text:
The Detroit Lions made a major statement on Sunday, handing the Minnesota Vikings their first loss of the season with a 19-15 triumph at Ford Field.
Detroit bounced back from a number of significant injuries to their players and made just enough plays to emerge victorious. They now trail the Vikings by one game in the NFC North standings, and will hold the head-to-head tiebreaker ahead of their return showdown in Minnesota in December.
Here are grades for each position group based on performance in Sunday's game.
The Lions knew the challenge the Vikings' defense presented, and had some unique looks to help Jared Goff navigate some of the challenges. Goff had an early interception when Jameson Williams slipped out of his break, which was his first pick of the season.
He also had some struggles fending off sacks, as his lack of mobility led to him being sacked four times in the team's first five series. However, he began to get more comfortable after halftime and helped pilot the offense to the win.
Goff threw the game-winning touchdown pass to Jameson Williams on a crossing route in the fourth-quarter, and sealed the win with a quarterback sneak for a first down on the final drive.
The Lions have to be pleased with the development of their run game against one of the league's best run defenses. Jahmyr Gibbs had 153 rushing yards, while Sione Vaki chipped in 65 rushing yards on 11 carries.
Detroit got multiple timely runs from Gibbs, but none was bigger than when he squirted out from tacklers and tip-toed into the end zone for a 30-yard score.
Gibbs' workload has been a big topic of conversation, as he entered Sunday's game on track for almost 500 touches over the course of the regular season. With Vaki's performance, he can quiet some of those worries as he proved he can handle the workload to give Gibbs a breather.
Offensive coordinator Drew Petzing rode the run game in the second half, and both Gibbs and Vaki delivered.
Early on, the Lions had some issues as both Jameson Williams and Amon-Ra St. Brown both drew taunting penalties. St. Brown had one on the team's first series, while Williams got his after a 46-yard catch.
Williams had four catches for 70 yards, while St. Brown had seven catches for 46 yards. The latter had a touchdown negated, as it was overturned after he appeared to lose the ball while going to the ground. Meanwhile Williams hauled in the game-winner with under five minutes to play.
Detroit did not target Isaac TeSlaa in the game, but utilized him plenty as a blocker throughout the clash.
Sam LaPorta caught three passes for 33 yards, and also notched a rushing attempt on the team's final drive. He was responsible for a big block on Gibbs' touchdown run as well, while he did fail to pick up a blitzing Andrew Van Ginkel on his first sack of the game.
The tight end group struggled at times to pick up Van Ginkel as well as Minnesota's other blitzing linebackers, as Tyler Conklin was also plainly beat for a sack by Van Ginkel. Conklin did have one catch for seven yards.
All-Pro Penei Sewell was whistled for a whopping four penalties in Sunday's game, including what appeared to be a phantom false start as part of two straight pre-snap penalties. Sewell was also penalized for holding twice.
As previously mentioned, the Lions struggled early with the Vikings' array of blitzes leading to four sacks in five drives. However, the group came alive in the second half with the run game setting the tone.
Cade Mays went down with an ankle injury and was replaced by Juice Scruggs, who continued his trend of playing well at the center spot.
Detroit put consistent heat on the Vikings and quarterback Kyler Murray throughout the game. Skyler Gill-Howard got his first career solo sack late in the first half, and Alim McNeill would add to that tally with a sack in the third quarter.
Aidan Hutchinson had multiple pressures throughout the game, including one that led to a big hit on Murray and an incompletion to force a turnover on downs in the fourth quarter. Hutchinson also had a tackle for loss.
DJ Wonnum suffered a head injury in the second quarter after a collision with Brian Branch, and both players left the game.
Early on, the Lions' linebackers were caught in play-action as Kyler Murray hit Ben Yurosek on the first play of the game for a big gain. Tight end T.J. Hockenson gave the Lions plenty of fits, catching four passes for 58 yards and a touchdown.
The Lions' linebacking corps will be tested moving forward. Jack Campbell suffered what appeared to be a significant injury in the fourth quarter and was carted off and taken to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury.
On the same play, Jimmy Rolder also suffered an injury and left the game. Rolder was having the best game of his career, with five tackles, two tackles for loss and his first career sack.
Amidst all the injuries, the Lions were forced to adjust and distribute their snaps as Malcolm Rodriguez, Trevor Nowaske and Amen Ogbongbemiga all had to contribute.
Justin Jefferson presented a significant challenge for the Lions, and to their credit the secondary handled business well. D.J. Reed notched his first interception of the season in the second quarter, with the diving play serving as a big momentum-changing sequence.
Jefferson did have an incredible one-handed catch for a score in the first half, but was held in check for the most part to the tune of five catches for 33 yards. Roger McCreary was the one in coverage on the play, as it was the second of a tough back-to-back stretch after he missed what would've been a tackle for loss on Aaron Jones.
Reed and Branch both exited the game, which could have a lingering impact on the secondary moving forward.
Jake Bates missed a field goal for the first time this season, as his third attempt of the day doinked off the left upright. Bates had makes from 25 and 37 yards out earlier in the game. Punter Jack Fox averaged 46.5 yards on his four punt attempts.
The Lions didn't get much out of the return game, though Jacob Saylors narrowly avoided disaster after muffing a kickoff return.
Both coordinators did a solid job in Sunday's win. Kelvin Sheppard varied the pressures on Kyler Murray, and was able to find a way to scheme defenders into the backfield throughout the afternoon. It's also the third-straight game where the secondary has looked improved.
Offensively, Drew Petzing had his work cut out for him against one of the NFL's best defensive minds in Brian Flores. However, he had plenty of unique formations and looks for the Vikings to digest, including a wild throw to Amon-Ra St. Brown where the receiver lined up nearly 20 yards in the backfield.
Ultimately, Petzing was able to find ways to get the run game going in the second half, which sparked the offense into their second-half scoring drives.
Now, the Lions have an interesting stretch coming up starting with Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins. If they can withstand the trip to Miami, they would enter another big showdown with the New England Patriots in Munich at 6-2.
After proving themselves with back-to-back divisional wins, the Lions now have to prove they can avoid a let-down against a pair of AFC East foes.

title: Lions Provide Jack Campbell Update After Scary Injury
full_text:
The Detroit Lions earned a bittersweet win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, moving their record to 5-2 on the young season.
While it was big for the team to earn a win over a previously unbeaten division rival, many of the players' thoughts after the game were not with the magnitude of the victory but rather the demoralizing injury to linebacker Jack Campbell.
A defensive captain in his fourth season with the team, Campbell is one of the group's biggest leaders. On Sunday, he left the game after suffering a serious injury . He was worked on for several minutes without moving on the Ford Field turf before being placed on a backboard and carted off the field.
Campbell was transported to a local hospital and evaluated for a neck injury. The latest updated was provided late Sunday evening by the organization.
"Jack Campbell is resting and will remain in a local hospital tonight, for continued evaluation and monitoring," a statement from the team read. "The team will provide further updates as we have them."
The injury to the linebacker preceded a massive fourth-down in Sunday's game. On the first snap out of the injury break, defensive end Aidan Hutchinson led the charge in pressuring Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray into an incomplete pass.
Hutchinson was observed bringing his teammates together on the game's TV broadcast, and appeared to share words of motivation for his teammates before the key fourth-down stop.
"I was just, man, it was just a lot of emotions. I got a good rush on that fourth-down. I mean, we're in the huddle, we were more united than we've ever been before that play," Hutchinson said in a postgame interview with Brad Galli. "You go out, and it's a weird dynamic between football being a game and then you snap out of it to see a dude getting carted off and then you're right back in it. Riding that roller coaster, it's a little foreign for sure."
Campbell signed a four-year contract extension that will keep him in Detroit for the foreseeable future  this offseason after an All-Pro season last year. A first-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, Campbell has asserted himself as one of the team's biggest defensive stars.
He was one of several players to depart Sunday's game with an injury, as the group also included DJ Wonnum (Concussion protocol), Brian Branch (Concussion protocol), Cade Mays (ankle), D.J. Reed (hip) and linebacker Jimmy Rolder (hamstring).
Detroit continues its season with a trip to Miami to take on the Dolphins next week, followed by a trip to Munich, Germany to play the New England Patriots.

title: 6 Winners, 3 Losers From Lions Win Over Vikings
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions squared off in their second straight divisional contest, taking on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings.
The Lions faced early issues with discipline and blocking, allowing three sacks alongside two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties in the first quarter alone.
The Lions wore down the Vikings, with the run game taking over the second half and bleeding the clock out to win 19-15.
Here are the winners and losers from the contest.
Reed started the day as a player with a tough assignment , but built on his solid outing against Green Bay with another strong showing against the Vikings.
Reed was whistled for a defensive pass interference on the day, but got the last laugh in the first half by intercepting Kyler Murray.
Unfortunately, his solid stretch came to a screeching halt with a third quarter injury.
Anytime there is a mobile quarterback in the backfield, there is extra stress on the defense. Sure enough, Murray had the capability to escape pressure, and the Lions found themself allowing scrambles.
Gill-Howard was able to net his first full sack of the season, showcasing his speed, something that he has been flashing since the preseason. Gill-Howard’s sack was the sole Lions’ sack of the first half.
Rolder finally got more time on the field Sunday, and he immediately made the most of it with a sack on Kyler Murray on third down, forcing a punt.
That sack came at a crucial time after Jake Bates missed a go-ahead field goal attempt off the upright. Any momentum was destroyed with a two-sack effort on the drive by the defense.
It was a slow start for Gibbs, as was the case for most of the Lions offense. The back was a focal point of the Vikings defense, forcing many of his runs parallel to the line of scrimmage with no running room.
However, in the second half, Gibbs and the Lions came alive, with the back accounting for 53 rushing yards in the first two drives of the third quarter alone. Both put the Lions in scoring position, with one missed field goal followed by Gibbs taking one in for 30 yards. His two-point conversion did not get through the Vikings line, however.
In his first rush of the fourth quarter, Gibbs had a 17-yard burst, making it another 100-yard game.
Gibbs was not the only back making the Vikings pay, as Sione Vaki flexed his muscle in the second half as the Lions run game dominated.
Vaki put together multiple crucial runs, including a pair of 10-or-more yard gains to finish with 65 yards on the day, alongside 5 yards receiving.
McNeill continues to showcase his 2024 form, adding another sack from the middle of the defensive line.
It was a statement game from the defensive line with star Aidan Hutchinson held in check and DJ Wonnum getting carted off in the first half. The interior stood strong and held the Vikings to 81 yards on 18 carries, too.
Anytime the starting assignment opposite a corner is Justin Jefferson, it is a rough outing. On Sunday, McCreary was among the corners facing off with Jefferson, and the corner got bested by the wideout for the Vikings’ opening touchdown.
To be fair to the corner, it was a spectacular catch deflected by Jefferson to himself. That said, the rest of his body of work does not make up for the day he had.
In a surprise twist Penei Sewell finds himself among the losers on the day after an outing that is one to forget. The Vikings pass rush had a prolific day, with early sacks and Andrew Van Ginkel disrupting Detroit at any moment.
Sewell in particular finds himself on the losers bracket after a series with back-to-back false starts securing him a spot in the negatives this week. Sewell was not done for the day on the penalty sheet, being whistled twice more including a holding in the second half.
St. Brown was held in check on Sunday, with only 46 yards on 7 catches, along with a rush for 10 yards.
The receiver could not get separation and it helped make Sunday’s contest into a close one that needed the run game to carry the slack from the passing. St. Brown’s 56 total yards look even worse when a 15-yard first quarter taunting is factored in.
Sports writer since 2022. Emmett Matasovsky started covering the Detroit Lions in 2025. He has extensive experience covering Michigan State Spartans athletics, including MSU basketball and football. Has demonstrated passionate, in-depth coverage of college athletics.

title: Dan Campbell: No New Update on Jack Campbell’s Neck Injury
full_text:
The Lions had a rough day on the injury front Sunday against the Vikings, losing multiple players to physical ailments.
Center Cade Mays, in just his second game of the season, exited the NFC North divisional clash early with an ankle injury. Backup Juice Scruggs, who started the first five games of the season for Detroit, replaced Mays for the remainder of the game.
In addition, DJ Wonnum and Brian Branch collided on a tackle attempt of Vikings wideout Justin Jefferson with 2:57 remaining in the opening half. Wonnum was carted off the field following the collision and failed to return to the game.
Just like Wonnum, Branch did not play another snap following the injury, as he was ruled out for the second half with a concussion. In Branch's absence, rookie Keith Abney II received a healthy dose of reps at safety.
On Sunday, Branch was suiting up for just his second game of the 2026 campaign. In his season debut against the Packers the previous week, he secured an interception on a Jordan Love pass intended for receiver Christian Watson. Plus, he recorded the highest Pro Football Focus overall grade of any Lions defender for the week.
That wasn't the last of the injuries for Dan Campbell's team on Sunday, either.
On the opening play of the fourth quarter, Pro Bowl linebacker Jack Campbell fell straight to the Ford Field turf on a tackle attempt of Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson. Campbell laid motionless on the field for several minutes after the injury, and needed the assistance of multiple medical staff members prior to being loaded on a stretcher and carted off the field.
Per the Lions , the fourth-year linebacker was eventually transported to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury. In his postgame presser, Dan Campbell did not have any additional info regarding the status of the linebacker.
Linebacker Jimmy Rolder, a fourth-round pick of the organization this past April, also suffered an injury on the same play. It came just one down after Rolder dropped Minnesota running back Jordan Mason for a five-yard loss on a second-down run.
Then on the following defensive series, Detroit lost its No. 1 cornerback, D.J. Reed, to a hip injury. The Vikings ended up exploiting the Lions’ banged-up secondary during the series, with Kyler Murray connecting with Jordan Addison on a 51-yard bomb. And Minnesota capped off the possession with an 8-yard TD strike from Murray to Hockenson.
Altogether, the Lions lost five defensive players in the divisional affair.
Additionally, Jacob Saylors suffered a neck injury in the first half and sat out the rest of the Week 8 contest .

title: Key Takeaways From Detroit Lions 19-15 Victory Against Vikings
full_text:
The Detroit Lions were hoping this week to avoid allowing Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores to wreak havoc on the offense.
Entering Week 8, Detroit's division rival had the No. 1 scoring defense in the NFL.
"These offenses are cracking significantly," Dan Campbell said during the week leading up to the Vikings game. "Turnovers, massive turnovers so, it's third-and-32. And that's where they want you, way behind the sticks. So, poise is going to be big for us. Poise, patience. And then our defense has got to step up. We've done a hell of a job these last two weeks. We're going to have to continue to do that because they're problematic on offense as we know. (Kyler) Murray, they brought him in to be the captain of that ship over there, get them in the right play, be steady, reliable, facilitator of the football. And then he certainly still has all that mobility that he's had before.
"You can do everything right for a full game and then just like last week, it's a third-and-8 or whatever, he takes off and it's 30 yards and you're down on the four-yard line. So, he can extend plays, he can extend drives. He's very dangerous that way. (Justin Jefferson) 18, as we all know, is a massive factor. He's a hell of a receiver, highly competitive range, ball skills, it's tough, the whole thing. Nothing new there. I mean, he's just an outstanding football player. (T.J.) Hockenson, his uptick in production here and Murray has found him quite a bit. He's separating, getting open for him."
It was a tough game for the Lions health-wise, as numerous key defenders were injured and departed the contest, prior to the conclusion of the game.
After 60 minutes of action, the Lions advanced their record to 5-2, as they avenged two losses last year to a division rival.
Here are the main takeaways from the Lions' 19-15 win at Ford Field.
After the Lions won the toss and elected to defer, Kelvin Sheppard's defense held firm on the Vikings opening drive.
Will Reichard missed a 57-yard field goal, keeping the game scoreless.
Detroit was able to gain a little momentum on their opening drive , but a taunting call on wideout Amon-Ra St. Brown derailed the drive.
On 3rd-and-13, the Vikings dialed up the pressure and sacked quarterback Jared Goff.
The third-down blitz design dialed up by Brian Flores featured an eight-man that had Jahmyr Gibbs being taken away from a late dropper, Sam LaPorta and Sione Vaki found themselves blocking the same Vikings defender, causing the breakdown and a sack.
Early in the game, the Vikings were quickly able to record three sacks on Goff.
Detroit opened the scoring on their second-drive, as Jake Bates connected on a 25-year-yard field goal.
Detroit landed on the scoreboard first. Jameson Williams was also called for taunting after a 46-yard reception from Goff.
St. Brown secured a 24-yard reception that appeared to be a touchdown, but a review overturned the call, forcing the Lions to settle for a Jake Bates 25-yard field goal.
The former fourth-down pick quickly left the game and headed to the locker room, but was back on the sideline prior to Detroit's next offensive possession.
The Vikings were able to answer quickly, as Kyler Murray led the Vikings on a seven-play, 74-yard scoring drive that took just under three minutes.
On Detroit's next offensive possession, Williams unfortunately slipped, resulting in the veteran signal-caller tossing his first interception of the 2026 season. Vikings cornerback James Pierre was the beneficiary of the first-half gift.
The former No. 1 overall pick did not throw an interception in his previous 231 tosses to start the season. Detroit's defense held the Vikings to a three-and-out.
D.J. Reed picks off Kyler Murray! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/pfHjURqCbO
After entering the game with the roster fully healthy, the injury bug came for the Lions in the second quarter. Center Cade Mays (ankle), safety Brian Branch (concussion protocol) and defensive end DJ Wonnum (concussion protocol) all exited throughout the quarter.
Wonnum was eventually ruled out for the game at halftime.
The Lions were able to shift some of the momentum working against them, however. Cornerback D.J. Reed pulled in a diving interception with under two minutes to play, giving him nine career interceptions with three coming with the Lions.
Detroit was able to overcome a holding penalty against Penei Sewell to drive into Minnesota territory and cut their deficit to 7-6 at halftime thanks to a 37-yard field goal by Jake Bates.
A scary scene occurred early in the fourth-quarter, as linebacker Jack Campbell was carted off the field after a scary collision with Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson.
In a defensive battle, the third-quarter also saw both teams struggling to move the football.
Following a missed field goal, the Vikings were not able to capitalize. Rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder earned his first career sack, as Detroit's defense continuously pressured Murray.
On Detroit's next possession, Gibbs was able to scamper to the end zone on a 30-yard run, evading multiple Vikings' defenders.
Unfortunately, the two-point attempt was chaotic and unsuccessful. Gibbs was celebrating on the sideline, but was the intended target on a poorly designed pitch play. After the failed attempt, the Lions took a 12-7 lead in the third-quarter.
Mr. Jahmyr Gibbs pic.twitter.com/48QhRTUVaL
In the fourth-quarter and trailing 15-12, Sione Vaki was able to secure valuable rushing yards in relief of Gibbs.
The inexperienced running back secured 11 rushing attempts for 65 yards (5.9 yards per rush) against a  staunch Vikings' defense.
Goff led the Lions on a seven-play, 69-yard scoring rive after the Vikings briefly took the lead on a Hockenson eight-yard touchdown reception.
Williams capped off the drive with a seven-yard touchdown toss.
1.) It was announced before the game Wu-Tang Clan would be the halftime performance during The Thanksgiving Day Classic this year.
2.) Kicker Jake Bates had his first missed field goal try of the season. Early in the third quarter, Bates missed from 46-yards out after directly hitting the upright.
3.) Rookie defensive lineman Skyler Gill-Howard recorded his first career solo NFL sack against the Vikings.

title: Detroit Lions LB Jack Campbell Carted Off After Scary Collision
full_text:
The Detroit Lions had a roster full of healthy players heading into their Week 8 game against the Minnesota Vikings. However, throughout the game things took a turn for the worst.
After losing four players to injuries in the first half, two more Detroit Lions exited the game early in the fourth quarter. Linebackers Jack Campbell and Jimmy Rolder collided while attempting to make a tackle, and both players remained on the turf.
At the time, the Lions led their division rival Vikings 12-7 early in the fourth quarter. Minnesota would score on their next drive to take a 15-12 lead.
Rolder was helped to the sideline, while Campbell remained down and was being worked on by a number of medical personnel. Medical staff worked on him for a lengthy period of time before he was eventually carted off the field. Lions PR reported that Campbell was being transported to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury.
Meanwhile, Rolder was ruled questionable to return with a hamstring injury. Cornerback D.J. Reed suffered an injury on the following play, and was ruled questionable to return with a hip injury.
Many players on both sides of the field appeared emotional upon Campbell being taken off the field, with defensive captain Aidan Hutchinson calling his teammates together and providing some words in a huddle.
Immediately following the injury, the Lions forced a turnover on downs as they hurried Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray into an incomplete pass on fourth-down. After getting the stop, the Lions' entire defensive unit huddled together on the sideline in support of their injured teammate.
Behind Campbell and Rolder, the Lions have Derrick Barnes, Trevor Nowaske, Malcolm Rodriguez and Amen Ogbongbemiga on the roster at linebacker.
Detroit lost safety Brian Branch (Concussion protocol), defensive end DJ Wonnum (Concussion protocol), center Cade Mays (ankle) and running back Jacob Saylors (neck) all to injuries in the first half of Sunday's game.
Branch and Wonnum both exited after a helmet-to-helmet collision in the second quarter, with Branch walking to the sideline and Wonnum needing to be carted off.
The Lions got off to a slow start in Sunday's game, trailing 7-6 at halftime with their only scoring being a pair of Jake Bates field goal. They did have a touchdown pass from Jared Goff to Amon-Ra St. Brown nullified due to St. Brown being unable to control the ball through landing on the ground.
In the second half, Detroit was able to retake the lead on a 30-yard touchdown run by running back Jahmyr Gibbs.
#Lions All-Pro LB Jack Campbell was carted off on a backboard after a very scary collision. Aidan Hutchinson was in tears and then rallied the team together. Tough to watch. pic.twitter.com/6XwoCuMj5C
