title: Texans' RB Trade Options to Watch With Saquon Barkley Off the Table
full_text:
The Houston Texans are less than two weeks away from the NFL trade deadline arriving. And one area of their roster that's been circled as a potential need for this team to address in the coming days is their running back spot.
However, don't expect that upgrade to come from Philadelphia Eagles star running back Saquon Barkley. According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network , Barkley is not expected to be moved anywhere in a deadline deal despite the Eagles' regular-season struggles.
For the Texans, it's a tough pill to swallow. For a team that ranks 29th in terms of total rushing yards and 29th in yards per rush on the season so far, adding a talent like Barkley into the backfield is a pretty immediate upgrade to those woes on the ground. Now, Houston is forced to pivot if they want to find better success on the ground.
However, there is still a good chunk of running back talent left up for grabs for the Texans to consider. If the front office want to make their second trade within the backfield of this calendar year following their move to land David Montgomery this offseason , they've got several guys to keep on their radar.
Let's take a look at five of the bigger names at running back who could be up for grabs in a trade this coming week that the Texans should keep in consideration.
He's still stuck on injured reserve right now with a lingering knee issue, but when James Conner is at his best, he can be one of the more consistent veteran runners in the league. And when factoring in the Cardinals' latest draft selection of Jeremiyah Love, a deal surrounding Conner makes even more sense as a possibility.
The biggest question mark surrounding Conner is his health. If he can be expected to play over the coming weeks, then there's no sense in any team investing a premium in his services. But he should still at least be on the radar of every running back-needy team.
We've at least got to make room for Jonathan Taylor on this list, who's undoubtably the biggest upgrade left out on the market at the running back position. However, there are some big question marks regarding the Texans' ability to go out and acquire him.
Not only did the Texans just part ways with a 2027 second-round pick in the form of their Marvin Harrison Jr. trade to take away a good chunk of their premier draft assets, but Houston's in the same AFC South division as the Colts. That makes a superstar acquisition of Taylor a whole lot harder to imagine.
One name at the running back position that could make a ton of sense for the Texans to look towards is Devin Singletary–– someone who just cashed in an overtime touchdown against Houston back in Week 7 , and could be a trade candidate to consider who adds up for both Houston and the New York Giants' perspective.
For the Texans, they've already had Singletary on their roster once before, and they know from their Week 7 loss that he's got more than enough juice left in the tank to help lift Houston's run game. For the Giants, he's in a crowded Giants run game that needs to find its identity, and maybe shipping him out could make those roles a bit more clear.
An interesting candidate to keep on the radar for the Texans: Tampa Bay running back Kenneth Gainwell, who was signed to their roster earlier this offseason as a potential running mate for Bucky Irving, but hasn't quite caught onto his new situation as expected.
Maybe a mid-season deal could be in play to get things back on track for Gainwell. And the Texans have both a need and a play style that could help him have a much more successful time in Houston: smaller, more of a gadget runner who can work well in the passing game, and be an interesting one-two punch with a similar back in Woody Marks.
Another name like Jonathan Taylor who has to be mentioned: Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard, who's also been in a fair share of trade rumors leading up to the deadline, and could cost a whole lot less than the Colts' star in the backfield.
Another problem from the Texans' perspective, though, is that Pollard is stuck on a division rival's roster. Even if Pollard isn't exactly a world-changer in the backfield, the Titans may have their reservations about sending him out to Houston and bolstering their roster as a result.

title: Texans' Biggest Need Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline Is Painfully Obvious
full_text:
The Houston Texans are less than two weeks away from the NFL trade deadline.
And for a 2-5 team looking to try and continue competing for a playoff spot as this Texans team is equipped to do, it might be in their best interest to go out and look around the trade market to see how they can improve this current squad.
But where could the Texans use help?
On paper, their defense should be much better than it is with the talent they have on hand. And offensively, Houston's already made a ton of moves over the past several months in an effort to try and get them to an above-average unit.
However, when taking a step back to look at what Houston's roster is currently working with , there's one area of this group that feels like a no-brainer to go out and attack at the trade deadline: and that's their running back position.
Yes, the Texans have already made a big swing to their running back room earlier this offseason when they went out to go and add David Montgomery .
But Montgomery hasn't performed up to the level that anyone in Houston would've hoped for the five games he's been on the field. And as of recently, he's been out for two-straight games due to a lingering groin injury.
That injury from Montgomery has slimmed down this Texans running back room immensely.
Outside of Woody Marks, Houston's primary contributors behind him in the backfield have been the likes of Jawhar Jordan (who's currently on the practice squad injured reserve) and Dare Ogunbowale, who still hasn't registered a carry so far this season.
So with Montgomery underperforming and Marks in need of some extra depth to help take some of the rushing workload off his shoulders, perhaps Houston would be best served to take their focus to the trade market and address that glaring need on their offense.
There's a few running backs around the NFL who have seen their names circulating in trade rumors.
Which for a running-back-needy Texans team is good news. But when looking at the situations that Houston could go out and make a call for, only a few might make sense for their particular case.
Of course, the Jonathan Taylor rumors are running rampant right now. But it's hard to really get your hopes up for such a move that, for the Texans, would be a deal made with their division rival, the Indianapolis Colts. For one of the franchise's best running backs to ever wear the uniform, that's a trade that looks to be wishful thinking.
The Indianapolis Colts now are open to trading star running back Jonathan Taylor, sources told @RapSheet and me. Multiple teams have reached out to Indianapolis, and those talks are said to be active and ongoing, according to sources. More on https://t.co/NcfwZLCjrb . pic.twitter.com/X2gYBnSFek
Tony Pollard is also seemingly in the mix as a deadline mover from the Tennessee Titans. And while it could be easier to expect the Titans to make a minor move like that with the Texans, divisional trades don't happen too often in this league. So Houston might need to look elsewhere.
A couple of names that make a whole lot more sense for Houston: Arizona Cardinals running back James Conner, who's been a trade candidate ever since the team went out to acquire Jeremiyah Love in this year's draft, and could add up for the Texans who just got done making a move involving Marvin Harrison Jr. with this same front office.
And, coincidentally, the second candidate to look towards is the guy that the Texans just got a front row seat to watch score a game-winning touchdown against them in Week 7: veteran runner Devin Singletary.
Singletary been a part of this Houston franchise once before, still has life in the tank based on what was seen last week in the Texans' deflating loss to the Giants, and would be a low-risk, potentially high-reward investment for this front office to pursue knowing their current weakness in the backfield.
Maybe the Texans decide to hold firm with their offense as is. But if there were one area to keep an eye on for Houston to reasonably upgrade in the coming days ahead of the deadline, running back makes a ton of sense to keep an eye on.

title: 7 Texans Trade Candidates to Watch Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is right around the corner; less than two weeks away.
Which means, for the Houston Texans, now becomes the perfect time to take a step back, look at this current roster, and see how this group could be tweaked or improved in order to bounce back from an ugly 2-5 start.
It also becomes time for the Texans to look at some talents on their roster and determine whether or not they should be considered long-term pieces of the puzzle. And if they aren't–– for whatever reason–– maybe putting them on the trade block could be a worthwhile decision.
And for these seven Texans players in particular, perhaps a mid-season trade could be within the best interest of both parties.
The Texans' wide receiver depth looks a whole lot different than it did at the start of the season when they traded for Kayshon Boutte , leading to a suspicion that Houston might not have him in their long-term plans after this season when factoring in his expiring deal.
Perhaps there's a case for the Texans to pivot on Boutte before even getting to the end of this season. The past two weeks have led to Boutte seeing his lowest snap totals of the season. And with guys like Marvin Harrison Jr. and Tank Dell due to eat into his snaps as an outside receiver, maybe it'd be best for Houston to punt on him now and cash in some value rather than later.
Another wideout in a similar boat as Boutte: he's in the last year of his respective contract, might not be a priority to re-sign this summer, and is in a wide receiver room where he might only continue to see his snaps taken away week by week.
The difference for Hutchinson is the fact that the Texans used him a ton within their offensive game plan last week. Between the last two weeks, Hutchinson has found his way onto the field for over 50% of Houston's offensive snaps for the week. So compared to Boutte, maybe he has a better chance of sticking around.
While the Texans had good intentions to bring in Wyatt Teller as a hopeful upgrade on their offensive line, he hasn't quite met the standard for what Houston has been looking for through the first half of the season. The only reps he's gotten as a starter since arriving is when Ed Ingram was out for two weeks thanks to a groin injury.
Maybe the Texans decide now is the right time to send Teller elsewhere. They could cash in some minor value for their offseason investment, and send out a veteran guard that might still have a chance to contribute better elsewhere.
Pretty much the exact same deal here for Smith. He was signed as hopeful starter on the Texans offensive line this offseason on his $20 million deal, but suffered a foot injury before the beginning of the season that derailed any momentum to beat out Trent Brown for his respective spot.
So maybe the Texans can go and find some value on the trade market for Smith, rather than make his $20 million investment look like a waste . And as a tackle, compared to a guard like Teller, there's a better chance that Houston's front office can strike on a bit better trade value here.
Jake Andrews is an underrated trade candidate to keep an eye on. While not the most flashy name on the offensive line, he was someone who proved to be a serviceable starter at center for Houston all throughout last year, yet saw his spot taken by Evan Brown to kick off the 2026 season, and has been left in the shadows ever since.
The return on an Andrews trade could be minimal, but maybe it helps sweeten their future pool of assets enough for the Texans' front office to ponder it.
Now, maybe the Texans don't want to send it in on David Montgomery this early. He's only played a quarter of the season with his new offense, and hasn't been able to bounce back from a poor start because of the groin injury he suffered in Week 5.
But Montgomery has certainly underperformed from where his initial expectations stood upon the Texans' trading a fourth-round pick for him. Maybe another team out there needs help in the backfield and feels that they can get a second wind out of the veteran running back that Houston hasn't been able to find. Mark this one down as unlikely, though.
Davis Mills is always going to be a name floating around in Texans trade rumors for as long as he's on the team––which is simply because of his status as a quality backup quarterback. If Houston sees a quarterback-needy team on the market, sending them a stopgap veteran like Mills could result in a nice return.
But there is a ton of value in having a strong backup being your QB1––even if that signal-caller is playing lights out like C.J. Stroud has so far this year. And when factoring in Mills' expired contract, a trade might become even more appealing.

title: Where Texans' Playoff Odds Stand at the Bye Week (There's Still Hope)
full_text:
The Houston Texans are heading into their Week 8 bye with a whole lot less optimism surrounding their chances to make the postseason compared to where things stood to start the year off.
Before the 2026 season started, many saw this Texans roster capable of not just winning the AFC South, but stacking up as one of the premier Super Bowl contenders around the NFL.
A dominant defense, a much-improved offense, and a quarterback-head coach duo that has made the playoffs each of their three seasons being paired with one another; there was lots to feel good about for this Texans unit.
However, fast forward to the middle point of the Texans' season, and things haven't quite panned out as well as they would have liked. Houston's 2-5, coming off one of their worst losses of the year against the New York Giants , and their chances of being one of the seven teams to claw into the postseason have dwindled pretty noticeably.
That's not to say their chances are totally dead in the water, though––especially knowing that this Texans team has been prone to make a late-season run just as recently as last season.
Honestly, when taking a peek at just where the Texans' playoff odds stack up after dropping five of their first seven games on the season, you might not believe that they're truly a 2-5 football team.
According to odds from FanDuel Sportsbook , the Texans are currently +200 to make the NFL playoffs, which, when stacking those chances up to the rest of the AFC, places them with the 10th-best odds within the conference to make a run to the postseason.
The only teams that the Texans rank ahead of? That's the Las Vegas Raiders (+560), Indianapolis Colts (+1500), New York Jets (+1600), LA Chargers (+3500), and a pair of teams that don't even have eligible odds to make the postseason: the Miami Dolphins and Tennessee Titans.
Of course, it's not exactly the most favorable company for the Texans to be included with. Those six teams with playoff odds below Houston have a combined record of 9-31. But there's certainly more reason to believe in a late-season run for this Houston roster than those aforementioned five.
For one, this Texans roster has more than enough talent on both sides of the ball. Houston has a total of six Pro Bowlers still onboard from last season that might've not played up to that level early on in the year––Kamari Lassiter, Azeez Al-Shaair––but has the resume to support that they can turn things around in the weeks ahead.
But on top of that, the Texans' successess in the second half of the NFL calendar have been well-documented ever since DeMeco Ryans took the reigns as head coach back in 2023.
From Week 9 onwards since 2023, Ryans has a collective record of 20-9, which reached its peak back when the Texans went on a nine-game winning streak to close out their previous 2025 campaign, and perhaps something similar could transpire in the coming weeks.
Through the next three games, Houston does have some winnable matchups on tap : a road trip to face the Chargers, a date against former Texans quarterback Deshaun Watson and the Browns, and a rematch against the Colts after their prior loss back in Week 3.
Perhaps another late-season run could be brewing for the Texans. However, there's no question that if Houston wants to make their fourth consecutive playoff berth, wins have to start piling up, and fast. Time will tell if they can.

title: Why Texans May Not Miss Jaylin Noel as Much as Expected
full_text:
The Houston Texans' latest injury to their roster is one that certainly stings.
Earlier this week, the Texans placed second-year wide receiver Jaylin Noel on injured reserve with a toe injury that's expected to sit him out for the remainder of the regular season .
Seeing any player go down with a season-ending injury is a tough pill to swallow, but that's especially so when losing out on a talent like Noel after the year he's put together. Noel has actually led Houston's offense in total receiving yards (331) and yards per reception (17.4) through their first seven games.
However, while losing Noel does take a hit to the Texans' overall offensive ceiling, it's certainly not time to panic as to how this passing attack is able to move forward.
In fact, the Texans might be able to stay afloat within their air attack pretty easily–– and that's because of the recent developments around their wide receiver position as a whole.
Sure, losing out on the explosiveness and playmaking ability that Noel provides is going to be hard to replace within the offense. He is the Texans' leading receiver on the year for a reason after all.
But the Texans' wide receiver room, which once was void of depth within the first few weeks of the regular season, has now turned a corner in a big way heading into their Week 8 bye.
That's because of the acquisition of not only Marvin Harrison Jr., who was brought in via trade after Houston's Week 5 win over the Tennessee Titans, but also the return of Tank Dell , who officially made his way back onto an NFL field for the first time in nearly two years this past weekend against the New York Giants.
Those two factoring into the mix are massive pieces of the puzzle for the Texans' offense. That pairing has a great chance to supplement that playmaking ability and depth that has since been lost at the position without Noel, which wasn't quite as available just a few games ago.
In Weeks 2 and 3, the Texans' leading contributors at wide receiver while Nico Collins was sidelined with a hamstring strain were none other than Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson. A little over a month later, now with Dell and Harrison Jr. as a part of the equation, Houston's fate at the position has taken a full 180.
The hurdle sitting between that playmaking really coming to fruition is for the Texans to find a way to get them on the field in longer stints. This past weekend against the Giants, the two failed to combine for more than 30 snaps on the offense , which is expected given their respective situations.
But that outcome could certainly change in a big way after the bye. Harrison Jr. will have another week of learning the Texans' playbook under his belt. Dell will be even more comfortable coming off of his knee injury and create a much more potent attack for Houston to lean on through the air.
When you add that pairing alongside an already bonafide top wideout like Nico Collins, there's more than enough reason to believe that the Texans' passing offense can stay steady, even without one of their most potent pass-catchers.
So of course, not having Noel on the field for the next two weeks is a noteworthy loss for the Texans, and takes away yet another high-potential receiver out of this offensive attack right next to his draft classmate in Jayden Higgins.
But if the Texans can continue to get Harrison Jr. and Dell involved in the game plan, and they hold up their end of the bargain, that'll be their best course of action in hopes that this offense can rebound moving forward. Time will tell if it'll come to fruition as expected.

title: 3 Concerning Texans Stats That Need to Improve After the Bye Week
full_text:
The Houston Texans are a 2-5 football team heading into their Week 8 bye .
Needless to be said, there's much work to be done heading into the second half of the season if the Texans want to get back on track for a similar late-season run like they put together around this time last year.
And to do that, the Texans have some clear flaws within their game plan and overall production to iron out; issues that can be clearly seen by looking at a select few stats in which Houston has not exceled in through their first seven games of the year, thus leadin to their roster looking like what it does now.
So with all of that in mind, let's take a look at three different stats from the Texans' pre-bye week slate that need to turn around in the right direction for the weeks ahead. Or else, it'll be really tough to picture Houston racking up the necessary wins for a surprise push to the postseason.
Now, to the Texans' credit, they've been able to run the ball a bit better over the past three weeks since Woody Marks has been leading the charge in the backfield .
Marks has been averaging 3.8 yards per carry over the past three weeks that David Montgomery has been sidelined with an average of over 80 yards from scrimmage throughout. He's been a big-time playmaker for this offense and a capable lead ball-carrier on the ground, while helping their run game lift from the depths they were previously at through the first quarter of the season.
However, even while Marks has been taking care of business on the ground, the Texans' offensive line could still serve to make some improvements from the level they're at now when factoring in a nearly 20% run stuffed rate.
For reference, only six other teams rank ahead of the Texans for run-stuffed rate. Over half of those teams have a record under .500, and that's a crowd that Houston currently falls right into.
If Houston wants to continue to progress on the offensive side of the ball, gaining more momentum on the ground and finding more positive runs is a critical step in the process.
The Texans' defensive turnovers as a whole have not been to the level that they were at throughout their dominance of 2025.
Through seven games of last season, Houston's defense had recorded a total of 11 turnovers, even with the early struggles they faced in the year. Seven games in 2026, Houston's total is nearly half that, with just six.
And a large part of that regression for the Texans' turnover numbers has surrounded their failure to attack the air for those giveaways.
Houston's only three interceptions on the year have been to backup linebacker Jake Hansen, along with safeties Calen Bullock and Reed Blankenship getting a pair of their own as well. As for the Texans' top two corners, Derek Stingley and Kamari Lassiter, they haven't seen any takeaways coming their way.
Simply put, the Texans need to take advantage of the turnover battle more than they have so far this season. And with a defense as talented as the one this roster has on paper–– especially within the secondary–– there's little excuse for Houston to have just three interceptions in seven weeks.
More often than not, teams who win the turnover battle can win a lot of football games. The Texans' offense has taken care of the ball extremely well, but now comes the time for the defense to hold up their end of the bargain.
An issue that really showed itself for the Texans in their latest game against the New York Giants : penalties.
Last week, Houston gave up 80 total yards for the eight penalties they accumulated throughout the day, which has turned into a common trend for this Houston roster to look both unorganized and undisciplined––especially on the line of scrimmage offensively.
The Texans are currently the third-highest number of total flags in the NFL behind only the Green Bay Packers and the Cleveland Browns, who each have 73. Houston is one of only two teams to have given up over 500 total yards on the season because of penalties.
When factoring in the flaws that the Texans have had on early downs running the ball, getting even further behind because of frequent penalty issues ends up setting this offense back even further. Penalties have to be cleaned up for Houston, and DeMeco Ryans knows it .
However, time will tell if the Texans are able to get this group of tight ends up in time to make a run for the second half of the season.

title: Should Texans Trade WR Nico Collins? Here's What It Would Cost
full_text:
The Houston Texans have seen a few big trades circle around them in the AFC South in recent days.
The Indianapolis Colts traded away Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner –– and there could be more pieces on the move sooner rather than later. The Tennessee Titans just moved off of their franchise cornerstone Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears in exchange for a haul of draft picks.
TRADE: Titans trading DT Jeffery Simmons to Bears. (via @AdamSchefter , @RapSheet ) pic.twitter.com/ZJnwnUtA9w
So naturally, as the trade deadline looms closer, the Texans could be another AFC South team to consider making a big shake-up to their roster. They already did make a move to add Marvin Harrison Jr. a few weeks ago, but maybe Houston opts to sell a piece or two off in the right circumstances.
And surprisingly, one name on the Texans' roster that's surfaced amongst some fans as a potential trade candidate to watch is star wide receiver Nico Collins, who's coming off his worst game of the season against the New York Giants where he hauled in just two of his five targets for six yards .
Collins is in a deep receiver room , hasn't been as involved in the game plan as he has been throughout the past three seasons with the Texans, and is due for a lucrative extension as soon as this offseason to cement his long-term future as a part of the franchise.
However, if the Texans wanted to be proactive on Collins' future, perhaps the front office could consider getting ahead of his situation by searching around the trade market for an appealing return. Wide receivers are a hot commodity, and Houston could certainly bring in a noteworthy package if they were to truly shop around.
So should the Texans even entertain a move to send out Collins? And if they do, what type of package could they get send their way? Let's break it all down:
There is reason to at least ponder a trade involving Collins from the Texans' perspective–– simply from a contractual perspective.
With the Texans' cost of the roster bound to get pricier over the next two seasons when factoring in the defensive talent and C.J. Stroud's pending extension, the cost to keep Collins around on a new deal might prove to be too much for Houston to pay out once the time comes .
So if the Texans simply wanted to cash in on Collins as an asset, perhaps now is the time to trade him if an extension wasn't in the cards next season.
However, what's also important to factor in is where the Texans stand as a franchise. They shouldn't be looking to recoup or build upon their pile of assets; this roster should be looking to do what they can to win games now.
Trading Nico Collins doesn't help the Texans get better. They're simply planning further for the future. And while there is value in keeping a forward-thinking mindset in any front office, shipping out a top 10 to 15 receiver in a year where Houston has invested a ton in this current core seems to be thinking too many steps ahead.
Over the next two years, this Texans roster might be equipped with the most talent they've had–– and will have–– in a while. Once Stroud gets his massive extension that could eclipse $60 million annually , it'll be much harder to build a roster with this type of talent on both sides of the ball.
If the Texans are truly committed to winning this season, trading Collins signals the opposite approach. And based on Houston's past offseason, and even their recent move to bring in Marvin Harrison Jr. for a second-round pick, this team is more equipped to be buyers on the market. Not sellers.
Now, to play devil's advocate for a moment, what might be an intriguing enough package to at least make the Texans really consider a move to ship out Collins?
The starting point for such a move feels like it'd have to be a first-round pick, and perhaps even more on top of it.
Just this offseason, we saw another similar star wideout on the move in the form of A.J. Brown being shipped to the New England Patriots in exchange for a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick.
Collins, being two years younger and just as productive as Brown, might be worth even more than that, and especially so given that the Texans don't exactly need to trade their star wideout unless a team offers a package they can't refuse.
So with that in mind, the Texans might need a future first-round pick, and maybe a third-round pick to play with the idea of sending Collins to another team via trade.
That still might not be enough to lead to Houston pulling the trigger, but such value seems pretty reasonable in the event a team had its eyes dead set on acquiring the two-time Pro Bowler.

title: Winners and Losers From Colts’ Demoralizing Week 8 Loss: Young Players Shine
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts had little go their way in Sunday's 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, extending their losing streak to four games.
While a handful of players managed to deliver encouraging performances, the afternoon exposed significant problems across the roster and raised further questions about the team's direction. With the trade deadline approaching, here's a look at the biggest winners and losers from Week 8.
The clear-cut biggest winner of them all. CJ Allen made his first NFL start in Jacksonville and did not disappoint.
Allen logged 10 tackles, a tackle for loss and a sack, leading the team in all three categories. The second-round pick h as had a slow start to his time in Indianapolis , being held back by numerous injuries, but now that he’s fully healthy, Allen provided a breath of fresh air to a linebacking corps that’s underwhelmed through eight games.
For a defense that has struggled to find consistency at linebacker, Allen's emergence is an encouraging development.
He showed an ability to make plays at multiple levels, contributing against both the run and the pass while providing the kind of physical presence the position group has been sorely missing. It's only one start, but Allen has given the coaching staff plenty of reason to take off the training wheels and let him go to work.
DJ Giddens didn’t enter the game until the fourth quarter. By then, any hope of a turnaround was gone. But still, Giddens made the most of his limited opportunities.
The second-year running back recorded 43 rushing yards on six carries, enough to finish as the Colts’ leading rusher. Giddens’ efficiency stands out (7.2 yards per carry). Although there is the caveat of Jacksonville playing several backups so late in the game, Giddens appears to have made significant progress compared to last year.
With a Jonathan Taylor trade feeling inevitable, Giddens and current backup Seth McGowan are the likely candidates to take over the Colts’ backfield. Giddens flashed just at the right time and should receive an extended look during the remaining games on the schedule.
The departure of DeForest Buckner in a trade back to San Francisco left a massive void on the Colts’ defensive interior. There’s no replacing Buckner, not this quickly, but Indianapolis’ defensive line gave us a pleasant surprise.
As a collective, the Colts pressured Jaguars’ quarterback Trevor Lawrence on 10 of his 19 dropbacks (52.6%), the best performance by the Indianapolis pass rush so far this season.
Individually, Jaylahn Tuimoloau recorded his first career sack and forced fumble. Rookie Caden Curry finished with seven tackles and a fumble recovery, second only to Allen. Laiatu Latu logged his first full sack of the season.
It’s unfortunate that Lawrence still sliced up the Colts’ back end, but the Colts certainly have pieces up front they can rely on moving forward.
Without a doubt, Shane Steichen entered Sunday’s game with his job on the line. Yet the urgency to find a way to win was nowhere to be found.
The Colts surrendered their largest point total of the season and scored the fewest they have all season. Steichen waited until the fourth quarter to make any lineup changes, reflecting that lack of urgency. Questions about player effort came about postgame, especially regarding Josh Downs’ apparent desire to get out of town.
There’s no sugarcoating it: Steichen has lost the locker room. And his job could be next .
Like Steichen, Daniel Jones was under pressure to perform against the Jaguars. His drop in performance from last year has contributed significantly to the Colts’ inability to find ways to win, and Sunday was just more evidence that Jones’ season is heading downhill quickly.
Jones finished 19-of-28 for 144 yards with a meaningless touchdown pass and two interceptions.
While it’s hard to put all the blame on Jones, given his receivers couldn’t separate, he had no run game or defense to lean on, and penalties set the offense back numerous times, Jones certainly didn’t present a strong case to remain the starter to finish out this season .
The Colts’ pass rush had their best game of the season, but it was ruined by a secondary that couldn’t hold up their end of the bargain. Trevor Lawrence carved up the Colts back end with scary efficiency, completing 10 of his 14 pass attempts for 210 yards and three touchdown passes.
It wasn’t just the pass defense that was poor, as $60 million safety Cam Bynum was bulldozed trying to make a tackle on Jacksonville running back Bhayshul Tuten on his way to scoring a touchdown.
Bhayshul Tuten rumbles in the rain for the Jaguars touchdown! 📺CBS & Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/vVs4FNf1Gp
Simply put, the Colts have invested too much in their secondary to receive such underwhelming results. Three of the top six paid players on the team are members of the secondary, yet the unit remains one of the weak spots on the roster.

title: It's Time for Colts to Give Anthony Richardson Sr. the Green Light
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts were destroyed and humiliated at EverBank Stadium on Sunday afternoon by the Jacksonville Jaguars, losing 42-7.
Running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs may dominate the news for the Colts amidst trade rumors, but the QB situation for Indianapolis can't be overlooked after this awful loss.
Daniel Jones has pulled a full 180 since looking better than ever last year; now, he looks arguably the worst he has ever looked through his eight NFL seasons.
Jones finished the game with 19/28 completions for 144 passing yards, two interceptions, and a garbage-time touchdown to Downs.
Jones also had one of his passes returned for a pick-six by Jaguars safety Rayuan Lane III in the second quarter.
RAYUAN LANE III PICK-SIX INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/bZN2FaLptY
Head coach Shane Steichen decided to sit Jones near the end of the game when all hope was lost. This gave Anthony Richardson Sr. a small chance to shine.
Richardson didn't dazzle, finishing with 2/2 completions for eight passing yards. He also tacked on four rushing yards.
It isn't much, and perhaps the Jaguars were playing some lax defense, but Richardson's mere presence was a breath of fresh air for Colts fans, and the offense.
Anthony Richardson Shows Off His Shiftiness And Then Finds Keenan Allen For The Colts First Down. Escaping Pressure And Still Delivering A Strike On The Move. Daniel Jones Can't Do This. 👀 pic.twitter.com/4VegTyJE6q
Given how Indianapolis is 2-6 and falling apart at the seams, it's very simple: it's time to bench Jones and roll with Richardson the rest of the way.
Through eight games, Jones has an eyesore of a stat line. Below are his metrics up to this point:
Jones has shown the heights of what he can do with this offense, and quite frankly, that ceiling is hardly higher than the floor, or even the basement.
There are two questions to pose to Steichen regarding Richardson: 'How can this get any worse than Jones?' and 'What else do you have to lose?'
It's hard to tell if Steichen will stay as Indy's head coach for the rest of the year, or if he'll be dismissed of his services following the worst performance of the Week 8 slate ahead of Monday Night Football.
Regardless, this offense has far more potential with Richardson running the show. Jones is more accurate, experienced, and has in-game rapport with the pass-catchers.
However, Richardson is a more capable runner, has better zip and arm strength, and forces defenses to consider much more due to how versatile of a QB he is.
Initially, my knee-jerk thought was that Jones has a higher football IQ than Richardson, but seeing how baffling Jones' decision-making has been this year, I'm not completely sold on that argument ringing true.
Steichen has stuck firmly to his desire to roll with Jones, but I think even he has to reconsider his approach.
Jones has held back the offense in brutal fashion, and it will only continue this way as the season drags on.
Richardson deserves one final shot in a completely lost campaign, and even Steichen has acknowledged that every position is open to evaluation, quarterback included.
#Colts HC Shane Steichen on the loss: “Flat out wasn’t good enough. Got out-played, got out-coached in all three phases. We got a lot to fix. I’ve been saying that for a while. …” On Daniel Jones as QB1: “I’m gonna evaluate everything. Every position going forward.” pic.twitter.com/YrHhJvn70T
The jury is still out on whether Taylor and Downs get traded, but that shouldn't change the fact that Indianapolis must switch things up at the field general spot.
The Colts have a battle ahead in Week 9 against the Dallas Cowboys (3-5) at Lucas Oil Stadium. This is the perfect opportunity to start Richardson against a Dallas defense that has struggled to stop any offense this year.
We'll see what Steichen and the Colts do at QB, but if they're smart, they'll make the call to let Richardson take the reins for the rest of the season.

title: CJ Allen Rises from Ashes to Meet Colts' Lofty Expectations with Rebuild Ahead
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts are 2-6 after losing their twelfth straight contest against the Jaguars in Jacksonville . Duval County has become a house of horrors for the Colts, but it pales in comparison to the scares that this regime has brought.
The Colts are staring down the barrel of a full-fledged organizational reset after firing longtime general manager Chris Ballard just six weeks into the 2026 regular season.
Indianapolis has kicked off its rebuild by trading away franchise cornerstones Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner , but they shouldn't stop there.
The Colts would be wise to shop all remaining trade assets , not only so they can gain as much valuable draft capital as possible going into their first season under new management, but also because it would open the door for young players to prove their worth.
Given that the season is all but lost, any player who is still on their rookie contract beyond this season should be provided the opportunity to prove they're worth keeping around for the long haul.
Trading Nelson and Buckner lowered the Colts' immediate floor, but it provided an opportunity for two of their young players , DT Adetomiwa Adebawore and G Jalen Farmer, to prove themselves as long-term options.
Someone who didn't directly benefit from a trade but still fits this mold is rookie linebacker CJ Allen.
Allen made his first career start against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8, and he already looks like the best linebacker on the Colts' roster .
This emergence is a massive first step for both parties. Allen finally gets to prove his worth, while the Colts get some extended looks at what could very well be their long-term green dot defender.
The Indianapolis Colts drafted CJ Allen to become Zaire Franklin's long-term replacement at MIKE linebacker.
Allen was taken with the Colts' first pick (53rd overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft, and was immediately slotted in as the defense's starting linebacker.
Everything was going as planned. Allen looked like the guy Indianapolis drafted him to be throughout rookie minicamp and mandatory OTAs, but a groin injury that popped up during training just days before training camp began set him back.
Allen missed the first chunk of camp before returning to the gridiron, and he still looked the part once he was back in action.
However, Allen sustained a hamstring injury a few practices later and was once again sidelined for the foreseeable future. He missed the Colts' preseason opener on top of missing the first of two joint practices, and these missed opportunities forced him into a rotational role to start the season .
This setback led to veteran safety Cam Bynum being named the green dot for the regular season opener, which Anarumo and Co. quickly realized was not sustainable. The Colts turned to veteran linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither instead, and Allen accepted the new challenge that said he'd have to earn his job back.
“Whether if I was starting – it doesn’t matter how that situation might look," Allen said during training camp about going from a projected day-one starter to a rotational piece. "I’m still going to show up the same way, work hard and control what I can control. I don’t look at it like that. Like I said, control what I can control and show up to work.”
The Colts' rookie linebacker wasn't happy about his situation, but he didn't let that affect his development. Instead, Allen stayed the course, and he was finally rewarded for his patience and hardwork behind the scenes.
Defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo was ready to start Allen for the first time this season in the Colts' Week 7 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings, but a mid-week ankle injury set him back.
Allen saw three separate setbacks before the regular season reached the midway point, and it was starting to look like he'd have to fight off injury-prone allegations.
Despite the increasing doubt, Allen put together a healthy week of practice and was named a starter for the first time in his young career.
Defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo said that CJ Allen's injuries in training camp set his development back, but it's clear that he's the best the room has to offer. Perhaps Allen only looked so prepared because he followed his coach's vision, but the talent is undeniable.
In his first start against a top-tier Jaguars' offense , Allen led the Colts in total tackles (10), sacks (1), and tackles for loss (1).
Allen didn't just fill up the stat sheet; he epitomized what the Colts were looking for this past offseason.
The Colts' rookie linebacker played fast, free, and physical, and it made for an impressive performance.
CJ Allen may wear 53, but his playstyle is more comparable to Zaire Franklin's than it is Shaquille Darius Leonard's. That's by no means a shot at Franklin, but he just doesn't have the same top-tier playmaking skills that Leonard had.
Both Allen and Franklin are hard-nosed run stoppers who have sneaky blitzing skills, but you're also not expecting them to force a ton of turnovers. Of course, that's what made Leonard so special, but what Allen has done in a short time is enough to get excited about.
Allen may not project to be an All-Pro candidate out of the gate, but he certainly looks like a longtime NFL starter. Who knows, we could very well be scratching the surface of what's to come.
While the rookie still has a long way to go, he's already proven that he possesses the necessary traits and instincts to lead a defense - something both Franklin and Leonard did in Indianapolis for numerous years.
Anarumo said earlier this week that veteran linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither will remain the green dot for the foreseeable future, but don't count out Allen's ability to earn his keep and take on even more responsibility down the stretch.
The Indianapolis Colts are actively transitioning their focus to the future, and they should be. None of the Colts' rookies are guaranteed stars at this point, but they deserve the opportunity to prove themselves before the season officially concludes.
One thing is for certain: CJ Allen is off to a fantastic start when it comes to proving himself as part of the franchise's long-term solution.
Noah Compton is the Publisher of Indianapolis Colts On SI. Noah is from the Indy area and has been covering the Colts since 2022, including stops at FanSided, The Blue Stable, and SBNation.

title: Shane Steichen’s Fatal Mistake: The Decision That May Cost Him His Job
full_text:
Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen traveled to Jacksonville on Sunday, looking to snap a road losing streak against the Jaguars that extended back to 2014.
With the Colts sitting at 2-5 going into the game, hopes of securing their first playoff berth in six years looking bleak and trade rumors swirling around the team, Steichen was undoubtedly coaching for his job.
But if you watched Sunday's game, you wouldn't have been able to tell. Indianapolis lost 42-7. In Steichen's own words, "we got out-coached. We got out-played."
"We got out-coached. We got out-played." #Colts head coach Shane Steichen on the loss to the Jaguars: pic.twitter.com/4mJxDRXccb
The scoreline and Steichen's comments speak for themselves. It was an embarrassing performance by Indianapolis , with several factors contributing to the beatdown. However, one decision by Steichen stood above the rest and could ultimately define his tenure in Indianapolis.
Throughout a season in which the Colts' offense has navigated several issues, Steichen has consistently been the first to come to the defense of starting quarterback Daniel Jones. The 29-year-old has struggled to regain the form he captured in 2025 before rupturing his Achilles, and the offense has taken a significant hit as a result.
Through eight games a season ago, the Indianapolis offense led the league in both points per game (33.8) and yards per game (385.3). So far in 2026, the Colts are scoring just 22 points per game (20th in the NFL) and recording 298 yards per game (25th).
One of the biggest differences between the two seasons has been the supporting cast around Jones. Indianapolis traded Michael Pittman Jr. to the Steelers in the offseason. His replacement as Indy's WR1, Alec Pierce, hasn't played since Week 2 due to a heel injury. Right tackle Braden Smith left in free agency and was replaced by Jalen Travis, a second-year player who has experienced his share of ups and downs this season.
That group has changed significantly, and not for the better. When 11-year veteran Laquon Treadwell, a former first-round pick who made his first opening day roster since 2018 this season, and 34-year-old Keenan Allen are among Jones' primary weapons, it's difficult to expect him to consistently pick up the slack.
That said, Jones isn't devoid of blame himself. His 12 turnovers (nine interceptions and three lost fumbles) have hurt the offense and made it difficult to find any consistency. Still, Steichen stuck with him.
During Sunday's loss, Indianapolis was down 28-0. The offense had hardly sniffed field goal range and the passing game wasn't effective at all. The Colts needed a spark, and fast.
Steichen had an opportunity to make a change at quarterback and give Anthony Richardson Sr. a chance to breathe new life into a floundering unit. But he didn't think so.
Jones started the second half, despite the mounting case for a quarterback change. While he did lead a 10-play touchdown drive in the third quarter, the score did little to change the game's trajectory. Indianapolis was still trailing by four scores, with little reason to believe the offense could mount a comeback.
It wasn't until 11:45 remaining in the fourth quarter that Richardson finally got his chance. By then, the result was no longer in doubt. Jacksonville had even made a quarterback change of its own, replacing Trevor Lawrence with Quinn Ewers, but for entirely different reasons.
Clearly, there was no sense of urgency from Steichen to try and turn the game, and his head coaching tenure with the Colts, around. His fate is all but sealed. The only question remaining is when the organization makes it official.

Colts lead owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon now faces a significant decision. After dismissing Chris Ballard following the loss to Tennessee, the organization has already acknowledged that changes are necessary. Allowing Steichen's tenure to continue without a clear path forward would only prolong the uncertainty surrounding the franchise. It's time to bring down the hammer and put an end to a tenure that appears to have run its course.
Moving on from Steichen would only be the first step toward changing the franchise's direction. Indianapolis would still need to determine its long-term future at quarterback, evaluate the roster and identify the leadership capable of getting the organization back to competing for a playoff spot. Those decisions will ultimately determine how quickly the Colts can turn things around.

title: Jonathan Taylor Sweepstakes Tracker: Colts Analysis, Trade Rumors, and More
full_text:
Unfortunately for Indianapolis Colts fans, Jonathan Taylor and trade request are two terms that have been used together in a sentence before.
Back in 2023, the Colts' prolific running back requested a trade from the Indianapolis Colts amid ongoing contract disputes. Taylor infamously showed up to practice in a black hoodie during his subsequent hold-in, signifying the trying times of a franchise that was entering its first season with then-rookie Anthony Richardson at quarterback.
Following the reporting of Taylor's trade request, former longtime Owner Jim Irsay made sure the league knew he was going to do whatever it takes to keep the star rusher around for the then-rebuild, which was really more of a slight re-tooling, a more conventional dart throw, but I digress.
“We’re not trading Jonathan [Taylor]... end of discussion,” Irsay said in a text to Sports Illustrated ’s Albert Breer . “Not now and not in October!”
And as fate would have it, the Colts would up re-signing Jonathan Taylor in October to a three-year $42 million contract extension, which included $26.5 million in guaranteed payments.
But just three years later, the star running back is back at the center of trade talks.
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline at 4 PM EST on November 10th is quickly approaching, and it's become increasingly likely that Jonathan Taylor has played his last snap as a member of the Indianapolis Colts.
We're breaking down everything we know about the state of the sweepstakes in question, and will update this article as new information presents itself.
Without further ado, let's dive into how we got here, which teams are reportedly interested in Jonathan Taylor's services and what they're offering.
Despite loud rumors and an ongoing fire sale suggesting otherwise, Taylor has not requested a trade.
In all honesty, it feels and looks like Taylor is one of the few remaining longtime veterans on the Colts roster who genuinely still wants to be in Indianapolis.
Earlier in the offseason, Taylor signed a two-year extension to stay in Indianapolis through the 2028 season. Taylor said he wanted to remain a Colt for life before the extension, hinting toward the goal of a long-term deal, but he and the Colts found a solution that satisfied both parties.
Chris Ballard was already on the hottest seat in general manager history as he entered the final year of his deal, and the Colts didn't want to fully commit to another era under his rule.
And it was smart to think that way, considering we are wrapping up Week 8 and Ballard has been out of the building for two weeks now. Along with him went longtime franchise pillars Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and all eyes have been on Jonathan Taylor ever since.
Mere months after committing to stay in Indianapolis for the next three seasons, Taylor appears to be on his way out.
In his first game without Quenton Nelson leading the way, Taylor rushed for just 23 yards on eight carries. The Colts failed to establish any sort of rushing attack against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8, and Taylor saw just five carries come his way in the first half.
After the game, Taylor appeared to be rather emotional and was giving multiple teammates and coaches hugs. Sure, it could've just been a lot to take in, or perhaps I am looking too far into it, but it truly felt like this was the last we've seen of Jonathan Taylor in Indianapolis.
Couple this with the fact that ESPN's NFL Insider Adam Schefter confirmed on Halloween, the day prior, that the Indianapolis Colts are officially open to trading Taylor and have been active in talks, and it seems like he's as good as gone.
Schefter also reported that the Colts have already received an offer of a 2027 second-round pick, along with additional compensation, for Taylor's services.
Colts Owner/CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon views Taylor as "a key part of the organization and a likely mainstay in their rebuild," according to Schefter and fellow ESPN Insider Ian Rapoport , the latter of whom added that Indianapolis could change its stance if the right offer comes along, leaving the door open without signaling that a deal is imminent.
Taylor's most comparable trade package, or at least the one Indianapolis is seeking, is that of Christian McCaffrey's blockbuster haul from 2022.
In exchange for McCaffrey, the Panthers received a 2023 NFL Draft second-round pick, a 2023 third-rounder, a 2023 fourth-rounder, and a 2024 fifth-round pick.
The Colts are understandably trying to pry a first-round pick from an interested suitor's hands, but it doesn't feel like they'll be able to achieve that.
However, if teams get desperate enough, the Colts may end up pulling off a much-needed heist to kickoff their rebuild.
Taylor doesn't quite warrant the first-round consideration as a pure rusher who is a subpar back in the passing game, though he does have an argument.
Regardless of his flaws as a third-down back, Taylor's ability as a true rusher is nearly unmatched. He remains at the top of his game at 27 years old, is durable, and carries a favorable contract for the next two seasons.
The Colts already paid Taylor his $15 million signing bonus before the season, so a potential suitor would only be on the hook for $15 milllion in 2027 and $9.46 million in 2028.
Of course, the highly unlikely yet somewhat feasible hypothetical first-round compensation would come via a contender, thus the projected draft pick would not be able to relieve the hurt that is the Colts' projected Top 5 pick that is sitting in New York, though it would help the next regime's outlook tremendously.
The good news for this pipe dream is that Taylor is garnering heavy interest across the league.
According to Schefter, the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, and New York Giants have reached out to Indianapolis, and those talks are said to be active and ongoing.
Per Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk, the New York Giants appear to be all-in on Taylor, but it must be at the right price.
"The Giants are one of those teams, and they are very interested. They view Jonathan Taylor as being on par with Derrick Henry in that second tier, just below the best running backs in the NFL. The general concern at this point, though, is that the Colts want too much," Florio said following Week 8's Sunday slate .
“One source with one of the teams currently in the mix with Taylor puts it at 50-50 as to whether it gets done before the trade deadline."
Furthermore, Denver Broncos beat reporter, The DNVR's Zac Stevens, said that he feels the Broncos are truly all-in on Taylor.
"I believe the Broncos are going to do everything in their power to trade for Jonathan Taylor...." Stevens said in a postgame reaction piece on the DNVR Broncos Podcast. "The Broncos are going to try to pull this trade off, from my understanding. They want Jonathan Taylor now."
That wraps up just about everything we're aware of as of Monday, November 2nd. Be sure to check back in for any updates regarding the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes.
NFL Insider Jordan Schultz added on Monday that the Cincinnati Bengals and Seattle Seahawks have entered the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes.
Here’s everything I know about the #Colts ’ trade talks involving RB Jonathan Taylor, WR Josh Downs, DT Grover Stewart and other players, including which teams are interested and why Indianapolis is trading players away. Discussed with @Realrclark25 on #ThePivot : https://t.co/ZANCGWaIE2 pic.twitter.com/h2YyOt9mb3
"My understanding is that 5-6 teams have been aggressively pursuing him: Giants, Packers, Broncos, Seahawks, Bengals, Vikings," Schultz said on The Pivot .
"I think it'll take at least a second-round plus additional compensation to get it done, and I actually do expect that to happen."
The aforementioned Christian McCaffrey blockbuster haul remains the ideal return for the Indianapolis Colts.

title: Indianapolis Colts Fire Sale Tracker: Analysis, Trades, Rumors, and More
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts will be the center of the NFL world for the foreseeable future.
This is the second consecutive season that Indianapolis will be featured in trade talks at the midway point, but unlike last year, it's not because they're the number one seed in the AFC.
Instead of buying at the deadline, the Colts will be selling.
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline (November 10th, 4 PM EST) is quickly approaching, and the Colts are amidst a complete teardown of their franchise.
The Colts fired longtime general manager Chris Ballard after they fell to 2-4 in a humiliating loss, and have been active in the trade market ever since as they look to recoup any valuable draft capital they can after Ballard traded away their 2027 first-round pick, as well as their 2026 first-rounder and WR Adonai Mitchell.
It was the beginning of a poetic end, as the last Ballard-led Colts game was a loss to the 0-5 Tennessee Titans, a team that many still consider the worst team in the NFL. Even then, this version of the Colts may very well be the league's worst.
On top of only one playoff win in three appearances, the Colts failed to win the lowly AFC South across 9.5 seasons (2017-2026) under Chris Ballard.
Despite ample evidence to suggest otherwise, Indianapolis Colts' Owner/CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon decided to bring back both Chris Ballard and head coach Shane Steichen for the 2026 season, referencing their hot start to the previous year as a reason to give them another chance.
The former had been given far too many chances to that point, but to be fair to Irsay-Gordon and her sisters, Co-Owners Kalen Jackson and Casey Foyt, this was the organization's first full offseason under new ownership.
Following the decision to give Ballard and Steichen one last shot in her postseason press conference, Irsay-Gordon said that the "sense of urgency has never been higher" for the GM/HC tandem.
Many didn't believe her, given that she was entering her first full offseason as an NFL Owner/CEO and appeared to be betting on an inevitable collapse, but Irsay-Gordon did what needed to be done, even if it came a bit too late.
In the past 14 days, the Indianapolis Colts have fired longtime general manager Chris Ballard, fallen to 2-6 on the season, and traded away two of their franchise cornerstones.

Navigate our trade central (finalized trades, rumors, etc.), future outlook, and more below.

It stings to see any team trade their homegrown future Hall of Famer, but this is the bed the Colts made, and now they must sleep in it.
The Colts' 2026 fourth-round rookie guard Jalen Farmer is Nelson's immediate replacement.
Buckner's departure creates a similar challenge on the defensive line. More responsibility will fall on the remaining interior defenders, including Stewart and Adetomiwa Adebawore.
Not only is the opportunity there, but Adebawore has earned the increased role in question.
After seven weeks, Adebawore is undeniably the Colts' best pass rusher. He is currently tied for second with the most sacks among interior defensive linemen league-wide and leads the team in most major pass-rush statistics.
We've known that Adebawore has some nasty pass-rushing chops, but the biggest development has been his improvement in run defense.
Adebawore has blossomed into a legitimate starting defensive tackle, and it comes at no better time as the Colts have parted ways with their longtime pillar across the defensive line.
However, the Colts' newfound star is on an expiring deal. Adebawore is playing in the final year of his rookie contract, so a big payday is set to come his way.

In exchange for McCaffrey, the Panthers received a 2023 NFL Draft second-round pick, a 2023 third-rounder, a 2023 fourth-rounder, and a 2024 fifth-round pick.
The Colts are understandably trying to pry a first-round pick from an interested suitor's hands, but it doesn't feel like they'll be able to achieve that.
However, if teams get desperate enough, the Colts may end up pulling off a much-needed heist to kickoff their rebuild.
Of course, the highly unlikely yet somewhat feasible hypothetical first-round compensation would come via a contender, thus the projected draft pick would not be able to relieve the hurt that is the Colts' projected Top 5 pick that is sitting in New York, though it would help tremendously.
The good news for this pipe dream is that Taylor is garnering heavy interest across the league. According to Schefter, multiple teams have reached out to Indianapolis, and those talks are said to be active and ongoing.
"The list of teams that have expressed at least some level of interest in trading for Taylor is thought to include the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, and New York Giants," Schefter wrote.

title: Leave the Past Behind: Colts' Future Outlook Intensifies After Loss to Jaguars
full_text:
A tale as old as time: The Indianapolis Colts leave Jacksonville with a loss.
Their 42-7 loss to the Jaguars confirmed what we already knew: The Colts' 2026 regular season is dead in the water .
The Colts are amidst a historic fire sale of their roster after parting ways with longtime general manager Chris Ballard following a Week 6 loss to the winless Tennessee Titans , but they weren't willing to fully pull the plug on the old era.
Indianapolis traded longtime franchise cornerstones Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner after a Week 7 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, but held off from selling off more of their roster as they looked to stay alive in the AFC South.
The Colts would have been just one game behind the Jacksonville Jaguars in the AFC South had they squeeked out a win, which would have given Indianapolis false hope that they can contend for the division.
Instead, in arguably the most beneficial outcome for Indianapolis, the Jaguars embarassed the Colts from start to finish.
Nobody is surprised that the Colts lost a game in Jacksonville, given they haven't beaten the Jaguars on the road since 2014, but especially because it's this version of these two teams.
The Jaguars and Colts couldn't be more polar opposites when it comes to their overall outlook, with the former hitting their stride as legitimate Super Bowl contenders, whereas the former is embarking upon a full-fledged organizational reset .
With that being said, here are my biggest takeaways from the Colts' most recent redefining of what it means to hit rock bottom.
The Colts' ownership trio of Carlie Irsay-Gordon, Kalen Jackson, and Casey Foyt collectively decided that their season was over when they fired longtime general manager Chris Ballard after six weeks.
In an expected turn of events, the roster has seemingly followed suit.
Indianapolis Colts' head coach Steichen entered the regular season on the hot seat, and he now sits on a throne from Hell after eight uninspiring games to show for.
The Colts are 2-6 through eight weeks of play, and although it was already looking like Steichen would elsewhere in 2027, his tenure as head coach may come sooner rather than later.
The current version of the Colts looks checked out, and they have become wildly undisciplined as a result. A handful of longtime veterans continue to put in their best effort, but a lot of them look fed up with the state of the organization.
This ultimately falls on the previous regime for building an unsustainable culture, though Steichen hasn't done himself any favors.
After a decade of mediocrity, the next era can't come soon enough.
There's absolutely no reason that quarterback Daniel Jones, running back Jonathan Taylor, or wide receiver Josh Downs should have played in this game.
It's almost a guarantee that Jones will not be part of the rebuild's future, Taylor headlines all NFL trade deadline candidates, and Downs has requested a trade out of Indianapolis.
Instead, head coach Shane Steichen rolled out the trio in question in a last-resort attempt to save the Colts' season, and more specifically, his job.
The only bright spot from their collective performance was when Daniel Jones and Josh Downs connected for the Colts' lone score of the day. Other than that, we were proven right that this version of Steichen's offense is broken beyond repair, something we claimed weeks back when the Colts were still technically in the hunt.
It took until being down 42-7 in the fourth quarter for Steichen to bench the trio against Jacksonville. This was right decision but the wrong time, and it will now serve as yet another blemish on Steichen's resume as a head coach.
It's officially time for the Colts to cut their losses and move on from Shane Steichen, Jonathan Taylor, Daniel Jones, and Josh Downs.
While he probably shouldn't, Steichen may last the rest of the season. However, the three players in question should not play another snap. It's that simple.
The Indianapolis Colts have already turned the page on their most recent era, but it's time to close the book altogether.
There's virtually no market for Daniel Jones after his atrocious showing so far this season, but still, he should remain benched.
Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs can and should be traded for draft capital, but as far as the quarterback position goes, there's no reason to continue trotting Daniel Jones out onto the field.
Jones ranks near the bottom of the league in most key statistical categories, so letting Anthony Richardson or Riley Leonard duke it out for the remainder of this lost season couldn't hurt.
The Colts are going nowhere, so concluding the experiment altogether is the best course of action moving forward.
Keeping this trio around does nothing for the Colts' future. If anything, their valuable snaps are eating into the future's opportunity to get some much-needed run down the stretch.
Taylor remains at the center of NFL trade rumors as we approach the November 10th deadline. Even though he has not officially requested a trade out of Indianapolis, the Colts would be wise to deal him to strengthen the next regime's early outlook .
Despite early reports claiming they view him as a building block of their rebuild, the Indianapolis Colts are open to trading Taylor, but they've been playing hardball as they aim to net as much valuable draft capital as possible.
If they wait for the deadline to get closer, the Colts can create a bidding war for Taylor's services, especially if he can continue producing at a high level.
However, despite Taylor's best efforts against the Jaguars, he only totaled eight carries for 23 rushing yards and was sidelined early in the fourth quarter.
Taylor's worst showing of the season so far speaks more to the dysfunction surrounding the Colts' offense, but it's not helping his personal stock.
The Colts are running out of time with the NFL Trade Deadline
The Ringer's NFL Insider Tom Pelissero reported on Saturday that the Colts have already turned a 2027 second-round pick plus an additional pick for Jonathan Taylor, so while it makes sense to hold him hostage in an attempt to drive up the price, continuing to trot him out with this broken offense is doing nobody any favors.
The Colts are understandably trying to pry a first-round pick from an interested suitor's hands, but it doesn't feel like they'll be able to achieve that.
Taylor's most comparable trade package is that of Christian McCaffrey's blockbuster haul from 2022.
In exchange for McCaffrey, the Panthers received a 2023 NFL Draft second-round pick, a 2023 third-rounder, a 2023 fourth-rounder, and a 2024 fifth-round pick.
As long as they can manage to net first-round value (i.e., multiple Day 2 draft selections), trading Taylor is worth it.
Josh Downs' value is a bit trickier to predict, given his expiring deal and the fact he plays a hyper-specific role as a slot receiver and punt returner.
ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the Colts are looking for a third-round pick for Josh Downs. That was always a high price, but one that a role-specific contender could be convinced by.
However, despite head coach Shane Steichen reminding Downs that he is a professional who is expected to give his all so long as he's repping the Colts, the fourth-year receiver played like he was already one foot out of the door .
Yes, Downs scored the Colts' lone touchdown on the day, but it came after a lacksadaisical performance to that point. The most damning evidence that Downs has checked out was during a failed reverse that saw him do his best Cam Newton impression and decline to jump on the fumbled exchange.
It looked like Downs began to give up on his Colts tenure during Indianapolis' Week 6 loss to the Minnesota Vikings as he lacked the effort he typically showcases.
Of course, this matchup in question was the Colts' first game since they fired longtime general manager Chris Ballard, the very man who took a shot on Downs in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft, so it makes logical…

title: Josh Downs Checked Out Against Jaguars, and Colts Need to Erase That Negativity
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts showed out in the worst way, falling to the Jacksonville Jaguars 42-7 on Sunday afternoon. This marks Indy's 12th straight road loss to Jacksonville on the road, dating back to the 2014 season.
Many things can be picked apart from Indianapolis' awful showing, but one player earns the spotlight for this article: Josh Downs.
After Indianapolis traded away superstars Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner to signal a rebuild, top wideout Downs requested to leave the franchise.
Josh Downs has requested a trade from the Colts, per @JFowlerESPN pic.twitter.com/0eMonnkhne
Downs was the undisputed top pass-catcher for Indy heading into this matchup with the Jaguars, even with Tyler Warren returning from a groin injury.
However, what ensued was a player who was checked out and had little interest in helping the team that was paying him.
Downs finished with four catches for a meager 23 receiving yards and a touchdown. While that score might make the reader think Downs put up a solid showing, it was the lone touchdown in a completely lost contest.
Josh Downs gets the Colts on the board in the third 📺CBS & Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/MjQV1HStMG
I've been a massive fan of Downs, especially this year. However, this game against the Jaguars showed where Downs' head is really at, and it had nothing to do with a catch or missed opportunity.
Instead, it came in the second quarter when a disastrous play call from Shane Steichen occurred.
In short, Daniel Jones handed the ball to Jonathan Taylor, who was supposed to toss a reverse to Downs, but it went as awful as the imagination can conjure.
If you look closely, Downs doesn't just screw up the fumble recovery, but he entirely avoids it like a player who's done helping the team he's representing.
The trick play goes awry and the Jaguars get it back! INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/AinguLvhQi
That ridiculous lack of effort had the vibes of Cam Newton denying a fumble recovery opportunity against the Denver Broncos in Super Bowl 50, which is still criticized to this day.
Look, Downs is an amazing slot receiver, and on his best day, the best at his craft and usage in the NFL.
However, he's clearly finished and over the situation in Indianapolis, and with the trade deadline fast approaching (November 10th), Downs is one of the hottest Colts players rumored to be dealt off.
Downs is in the final year of his rookie deal, and, quite frankly, looked like a sure-fire piece to be re-signed to a new deal to help Indy in its rebuild.
However, after his trade request and subsequent lackluster showing in the blowout loss to the Jaguars, he seems like a talent who might be a liability more than an asset.
The Colts are lost and smothered, and currently appear to be the absolute worst squad in the NFL after terrorizing the league for 10 weeks in 2025.
It's sad to admit, but Downs is mentally finished with playing for the Colts, and Indianapolis should pick up on that vibe.
The Colts still have nine games left in 2026, but Downs doesn't need to be a part of the upcoming disaster.
I fully expect, and hope, that the Colts trade away this slot star to a team where he can be present, and the franchise can recoup some draft capital, in a season that has turned into an utter trash heap.
