Drake Wally is a Senior Writer for the Indianapolis Colts On SI. His works have also appeared on Bleacher Report, MSN, Yahoo, and SBNation. He also co-hosts the Horseshoe Huddle Podcast.

title: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly from Colts’ Lopsided Defeat in Jacksonville
full_text:
Halloween has passed, but the Duval demons continue to haunt the Indianapolis Colts .
Indianapolis’ rough week got worse on Sunday, as their season officially went down the drain in Jacksonville with a demoralizing 42-7 loss to the Jaguars. The Colts remain winless in Jacksonville since 2014, and now their unlikely chances to win the AFC South are over.
Although there weren’t many, there were some bright spots among the hideousness of the performance. Let’s take a look at just some of the good, the bad and the ugly.
CJ Allen made his first career start Sunday, at long last after dealing with various injuries to begin his NFL career. Once he finally made it onto the field, he instantly showed why he’s a player the Colts can build around moving forward.
Allen recorded 10 tackles, a tackle for loss and a sack, all team-highs. It took a while to see results, but the rookie is showing that he’s capable of being a starter moving forward.
The light at the end of the tunnel is way too far away to see it at this point, but at least Indianapolis has someone to help get it through the darkness.
Indianapolis seems to have another defender who can contribute moving forward. Second-year edge defender Jaylahn Tuimoloau had easily the best game of his career up to this point, logging his first career sack.
On top of the sack, Tuimoloau made some plays in the run game and created some other pressures, too. Refreshing to see a Colts edge player finally step up and make an impact this season.
The Colts’ rookie class has shown some solid potential, including Seth McGowan.
The stats aren’t too pretty—five carries for 29 yards—but McGowan made some nice blocks in pass protection and had a couple nice, hard runs.
Seems sad that a performance like Sunday’s means a running back with less than 30 yards is one of the better things on the field. And it is. But if Jonathan Taylor is traded in the near future as expected, McGowan has absolutely earned the opportunity to be the lead back for the rest of 2026.
Like many who follow the Colts, Josh Downs is fed up. The 25-year-old requested a trade earlier this week and officially checked out once doing so.
Sunday was beyond bad for Downs, despite being responsible for the Colts’ only points on the day. His effort was appalling, summed up no better than buy his first half blunder that lead to a turnover.
The Jaguars get the takeaway and are back in business at midfield. 📺CBS & Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/ComkyGwMGp
The Colts decided to run an end around, with Jonathan Taylor taking the initial pitch before tossing it back to Downs to take it the other direction. But Taylor slipped, tossed the ball a little too high and fast and watched it bounce off Downs’ face mask and onto the ground.
The problem? Downs didn’t even attempt to jump on the loose ball. There is no better evidence that he’s ready to get out of Indianapolis.
Tyler Warren’s return from a two-game absence was anything but ideal.
The second-year tight end caught four passes for a meager 18 yards and was the culprit responsible for Jacksonville’s pick-six, as Daniel Jones’ pass bounced off his hands and into the hands of Rayuan Lane III, who took it the distance.
The Jaguars with the pick-six right after turning over the ball! 📺CBS & Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/HuHMPpb0sv
It’s been a rough season for Warren, who hasn’t been able to replicate the impact he had as a rookie.
Unfortunately for Daniel Jones, his time as the Colts starter may be over.
Jones’ stat line is tough to look at: 19-for-28 for 144 yards, one touchdown pass and two interceptions (one pick-six).  To make it worse for Jones, it isn’t all his fault. Receivers couldn’t separate and the Colts’ lack of a deep threat continued to severely limit what Indianapolis could try in the passing game. Jones averaged just 5.1 yards per completion.
With the Colts scoreless at halftime, head coach Shane Steichen could’ve easily made a change and pulled his quarterback. But he gave him a little bit of a longer leash, waiting until the fourth quarter to replace him with Anthony Richardson Sr.
Jones isn’t immune from any blame when it comes to Indy’s dreadful offense, but he’ll most likely end up taking the fall, despite never really having proper support around him.
It’s hard to fault Jonathan Taylor for his play today, as he’s done more than enough for the Colts throughout his time with the franchise. But he did make the ugly misstep that led to a back-breaking fumble.
In what was likely Taylor’s final game wearing the horseshoe, he touched the ball 12 times for only 47 yards and was understandably benched to preserve his health ahead of his inevitable trade out of Indianapolis. A tough way to go out for a guy who’s delivered so many awesome moments to the fan base.
I’ll give Shane Steichen a little bit of credit—he finally had the strength to make lineup changes when he pulled Jones, Taylor and Downs, albeit way too late in the game.
But the praise stops there. Steichen, likely coaching to save his job, sealed his own fate with the inexcusable all-around performance by his team.
Playcalling was suspect throughout, getting cute on the goal line the one time the offense progressed that far. While he did make the personnel switches, they were way too late. By halftime, with the game already decided, there was no reason not to give guys like Richardson, McGowan and Deion Burks a chance to show what they can do.
Taylor and Downs have one foot out the door and Jones gave no reason to still believe he can spark a comeback.
At this point there’s no coming back for Steichen, and the ball is in Carlie Irsay-Gordon’s court to make a decision on his future.
Special teams has been uncharacteristically poor for the Colts this season, particularly the kick return game, which can’t seem to execute cleanly.
Two excellent Seth McGowan kick returns were negated by holding penalties, an issue which has popped up unusually often this season. Still, McGowan managed over 100 kick return yards, and could’ve doubled that number had the Colts stayed out of their own way.
Unfortunate, but still not the main issue for Indianapolis down in Duval.

title: Colts Week 8 Best Bets: Finding Value Amid the Chaos
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts are headed back to Jacksonville, a place they haven't won since 2014.
Usually, that would be enough reason to keep the card light. But this Colts fire sale has created some interesting betting opportunities.
Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner are gone, Josh Downs has requested a trade, and Jonathan Taylor is available for the right price. From a morale perspective, it feels like the life is being sucked out of this team.
From a betting perspective? We've managed to capitalize on the chaos, going 15-4 on Colts-specific bets and 17-16 overall through seven weeks.
Jacksonville's elite run defense against Taylor and this brand-new offensive line will dictate the Colts' side of the ball. On the other side, Trevor Lawrence gets a depleted secondary without Justin Walley or Cam Taylor-Britt.
We're hunting for value this week. Here are my five best bets for Week 8.
Jonathan Taylor in the end zone at plus money doesn't come around very often.
Yes, Jacksonville has one of the best run defenses in football, and Nelson isn't creating holes for Taylor anymore. But Taylor just put up 95 rushing yards and a touchdown against an elite Minnesota defense and has scored in each of his last two games.
Taylor has eight rushing touchdowns this season, tied for the NFL lead, and has scored 10 total touchdowns over his last 10 games.
He's also scored at least once in each of his last three matchups against Jacksonville.
I can't stay away from this at plus money.
The Colts badly missed Tyler Warren while he was sidelined with a groin injury.
Now he's back against a Jacksonville defense that ranks 19th in tight end coverage, and this line has hit in each of Warren's last three healthy games.
He also had 43 receiving yards the last time he faced Jacksonville.
With Downs requesting a trade and the wide receiver room depleted, I expect Shane Steichen to get Warren involved early and often.
We're going right back to one of our regular plays.
Shrader has cleared this line in 11 of his 15 games with Indianapolis and has made 19 field goals over his last seven games.
He finally missed a couple against Minnesota, but I'm putting my trust right back in him.
With this stagnant Colts offense, Shrader might once again be Indianapolis' main source of scoring. Getting this at plus money feels too good to pass up.
This matchup could get ugly for the Colts' secondary.
Lawrence ranks fifth in passing grade against man coverage, while Indianapolis plays man at the seventh-highest rate in the league, according to PFF.
He's recorded 24 completions in each of his last two games and finished with 28 and 23 in his last two matchups against Indianapolis.
Walley is out, Taylor-Britt is on IR and Sauce Gardner is just returning from injury.
Twenty completions feels very attainable.
This might be my favorite sneaky play on the card.
Tuten has cleared this number in four straight games with 48, 24, 18 and 17 receiving yards.
He also ranks second among running backs in PFF receiving grade, while Indianapolis ranks 30th in receiving yards allowed to running backs per route run.
Against a depleted secondary and inexperienced linebacker room, Tuten should have opportunities underneath.
The Colts might be falling apart, but there's still value to be found, and we're going to keep cashing while this franchise burns.
Good luck and bet responsibly.

title: 3 Trades the Jaguars Must Immediately Consider to Replace Eric Murray
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The hits keep coming.
On the same day the Jaguars officially lost nose tackle Davon Hamilton for the rest of the season, they also lost another veteran defensive starter in safety Eric Murray.
Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Monday in a Zoom with local reporters that Murray will also miss the rest of the season after he sustained an elbow injury on the opening kickoff of Sunday's game against the Indianapolis Colts.
The Jaguars have other options at the position; the hope is Antonio Johnson will return from his ankle injury, Rayuan Lane has impressed, and so has Kaevon Merriweather. Then there is third-round safety Jalen Huskey. But Murray played a big role, and the Jaguars already have Caleb Ransaw on injured reserve, so reinforcements are needed.
So if the Jaguars were to look to the trade market for safety help, which options would make sense? We break it down below.
We mentioned Budda Baker last week as an option the Jaguars should pursue right away, and that was before Murray went down for the season. Now that the Jaguars are without their most veteran and experienced safety, Baker would somehow make even more sense for the Jaguars now than he did this time a week ago. With the Jaguars badly needing somebody in the back-end outside of Jourdan Lewis who has simply seen and played a lot of football, few options make more sense than Baker.
The Jaguars' brass should know exactly what Baker can do, too, considering the time that Liam Coen and James Gladstone each spent in Los Angeles facing Baker twice a year in the NFC West. Baker is productive, experienced, versatile, and would give the Jaguars quite a sense of security in the back-end. The Cardinals have won a few games, but they need picks more than anything right now.
Yes, the Atlanta Falcons are still in the mix of things in the NFC South since it is such a rotten division. But it is tough to say the Falcons are going to have great chances to re-sign star safety Jessie Bates once his contract expires since all they have really done since he was signed is lose games. If they are going to lose Bates anyways, why not take some picks for him now? Especially with an ascending safety next to him in Xavier Watts.
Bates would be a potential rental depending on how the Jaguars move forward with his free agency, but what a rental he would be. He has 14 interceptions and 11 forced fumbles in four seasons in Atlanta and has simply been a walking big-play threat. After almost a decade of elite safety play, the All-Pro would be exactly what the Jaguars need on defense right now. They would haver to make it worthwhile for the Falcons, but it would certainly be worth it.
If the Jaguars want a cheaper option at safety, what about Los Angeles Chargers defensive back Elijah Molden? He is versatile due to his ability as both a single-high safety and in the slot as a nickel defender, he tackles, and he is cheap. With the Chargers sitting at 0-7, there is no real reason they wouldn't be willing to deal a player like Molden unless they are just determined to be stubborn entering next Tuesday.
Molden may not offer the ceiling of players like Baker and Bates, but he does represent a high floor while also bringing plenty of experience. Molden would also likely cost a mid-to-late Day 3 pick, making him the cheapest player on this list by a few different definitions. Molden is a good player, and he would certtainly help the Jaguars in the wake of Murray's injury.

title: 3 Takeaways on Jaguars Signing Austin Johnson, What it Means for Replacing Davon Hamilton
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have added a defensive tackle, and it is a familiar face.
The Jaguars signed veteran defensive tackle Austin Johnson to the practice squad on Monday in the wake of Davon Hamilton's season-ending injury. With the Jaguars last season, Johnson appeared in 14 games and registered 12 tackles, 1.0 sack, one forced fumble and a pass defensed.
So, what does the Johnson addition mean as the Jaguars forge a path forward without Hamilton in the lineup? We break it down below.
The Jaguars did not quence the fan-bases thirst for a big-name trade target with their first choice for defensive tackle reinforcements, but it makes a ton of sense why. Any new player the Jaguars would add this week would be unlikely to help Jacksonville in Week 9 against the Baltimore Ravens considering the game is under 80 hours away. Had the Jaguars traded for a player on Monday, chances are he would be inactive come Thursday night in Baltimore.
With Johnson, though, that timeline is thrown out the window. He played in this same defense just last season, playing in the same scheme, for the same coordinator, with the same teammates, and with the same position coach. If there was any target who could be added Monday and ready to give snaps in run defense Thursday, it was always going to be a player like Johnson who has been on the roster recently.
It is always going to be tough to find a replacement for special players, and that is the obstacle the Jaguars now face when it comes to the run defense post-Hamilton. With the Jaguars adding Johnson to the practice squad on Monday, it is clear that their immediate solution to replacing Hamilton will have to be someone who is already on the roster and ready to go for Thursday Night Football.
Some people's thoughts might go to third-round rookie nose tackle Albert Regis right off the bat, but it instead seems like Matt Dickerson is the most likely candidate to step into the nose tackle spot vacated by Hamilton. Dickerson has done some good things for the Jaguars in a backup role over the last two seasons, but chances are we are set to see that role expand once Week 9 kicks off.
"Matt Dickerson has been a guy since he got here, he's been working, working, working. I think he was on practice squad when he first got here, but he was disruptive right away," Jaguars linebacker Foyesade Oluokun said Monday.
"And it's just the way that he plays selfless, like I'm talking about building the wall for the team, holding double teams, running the stunts right and stuff; he's selfless and definitely plays with a lot of grit and determination. I definitely appreciate him for it. So, we have a lot of faith in Dickerson and then whoever else we're going to put in there. Just knowing the kind of guy that he is, he's ready for success in that same spot.”
Just because the Jaguars added to the practice squad with Johnson on Monday doesn't mean the Jaguars are done. This is also not to say we should be considering the Jaguars a lock to get involved in the trade market either, because there are too many variables at play there. After all, it does take two to tango for a trade to happen. But to think the Jaguars will be content simply after adding Johnson does not really pass the smell test.
I would expect the Jaguars will make a healthy dose of phone calls over the next week when it comes to defensive tackle help for December and January, because the Johnson signing is more about this Thursday than it is about anything else. Do not be surprised to continue to see the Jaguars connected to the defensive tackle unit.

title: Good, Not So Good From Jaguars' Week 8 Colts Triumph: Nate Boerkircher's Development
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are entering a critical stretch of games over the next few weeks, and they got off to quite the good start with a Week 8 manhandling of the Indianapolis Colts.
But even with a 42-7 blowout of their AFC South rivals, there was some good, some bad, and some in between for the Jaguars in Week 8. So, what was the good and the not so good from the Jaguars' Week 8 win? We break it down below.
Nate Boerkircher caught his second touchdown in two games on Sunday, and it was a beauty. Boerkircher has five catches for 59 yards and two touchdowns since the Jaguars left for the London trip last month, and he has made the selection of him in the second-round look smarter than anyone anticipated. He isn't setting any game on fire with his receiving skills, but he clearly has the pass-catching traits to win on big plays and get designed touches in the passing game. Add in his run-blocking, and this has been a very impressive pick so far.
The Jaguars clearly came into this game thinking they could run the ball, which resulted in Trevor Lawrence only throwing 14 passes in three quarters. It isn't hard to see why the Jaguars leaned on the rushing game, with the unit producing 183 yards, 5.5 yards per carry, and two explosive touchdowns. The Colts only played with a light box on 19.2% of snaps, the lowest of any defense against the Jaguars this season, but the Jaguars still hammered away with relative ease.
What a day for second-year Jaguars. Let's run down the list:
Jalen Huskey had not seen any playing time on defense during the first six weeks of the season, but that changed in the fourth-quarter on Sunday. Huskey got some run at the end of the Jaguars' blowout and was able to record his first-career sack off a blitz call from Anthony Campanile on 3rd down, and his emotional celebration afterward says all that needs to be said about the confidence that it can give him moving forward.
First career sack for @HuskeyJalen ‼️ 📺 NFL Sunday Ticket on YouTube pic.twitter.com/s3x9clbO5g
Walker Little allowed zero pressures against the Colts, which means he has allowed just two pressures in his two starts at left tackle this season. The Jaguars may have lost star offensive tackle Anton Harrison for the year with a knee injury, but Little has managed to slide into the left tackle role and give the Jaguars strong play in back-to-back weeks.
Little has proven his worth to the Jaguars in spot starts before, but he is now continuing to show that he is a critical piece of the offensive line depth chart. If Little can play like this the rest of the year, he might deserve a real shot at entering Week 1 as a starter when it comes to the Jaguars' 2027 offensive line.
Have a day, Anthony Campanile. After one of the worst defensive performances from the Jaguars in the Campanile era in Week 6 against the Houston Texans, the Jaguars rebounded with one of their best against the Colts in Week 8. Almost nothing the Colts did worked in Week 8, with Campanile's pressure schemes working perfectly to force Daniel Jones into a bevy of mistakes.
Add in another week of slowing down Jonathan Taylor, and this was a vintage Campanile performance. Daniel Jones is no CJ Stroud and Keenan Allen is no Nico Collins, but it is still worth respecting after the previous performance. He is going to be a head coach one day, Duval, so appreciate him while he is here.
This goes without saying. Davon Hamilton has been the key to the Jaguars' stellar run defense over the last two years, and now it almost feels like the Jaguars will be forced to make some kind of move at the deadline. Feeling the pressure of a must-move at the deadline is normally not a spot you want to be in from a leverage perspective, and that doesn't even mention the fact that a trade is not guranteed to even help replace Hamilton.
With the Baltimore Ravens and Derrick Henry next up for the Jaguars, we should find out very quickly what the loss of Hamilton looks like. Still, this is a brutal result for a player who had truly hit his stride and prime at the position. Hamilton was having a Pro Bowl season, and now we will have to wait to see what happens with
Davon Hamilton wasn't the only Jaguars player who got banged up on Sunday, with the Jaguars also having a few other players leave the game with injury. Three other starters (Eric Murray, Ezra Cleveland, Travon Walker) sustained injuries at one point or another, and this wouldn't be good news for the Jaguars no matter what the circumstances. But in the specific situation the Jaguars are in at all three of those positions, it is far from ideal.
Antonio Johnson could be back in Week 9 after missing Week 8, but Murray would still be missed at safety since Caleb Ransaw is also injured. Rayuan Lane and Kaevon Merriweather have flashed, but safety has been hit hard this year. Then there is the offensive line, where Wyatt Milum did play well at right guard, but where they have already lost Anton Harrison and likely would not want to risk much more offensive line depth. As for Walker, he might be the team's second-best run defender after Hamilton; it is either him or Josh Hines-Allen.
While the Colts entered the game with one of the worst pass-rushes in the NFL and without DeForest Buckner, they still got after the Jaguars' pass protection a bit. Trevor Lawrence was sacked three times and the Colts recorded a season-best pressure rate (50%) and sack rate (13.6%). The Jaguars' pass-protection normally more than holds its own against so-so pass-rushes, but this was not the case this week.
These were not all on the offensive line, of course. There were some plays that looked like they were on the running backs, some on the tight ends, some on the edge, and some in the interior. Outside of Walker Little, it seemed like everyone took a turn. The Jaguars will need to be better than that when they play better fronts.

title: 2 Trade Targets and 1 In-House Option for the Jaguars to Replace Davon Hamilton
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars won in Week 8, but they also suffered a significant loss.
According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, the Jaguars are set to be without star nose tackle Davon Hamilton for the rest of the season with a torn quad. Hamilton was injured in Sunday's 42-7 win against the Indianapolis Colts, getting carted off in the first-half.
Sources: #Jaguars standout DT DaVon Hamilton suffered a torn quad in Sunday’s win over the #Colts , and he’s expected to be out for the season. Hamilton will undergo more tests today, but a massive hole for Jacksonville. pic.twitter.com/suJ2Hvp1av
So with Hamilton now out for the year just a week before the trade deadline hiits next Tuesday , what are the Jaguars' options to replace him? There are some options outside the walls of the Miller Electric Center to consider, as well as some options inside as well. Here are two trade options, and one in-house option, for the Jaguars to replace the heart and soul of their run defense.
We have not really considered the idea of trading for Patriots defensive tackle Christian Barmore before because we did not think it was much of a possibility that he would be moved. That now seems to be the case, though, with Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer noting that the Patriots have talked to teams about the former top-40 pick. Barmore, who turned 27 in July, has seen his numbers go down in recent years as the Patriots have turned to Milton Williams as their point-man at defensive tackle. Barmore is now fighting for snaps in the rotation, and it seems like the veteran defensive tackle could certainly be had.
Barmore is not exactly a run-stuffer like Hamilton, but he would give the Jaguars more punch and more versatility than many other defensive tackles out there. Most other options are players who can not fill the void at nose tackle, such as potentially Zach Sieler , or are nose tackles who would offer little else but run defense. Barmore would fit somewhere in the middle, and chances are he would not take a significant draft pick to nab.
Barmore does not carry any dead cap after this season, either. He would still be under contract for another two seasons for about $41 million, but the Jaguars would have time to see if he fits in their scheme and culture to determine if that is a price worth living with. Daron Payne would have made a ton of sense here, but Barmore works as a quick pivot if the Patriots are ready to cut ties.
If the Jaguars want to trade for a true nose tackle option who could plug rushing lanes from the second he gets to Duval, there are not many who would make more sense than Dalvin Tomlinson. The 32-year-old defensive tackle has been there and done that with nearly 150 games of NFL experience since joining the NFL in 2017, and he has been a reliable and effective run-stuffer at really every stop of his career.
This makes perfect sense considering where the Chargers are right now. Los Angeles is sitting at 0-7 after another bad loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, and they truly have zero reason to not start selling off parts of their roster for draft picks. Tomlinson is on a cheap one-year deal and is more of a run-stuffing mercenary at this point in his career than anything else, which would make him a logical fit for a Jaguars team that needs someone to step in for a run, ala Corey Peters in 2022.
Tomlinson wouldn't cost much, and the Chargers have zero reason to keep hanging onto him. This would make perfect sense for both sides, and probably could also happen fairly quickly all things considered.
This would be the option the Jaguars would have to turn to if they do not make a move. Matt Dickerson has been Hamilton's backup throughout the season and is a well-respected player inside the building, while Albert Regis has had limited reps on the field as a rookie after being drafted in the third-round in April. Regis has been a healthy scratch in recent weeks, which suggests the Jaguars would turn to Dickerson first and foremost when it comes to replacing Hamilton.
Dickerson has been a strong player against the run sign joining the team last season, while Regis was one of the better run defenders in the 2026 NFL Draft class. Both players are backups for a reason, though, and the upside with either is likely not close to the upside of adding a player via a trade. The Jaguars have shown that they can develop backups into serviceable starters, but this is a scenario that would bring a decent bit of risk.
There is no real replacing Hamilton, but maybe the Jaguars could try to find reinforcements in the aggregate. If they do not make a trade, then this is their only real option for the next 10 games of the 2026 season.

title: Shipley's Dozen: Jaguars' Domination of Colts Puts Them in Contenders Lane, But at a Cost
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- You're living in the good days right now, Jacksonville.
The Jaguars are not just a good team. They are a great team capable of dominance, which was put on full display in their 42-7 butt-kicking of the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. In today's Shipley's Dozen column, we break down what the win means and why the Jaguars are here to stay.
Reminder: Shipley Dozens columns release the day after each game, which means we get a two-for-one this week with the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday Night Football. But back to the Colts for a moment.
It was hardly a surprise that the Jaguars took care of business against the Colts. It was even less of a surprise that it was a blowout. But 42-7 games do not exactly happen very often in the NFL, and we shouldn't just gloss over it because the Colts are tearing everything down. The Jaguars were already contenders in a wide-open AFC and beating a bad Colts team doesn't change that. But the Jaguars' complete domination week in and week out at home is worth pointing out considering the AFC could very easily go through EverBank Stadium this week,
After yesterday's win, Jacksonville has won seven consecutive games at EverBank Stadium by 17 or more points. That is tied for the third longest such streak of games at a team’s home stadium in NFL history, trailing only the 1999 Rams and 1948-49 Eagles. In that span, they’ve scored at least 34 points in each of their last seven games. That matches the longest streak of such games in a team’s home stadium in NFL history, joining the 2012-13 Broncos and 1960-61 Chargers. If the playoffs go through Jacksonville, this very well could be a Super Bowl team. Enjoy it, Duval.
While the Jaguars throttling the Colts is always a good week for the Cardiac Cats, it didn't come without a cost. Winning is never a net negative, but the Jaguars saw star nose tackle Davon Hamilton go down with a knee injury and get carted off in the first half. Hamilton might not be a household name outside of Jacksonville, but those who are in the building and those who watch this team each week know just how important he is. It isn't hyperbolic to say this was the injury the Jaguars could least afford on defense.
The Jaguars have eight days to swing a trade to reinforce the middle of their defensive line, but it will be hard, if not impossible, to truly replace Hamilton. He is the reason their run defense works, and their run defense is the entire reason the scheme as a whole works. The Jaguars won on Sunday, but this was a tough loss.
Trevor Lawrence has been the best quarterback in the NFL this season. That is far from extreme when you consider the raw results. Lawrence's two games with a passer rating of 150+ this season are more than the rest of the NFL combined (Drake Maye, 1), after entering 2026 with zero such games in his career. Lawrence is third in touchdown passes with 17 despite ranking ... 22nd in pass attempts. Lawrence has only thrown 130 passes this year but is outpacing quarterbacks with close to 200 attempts because he has been as surgical and efficient as any passer in the NFL.
If the Jaguars were looking for style points and weren't playing a productive, balanced brand of offensive football, Lawrence could go the Joe Burrow route and treat each week like 7-on-7. But the Jaguars rank No. 26 in pass rate. All the while, Lawrence ranks No. 4 in EPA/Play, No. 1 in touchdown %, and No. 2 in adjusted net yards per attempt, the best stat for filtering efficient quarterback play. Imagine if he was throwing it more?
It was never going to make sense for the Jaguars to sell low on Brian Thomas Jr. when it came to a potential trade by next week's deadline. Count this double after the Jaguars opted to let Thomas get his starting spot back in the offense on Sunday after he was benched against the Houston Texans in London in Week 6. Thomas was third on the team in routes with 11 during the run-heavy day, and Thomas played 52% of the snaps. Still third amongst the receivers, but far from benched for Josh Cameron.
The Jaguars look like they are more than OK with Thomas serving as a background character in the offense, giving them the chance to find him at times throughout the game without devoting the sake of the entire passing game to his success like at the start of the 2025 season. Had the Jaguars not let Thomas see the field Sunday, I think we could have said he was as good as gone. The fact they still trusted him, though, makes me believe there is a scenario where the Jaguars just hold onto him.
We said the Jaguars would stop Jonathan Taylor in his tracks on Sunday, and that is exactly what happened. Taylor might have played his last game as a Colt, and it is only fitting that it came in the lone NFL stadium where he just can never find success. Taylor is one of the best running backs of his generation but he produces like Toby Gerhart whenever he is in EverBank Stadium. It takes a group effort every time, but plays like this one show just how much of a cultural trait it is to be strong against the run each season.
Jonathan Taylor was in hell in Jacksonville (again) yesterday pic.twitter.com/wxpzc3yXPy
When a team's depth gets tested is when you can really get a pulse for how well they scout and how well their staff develops young talent. On Sunday, the Jaguars had turnovers created by two undrafted free agents signed in the last two seasons and a pick-six by a Day 3 2025 draft pick who has otherwise been a special teams piece. How is this for a fun James Gladstone fact: the non-Travis Hunter players the Jaguars got in the Hunter trade (Tuten, Rayuan Lane) scored three touchdowns on Sunday. The Browns didn't score a single touchdown. That, people, is what they call a fleece.
Travis Hunter has only touched the ball eight times this season, and defenses are still putting all 11 sets of eyes on him every time he is on the field. He is the only shutdown cornerback in NFL history whose gravity is creating touchdowns for other skill players on offense. That seems good! Very good, in fact! I do not know if Hunter will have any real rhythm this season in terms of back-to-back weeks as a focal point on offense, but his gravity on the field is clear.
Look at all of the eyes on Travis Hunter on the Tuten TD after setting this play up in the first quarter pic.twitter.com/JbniHAFZ8L
That the Colts are still doing the Daniel Jones thing. The Colts are in rebuild mode for a number of reasons, but paying a lemon at quarterback is a big one. Jones looked horrible on Sunday from the very first drive, but it took until it was 42-7 for the Colts to put Anthony Richardson in. I was shocked the Colts didn't bench Jones at halftime, but maybe I shouldn't have been considering, well, it is the Colts. They are officially a few years away from being a few years away, and it starts with their quarterback issue.
Tuten having a breakout game. The Colts are weak in the front-seven without DeForest Buckner and their defensive backs do not seem like they like to tackle all that much. Tuten is the first Jaguars player to record 100 or more rushing yards, a rushing touchdown, and a receiving touchdown in the same game since James Robinson accomplished the feat against the Chargers in 2020, and he has officially become the future at the Jaguars' running back position.
Rayuan Lane. His pick-six was an electric moment, and he just keeps being ready for anything the Jaguars throw his way. This is the second time this season he has stepped in after an injury to Eric Murray and made a game-changing play, with the first coming in Week 4 against the Cincinnati Bengals. Lane is a special teams demon who has made plays when called upon, which is the definition of a Day 3 home run.
The AFC South is ... not very good. The Colts are done at 2-6. The Tennessee Titans lost a heartbreaker to the Cincinnati Bengals that at the very least exposed the Bengals as a non-serious threat in the AFC. The Texans lost a productive and exciting…

title: Davon Hamilton's Injury Just Changed Everything About the Jaguars' Trade Deadline Plans
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars' trade deadline urgency just ramped up. A lot.
The Jaguars had already been connected to the defensive tackle trade market ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline, and that was before Davon Hamilton was carted off the field in Week 8's win over the Indianapolis Colts.
While there are still updates to be had for Hamilton's health moving forward, there is no question that his injury has changed everything for the Jaguars before next Tuesday: the need, the fits, and most importantly, the urgency.
Simply put, the Hamilton injury has changed everything for a Jaguars team that already needed some help along the defensive line. Jacksonville was likely already in the market for a pocket-pushing three-technique who could make an impact on passing downs next to Josh Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, Arik Armstead, and Ruke Orhorhoro. That is still a need, too. But now so is nose tackle.
Hamilton has often been pointed to by his teammates as the primary reason the Jaguars have been so dominant against the run over the last two seasons. While we will likely not get an official update on him for a bit, it is fair to say the injury looked bad enough that the Jaguars will now have to look for and wide to replace him.
"We’re going to have guys that need to step up. We know what type of role D-Ham plays on our defense, and so the next person up has big shoes to fill, but there’s no disbelief that they can’t get the job done. We just have to keep going," Jaguars defensive end Josh Hines-Allen said after the game.
The Jaguars drafted a young nose tackle in the third-round in Albert Regis, but he has been healthy scratched for the last several weeks . Even if he had been playing, asking a rookie to step in and provide the Jaguars with what Hamilton does was always going to be a long  shot. Hamilton is one of the best nose tackles in football and has arguably been the Jaguars' defensive MVP this season thanks to the attention he commands against the run, and that is something the Jaguars can't replace with a next-man-up mentality
This means the Jaguars very well could have to look to the trade deadline. They already needed to add a defensive tackle, but now the urgency has been ramped up and the need has changed. The Jaguars don't just need a quality pass-rusher. They need someone they can trust in the middle of the defense to command double-teams.
There are certainly names to watch, such as Roy Lopez in Arizona, Vita Vea and A'Shawn Robinson in Tampa Bay, Moro Ojomo in Philadelphia, Dalvin Tomlinson in Los Angeles, and so on and so forth. But the Jaguars went from a notable need at defensive tackle to now a season-changing one. Even if the Jaguars had Hamilton, they needed some help. Now they need to find someone who can help replace their best defensive tackle.
That is no easy task, of course. Jaguars general manager James Gladstone isn't the only general manager likely taking phone calls on the defensive tackle front. We just saw what the Chicago Bears did to land a game-changer at the position, after all. There are no other Jeffrey Simmons out there for the Jaguars to pursue, but that shouldn't stop them.
The Jaguars look like a true Super Bowl contender in the AFC, and they can not let the Hamilton injury change that. What was already a need has become a move that demands action. Just like the Jaguars needed Jakobi Meyers to lift up the wide receiver room after injuries a year ago, the Jaguars will need to find a similar fit and impact at defensive tackle.
If they don't, the season very well could be on the line. That is how dire of a need defensive tackle became for the Jaguars on Sunday, with Harrison's injury serving as the line down point in an otherwise smooth game at EverBank Stadium. The next move is now up to Gladstone and the Jaguars.

title: Jaguars-Colts Game Balls: Bhayshul Tuten Has Forced Us Into Asking New Questions
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are rolling.
The Jaguars took care of their rival Indianapolis Colts with a 42-7 blowout at EverBank Stadium that, honestly, didn't even feel that close. It was the third home game in a row in which the Jaguars have been so dominant that their starters have sat by the fourth quarter, which might happen in the SEC but simply just doesn't happen at the NFL level.
Under head coach Liam Coen, Jacksonville has outscored AFC opponents 319-113 at home and have won nine consecutive games against the AFC in Jacksonville, including a 4-0 record against the AFC South. Today’s +35 margin of victory was Jacksonville’s largest since Week 15 of 2017 (+38). In short ... the Jaguars are kicking butt and taking names under Coen, and Sunday was the first of several steps toward a critical late-season run.
So, who were the Jaguars' best players on each side of the ball during the win? We break it down below.
Toot toot, and all aboard. The Bhayshul Tuten hype train took off several weeks ago, but don't worry because it is full-steam ahead and is bound to do a second lap after Sunday's win. Tuten had the best game of his young NFL career on Sunday, proving the Jaguars very right once again when it comes to their bold offseason deicison to let Travis Etienne walk in free agency. Tuten was one of the best players on the entire field on Sunday.
Bhayshul Tuten had a breakout performance, racking up 159 total yards and 2 touchdowns against the Colts. 16 CAR, 104 RUSH YDS, 1 RUSH TD, 2 REC, 55 REC YDS, 1 REC TD Jacksonville improves to 5-2 and is in a great position to host a playoff game. https://t.co/2K6VxSU40N pic.twitter.com/22Y0n0IRa5
Tuten ran for a career-high 104 yards on 16 carries and one touchdown, while adding two receptions for 55 yards and a touchdown, giving him his first 100-yard game in his career. His 159 scrimmage yards today are the most by a Jaguar since Week 5 of 2023, and Tuten is the first Jaguar to score on rushing and receiving touchdowns of 25-plus yards in the same game in the regular season.
This means there are new questions to ask about Tuten. The question is no longer whether he can replace Etienne, because that has clearly been answered. The question now is just how many running backs are playing better than Tuten in 2026. Tuten has been efficient, consistent, and has won in multiple ways throughout the season. We are seeing a star being born.
What an eventful year it has been for second-year safety Rayuan Lane. He entered the year as a backup on defense and a core special teamer, but the Jaguars have had to call his number on defense a few times due to injuries. In Week 4, it resulted in him making the game-winning tackle on fourth-down against the Cincinnati Bengals. This time, it was him stepping in when starting safety Eric Murray went down with an elbow injury on the opening kickoff.
Lane was simply in the right place at the right time once again, taking a tipped pass from failed first-rounder Tyler Warren's hands and returning it 92 yards for a touchdown. On top of that massive play, Lane recorded three tackles, three pass breakups, and a quarterback hit. He was all over the field in a game in which the Jaguars badly needed him to be ready to make an impact.
Rayuan Lane III reached a top speed of 21.83 mph on a 92-yard pick six of Daniel Jones, the fourth-fastest speed by a ball carrier this season. #INDvsJAX | #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/nZLh1meRgI
"I mean, it’s really cool and I think it just enforces the next-man-up mentality. Obviously on the first play of the game or something, we had somebody go down so just being able to step up and be able to make the plays and help my team out," Lane said in the locker room after the game.
Branson Combs also recorded an interception in a breakout performance, but it was his work on special teams that gets Combs a game ball. Combs was all over the place when it came to kickoff coverage, laying out several Colts blockers and returners in the process. The Jaguars didn't need their special teams units to do all that much on Sunday, but Combs was a big exception.
"I mean, that's something we talked about actually over the bye. It's just going after people, and I felt like I did that today," Combs said after the game.
"I take pride in special teams. Even coming in the league, that's kind of how I knew I could kind of find my way, and then earn more reps as I as I went. But yeah, I take pride in that. I expect myself to go down and make a play every time I'm out there. And you know, some a couple of them were able to fall back to me, and I was able to make a play."

title: 6 Winners, 3 Losers From Jaguars' Domination of Colts: Brian Thomas Jr's Response
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are riding high after that one.
The Jaguars are 5-2 and fresh off one of the most dominant wins of the Liam Coen era , a 42-7 manhandling of the Indianapolis Colts that saw the starters only have to play three quarters. So, who are the biggest winners and losers from the big win? We break it down below.
We said coming into the game that Trevor Lawrence was due for an MVP-level performance, and that is exactly what he put together on Sunday. Lawrence went 10-of-14 for 210 yards and three touchdown passes, giving him a passer rating of 153.3. Lawrence had one of the most efficient quarterback outings of the last plus-decade with his performance, and he is just looking more and more like an MVP candidate with each performance.
Efficency at its best 👌 Trevor Lawrence is the first QB with 3 Pass TDs on fewer than 15 pass attempts since Carson Palmer on Oct. 11, 2015. He finished the day going 10/14, 210 yards with 3 TDs. pic.twitter.com/Qn2jWxsUQF
Lawrence has been able to put together some of the best performances of his career over the course of the season, and there is a good argument to make that there is no better quarterback playing football right now than Lawrence. He didn't need to try very hard against the Colts, and it hardly even mattered.
Bhayshul Tuten has made himself the clear RB1 over the course of his second season, and he was able to establish himself once more with the best game of his career on Sunday with 16 carries for 104 yards and a touchdown, along with two catches for 55 yards and another touchdown. Tuten became the first Jaguars running back to rush for 100 yards and record 50+ receiving yards while also scoring a touchdown on the ground and through the air. He did something Fred Taylor and Maurice Jones-Drew never did, which says it all. Consider letting Travis Etienne walk a genius move from James Gladstone.
"Yeah, it was awesome. I thought Tuten played really well, was seeing it. Thought he was a little bit more patient this game, was running through contact, obviously, was explosive in the pass game as well, which was nice to see in the screens," Liam Coen said after the game.
What a game from Branson Combs. The Jaguars' second-year linebacker had his first-career interception, several big tackles on special teams, and nearly had a second interception. Combs had a terrific training camp for the Jaguars and turned in the best perofrmance of his career on Sunday, all while rebounding from some lesser performances earlier in the season, such as Week 2 against the Denver Broncos.
"I mean, there's some plays I'd like to get back throughout the year, especially early in the year, and just going through it every week, repping it, continuing to get better, continuing to be more confident in what I'm doing," Combs said after the game.
How many Jaguars have made bigger plays in spots than Rayuan Lane this season? For the secod time in eight games, Lane came off the bench due to injuries at safety and made a giant play. It was his game-winning tackle against the Cincinnati Bengals last time and then his 92-yard pick-six of Daniel Jones in the blowout win on Sunday. Lane has stepped up for the Jaguars in a big way throughout the season, and Sunday was the best example yet.
"Rayuan with the huge interception. That kind of really broke the game open. It was a massive play to stay focused throughout the tip and be able to control that ball and take it to the house," Liam Coen said after the game. "He's made a number of those plays, right? Big plays for us this year. And we need it, right? We need some guys to step up today. Had some guys get nicked up, and when you have second-year players that have been primarily special teams contributors step up and make plays for you on defense, that's huge."
That was a very nice moment for Brian Thomas Jr., who has been the subject of trade talks for the last few weeks. Thomas was only targeted twice in the low-volume passing day, but he turned one of those into a 12-yard red-zone touchdown after the Jaguars faced 3rd-and-12. It was a nice catch in the middle of the field, the area he has struggled in, and it led to a very loud "BTJ" chant from the home crowd and an emotional spike of the ball from Thomas. That was a very nice response to some real adversity.
The Jaguars' rookie tight end just keeps making plays when his number is called. Boerkircher said after the game that he feels like the game has slowed down for him, and it has shown with two touchdown catches in his last two games. Boerkircher's 31-yard touchdown in the first-half was designed just for him and it was the biggest play he has made as a rookie, all while still doing a lot of good things in the running game. His stock keeps rising.
If there is one area of the Jaguars' offense that didn't shine on Sunday, it was some of the pass protection. Trevor Lawrence was sacked three times and pressured quite a bit more, and right tackle Cole Van Lanen was guilty on the worst of those sacks. Van Lanen has had an up-and-down season thus far, which is not ideal for a Jaguars team that already lost left tackle Anton Harrison to a season-ending injury.
The Jaguars' run defense had an elite game, but they did lose Davon Hamilton in the first half to a non-contact injury that saw him get carted off. Hamilton is the key to the Jaguars' run defense, and losing him for an extended period of time could really hurt this tea,.
"Yeah, extremely difficult. There's not many better humans, better competitors, team guys. You should have saw D-Ham this week in practice. His leadership and defensive line, individual periods this week," Coen said. "Just the human, the competitor. I can't say enough about him. When he's out there laying down and he's reassuring me. That's who he is. He's reassuring me, and has a smile on his face, actually. He trusts God. He trusts himself. He trusts life. He's just one of those types of people. Tough to see that, obviously. Really tough. So have to evaluate what it truly is."
We will see if the film says anything differently, but for now it looks like Jourdan Lewis was on the wrong end of the lone touchdown the Jaguars allowed. He has allowed three touchdowns in the red-zone this season, making him the only defensive back who is struggling to contain big plays in that end of the field.

title: 9 Instant Observations on Jaguars' Homecoming Blowout of Colts: Trevor Lawrence Makes MVP Case
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars added another chapter to their long, storied history of domination over the Colts on Sunday.
The Jaguars completely throttled the Colts in a 42-7 blowout that looked more like a homecoming game scheduled agains thte smaller, plucky school from the next county than an AFC South rivalry game. The Jaguars are now 5-2 as a result, and here is everything we saw.
The Jaguars were always expected to blow the Colts out. Even if the Colts didn't trade Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, this would have been a game the Jaguars should have been expected to win by multiple scores. Once the Colts stripped their team of two All-Pro trench players, it obviously became a bit easier, but that still doesn't quite put into context just how bad of a beatdown the Jaguars gave the Colts.
The Jaguars had 42 points in the first three quarters alone. They had yet another game where Trevor Lawrence could just watch and sip Gatorade from the sidelines during the fourth quarter, and this was in a game against AFC South rivals who one would think would be inspired, both by the team's maangement throwing up the white flag and by the fact that they haven't won here in a decade-plus. But that isn't what happened. The Jaguars and Colts played two different sports Sunday, and it will likely take the Colts quite some time to earn the right to compete with the Jaguars in a close game.
Trevor Lawrence just keeps winning, and he just keeps throwing touchdown passes. He had his fourth game of the season with three touchdown passes or more on Sunday after touchdown tosses to Brian Thomas Jr., Nate Boerkircher, and Bhayshul Tuten, and it seemed like he did all of it without ever really breaking a sweat. Even the most superhuman plays that Lawrence puts forth have started to look routine, such as his first-half touchdown to Boerkircher.
Trevor Lawrence finds a wide open Nate Boerkircher for his 2nd TD  pass of the first half! INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/H3ubmhXBZo
Trevor Lawrence keeps stacking MVP-level performances, and he now has 17 touchdowns/4 interceptions for a 5-2 team that looks like one of the best in the NFL. He finished the day 10-of-14 for 210 yards and three touchdowns, putting the Colts away in what was one of the more efficient and surgical performances of his NFL career.
If there was one position where the Jaguars simply could not sustain a serious injury, it was defensive tackle. The Jaguars were already thin when it came to impact players along their interior defensive line, and as a result we have seen the Jaguars connected to the defensive tackle market ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. That pressing need became a whole lot more pressing Sunday after the first-half knee injury to nose tackle Davon Hamilton, who stayed on the field for quite a while before being carted off.
Hamilton has been arguably the Jaguars' defensive MVP through the first third of the season, and losing him for any time would be a big blow. Losing him for an extended period of time, though, would be the kind of injury that would likely force the Jaguars to make some kind of move for defensive tackle help sooner than later.
We have seen Travis Hunter return punts during practices for a few months now, but the Jaguars had not let him return a punt during the first six games of the season. That changed on Sunday, though, with Hunter as the Jaguars' punt returner on the second- and third-punt returns of the game after Parker Washington handled the first punt return. Washington did return the fourth punt, but it was notable the Jaguars put Hunter on the field in that situation.
Hunter is fresh off arguably the most electric game of his NFL career , so it makes sense the Jaguars would want to give him more chances to get the ball in his hands. The two punts he was out there for resulted in one fair catch and one downed punt so we didn't see any fireworks yet, but it was an interesting wrinkle that the Jaguars will likely continue to add to.
The Jaguars already had a safety issue entering the game due to injuries, with starting safety Antonio Johnson held out of practice all week with an injury and second-year safety Caleb Ransaw still on injured reserve after his Week 4 knee injury. Things got worse for the Jaguars early on in Sunday's contest, too, with starting safety Eric Murray injured on the game's opening kickoff with a left elbow injury. Murray was quickly ruled out of the game, which is normally not a great sign.
Jacksonville could get Johnson back on the field against the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday Night Football, but it sure feels like they could be without Murray on a short week. With the backup safeties consisting of special teamer Rayuan Lane, backup Kaevon Merriweather, and rookie safety Jalen Huskey, who can't find the field, the Jaguars might need to make some kind of move for a safety
We noted earlier in the week that getting Montaric Brown back in the lineup could be good news for the Jaguars' cornerback room since it would allow them to experiment more and that is exactly what we saw happen on Sunday. With Brown back on the field, the Jaguars were able to start Brown at the outside cornerback spot across from Travis Hunter and move Jarrian Jones to his more natural spot in the slot.
The Jaguars are at their best when they have their top-four cornerbacks available like they did today. That goes without saying of course, but it is especially true with the way the Jaguars like to utilize their cornerback room. Jones was stuck on the outside during the time that Brown was held off the field due to his hamstring injury. It isn't surprising that the coverage was stickier on Sunday as a result.
Things went mostly perfectly for the Jaguars in all three phases today, but there was one area where I thought the Jaguars were not only iffy in, but a potential red flag has been raised. The Jaguars' offensive line allowed far too many sacks and hits on Trevor Lawrence on Sunday, and it came from a variety of spots: Cole Van Lanen was beat badly during a first-half sack, the running backs missed a few blitzes, and Emmanuel Pregnon had a so-so day.
This is concerning because the Colts have one of the worst pass-rushes in the entire NFL. The Colts haven't been able to get pressure on anyone this season, but they were able to get after Lawrence quite a bit more often than they should have been able to. For as well as the Jaguars' line did in the running game, they had an off day in terms of pass protection.
On a wet and sloppy weather day in Jacksonville, there was bound to be a good amount of slipping around on Sunday. The conditions played out like many thought they would with a heavy dose of rain after the first-quarter, and that is around the time we started to see the injuries pile up. There was the Hamilton and Murray injuries, of course, but they aren't the only ones. Ezra Cleveland (ankle) and Travon Walker (ribs) also sustained injuries during the blowout, making both trenches a spot to watch moving forward.
The Jaguars started the season without many injuries, but they are starting to pile up a bit. Safety has been hit hard, and an injury to Cleveland would mean the second Jaguars offensive lineman to go on the mend in the last month after Anton Harrison's season-ending injury. The bye week didn't get the Jaguars that much healthier, and then injuries got a good bit worse on Sunday.
Liam Coen has been saying for a few weeks now that while he has been happy with the progress and improvement from the running game, he is also looking for the ground attack to get more explosive over the final few months of the season. title: Veteran Jaguars WR Jakobi Meyers' Week 8 Status vs. Colts Revealed
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have announced their list of inactives against the Indianapolis Colts for Week 8, and there is one key name left off the list.
Jaguars wide receiver Jakobi Meyers is officially active for the Jaguars after being listed as questionable with an ankle/hamstring injury earlier in the week. Meyers did not practice on Friday, but he is set to play for the Jaguars in their key Week 8 AFC South battle with the Indianapolis Colts.
Having Meyers available is good news for a Jaguars' passing game that has been ascending all season long. Meyers has been one of the Jaguars' most reliable and impactful pass-catchers since he was traded to the roster last November and he is a key reason Trevor Lawrence has been playing at an MVP-level ever since then.
With Meyers set to play, that does create some other questions in the receiver room. Meyers and Parker Washington are the clear top-two wideouts, and then the Jaguars will have to figure out how they want to deploy Brian Thomas Jr., Josh Cameron, and two-way star Travis Hunter against a struggling Colts team.
The official inactives for the Jaguars on Sunday are as follows: safety Antonio Johnson, defensive end Wesley Williams, defensive tackle Albert Regis, wide receiver CJ Williams, cornerback Alijah Huzzie, and linebacker Jamal Hill. The Jaguars will have cornerback Montaric Brown back on the field.
The Jaguars will certainly need Meyers and the rest of Lawrence's supporting cast in Week 8. While the Colts have been sending away their top players all week long while keeping their other top players waiting to see what will happen to their future.
"I think we have a ton of confidence and belief that we're a really good team. And how good is that? I think we all want to find out," Lawrence said earlier this week when discussing the Colts matchup. "And the only way that happens is if you put the work in every day, put your best foot forward and just take it one week at a time and we'll see where we stack up at the end of this thing.
"I think that's where there's a lot of confidence in our team, but there's also the reality that you have to take it one day at a time. It doesn't matter how good you think you are. You look at our schedule, we got 11 games left, and there's a long road before we even talk about postseason and all that stuff. So, we got a lot of work to do, and I think our team is just focused on today and then tomorrow and getting ready for Sunday as opposed to the big picture of what we could do.”
John Shipley has been covering the Jacksonville Jaguars as a beat reporter and publisher of Jaguar Report since 2019. Previously, he covered UCF's undefeated season as a beat reporter for NSM.Today, covered high school prep sports in Central Florida, and covered local sports and news for the Palatka Daily News. title: Chiefs Stock Watch: Kansas City Failed Patrick Mahomes in Week 8 Defeat to Broncos
full_text:
Life comes at you quickly in the NFL, and the Kansas City Chiefs are perhaps the best example of that right now. In a matter of just two Sundays, the team's gone from riding high as an undefeated powerhouse to a club that's licking its wounds after suffering back-to-back losses.
Week 7's defeat at the hands of the Seattle Seahawks was a beatdown, but Week 8's shortcoming against the Denver Broncos raised the panic level even more. Despite some inspired performances from multiple players, others served as big enough culprits to drag everyone else down with them.
Let's dive into the good and bad from Week 8's Chiefs loss against Denver and single out three players whose stock is trending up, as well as three who could use a better showing in Week 9 and beyond.
These players stood out for positive reasons on Sunday, potentially changing the trajectory of their seasons in the process.
After going consecutive contests with no touchdown passes and an interception, quarterback Patrick Mahomes found himself on the wrong end of the post-Week 7 edition of this column. That came with a sentiment that he wouldn't be there for long, which wound up being the case thanks to his rebound effort on Sunday in the Mile High City.
Mahomes completed a staggering 30 of his 41 pass attempts for 321 yards and a trio of touchdowns, also going without a turnover for the first time in nearly a month. The two-time MVP was crisp, efficient and did a nice job of extending plays when needed. According to RBSDM , No. 15 was good for 0.24 EPA per play, and that might've been selling him short.
Kansas City let an improved Mahomes outing go to waste, which is a shame for everyone involved.
Entering Sunday's play, rookie running back Emmett Johnson had failed to receive a single rushing attempt in two of his previous three games. In the one contest he did get some work in, it was a three-tote, six-yard output against the Los Angeles Chargers. That left many to wonder whether the fifth-round pick would see an increased role at any point, only for the course to completely reverse on Sunday.
Johnson experienced by far his best game as a professional, and he did it in multiple ways. As a receiver, he made the most of his five targets by ripping off five catches for 128 yards and his first regular-season touchdown. He also broke off about as fun and hard-earned a 15-yard rush as you'll ever see. His work didn't stop there — he had a nice kickoff return on special teams, too.
The Nebraska product's blend of tough running, contact balance, smarts and improving pass protection make him closer to a starting-caliber player than someone who should be buried on the depth chart. Kansas City's completely revamped its halfback room in the best of ways.
Being a nose tackle in the pros is a pretty thankless job. Oftentimes, it's your name not being called that means you're fulfilling your role at a high level. Everyone knew that'd be primarily the case when Khyiris Tonga signed with the Chiefs earlier this year, but he's making a name for himself. After a six-tackle performance against Seattle, the 30-year-old picked up right where he left off.
Tonga finished with just two tackles in Week 8, but one was a run stop on halfback J.K. Dobbins that stood out on tape. He also batted a pass in the second half of play and, per Pro Football Focus , was credited with a pressure on quarterback Bo Nix. On an afternoon and evening that saw several members of the Chiefs fall short, Tonga Time was out in full force.
This group of three didn't meet the appropriate level of expectations in Week 8 and desperately needs to recover moving forward.
Another week, another instance of star center Creed Humphrey failing to do perhaps the simplest part of his complex job. How concerning is it that a four-time Pro Bowler and two-time All-Pro has been charged with a career-high six fumbles before the season is even halfway over? Humphrey acknowledged last week that he was working on resolving his problem, then he proceeded to fail again in a pressure-packed game.
Head coach Andy Reid spoke to the media on Monday and said Humphrey simply needs to "get the snaps up," yet it appears to be much easier said than done at this point. Until the former second-round pick strings together a few good showings in a row, it's hard to be confident that he'll put this confusing trend behind him.
When the Chiefs announced that L'Jarius Sneed was going on the injured reserve list and rookie Mansoor Delane would sit out Week 8 , they knew they'd be shorthanded at the cornerback spot. Not many folks doubted the ability of someone like Nohl Williams to get the job done on the outside or someone — anyone — to at least match Sneed's production in the slot, but the jury remained out on Kristian Fulton.
A whopping 60 snaps later, it's virtually impossible to feel much better about Fulton being a viable replacement for anything more than brief stints.
The veteran defensive back committed defensive pass interference on the Broncos' opening drive and later had an illegal block in the back on special teams. In the second quarter, he also totally whiffed on an attempted jam on wideout Courtland Sutton and got burned because of it.
Fulton remains someone who's a valuable depth piece and maybe even a trade chip , but don't confuse him for a starter on the same level of Williams or Delane.
Yes, we're cheating here and including a coach instead of a player. I think it's entirely justified, though, considering how much Reid melted down over the course of Sunday's contest. Penalties and on-field execution by the players were deserving of blame, sure, but Reid's baffling game management is still at or near the top of the list.
When the Chiefs opted to kick to try to go up 6 (never great!) our model had it as a toss-up between go...and punt. It saw field goal attempt as clearly the worst option. pic.twitter.com/Z7ugriKYkj
From botching a fourth-and-short to trotting out placekicker Harrison Butker for a boot he was bound to face an uphill battle to make, Reid fell flat against a bitter rival. He also still isn't explaining what's going on with benching left guard Kingsley Suamataia ; backup Mike Caliendo predictably struggled in relief.
Reid doesn't owe anyone answers, and his track record speaks for itself, but part of that includes decision-making concerns that crept back up at the worst time in Week 8. He needs to bounce back as badly as any of his players do.

title: The Good News and Bad News About the 2026 Kansas City Chiefs
full_text:
After back-to-back losses in the last two weeks , the Kansas City Chiefs are no longer the No. 1 seed in the AFC. They no longer hold the top spot in the AFC West . They've split with the Denver Broncos, meaning that the head-to-head tiebreaker they earned in Week 1 was one of many things wasted in their Week 8 meltdown.
Still, there is good news and bad news about where the Chiefs stand, particularly in the AFC. Do you want the good news first or the bad news?
The illusion of choice strikes again. It's all the same news.
Until further notice, the Chiefs are just another flawed contender in the AFC. How that makes you feel is a matter of perspective.
The AFC has somewhere between six and 10 teams that I could genuinely see making a playoff push that lands them in the AFC Championship Game. I could also see any of those teams being ousted in the wild card round. Sure, the Buffalo Bills seem like the worthy favorite, but who could be surprised by a mistake-filled opening-round loss to a barely-qualifying Houston Texans team that forces a few turnovers in January? No, I don't really believe in the Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) or Cleveland Browns (5-3), but at least one of those teams seems likely to be playing in the postseason, even if the Cincinnati Bengals (5-2) end up winning the AFC North.
Meanwhile, those heating-up Bengals just needed overtime to squeak past the lowly Tennessee Titans. Before that, they handled the Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore Ravens. Before that, they beat the then-winless Miami Dolphins by just seven points.
Look around the AFC and you'll see a wave of competent but unspectacular teams who do some things well and some things poorly. The good news is that the Chiefs still exist firmly within that class. The bad news is that they have been better than that for the majority of the Patrick Mahomes era.
The Chiefs, quarterbacked by Mahomes and with the AFC's only Super Bowl rings since Tom Brady's New England Patriots, are essentially neck-and-neck with Bo Nix's Broncos. Right there with the AFC North contenders who leave me uninspired. Tied in the standings with the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Bills are the only AFC squad with just one loss through eight weeks.
Kansas City isn't standing above their competition, reclaiming their boogeyman status for the rest of the AFC. They aren't sitting in the basement with other squads focusing on their 2027 NFL Draft boards. They're just sharing "flawed contender" status with the rest of the conference that has high hopes and measured expectations.
The Chiefs' path to the top should still be more climbable than others—Mahomes alone changes the math of what Kansas City can accomplish—but the Chiefs have enough flaws and have suffered enough self-inflicted wounds now that it's no longer reasonable to expect the best at every turn. Could they still represent the AFC in the Super Bowl? Absolutely. Could they be bounced weeks prior? Sure could. Just like everybody else.

title: Chiefs’ Need for a Wide Receiver Becomes Even More Glaring After Second Straight Loss
full_text:
After falling 28-24 to the Broncos yesterday, the Kansas City Chiefs suffered their second consecutive defeat and effectively lost their hold on the AFC West. Denver scored 15 unanswered points in the final quarter as the Chiefs' offense completely stalled out.
While the defense was largely responsible for the fourth-quarter collapse and Patrick Mahomes had one of his best statistical performances of the year, the issues with KC's offense became even more glaring . Andy Reid's squad had three opportunities to put points on the board in the final quarter and came up empty every time, including a two-minute drill where one more touchdown could have won the game.
Aside from Rashee Rice, who made his return from a hamstring injury, no Chiefs wideout surpassed 20 yards on the day. It was painfully evident down the stretch that Mahomes and his unit had no reliable options open downfield. This inevitably brought back doubts about the state of the wide receiving corps. During Monday morning's segment of Get Up on ESPN, NFL insider Adam Schefter resurfaced the idea that Kansas City has been actively searching for targets for Mahomes to throw to. He suggested it would be a surprise if a new face does not join the pass-catching group by next week's trade deadline.
"I think they are looking around for a wide receiver," Schefter said. "I think it would be a surprise if they didn't make some type of deal for some receiver before next Tuesday's trade deadline at 4 p.m. Eastern. They're going to look for a wide receiver, but that doesn't change that idea that this team needs better help up front and better play from its offensive tackle position."
“I think it would be a surprise if [the Chiefs] didn’t make some type of deal for some receiver before next Tuesday's trade deadline.” — @AdamSchefter on what he believes the Kansas City Chiefs will do heading into the trade deadline. pic.twitter.com/MopDZBiFru
Whether a move for a receiver comes later today or an hour before the deadline, general manager Brett Veach knows this is a primary point of concern for the Chiefs. It's only a matter of time before he pulls the trigger on a deal.
Even in a contest where the offense looked effective across three quarters, Kansas City's need for a receiver has become even more apparent. We've already explored a number of players they could look to acquire before the deadline, though the caliber of receiver they get depends on the draft capital they are willing to give up and the salary they are willing to take on.
Since losing Tyquan Thornton earlier this season to a dislocated ankle, the Chiefs' passing attack has often looked anemic. Thornton had unexpectedly emerged as perhaps Mahomes' favorite deep target, and his absence has been a significant blow. No matter how much we try to defend Xavier Worthy on a weekly basis, the reality is that he hasn't been living up to his billing as a WR2 . His route running has been anything but crisp, he struggles to make defenders miss in the open field, and his lack of size makes him a liability when he cannot utilize his speed in a straight line.
Internal options Cyrus Allen and Jalen Royals have flashed their talent at times, but it doesn't feel like they are ready to take on a prominent role just yet at this point in their careers. The outrage from Chiefs Kingdom if KC simply turned to its in-house prospects would be immense.
Going into this season, there were already lingering questions about the receiver group and how it would fare. Losing Thornton early in the year and seeing how the offense looked without Rice only magnified those concerns.
Schefter and many other reporters have confirmed the notion that Kansas City has been exploring the trade market. If the front office is truly committed to maximizing the championship window and giving Mahomes the weapons he needs, a trade needs to be made as soon as possible.
