title: 10 Takeaways From Rams' Win Over Chargers: Blake Corum Shines, WR3 Concerns Grow
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams won back-to-back games for the first time this season as they defeated the Los Angeles Chargers, 24-9. It may not have been as convincing as some had hoped, but the Rams are back to .500. Let’s get into this week’s 10 takeaways.
If Sunday’s game against the Chargers didn’t make it obvious, the Rams need a third wide receiver. While 13 personnel is a big part of the offense, they still use 11 personnel at a 54.6 percent rate. It’s true that Terrance Ferguson and Davante Adams will come back, but can the Rams trust either to stay healthy?
The Rams used 11 personnel at a 75 percent rate in the first half and it was clear that Matthew Stafford was unsettled and uncomfortable throwing to players not named Puka Nacua. Stafford's interception came when targeting Konata Mumpfield, and he wasn't always on the same page as Jordan Whittington.
“I have a ton of reps with Puka. I think our tight ends are doing a great job. Tutu did a really nice job today, had a couple opportunities,” said Stafford after the game. “It's something that will continuously build, but excited to move forward.”
There will come a point when the Rams have to rely on 11 personnel again and when that happens, it gets very difficult to rely on role players. It’s not sustainable.
In the first half, the Rams had five rushing attempts for just 10 yards. The Rams were averaging -0.02 EPA per rush with a 40 percent success rate. For much of the first half, the Rams couldn’t get into a rhythm running the football and that showed as they didn’t get a first down on their first five drives.
To start the second half, Corum ran the ball four consecutive times for 32 yards and then capped off the drive with a 23-yard touchdown run. Corum finished with 11 carries for 73 yards and found the end zone for a second straight week. When the offense and run game needed a spark of energy , it was Corum who provided it.
There’s no doubt that the Rams’ passing game goes through Puka Nacua.When the passing game finally found success, it came as the Rams got Nacua more involved. He was on the other end of 11 of Stafford’s 17 completions and was responsible for 80 of his 157 yards.
With the performance, Nacua has 12 games with at least 10 receptions in his career, surpassing Ja’Marr Chase for the second-most games with at least 10 receptions by a player in his first four seasons in NFL history. His 56 receptions in his first six games are tied with Cooper Kupp for the second-most receptions by a player in their first six games of a season in NFL history. If Nacua hadn’t missed two games, he’d be in the Offensive Player of the Year conversation.
The only undrafted free agent to make the Rams’ roster this season was edge rusher Wesley Bailey. Bailey had a fantastic preseason and left the Rams with no choice but to keep him. Through the first eight games of the season, he’s played a role in the pass rush rotation.
While Bailey hasn’t surpassed Josaiah Stewart on the depth chart, he’s still making his presence felt. He had a good hustle play to create a sack-fumble opportunity and has gotten better in the run game. For as little of an impact as the Rams’ rookie class has had as a whole, Bailey continues to be a bright spot.
When the Rams were able to execute the dirty kickoff, it worked as intended. However, there were two instances in which the ball didn’t make it to the landing zone, and the Rams were given a penalty and the Chargers started at the 40-yard line. However, when it did work, the Chargers started at the 23, 28, and 19. It’s something worth continuing if the Rams can find consistency.
“You go back and forth because if you're going to kick touchbacks, that ends up being a five-yard penalty if you put it on the 40 when we ended up landing it short of the landing zone twice. We have to be better in that area,” said McVay. “When we were able to cover it because he hit a good ball that's hard to field, just based on the semantics of how the play is officiated, you're telling me they're not going to be able to field it clean and we're getting a start before they're getting their return set up and the momentum to be able to field it, that was the thinking behind it.”
We’ll see if the Rams continue the approach next week. It was certainly unconventional to roster two kickers on game day and for one just to handle kickoffs. Still, if the Rams can get it to work, it’s an approach that might pay off and end up helping their kickoff coverage unit.
In the first half against the Chargers, the Rams operated out of 11 personnel at a 75 percent rate. Without Colby Parkinson, the Rams were forced out of their usual 13 personnel and the offense struggled because of it. While they were able to get away with that in Week 4 against the Philadelphia Eagles, not having Davante Adams on Sunday made that very difficult.
For the first time in the McVay era, the Rams went three-and-out and were without a first down on each of their first five drives. In the second half, the Rams got back to what they do best and used 13 personnel at a 63.6 percent rate. That helped the run game as Corum and Williams combined for 22 carries for 119 yards in the second half.
“It was just better execution,” said McVay. “There was a little bit different approach, but all we were interested in doing was coming away with the win. I thought we were able to do that and we'll learn from it.”
As the offense struggled, the defense kept the Rams in the game. Quentin Lake had an early interception to put the Rams on the board. Later, Trent McDuffie had an interception as well that the offense used to put the game away. Based on EPA, the Chargers had their worst game offensively all year against the Rams’ defense.
The Rams kept the Chargers out of the end zone and didn’t allow a touchdown for the second time in three weeks. They created opportunities with turnovers and sacked Herbert twice. It was an overall good performance from the defense and they should only get better when Myles Garrett returns.
Without Trent McDuffie in the lineup the previous two weeks, the Rams have done enough to get by. Both Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes have stepped in well. With that said, Sunday was a reminder why he’s such an important piece of the defense.
McDuffie intercepted Herbert, but his ability to tackle in space is also important. He was targeted just once in the game and had the turnover. McDuffie is critical to what the Rams do on defense and when he’s been on the field, he’s played like one of the best cornerbacks in the NFL.
With the Rams trailing 9-3 with less than two minutes to go in the half and not having a single first down, it appeared like Sunday was going to be a struggle. Then, Stafford hit Atwell for a big play, and the Rams scored to take the lead and didn’t look back. After experiencing something similar two weeks ago against the Arizona Cardinals, it would have been easy for the Rams to accept how it was going to be. Instead, they responded and took control of the game.
That’s not to say they don’t need to be better. Stafford had a QBR of 35.7, which is the third time this season that he’s had a QBR under 50. Offensively, the Rams need to find some consistency. Still, when things got tough, the Rams powered through it and did enough to get the win.
Again, the win wasn’t perfect. The Rams followed up a great offensive performance last week with one in which they went nearly an entire half without a first down. However, this was the first time this season in which the Rams earned back-to-back wins and that’s a step in the right direction. The Rams can finally start to pick up some momentum and build on what they’re doing. There’s still plenty of room for improvement, but winning a second straight game was important.
The Rams need to be able to keep this going. With the Commanders and Cardinals on deck, the Rams will have an opportunity to head into the bye week at 6-4. As they get healthy, the Rams should start to find their stride…

title: Monday Morning Rambling: Rams Are Starting to Look Like Themselves Again
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams beat the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday to improve to 4-4, but it didn’t come easy. There was a moment during the Rams’ bad start when they had to ask themselves if that was just something they were going through or if that was who they had become.
Throughout much of the first seven games of the season, the Rams have lacked consistency. After taking the Buffalo Bills to overtime and playing their best game of the season, the Rams lost to the Arizona Cardinals the next week. The Rams played a great game against the Las Vegas Raiders, but through five drives on Sunday, the offense didn’t have a first down.
Then, Matthew Stafford found Tutu Atwell down the left sideline for a 40-yard gain and Kyren Williams capped off the drive with a touchdown before the end of the first half. To start the second half, Blake Corum got in on the action as well, scoring from 23 yards out. With the passing game struggling, Puka Nacua stepped up in the way that he always seems to.
After struggling to move the ball for much of the first half, the Rams finally started to move their season forward. It wasn’t perfect, but the win did provide something they needed. They responded in a positive way and earned back-to-back wins for the first time this season to get back to .500.
The Rams are playing complementary football. As the offense struggled to move the ball, the defense provided opportunities and kept the Chargers out of the end zone. Offensively, the Rams are starting to find themselves, and that was the case in the second half as they got back to 13 personnel, despite being without Colby Parkinson.
Coming into the season, the Rams had Super Bowl expectations. A lot has changed since mid-August and the Rams certainly aren’t where they wanted or were supposed to be. Beating an 0-6 Chargers team doesn’t change that. However, they are still in the conversation.
This week, Myles Garrett is expected to return to practice. Tight end Terrance Ferguson will soon return to the field as well. If the Rams can get healthy in December and January, they aren’t a team many will want to face. With the trade deadline approaching, the Rams could still make a move to help get them over the top. If Sunday showed anything, it’s that the Rams still need a wide receiver they can count on outside of Puka Nacua.
The Rams still have a lot to prove. Their win against the Chargers was anything but impressive. However, winning back-to-back games has given the Rams a reason to keep going. After losing to the Cardinals two weeks ago, they were a team that had officially hit rock bottom. Since then, they’ve begun the ascent back up to where they belong.
Many have tried to label the Rams as a failed Super Team and the latest example of why that doesn't work. It’s possible that’s true. However, as the Rams continue working toward the team they hoped to be before the season, they have refused to let their early struggles define who they become. If the Rams can pull this off, it won’t be about the destination, but the journey that it took to get there.
During the first half, the reality of the Rams’ wide receiver situation behind Puka Nacua with Davante Adams out became obvious. Maybe Tutu Atwell is just a vertical clear-out guy, Konata Mumpfield and Jordan Whittington are just role players, and CJ Daniels actually wasn’t ready. Nacua caught 11-of-12 targets on Sunday while all other Rams wide receivers combined for two catches on six targets. For much of the first half, Matthew Stafford seemed unsettled and didn’t trust his throws when he wasn’t targeting Nacua.
This season, Mumpfield is averaging -0.32 EPA per target with a 38.1 percent targeted success rate. Whittington is averaging -0.43 EPA per target with a 25 percent success rate. Atwell has a role, but is limited. The Rams need a reliable option. Mumpfield, Whittington, and Atwell are all role players. It’s not sustainable to rely on them consistently, and for as much as the Rams operate out of 13 personnel, they still need wide receiver depth .
There is no doubt that the Rams’ running game is at its best when both Blake Corum and Kyren Williams are getting involved. It’s understandable that the Rams want to use both players in a rotation. However, there are games such as yesterday in which the Rams need to be ok with just riding the hot hand. Corum was averaging 6.6 yards per carry with a 54.5 percent success rate. Williams averaged 3.5 yards per carry with a 43.8 percent success rate. The 1-2 format has proven to be successful, but it was evident against the Chargers that Corum was the more effective player.
It’s another week, which means we’re once again talking about the Rams’ special teams unit. Overall, it looked better. When the dirty kickoff worked, it was effective. The Rams just need to find some consistency and hopefully another week of practice provides that. Ethan Evans had a solid day punting with a net average of 49.2 yards. Alex Bachman remains reliable, but doesn’t offer much outside of that. There is still room for improvement, but the Rams appear to be taking positive steps forward.
Sean McVay handed game balls to Quentin Lake and Trent McDuffie, and they were certainly deserving. However, for a second consecutive week, Blake Corum gets my game ball. When the offense needed energy and a spark, he provided that. Corum began the second half with four straight carries for 32 yards and then capped it off with a 23-yard touchdown run. The Rams’ ability to go from down 9-3 to winning 17-9 by scoring immediately before and after the half helped them take control of the game.
My stat of the day is 43.6. That's the percentage-point difference in how often the Rams operated out of 13 personnel in the first half compared to the second half. Without Colby Parkinson, the Rams tried to operate out of 11 personnel, but it wasn’t working. They simply aren’t built for it, especially without Adams. The Rams forced 13 personnel in the second half and that’s when the run game and play action passing game off of that finally got going. The Rams operated out of 13 personnel at a 20 percent rate in the first half compared to a 63.6 percent rate in the second half. That adjustment turned out to be key in the Rams winning.
The Rams earned back-to-back wins for the first time this season and will need to prove they can keep it going. They will head to Washington to play a Commanders team that has played the NFC West hard this season. The Commanders beat the Seattle Seahawks and then lost to the San Francisco 49ers by six.
If the Rams are going to beat the Commanders, they need to be much better than they were against the Chargers. That game will have a 10 a.m. PT start as well. The Rams need to continue building momentum through their bye week and the Commanders should provide an opportunity to do that.

title: 6 Winners and 1 Clear Loser in Rams' 24-9 Win Over Chargers
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams beat the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 8, 24-9, to improve to 4-4 on the season. It may not have been perfect, but the second half was another glimpse of what the Rams can be when they put it all together. While the first half was rough, there was a lot to like in the second half. Here are the winners and losers from Sunday’s win against the Chargers.
For a second consecutive week, Blake Corum provided the spark that the Rams' run game needed. In the first half, the Rams had five carries for 10 yards. On the first drive of the second half, Corum had five carries for 55 yards, capped off by a 23-yard touchdown run. Corum finished with 11 carries for 73 yards, and up until the final drive, he was out-carrying Kyren Williams. Corum has been an ‘x-factor’ over the last two weeks and his 23 yards after forcing missed tackles was a season-high.
Really good day for Blake Corum in the run game. Provided spark and energy that the Rams offense and run game lacked in the first half. Via NFL Pro he generated a season-high 23 yards after forcing missed tackles. pic.twitter.com/eAsW6i32y9
Donald still doesn’t have a sack this season, but his impact was felt throughout the game on Sunday. He had a tackle for loss in the run game and consistently made his presence felt. After a Wesley Bailey strip sack, Donald very nearly had a scoop and score for his first career touchdown. Things are starting to click for Donald once again, and it seems like only a matter of time before he finally gets to the quarterback.
Aaron Donald doing Aaron Donald things 😌 LACvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/kBqz4E1udQ
Over the last two weeks, an argument can be made that Omar Speights has been one of the best defenders on the field. He had four impact plays via Sumer Sports, including a tackle for loss. Speights also had a pass breakup in coverage. He was all over the field and, most importantly, had zero missed tackles.
The first half should have been all the evidence that the Rams needed to convince themselves that they should trade for a wide receiver . Outside of Puka Nacua, Tutu Atwell was the only wide receiver with a reception. Nacua caught 11 of his 12 targets, while Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, and Jordan Whittington combined for two catches on six targets. Stafford’s interception came when targeting Mumpfield. It was evident that Stafford was uncomfortable and unsettled when Nacua wasn’t open. Whether it’s Josh Downs or Brian Thomas Jr., the Rams need to make a trade for a wide receiver.
For the first time in two weeks, Trent McDuffie was back on the field for the Rams’ defense and he made his presence felt. McDuffie led the Rams with nine tackles and also had an interception that turned into a touchdown for the offense. Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes have stepped up well in McDuffie’s place. However, Sunday showed why the Rams traded for him. He’s important to the Rams’ success on defense.
There’s a conversation to be had that Wesley Bailey should be getting more snaps in the edge rusher rotation than Josaiah Stewart. Both players had a sack on Sunday against the Chargers, but it’s hard not to come away impressed with Bailey. Bailey stripped Herbert and forced a fumble on his sack, nearly creating a turnover, and was stout in the run game.. For an undrafted free agent, he is exceeding expectations and has become an important piece of the pass rush.
Josh Karty and the dirty kickoff certainly weren’t perfect. It needs to be more consistent as the Rams can’t give teams the ball at the 40-yard line. With that said, when it did work, the Chargers took over at the 23, 28, and 19. That’s better than what the kickoff coverage unit had been doing. It needs work and a better team would take advantage of the opportunity before the half. However, it seems to be a step in the right direction.

title: Rams Overcome Slow Start to Beat Chargers, but Need for Trade Deadline Help Remains
full_text:
One week after the Los Angeles Rams appeared to find their identity, it looked like they had lost it early against the Los Angeles Chargers. In the second half, the Rams stole it back on their way to a 24-9 win.
On the back of the run game and 13 personnel, the Rams finally found some consistency on offense. However, an injury to Colby Parkinson coming into the game on Sunday changed the entire dynamic and it took time for the Rams to adjust.
In the first half, the Rams operated out of 11 personnel on 75 percent of their offensive plays. When the Rams were without Parkinson against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 4, they at least had Nacua and Davante Adams. As the Rams were forced into 11 personnel on Sunday, they were looking at a rotation of Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, and Jordan Whittington in the passing game.
For the first 28 minutes of the game, the Rams didn’t have a first down. While the offense took advantage of a Quentin Lake interception on Justin Herbert, the Rams’ offense looked broken. Matthew Stafford started the game with an interception and was 6-for-10 for 20 yards until the team’s final drive of the opening half. Stafford didn’t seem comfortable throwing to any wide receiver not named Nacua.
If the Rams needed evidence that they needed to trade for a wide receiver , Sunday certainly provided that. While Nacua caught 11-of-12 targets, Mumpfield, Atwell and Jordan Whittington combined for 2-for-7. Nacua finished with 80 of Stafford’s 157 yards on the day.
Sunday marked the first time in the Sean McVay era that the Rams went their first five offensive drives without a first down. The Rams had 14 yards on their first five drives of the game.
Finally, with less than two minutes to go in the half, the offense got going. Stafford found Tutu Atwell for a gain of 40 yards deep down the left sideline for the team’s first first down of the half, and then hit Nacua open over the middle to set the offense up at the two-yard line. On the next play, Kyren Williams walked into the end zone to give the Rams a 10-9 lead.
After getting away from the run game in the first half and running the ball just five times, the Rams came out with a mission on their opening drive of the third quarter. Blake Corum carried the ball four straight times for 32 yards to spark the run game . Corum then capped the drive off with a 23-yard touchdown run, putting the Rams ahead 17-9.
The Rams made it a point to get back to the same rushing identity that they established last week. In the first half, the Rams ran the ball five times for just 10 yards. Corum and Williams combined for 22 carries for 119 yards in the second half. Both players rushed for a touchdown for a third time this season.
While the offense struggled at times throughout the afternoon, the Rams’ defense remained rock solid. Lake had an interception in the first half and the defense didn’t allow a single touchdown for the second time in three weeks.
Back in the lineup, Trent McDuffie intercepted Herbert in the third quarter to give the offense good field position. The Rams took advantage and took a 24-9 lead as Stafford found Nacua on a back-side screen, and Nacua did the rest.
As the Chargers made a final push in the fourth quarter, Josh Wallace tackled tight end Orande Gadsden one-yard short on 4th-and-8 to force a turnover on downs. The Rams then ran Williams 11 times on the next drive to close out the game.
It certainly wasn’t perfect, but the Rams responded in the second half and the offense did enough when it needed to. For the first time this season, the Rams got back-to-back wins. Coming into the game, the main goal was to find a way to start stacking wins and the Rams did just that. They are now back at .500 before they travel to Washington next week to take on the Commanders.
Through eight games, the Rams have yet to play a complete game and find their stride. However, earning a second straight win is a step in the right direction. Now, the Rams need to build on their current momentum and show that the last two weeks are the beginning of something more.

title: Why a Jonathan Taylor Trade Could Complicate Rams' Pursuit of Josh Downs
full_text:
As the NFL trade deadline approaches, one name the Los Angeles Rams have been connected to is Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs . After the Colts traded franchise cornerstone Quenton Nelson and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner earlier this week, the team officially entered a fire sale. While the team was already fielding calls on Downs, he officially requested a trade. Running back Jonathan Taylor was initially thought to not be available, but trade talks around him have begun to heat up as well.
With Downs reportedly available, the Rams have a prime opportunity to address one of their biggest roster needs at an affordable price. However, if the Colts were to trade Taylor, it could significantly complicate those plans.
There’s no doubt that the Colts are looking to trade players who may not have a future on the team. However, there comes a point when the Colts can only trade so many players before they are no longer competitive. If the Colts trade one, it seems unlikely they would trade the other. Given the haul that the Colts could get in return for Taylor to use in their upcoming rebuild, he may be the preferred option.
Trading Downs even before moving on from Taylor is complicated for the Colts. According to ESPN’s Stephen Holder, the Colts value Downs at a third-round pick and would prefer to keep him. This offseason, the Colts signed Alec Pierce to a large contract, but he’s currently on injured reserve and has been hurt most of the year.
If the Colts were to trade Downs, it would leave them with Keenan Allen, Laquon Treadwell, and Ashton Dulin at wide receiver. Moving on from Taylor and Downs would give the Colts almost no offensive weapons outside of Tyler Warren.
As I noted last week, if the Rams wanted to trade for Downs, they needed to move quickly . Not only was the wide receiver market heating up, but there was always the possibility of the situation changing. The Colts are currently in fire-sale mode, but they won’t stay there forever.
The Colts may be prioritizing the future, but they still need to be able to field a competitive offense to be able to evaluate the players still on the roster. Trading Taylor would already take away the focal point of the offense, and trading Downs would leave them with very little to work with, especially with Pierce injured
This creates a dilemma for the Rams and general manager Les Snead. They could wait until closer to the deadline and for the wide receiver market to take shape. However, waiting also risks the Colts making another blockbuster move by trading Taylor, which could effectively take Downs off the market.
At 25 years old, Downs could be seen as someone the Colts can build a receiver room around when they are ready to compete again. It’s possible that the Colts decide that keeping Downs and trying to extend him this offseason or taking a future compensatory pick is more beneficial than moving him for just a mid-round selection in next year’s draft.
While the Colts were willing to move on from Nelson and Buckner, they may be more reluctant to trade Taylor and Downs. In 2022, the 49ers traded second-, third-, fourth- and fifth-round picks to the Carolina Panthers for running back Christian McCaffrey. That’s a lot more than what the Colts will get for Downs and will give them more assets to help their rebuild.
If the Rams want Downs , they may need to make their move before the Colts make a decision on Taylor. Waiting for the market to settle is typically smart, but in this case, it could cost the Rams an opportunity before the trade deadline. If the Colts decide to trade Taylor, it could change their priorities and make a deal for Downs much more difficult.

title: Rams Sunday Morning Notebook: Optimism Grows for Myles Garrett Return, Trade Buzz Heats Up
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to play the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 8 at SoFi Stadium. With the Chargers entering with an 0-6 record, it’s an opportunity for the Rams to earn their first back-to-back wins of the season.
Sunday will also be unconventional in the sense that both teams share SoFi Stadium. However, not too much will change for either team. Both teams will remain on their typical sideline and use their own team locker rooms. The only difference is that Chargers coaches who typically sit in the booth will use the visiting team's boxes.
With the trade deadline quickly approaching and Myles Garrett’s injury situation ever-changing, there’s a lot to discuss before Sunday’s game. Let’s get into this week’s Sunday Morning Notebook.
A story that continues to drag on for the Rams is when edge rusher Myles Garrett will finally return to the field. Garrett has been on injured reserve since before Week 2, and the timeline for his return continues to get pushed back. However, on Sunday, NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport reported that the Rams are optimistic Garrett will return to practice for Week 9.
“Once again, there is optimism that Myles Garrett will return to practice this week. I know there was optimism last week, much more this week,” said Rapoport. “He should practice and should be on the field playing relatively quickly.”
From @NFLGameDay Morning: The NFL continues to review #Packers RB Josh Jacobs, as more allegations come to light; Plus, the latest on when Micah Parsons and Myles Garrett could return. pic.twitter.com/KKQp1BWAsS
It’s worth noting that Rapoport reported last week that Garrett would return to practice. There is also a key distinction with this report. Rapoport simply reported that there is optimism for Garrett to return to practice. With Garrett on injured reserve, the Rams have the ability to open his 21-day practice window. That allows Garrett to practice for up to 21 days until the team has to decide to elevate him to the roster.
With that being said, even if the Rams activate Garrett’s practice window, that doesn’t mean he would play next week. Given how safe the Rams have played it with Garrett, they could activate his practice window, see how his knee responds to being back in action, and then proceed from there. That’s not to say that Garrett won’t play next week, but a return after the bye remains more realistic. If the Rams open his 21-day practice window this week, they could wait until ahead of their Week 12 matchup with the Green Bay Packers to activate him.
There is some thought that the Rams could try to trade for a wide receiver. However, things have remained quiet on that front as Les Snead waits for the market to shake out. One name who has been connected to the Rams is Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs .
Downs requested a trade from the Colts this week, but according to ESPN’s Stephen Holder , the team would prefer to keep him. While Downs is in the final year of his deal, he is also one of the few healthy targets in the passing game. Alec Pierce has been hurt. If the team deals Jonathan Taylor, Downs would be one of the only playmakers remaining on offense.
Now, that doesn’t mean Downs can’t be had. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Sunday NFL Countdown that the Colts want a third-round pick. Now, that might mean they would take a fourth-round pick, but they don’t appear to be in a rush to trade him.
Also on the wide receiver market, the Jacksonville Jaguars are open to trading Brian Thomas Jr. Thomas is also a player who the Rams have been connected to. There is ongoing belief that the Jaguars will move Thomas by the deadline as his role in the offense continues to decrease.
On Saturday, the Rams elevated kicker Joshua Karty from the practice squad to the active roster, meaning he will play on Sunday against the Chargers. That would give the Rams two kickers active , which is certainly unconventional.
However, given the Rams’ struggles in kickoff coverage, the Rams may use Karty solely on kickoffs. Karty found success with a “knuckleball” kickoff last season, making it difficult for opposing teams to handle kickoffs. With Karty, the Rams allowed a league-best 17.7 yards per return.
The Rams won't want to activate two kickers on gameday all season. Karty only has three eligible practice squad elevations. Ideally, the Rams can activate Karty for the next three games and become comfortable enough with him to eventually take over field goal duties as well. This is certainly going to be a situation to watch, especially as the Rams get healthier going forward and roster spots get more limited. Once that happens, it would be very difficult for the Rams to have two kickers active.
The Carolina Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero on Friday following their loss to the Green Bay Packers. Evero spent five years with the Rams as their safeties coach before being promoted to secondary coach and passing game coordinator.
Evero will be a name to watch for the Rams, especially if Chris Shula ends up getting hired somewhere as a head coach. Shula has led a Rams defense without Myles Garrett to rank 11th in EPA per play and an impressive sixth in EPA per pass allowed. The Rams rank fifth in total defense and sixth in defensive DVOA.
Over the past two years, Shula has garnered head coach interest around the league, and that will likely be the case again this year. If Shula does get hired, Evero will be a top candidate to replace him. It wouldn’t be surprising if the Rams brought Evero back at some point this season as a consultant of some sort.

title: Rams Injury Report: Multiple Key Starters Questionable vs. Chargers in Week 8
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams could be managing several injuries in Week 8 as they take on the Los Angeles Charger s. Center Coleman Shelton, tight end Colby Parkinson, wide receiver Jordan Whittington, and cornerback Trent McDuffie were all listed as questionable for Sunday’s game while long snapper Joe Cardona was listed as doubtful.
Shelton is one of the bigger names on that list given his role as the starting center on the offensive line. Shelton was a non-participant in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but was upgraded to a limited participant on Friday.
If the Rams are without Shelton, they will turn to backup Dylan McMahon. McMahon has been in the system for the past two years, developing on the practice squad. This is the first year he’s spent most of his time on the active roster.
“What's been good is Dylan McMahon has done a great job this week. He's had a lot of work,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Dylan's had a lot of work this week because of the approach we've taken with Coleman. I think he's handled it really well. He's been here for a handful of years so he would be the guy that would step up.”
Another player the Rams will be closely watching heading into Sunday's game is McDuffie, who has missed the last two weeks with a groin injury. While McDuffie was a limited participant in practice all week, he will be listed as questionable against the Chargers. McVay was hopeful about McDuffie going into Sunday, but the Rams can feel confident with the players behind him as Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes have each played well.
Additionally, Parkinson didn’t participate in practice all week. If Parkinson is out, it would likely leave the Rams with just Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen, and Max Klare at tight end and limit what the offense could do out of 13 personnel. Parkinson is extremely valuable in those formations, especially with his ability as a blocker in the run game.
“He brings a lot,” said offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase. “I think he's as good as anybody in the league right now at the point of attack on the line of scrimmage. I think his ability to impact in the pass game has been tremendous. He gives you more than what I think anybody even realizes or expects.”
Popping up on the injury report on Friday was Whittington. McVay noted that Whittington’s back locked up in practice, which is why he’ll be listed as questionable.
On the Chargers’ side, they’ll be without guard Kayode Awosika, safety Derwin James Jr., defensive back Deane Leonard, and wide receiver Brenan Thompson. All four players have been ruled out. Additionally, cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley will be questionable with hamstring injuries.
The Rams have been managing injuries all season and Sunday will be no different. If the Rams are going to win back-to-back games for the first time this season, they’ll be relying on their depth to get by. Going up against the 0-6 Chargers, the Rams will hope that they can get by another week with key starters injured.
