title: Breaking Down the Dolphins Saturday Updates, but More Importantly What Went On with New England
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins made their customary practice squad elevations Saturday, including that should precipitate an upcoming move, but it was what went on with the England Patriots that really was newsworthy.
For the second consecutive week, the Dolphins elevated both kicker Zane Gonzalez and edge defender Max Llewellyn.
Gonzalez was a given considering the Dolphins don't have a kicker on the 53-man roster and it was his second such promotion. After one more elevation, the Dolphins then will have to sign him to the active roster and find themselves a new kicker. And for those wondering, there's no financial or cap incentive to just elevate kickers from the practice squad because that move entails the elevated player getting the prorated active roster salary for that week, along with the accompanying cap hit.
Llewellyn, for his part, actually will be out of practice squad elevations after this week because along with the Week 7 game against the New York Jets, he also was elevated in Week 2 for the game against the San Francisco 49ers.
Llewellyn could put himself in line for a permanent promotion with a strong outing against the Patriots on Sunday. The Dolphins already had five healthy edge defenders for the New England game with Chop Robinson, Josh Uche, Malik Herring, Rodney McGraw and newcomer Jamree Kromah, but the latter just joined the team late in the week and it's almost a given to be inactive.
The big news with the Patriots came earlier Saturday afternoon when the team announced that both wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back TreVeyon Henderson had been downgraded to out after both being listed as questionable Friday.
To replace them, the Patriots signed running back Lan Larison from their practice squad to their 53-man roster and elevated wide receiver Ryan Miller from their practice squad. Yes, that's the same Ryan Miller who played four games for the Dolphins this season and has the team's longest offensive play of 2026 with his 77-yard touchdown reception from Malik Willis toward the end of the Week 2 loss against the San Francisco 49ers.
Brown and Henderson being out is big news for the New England offense, which already has wide receivers Romeo Doubs and former Dolphins player Mack Hollins on injured reserve. With those two out, the biggest threats for the Miami defense, besides obviously QB Drake Maye, will be running back Rhamondre Stevenson and tight end Hunter Henry.
New England's top three wide receivers for Sunday will be Kyle Williams, Efton Chism III and DeMario Douglas. Corey Kiner will become the second running back option after Stevenson.

title: The Chris Grier Firing One Year Later: Revisiting the Former Dolphins GM's Hits and Misses
full_text:
Halloween arrived Saturday, but for the Miami Dolphins it also marked the one-year anniversary of the firing of Chris Grier as general manager, a move that was met with almost universal approval from the team's frustrated fans.
His eventual replacement, Jon-Eric Sullivan, has on the flip side won over a lot of folks with his early moves in a massive rebuilding project that was almost necessary because of previous mistakes by his predecessors and the other decision-makers in the organization.
While Sullivan's draft class has the looks at this time of a slam-dunk winner with the early contributions of Kadyn Proctor, Chris Johnson, Jacob Rodriguez, Caleb Douglas and Michael Taaffe, though it probably will take some time to offer an accurate verdict, and the same goes for the most involving the veterans (though, again, the Jaylen Waddle trade looks a winner at this time).
Grier's firing came on the morning of October 31, 2025, hours after the Dolphins dropped a 28-6 Thursday night decision against the Baltimore Ravens at Hard Rock Stadium.
Sullivan was hired as GM in January after Champ Kelly finished out the 2025 season as interim GM, making one trade during his time.
That was the move to send Jaelan Phillips to the Philadelphia Eagles in exchange for a third-round pick, a decision that was sound at the time and even more so now after the huge contract Phillips got in the offseason from the Carolina Panthers as an unrestricted free agent.
Grier had taken over that role in 2016 after more than a decade with the organization, though in many ways he assumed true GM duties in 2019 after the Dolphins moved on from Executive Vice President of Football Operations Mike Tannenbaum.
The Dolphins failed to win a playoff game during Grier's time as GM, extending a drought that began in Grier's first year with the team in 2000.
Along the way, Grier oversaw a series of personnel decisions that did lead the Dolphins to the playoffs three times, including his first year in 2016, but also came up way short considering all the financial commitments the Dolphins made.
In breaking down the Dolphins' personnel decisions, we should point out that the organization always went out of its way to talk about a collaborative approach but as GM the hits and misses should fall on Grier more than anybody else.
And, without question, it's in the draft where Grier had most of his misses.
-- The Dolphins whiffed on too many early draft picks over the past decade, a trend that started with first-round pick Charles Harris in 2017 and continued with Noah Igbinoghene in 2020, Liam Eichenberg in 2021, Channing Tindall in 2022 and Cam Smith in 2023.
-- The Dolphins also missed out on some big-time talent, which happens to every franchise but seemed to happen more often for Miami. Just last year, the Dolphins took Kenneth Grant at number 13, one spot before the Colts took Tyler Warren, and that decision still doesn't look very good 18 months after the fact. But while the final verdict isn't in on that dubious choice, here's a long list of more clear regrettable choices:
• DE Charles Harris over T.J. Watt in 2017 Round 1 • QB Tua Tagovailoa over Justin Herbert in 2020 Round 1 (yes, even though Herbert is struggling badly with former Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel as his new offensive coordinator this year) • T Austin Jackson over WR Justin Jefferson in 2020 Round 1 • CB Noah Igbinoghene over RB Jonathan Taylor or S Antoine Winfield in 2020 Round 1 • OL Liam Eichenberg over C Creed Humphrey or LB Nick Bolton in 2021 Round 2 • CB Cam Smith over OLB Tuli Tuipulotu or G O'Cyrus Torrence or TE Tyler Kraft in 2023 Round 2 • OLB Chop Robinson over CB Quinyon Mitchell in 2024 Round 1
-- The Dolphins also made a lot of high-profile trades under Grier when they decided to go all in to try to make a deep run into the playoffs and came up short. In that department, the Dolphins got mostly decent value in most of those trades and it's difficult to complain about Grier's work if the mandate was to go for it.
In retrospect, giving up a first-round pick for Bradley Chubb was a questionable (or bad) move because the edge defender was an impact player for only one season, and that 2023 season ended prematurely because of his Week 17 knee injury.
The Tyreek Hill trade can be debated for a while, but it's impossible to call it an out-and-out miss for Miami.
Likewise, it's difficult to criticize the terms of the Jalen Ramsey trade after getting him for a third-round pick and a backup tight end, but the question is whether Grier should have known his personality could be an issue at some point.
The reality is that Grier usually got good value in the trades he orchestrated, with the caveat that it helps when the team is willing to make a financial commitment to a player whose team doesn't want to do that.
-- His best trade in terms of value probably was the huge Laremy Tunsil deal with the Houston Texans in the rebuild of 2019 that netted the Dolphins all sorts of high draft picks.
-- The Dolphins also got great value in a draft trade involving picks in 2021 draft when they got two future first-round picks to move down from 3 to 12, but from this vantage point that win was somewhat negated when they turned around and traded one of those future No. 1s to move back up to 6. And then it also says here the Dolphins made a mistake by taking Jaylen Waddle, even though he's a very good wide receiver, instead of Penei Sewell, who has become an elite tackle on his way to the Hall of Fame.
-- Grier did hit on some draft picks during his time, never more than his very first draft when the Dolphins landed Tunsil in the first round and Xavien Howard in the second. Christian Wilkins was a good first-round pick in 2019, and other hits have included Robert Hunt in Round 2 in 2020, De'Von Achane in Round 3 in 2023, Malik Washington in Round 6 in 2024 and Patrick Paul in Round 2 in 2024 as well.
In the end, though, the misses clearly stood out more than the hits and one year later it's difficult to argue against the decision the Dolphins made because it does appear the organization is on the right path, even though it might take a little bit of time to get there.
While he always took more blame that he probably deserved, it's also very difficult to give Grier a high grade as Dolphins GM.
Let's just say his tenure was uninspiring, though not nearly as bad as a lot of Dolphins fans want to portray it.
Sullivan, meanwhile, can do no wrong in the eyes of a lot of fans right now because of the massive contributions of the rookie class, though the caveat must be included is the fact the roster being stripped provided a lot of immediate opportunities for those young players.
That said, it's really difficult to find fault with many, if any, of the moves he has made so far.
One that stands out was the decision to bypass the popular choice of Rueben Bain Jr. with the Dolphins' first of their two first-round picks. While we're not even at the halfway point of their rookie season, Kadyn Proctor right now has the look of a future star on the offensive line — wherever he winds up lining up — while Bain has done nothing to dispell the concern some draft analysts and media members brought up about his shorter arms being a major detriment as an NFL pass rusher.
The Dolphins regulardly have had six or seven rookies in their starting lineup this season, a testament both to the rebuild and to Sullivan's work.
The real test will come in future years when we see how many of those players remain starters.
Again, though, Sullivan is off to a great start. And for some Dolphins fans, the best part is he's not Chris Grier.

title: What to Know About the New Dolphins Edge Defender
full_text:
For the second time this week and the 16th time in 2026, the Miami Dolphins have picked up a player on waivers and they reportedly tried to a third and 17th, respectively.
The Dolphins' latest roster addition is edge defender Jamree Kromah, who was awarded off waivers from the Chicago Bears, with the Dolphins released Robert Beal Jr. to make room on the 53-man roster.
This comes in the same week the Dolphins landed guard Christian Haynes off waivers from Seattle and also put in a claim for former Las Vegas Raiders defensive tackle Joshua Laulu, though Laulu was awarded to the Tennessee Titans with the second-highest waiver wire priority behind only the winless L.A. Chargers, who did not put in a claim for him.
Kromah is a first-year player out of James Madison, though it's actually his third year in the NFL.
He has appeared in two career games, both this season with the Bears, making his NFL debut against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 6 before recording his first two NFL tackles (one for a loss) in Chicago's 30-24 victory against New England in the Week 7 Thursday night game.
Kromah made a 53-man roster on his third try this summer after recording three sacks in the preseason, including two against the Cleveland Browns.
Kromah went undrafted in 2024 before signing with the Bears and eventually landing on their practice squad. New England signed him off Chicago's practice squad but waived him after three weeks without him appearing in a game and he rejoined the Bears practice squad, where he spent the rest of 2024 and all of 2025.
He had a strong final collegiate season at James Madison with 10 sacks, but was not invited to the scouting combine.
His draft projection was a priority free agent, with NFL.com draft analyst writing: "Kromah posted impressive impact production in 2023 after playing a bigger role than he had in the previous four seasons between Rutgers and James Madison. He’s muscular with very long arms and might have the frame for additional weight to bump inside. Kromah features jarring pop in his hands but might lack enough fluidity and athleticism to capitalize on it as a pro. He’s an effort rusher who is unlikely to create enough consistent pressure to warrant rush-down snaps, but he does have a shot at making the back end of a roster as a base end or future 3-technique."
As with the previous 15 waiver wire pick-ups this year, Kromah is an unproven commodity and the Dolphins just want to have him aboard to see if maybe he can turn into a hidden gem.

title: Why the Dolphins Could Be (Very) Quiet at the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
There have been three significant deals around the NFL this week, but that might be just beginning ahead of the trade deadline November 10, and it's pretty obvious that some teams are in selling mode — maybe even firesale mode.
The Miami Dolphins do not appear one of those teams.
The Indianapolis Colts already have unloaded star veterans DeForrest Buckner and Quenton Nelson, while their AFC South counterparts Tennessee Titans just moved star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.
The Los Angeles Chargers have their share of veteran players expected to be traded as well, starting with edge defender Khalil Mack and possibly including star safety Derwin James.
What those teams have in common is they're not going anywhere in 2026 — when it comes to the playoffs, that is — with records of 2-5, 1-6 and 0-6.
The Dolphins are 1-5 and also realistically not going to be factors in the playoff race, and they do have some players who might be of interest to other teams.
That doesn't mean they're in sellling mode and willing to trade any veteran who's not on his first contract and could fetch a decent draft pick in return.
Just Friday morning, for example, SI national writer Albert Breer reported that the Dolphins have taken calls on defensive tackle Zach Sieler and center Aaron Brewer "but quickly rebuffed that."
Yes, they're in rebuilding mode. Yes, they could use all the additional draft capital they can get to beef up their nucleus of young players who hopefully can bring the team back into contention.
But the reality is the Dolphins are going to need good veteran players beyond 2026 and not have a team filled with second-, third- or fourth-year players.
They'll need players like Sieler and Brewer, and linebacker Jordyn Brooks is another who fits into that category.
And, yes, there was a suggestion not too long ago that he could be involved in a trade.
And the same thing we said about Brooks back then applies to Brewer now: Why in the world would the Dolphins trade him now after signing him in the offseason to a contract extension precisely because he represented the kind of player with whom the team wants to fill its roster.
Sieler is a different case because he's over 30 and he's got big cap numbers coming up over the final three years of his contract, but he's also still a very good player (he's the best defensive lineman on the team and there's probably not a close second right now) and he's also a very good leader on a very young team.
Simply put, Sieler is more valuable than whatever the Dolphins realistically could get in a trade, and this won't change unless a team gets desperate for D-tackle help after watching Buckner and Simmons go off the market.
It also shouldn't be dismissed that Sieler has made it very clear — as he keeps getting asked every time he speaks to the media these days — that he wants to stay in Miami, where he's been since the Dolphins claimed him off waivers from the Baltimore Ravens in December 2019.
Edge defender Joshua Uche is another player who has expressed his desire to stay in Miami, citing among other things his respect for first-year head coach Jeff Hafley.
He's another one who was pegged as a trade candidate, in his case because he's a veteran who signed only a one-year deal this offseason and is scheduled to become an unrestricted free agent in March.
But Uche has played more than well enough that the Dolphins should very strongly consider bringing him back at least another season — at the right price, of course.
And, again, it says here he'll be worth more to the Dolphins in 2027 and maybe even 2028 than whatever late-round pick they could get for him.
The one player who always has stood as the most likely to be trade is tackle Austin Jackson, who is the second-longest-tenured player on the team after Sieler.
The 2020 first-round pick is scheduled to become a free agent after the season after accepting a pay cut to return to the Dolphins this year, and his performance in 2026 has been pretty uneven.
Bigger issues are what kind of money Jackson would want in his next contract, whether the Dolphins want to move rookie first-round pick Kadyn Proctor to right tackle, as has been assumed all along, and whether Jackson would want to come back — he hasn't been as adamant as Sieler and Uche about wanting to stay.
The Dolphins probably have an idea by now whether they see Jackson as part of their plan beyond 2026, and if he's not, then it would behoove them to try to get any kind of draft pick for him because they're not likely to be in the free agent compensation game next offseason.
At this time, though, this has the makings of a pretty uneventful trade deadline for the Dolphins even if their record might have suggested otherwise at one point.

title: Thursday Injury Update: Big Names Could Be Missing from Dolphins-Patriots Matchup
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins look like they're going to be without their top rookie draft pick when they try to upset the New England Patriots on Sunday, but they also might not have to face New England's prized offseason acquisition.
Starting with the Dolphins, guard Kadyn Proctor missed a second consecutive practice with a concussion, and it's very difficult to envision him getting clearance to play Sunday.
Based on the NFL's five-step Return to Play protocol, Proctor still has to go through "non-contact training drills" and then "full football activity involving contact."
With the Dolphins down to one practice before a walk-through Saturday, it's again difficult to envision Proctor getting clearance in time and also know that the team is going to err on the side of caution here.
The final injury report will come out Friday and at this time it would be a surprise if Proctor weren't ruled out.
Head coach Jeff Hafley indicated Wednesday that backup Jarrett Kingston would be taking Proctor's reps at left guard during practice. Kingston was the one who replaced Jonah Savaiinaea at right guard after the 2025 second-round pick was injured in the first half of the Week 5 loss at Hard Rock Stadium.
Kingston, who obviously is the No. 3 guard on the roster, was claimed off waivers from the Houston Texans after the cuts to 53.
For those wondering about new guard Christian Haynes, claimed off waivers from the Seattle Seahawks on Wednesday, there's basically zero chance he would start that quickly and he actually probably will be inactive for his first game on the Dolphins roster.
With the Patriots, the big news involved wide receiver A.J. Brown, who the team acquired in a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles in the offseason.
After being limited in practice because of an ankle injury Wednesday, Brown sat out Thursday and now also is dealing with a knee issue.
This sort of downward trend would make it seem unlikely he'll play against the Dolphins on Sunday, though we'll get more info on the final injury report.
This obviously would be an advantageous development for the Dolphins, who had all sorts of problems with Brown when they faced the Eagles in 2023. Brown had 10 catches for 137 yards and a touchdown in Miami's 31-17 loss at Lincoln Financial Field in a Sunday night game that year.
At least the Dolphins got a positive development with cornerback JuJu Brents, who's also dealing with a concussion.
After sitting out practice Wednesday, he was back at practice Thursday, albeit on a limited basis.
This puts him on track to go through a full practice Friday and then get clearance to play against the Patriots.
The rest of the Dolphins injury report Thursday remained the same with the same 13 players on it, highlighted by quarterback Malik Willis.
After earlier this season being listed with a toe issue and then with a thumb injury, this time Willis is dealing with a groin injury, but he was again a full participant in practice Thursday.
Also fully participating for a second consecutive day was edge defender Rob Beal Jr., who has missed the past four games because of a hamstring injury.
The injury report again eight other players listed as limited participants.
On the list was cornerback Reese Taylor, who missed the past three games with a quad injury, and long-snapper Tucker Addington and tight end Will Kacmarek both were on the injury report last week before playing in the 28-25 victory against the New York Jets.
The other five players listed as limited were TE Greg Dulcich (ankle), S Michael Taaffe (neck/foot), S Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder), WR Malik Washington (knee) and WR Jared Wayne (knee).
Besides Brown, the one change on the Patriots injury report involved running back TreVeyon Henderson, who did not practice Thursday because of illness.
Henderson, a second-year second-round pick out of Ohio State, has had a slow start to his 2026 seaosn as the backfield partner to Rhamondre Stevenson, but he did score two touchdowns against Miami in the 2025 season finale.
Starting right tackle Morgan Moses (foot) against was limited, while QB Drake Maye was listed with a right shoulder injury, but he was a full participant.
As expected, DJ Campbell cleared waivers, so the Dolphins now can re-sign him to their practice squad if they choose.
The team's rookie sixth-round pick was waived to make room on the roster when the Dolphins claimed Haynes off waivers, and it's not a reach to predict Campbell will be re-signed and replace converted defensive lineman James Ester on the practice squad.
In former Dolphins news, veteran Charlie Heck has found a team after failling to make the 53-man roster as an unrestricted free agent pick-up. He signed with the Indianapolis Colts.

title: 3 Vikings Flaws Must Be Addressed ASAP After Perfect Season Dies at Hands of Lions
full_text:
Sunday marked the Minnesota Vikings’ first loss since Nov. 30, 2025, but if fan and media reactions were your only measure, you might think the team was on a season-long winless streak. The wild part? The pessimism is more than warranted .
Minnesota’s stellar defense showed its first signs of humanity in the second half of Sunday’s matchup with the Lions, after the struggling Vikings’ offense failed to get anything going for most of the afternoon, resulting in a 19-15 loss. Turns out defensive coordinator Brian Flores’s unit won’t be able to drag the team to an undefeated Super Bowl run after all.
So, what comes next? Let’s break down three areas in desperate need of saving if the Vikings want to make a serious run.
The Kyler Murray era in Minnesota may be over after just five full games with the former Cardinals’ quarterback.
There was plenty of reason for optimism when Murray signed with the Vikings on a one-year league-minimum deal in March to compete with J.J. McCarthy. Murray’s patented athleticism, head coach Kevin O’Connell’s play design, and Minnesota’s stacked wide receiver core seemed like a dangerous combination. Training camp showed flashes of what could be, even as fair concerns lingered about the fit between QB and coach and the schemes they’ve thrived in previously.
So far, the on-field product has been a disaster, as Murray looks to be actively regressing. He appears to lack any confidence in his decisions and is leaving wide-open wideouts frustrated downfield. It's clear the complexity of O’Connell’s scheme is overloading Murray as he basically relearns how he’s always played football. It’s the only explanation for why he’s actively worse with the best offensive tools he’s ever had. This was always a possibility, but the time to shift plans is now.
While Carson Wentz isn't an exciting solution, he should serve as a solid placeholder while the Vikings explore the QB trade market . If they find no sellers, it may be panic time.
Minnesota spent most of the offseason touting their new and improved run scheme led by assistant head coach Frank Smith. The shift to an outside zone approach meant backs would have more opportunities to turn the corner and hit the gas for explosive runs.
So far, that has not been the case. Aaron Jones battled valiantly through injury while Jordan Mason was on injured reserve, but his inability to sustain runs longer than 5-10 yards downfield emphasized the need for a boost to the room. Current Colts RB Jonathan Taylor quickly became the top trade target for most Vikings fans.
Sunday further emphasized the failures of a run game that never truly seemed to improve in the way we were sold. Rookie Demond Claiborne’s inability to see the field certainly doesn’t help, as the Vikings had hoped his speed would provide some value this season.
The Vikings' offense has many issues, but the run game remains problematic. The team talked about prioritizing it for the 4th straight offseason. Tons of changes over time: RBs, iOL, TE, OL coach, etc. Right now, they rank 31st in rushing success rate and 27th in EPA/play.
Minnesota’s interior offensive line isn't doing the passing or running game any favors, and one lineman’s play in particular is especially concerning. Right guard Will Fries signed a massive five-year, $87.72 million contract in 2025, giving Vikings fans hope that the team had finally solved a long-term interior need.
Turns out, he’s been anything but reliable.
Genuinely hilarious rep from Will Fries here https://t.co/oSC7kOl84r pic.twitter.com/8g83cL1nH9
Fries has often looked like a revolving door , allowing pass rushers to blow past him with ease. Luckily, the Vikings can opt out of his contract after the season.
The Vikings may not find an immediate upgrade this season, but they still need more depth. Left guard Joe Huber has done well in relief of rising star Donovan Jackson, and starting center Blake Brandel still seems to be learning the position in his first year as a starter.
The team needs security on the interior line, especially with Fries’s already inconsistent play.

title: Vikings' Snap Count vs. Lions: Biggest Winners, Losers & Role Changes in Week 8
full_text:
The Vikings are undefeated no longer . The Purple and Gold were outscored 19-15 at Ford Field in Week 8, moving their record on the season to 6-1 while remaining on top of the NFC North.
Minnesota has relied on the defense and the leg of their kicker, Will Reichard, to keep them in games this season, but that formula didn't work against the Lions. The Vikings' kicker missed his only field goal attempt. Thankfully, the offense scored two touchdowns to keep the game competitive, but that isn't exactly a long-term recipe for success .
A big reason the Vikings were in this game until the final minutes is the play of key contributors. Deciding who to play and when is important for head coach Kevin O'Connell, but there were bound to be winners and losers from the snap count.
Josh Metellus was in for every defensive snap of the game—the only Minnesota defender to achieve that feat this weekend. The versatile safety led the team with 13 tackles against Detroit and added one broken-up pass.
Metellus has been a cornerstone of defensive coordinator Brian Flores's defense this season. He has played 426 of 427 defensive snaps for the Vikings so far and should continue to be used as much as possible going forward, especially if the safety room stays out of trouble .
Max Bredeson's declining usage hit a new low against the Lions in Week 8, playing only seven offensive snaps. Compared to the season opener, when he was in on 24 offensive snaps, that's a significant difference.
It's not surprising that Bredeson didn't record a single stat against Detroit. When a player only gets nine total snaps in a game, getting an opportunity to make a significant impact can be a challenge. It will be interesting to see if his snap count shrinks again next week.
It was a season-high 17 offensive snaps for DeeJay Dallas against the Lions, almost tripling his count from last week against the Colts. His usage is already surprising since he was elevated from the practice squad while rookie running back Demond Claiborne was inactive for the second week.
Dallas was a major benefactor of Jordan Mason's ineffective day. He actually ended with two more offensive snaps than Mason, despite having seven fewer rushing opportunities. Dallas finished with one rushing attempt for four yards.
Even with safety Theo Jackson suffering an injury in the game after playing only 25 defensive snaps and rookie Jakobe Thomas being inactive for the seventh time this season, Jay Ward couldn't get on the field beyond special teams.
Ward finished the game with one tackle, but could get a defensive opportunity in Week 9 against the Bills on Monday Night Football next week if Jackson is unable to suit up. Of course, that might mean taking snaps away from a veteran defensive back.
This season, Harrison Smith has been a rotational safety. Before Sunday's game against Detroit, he had played a maximum of 31 defensive snaps in games against the Colts and the Buccaneers.
Harrison Smith is playing in place of Theo Jackson (quad), who is questionable to return.
Smith picked up many of Jackson's potential snaps. Jackson's quad injury forced him out of the game, and Smith appears to be the player Flores and O'Connell were most comfortable with to pick up the slack.

title: 4 Realistic QB Trade Targets for Vikings as Kyler Murray Raises Red Flags
full_text:
Another lackluster offensive performance in Sunday's loss to the Lions likely has the Vikings evaluating all options moving forward. Adding a running back at the trade deadline was already plausible , but does Kyler Murray's disappointing play warrant a look at a quarterback as well?
Murray is a tough quarterback to evaluate. His numbers indicate he's been solid, but the eye test tells another story. Despite finishing games with respectable completion rates (64.9%), few turnovers (3), and a few rushing first downs to boot (8), Murray also continues to miss open receivers, take bad sacks, and appears to be allergic to touchdowns.
It's unlikely that Murray experiences some magical growth in early November after struggling for months, but moving on to Carson Wentz or another quarterback via trade doesn't guarantee improvement either.
Still, if Murray puts up another stinker against the Bills on Monday Night Football in Week 9, there are a few names the Vikings could call on to try and save this season.
A quarterback putting up MVP-type numbers who also happens to have familiarity with the scheme should be general manager Nolan Teasley's first call. Cousins is playing some of his best football at 38 years old, with 19 passing touchdowns to just five interceptions, but that's also what makes this trade tricky.
The Raiders are 4-4 and squarely in the playoff mix in a wide-open AFC. Obviously, first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza is the future, but if he can learn for a year while Las Vegas makes a playoff push, what motivation would the Raiders have to trade Cousins?
Cousins would almost certainly be an upgrade over Murray, but getting the Raiders to play ball may be quite difficult barring an epic collapse next week against San Francisco.
Would the Vikings dare make a move for yet another Cardinal to try and solve their quarterback woes? Brissett was benched in favor of Gardner Minshew II late in Sunday's game against the Cowboys and may have lost his job after the Cardinals' epic comeback win.
After an impressive 2025 season with 23 touchdowns to just eight picks, Brissett hasn't looked as sharp in 2026, with seven interceptions already. If the Cards do opt to roll with Minshew moving forward, Brissett could likely be had for a late Day 3 pick.
Brissett may not move the needle enough for the Vikings, although he does have four games this year with at least 270 passing yards. Head coach Kevin O'Connell's system clearly isn't super adaptable either, so even though getting a capable passer for a relatively low price could be interesting, learning this offense to a point of making a difference feels like a steep mountain to climb.
Jones is another quarterback familiar with the Vikings' ways, and was wanted by this coaching staff as recently as a year ago. Have things changed, though? Jones is looking like the worst quarterback in football after the 42-7 drubbing against the Jaguars, and could be a part of the Colts' impending teardown.
The Jones before his Achilles injury halfway through 2025 appears to be gone, but obviously his knowledge of KOC's offense goes a long way. With five touchdowns to nine interceptions this year, though, it's actually quite difficult to look back over the weeks and say Jones has had even one good game this season.
He knows the playbook and is theoretically available, but there would be a lot riding on O'Connell finding the 2025 version of Jones underneath this pile of you know what.
Like Jones, Herbert has apparently forgotten how to play football in 2026, and the 0-7 Chargers might be tempted to hit the reset button. While there's been no indication that things are trending that way (yet), the Vikings would be smart to at least make the call.
Herbert was widely regarded as a top-10 quarterback, but has seemingly been broken by offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. The Chargers' signal-caller leads the league in interceptions and hasn't thrown a touchdown in nearly a month. If the Vikings think they can reignite Herbert's career, though there's a lot to like about his long-term prospects.
But despite his struggles in 2026, the Chargers—if they're open to moving him at all—would still ask for a pretty penny for their typically elite quarterback. Do the Vikings feel strongly enough that Herbert is fixable to send a first-round pick and more to land him?
It's possible, but sending multiple high picks would also be a hard sell to Teasley, who hasn't even selected a player yet as GM.

title: Harmon's Longship Week 8: 4 Vikings Thoughts on Offensive Woes, O'Connell, MNF vs. Bills & More After 1st Loss
full_text:
One thing is true for football teams and Nordic warriors: you can’t win every battle.
If you told any Vikings fan before the season that the team would be 6-1 at the start of November, they’d be ecstatic. Yet the team has walked a fine line all season, leaving the door open for serious questions about its legitimacy as a contender . Let’s add this to the list of things that could only happen in Minnesota…
The Vikings officially kicked off the “prove it” portion of their schedule on Sunday in Detroit. Would they silence the noise with a statement victory over a divisional rival, or would their cracked ship finally break?
Let’s dive into the game and what’s to come.
It’s been a weekly tradition at this point. Writing an article about how the Vikings remained undefeated despite a worrying and often awful offense. Well, that changed this week, as the team’s offensive failures finally caught up to them.
It’s clear at this point that quarterback Kyler Murray and head coach Kevin O’Connell are not the match many had hoped for. Murray looks to be actively regressing in his accuracy, an area that was supposed to be one of his greatest strengths. Sure, we knew there’d have to be adjustments between quarterback and coach, but even the most pessimistic of outlooks likely didn’t look like this.
Murray’s brief fourth-quarter flashes ultimately proved to be too little, too late, as he ended the day 17 of 29 for 210 yards with two touchdowns and one interception in a game where the stat sheet looked far better than the product on the field.
Star wideout Justin Jefferson would have been a complete nonfactor if it wasn't for an incredible leaping grab to come down with a poorly placed TD pass from Murray. The star receiver finished with only 33 yards on five catches. On the bright side, his nine targets should move him slightly up one specific list, as Jefferson entered the game ranked 47th in targets per game, averaging 6.2 looks per contest.
Jefferson’s frustration is palpable, and can he really be blamed? The star wideout is still waiting for consistent QB play and his first playoff win in year seven.
This is unacceptable pic.twitter.com/R5lxp4Xu4n
The Vikes’ run game was also a no-show. Vikings running backs totaled only 46 yards on 14 carries, in stark contrast to the dominance of Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs . The running back position is a massive need for the Vikings, but is it worth investing in if the passing game and interior offensive line are so unreliable?
Brian Flores and the Vikings’ defense did everything they could to slow down the Lions in the first half. Andrew Van Ginkel had 2.5 sacks, James Pierre had an interception, and most importantly, they held Detroit’s high-flying offense to only six first-half points.
. @AndrewVanGinkel is having himself a day. 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/SJjsbNH9H9
Lions head coach Dan Campbell and offensive coordinator Drew Petzing would ultimately make adjustments at halftime, and with no help from their offense, the gassed Vikings’ defense eventually folded to Gibbs and Sione Vaki. Still, if you told me before the game that the Lions would only score 19 points, I’d assume the Vikings walked away victorious.
Let me be clear: I firmly believe O’Connell is a top offensive mind and play designer in the NFL. He’s well respected throughout the league, and there are countless teams who’d be glad to swap him out with their current head coach. But there’s a pattern we need to start acknowledging: O’Connell is often the worst enemy for himself and his quarterbacks.
A tenure-long deep dive may require its own separate piece, but the present reality is that the Vikings' passing game is failing disastrously with a QB O’Connell handpicked this past offseason. With the odd timing of the Vikings’ general manager firing/hiring process, interim general manager Rob Brzezinski was not going to prevent O’Connell from pursuing his QB of choice.
With Kirk Cousins or even Geno Smith available, O’Connell took a swing on the highly athletic Murray. So far, the marriage looks like it's heading toward a fast divorce.
Kyler Murray is pretty easily playing the worst football of his career pic.twitter.com/Tmy2HoNKx2
The decision to trade J.J. McCarthy to the Giants for a fifth-round pick leaves the Vikings with only Carson Wentz or Max Brosmer as possible on-roster replacements. It doesn’t help O’Connell’s case that McCarthy looks more comfortable through two games as a Giant than he ever did with the Vikings.
Minnesota’s loss on Sunday knocked them from the top of the NFC and into the second seed in the conference. The good news is there’s a lot of season left, and the Vikings will have a chance to face the top-seeded 49ers head-to-head in a few weeks.
The NFC North continues to be an absolute gauntlet, with each team currently holding one of seven conference playoff berths. The Vikings are currently the only team in the North to lose this week. The Packers beat the Panthers on TNF, the Bears head to Seattle on Monday night, and the Lions ended the Vikings' undefeated streak.
Minnesota has to get on track to keep their divisional lead in the midst of a brutal November stretch. They’ll head to Green Bay in two weeks with a chance to add additional cushion.
Good news: the Vikings get one extra day to recover and learn from this weekend’s loss as they’ll host the 6-1 Bills next Monday Night.
Buffalo will present a similar challenge to Detroit: a stellar offense and a bottom-three passing defense. Unfortunately, there’s little reason to think the Vikings offense can take advantage without some major change.
With the trade deadline approaching , it's completely possible that GM Nolan Teasley finds a way to add some new faces before Monday Night Football kicks off next week.

title: New Vikings Issue Is Now a Full-Blown Problem After Jahmyr Gibbs's Week 8 Performance
full_text:
It took eight weeks, but the Vikings finally lost their first game of the season on Sunday. The 19-15 loss to the Lions was a close game, but there was an aspect of the contest that should leave a sour taste in fans' mouths.
Before Week 7, the Vikings hadn't faced the top running backs in the NFL. However, Jonathan Taylor of the Colts had 18 carries for 95 yards and a touchdown against Minnesota, which was concerning considering the explosive running backs coming up on the schedule .
That fear became a reality on Sunday. Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs had a huge day with 23 rushing attempts for 153 yards and a touchdown (6.7 yards per carry), along with two catches for 15 yards
Given that the Vikings are about to enter their toughest stretch of the season, it's safe to say that their inability to stop elite running backs is officially a red flag.
The Vikings gave up 230 rushing yards to Detroit on Sunday. The Lions ran the ball 39 times compared to passing 25 times, proving that they knew they could take advantage of the Brian Flores defense on the ground. Don't be surprised if other teams take note.
A huge problem for this is how many missed tackles Minnesota had during the game. The FOX announcers shared that the Vikings missed 11 tackles in the second half alone, which explains why the Lions were able to secure the win. And that statistic wasn't even given at the end of the game.
The problem is amplified by the upcoming schedule for the Vikings. The list of running backs they face is brutal:
Cook is averaging 108.3 rushing yards in his last six games, including two performances of 135-plus yards. Jacobs hasn't popped off yet this season, but he does did have 69 rushing yards and a TD on 17 carries in his last game against Minnesota in Week 17 of the 2024 season. Meanwhile, McAffrey is on a six-game TD streak (eight total TDs) while Robinson paces the league with 780 rushing yards as of Monday morning.
Oh yeah, and then they get to face Gibbs again in Week 15.
Jahmyr Gibbs races into the end zone to give the Lions the lead! MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/X42rZbve42
The good news is that the Vikings have until next Monday night to figure out how to better contain a strong rushing attack. Even if they can't stop the run, being able to limit yards after contact and prevent big runs would be a vast improvement.
In each of Minnesota's last two games, the defense has given up a long rushing touchdown. This week, Gibbs recorded a 30-yard touchdown run in the third quarter. Last week, Taylor had a 38-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter.
Kyler Murray and the Vikings offense aren't in a position to be in a shootout this season. The Purple and Gold rely on their defense to keep them in games while controlling field position and playing solid special teams.
Until Minnesota figures out its offense, the pressure is on the defense to keep teams from running up the scoreboard. That could force general manager Nolan Teasley to deepen the Vikings' defensive trenches before the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 10.

title: Theo Jackson Injury Concerns Could Give Jakobe Thomas the Vikings Opportunity He's Needed
full_text:
Heading into Week 8 against the Lions, the Vikings listed safety Jay Ward as questionable on the injury report . The team decided to keep Ward active rather than give Jakobe Thomas his first taste of NFL action , continuing to put the rookie safety's debut on hold.
Thomas has been inactive for every game this season, but could see his chance come in Week 9 against the Bills on Monday Night Football. Not only because the Vikings might want to switch things up after losing, but also because safety Theo Jackson left the game with a quad injury, according to the Vikings' official X account.
S Theo Jackson (quad) is questionable to return.
Now that Jackson is banged up, could Thomas finally see the field against the Bills? Or will the rookie safety once again be inactive on game day and need to continue being patient for his opportunity to eventually come?
The Vikings selected Thomas with a third-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. The No. 98 overall pick brought the former Tennessee and Miami (FL) standout to the Purple and Gold to prepare for a possible future without veteran Harrison Smith, who's made it clear that his 15th season will be his last .
Smith has struggled this year and is likely to be Minnesota's top choice to fill in for Jackson if he misses time. However, Smith has an overall Pro Football Focus grade of 43 this season and a coverage grade of 41.9 .
Smith doesn't look like the dominant defender he once was, but that isn't surprising considering he is 37 years old and in his 15th season as a pro. He is a six-time Pro Bowl safety, but it might be time for him to move aside and see what Thomas has to offer. After all, the rookie did look solid in his lone preseason appearance vs. the Broncos, recording four tackles and the second-highest PFF tackling grade (79.4) on the team that game.
Jackson is playing 64% of the Vikings' snaps this season. That means he is averaging about 37.8 defensive snaps per game. If Smith takes those on Monday Night Football against the Bills, Smith already gets approximately 28.5 defensive snaps per game, which would leave plenty of opportunities for Ward and Thomas to split.
It is confusing why Thomas hasn't taken the field yet for Minnesota. It made sense when the Vikings' safeties were healthy, but now that a few of the defensive backs are banged up and Smith is struggling to be effective.
Getting the 23-year-old rookie on the field to prepare him for the future and give him some experience to continue his development is essential. And it should happen in Week 9.

title: 3 Vikings Studs & 2 Duds in Week 8 Loss to Lions: Ongoing Concerns Overshadow Van Ginkel's Big Day
full_text:
The Vikings are no longer undefeated . The Lions handed the Purple and Gold their first loss of the in Week 8 during a defensive battle that ended with the Vikings coming up short.
The 15-19 loss to an NFC North rival hurts , but the Vikings were competitive throughout the game. Minnesota even showed some flashes of offense on Sunday, giving hope that Kyler Murray and company can put up more points in future games.
There were players who stepped up against the Lions, while others struggled to contribute in a positive way. Let's take a look at three studs and two duds for Minnesota after the Week 8 loss to Detroit.
It was a great day for Andrew Van Ginkel. The Vikings edge rusher was a consistent thorn in the side of Lions quarterback Jared Goff, registering 2.5 sacks and three quarterback hits while acting as a pass rusher.
. @AndrewVanGinkel is having himself a day. 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/SJjsbNH9H9
He finished with four tackles, with two of those being solo efforts. For Van Ginkel, his four tackles and 2.5 sacks are the most in any game this season. He continues to be one of the most consistent and reliable defenders for Minnesota, supporting the idea that a potential contract extension could be on the horizon .
Last week, Vikings running back Aaron Jones aggravated his knee injury but still played against the Lions this week. Jones had five carries for 22 yards (4.4 yards per carry). Mason got the bulk of the carries, recording eight.
Unfortunately, Mason finished with 20 yards, averaging only 2.5 yards per carry. He wasn't a factor in the passing game, not receiving a single target from Minnesota's quarterback. That type of production won't get the job done, perhaps giving the Vikings even more reason to think about a Jonathan Taylor trade .
T.J. Hockenson finished second for Minnesota in receiving yards, catching four of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown. When Murray threw the ball his way against Detroit, good things happened. His 14.5 yards per reception showed his value in the Vikings' passing game.
TJ Hockenson for the lead! MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/cPj2oQQZzU
One of the best plays was a nice seam route by Hockenson late in the first quarter when he caught a 22-yard pass from Murray for a first down that moved Minnesota across midfield. That drive ended with a one-yard Justin Jefferson touchdown catch, showing how valuable that play was for the Vikings.
Fries has struggled in pass protection this season. Minnesota's starting right guard has a Pro Football Focus pass-block grade of 48.7 this season. Those struggles continued on Sunday against the Lions at Ford Field.
Fries was beat for a sack and attempted to push the defender inside to get help that wasn't there. Then, in the third quarter, he was called for a holding penalty that negated Mason's 29-yard run and moved the line of scrimmage back 10 yards.
The interior of the Vikings' offensive line took a hit when it lost Donovan Jackson, and the last thing they need is for Fries to add to those concerns.
The Vikings rely on Eric Wilson and Blake Cashman to contain plays in the middle of the defense. The duo was solid again today, with Wilson finishing second among Vikings defenders with 11 tackles, seven solo and two for a loss, including one sack.
Wilson and Cashman combined for 21 of Minnesota's 79 total tackles. Their play was a major reason the Lions struggled to get their run game going until later in the contest, but the exhausted defense played 68 snaps against Detroit and wore down as the game went on.

title: Vikings Week 8 Report Card: Grading Every Position After Sunday's Heartbreaking Lions Loss
full_text:
The Vikings handed their first loss of the season in Detroit, and it came in the most predictable way possible.
Once again, the Vikings' offense was unable to muster much, leaving the defense to handle all the heavy lifting. After seven weeks, though, that task was becoming more laborious, and the Lions finally took advantage of a tired unit, ending the day with the 19-15 victory.
Here's how each of the grades for every position shook out for me in the loss.
Kyler Murray finished the day with respectable numbers after a late 51-yard heave to Jordan Addison, but for the most part was inaccurate and underwhelming once again. He started the game 1-for-5 and sailed multiple passes into Row E for much of the first half before settling in a bit late.
Murray hadn't turned the ball over since September, before his interception on Sunday, and it's one of the reasons that his leash has stayed so long despite mediocre play. The Vikings won't—and probably shouldn't—pull the plug on this experiment yet , but if another game goes by without obvious improvement, maybe the call to Las Vegas gets made.
Did they play today? Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones Sr. combined for just 13 attempts and 42 yards on the day, and proved why the Vikings have had such reported interest in Jonathan Taylor. There's no explosion, and frankly, defenses just aren't afraid of the Vikings duo. They're both very good RB2's, but it's getting abundantly clear this offense is missing a go-to back to open up some of the passing lanes.
There were no drops, no miscues, but again, for what seems like the seventh straight time, the Vikings' wide receivers just weren't given tons of opportunities. Minnesota tossed Justin Jefferson his most targets of the season, but he still was only able to muster just five catches for 33 yards--oh, and one spectacular touchdown grab.
Jauan Jennings reportedly vetoed a trade to San Francisco earlier this week, according to NFL insider Jay Glazer, but still hasn't found a home in Minnesota, either with a hum-drum two catches for 11 yards line.
Here’s Jay Glazer talking about Jauan Jennings not wanting to get on a FaceTime call with Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch to get traded back to the 49ers https://t.co/JWWNIT0zQQ pic.twitter.com/ceOmmEpLvF
The heave to Addison was a work-of-art, but it really feels like the Vikings are leaving a lot on the bone with this talented group.
T.J. Hockenson is about the only thing working on this offense. His four catches extended his team-leading 31 receptions for the season, and it's clear that Murray loves that seam route with the big tight end.
Obviously, fans want to see Jefferson in the mix more, but at this point if Hockenson needs to become the guy, then so be it.
Another three-sack day with little to show in the run game has reminded us why the Vikings were in on guard Quenton Nelson until the bidding got too high. Will Fries has been almost unplayable, and the rest of the interior has struggled at times too, with Donovan Jackson out for the year.
Is a trade incoming this week?
Between Levi Drake Rodriguez roughing the passer, Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins jumping offsides on a crucial down, and getting gashed on the ground in the second half, it wasn't the defensive front's best day.
The offense did the defense no favors, however, and this unit was clearly gassed by the end after spending over 35 minutes on the field. Still, yielding 230 rushing yards to Detroit isn't all on the offense's ineptitude.
What started out as multiple big plays by Eric Wilson and Andrew Van Ginkel ended with the team registering 17 missed tackles on the day. That's not all on the linebacking crew, but much like the defensive line, the wheels fell off a bit in the second half. This is still an elite unit, but the next three weeks against Buffalo, Green Bay and San Francisco won't allow for a breather.
James Pierre handed Jared Goff his first interception of the season, and the secondary held the Lions quarterback to just 176 yards through the air.
James Pierre picks it off! MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XZ8sQnAqCx
Opposing signal-callers have continued to find it difficult to pass on the Vikings, but the injury to Isaiah Rodgers will be something to monitor this week.
In a very rare 'L' for the Vikings' special teams unit, Will Reichard missed his only attempt on the day, and punter Brett Thorson shanked his way to a 43-yard average. Myles Price was unable to do much in his limited opportunities either.

title: 3 Biggest Vikings Takeaways as Perfect Season Ends With 19-15 Loss to Lions in Week 8
full_text:
Twenty-six years. That’s how long it’s been since your Vikings were 7-0 to start a season. With doubts swirling around the sustainability of their season and trade rumors abundant, the Vikings journeyed to the Motor City for a crucial NFC North matchup with the Lions .
Ultimately, Minnesota fell short and are no longer the league’s last undefeated squad following a 19-15 loss to the Lions.
The first half followed a familiar script: the Vikings' defense doing everything in their power to shut down a potent Lions offense. The offense struggled mightily to get anything going for much of the game, continuing a trend that could ultimately prove to be Minnesota’s undoing.
Here’s what mattered most coming out of the Vikings' first loss and heading into the NFL trade deadline .
The Vikings have spent their entire season searching for some form of offensive consistency.
Unfortunately, Sunday proved to be no different, even against a porous Detroit passing defense. Kyler Murray struggled with ball placement and accuracy throughout the game, with his first touchdown coming off an incredible effort by Justin Jefferson.
JUSTIN JEFFERSON OH MY MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DUTDY0f59E
The star receiver’s fourth touchdown of the year doubled his season total from 2025. Murray ended the first half seven-for-15 for 86 yards with a TD and an interception. The third quarter was not much better for Murray and company, and Jefferson started to show hints of frustration with shrugs and head shakes.
Then, with just over 10 minutes left in the game, Murray threw an arching deep ball to Jordan Addison for a 51-yard gain, setting up a touchdown to T.J. Hockenson. Addison would then snag a two-point conversion catch in the back of the end zone.
The Vikings' defense came out swinging, with four first-half sacks and an interception to hold the high-flying Lions’ offense to only six points through two quarters.
Then, an eerily similar script started to unfold.
The second half echoed Week 18 of the 2024 season, when the Vikings had a chance to secure the number one seed in Detroit. The defense held the explosive Lions offense to only ten points in the first half, but a dud performance from Sam Darnold and the Vikings offense meant the defense was left on the field for a majority of the game, leading to an eventual break in the wall and a 31-9 loss.
Detroit ended Sunday’s game with 381 yards of offense after struggling against Flores’s unit in the first half. The Vikings' defense is simply too great to be wasted on an often incompetent offense .
If there’s one thing this game emphasized, it’s the need for the Vikings to improve their offense via trade .
While an update at the QB position may seem to be an impossible task in November, there may be a few names to check in on. The best way to get things on track? A game-changing running back. The Vikings finished with a total of only 81  rushing yards on the day, and 35 of those came from their QB.
Trade speculation around Colts running back Jonathan Taylor has dominated NFL rumors and discourse, and the Vikings are in desperate need of a home run hitter at the position. Hopefully, the close-up view of Jahmyr Gibbs gave Nolan Teasley the inspiration needed to find his star back.

title: 3 Dream Vikings Trade Targets to Help Go on a Potential Super Bowl Run
full_text:
Now that the Vikings are the NFL's last undefeated team as of Sunday afternoon, expectations are high for the Purple and Gold this season. An NFC North crown and a playoff appearance would be great, but the Super Bowl must be the goal.
Fans who enjoy playing EA Sports ' "Madden NFL" franchise would likely try to make blockbuster trades at this point in the season to make the roster even more intimidating. While those types of trades are difficult to execute in real life, it is a lot of fun to dream about them happening.
Let's take a look at three dream trade targets for the Vikings who would help the team continue its winning ways and make a push toward returning to a Super Bowl for the first time since losing to the Raiders in January 1977.
Many fans really want the Vikings to trade for Colts superstar running back Jonathan Taylor, but making that deal happen for Minnesota would be incredibly challenging right now. Not only would the team likely have to give up a first-round draft pick , but there are also salary cap concerns.
Taylor signed a two-year, $44 million extension that keeps him under contract through the 2028 NFL season. His cap hit for 2026 is also over $16.1 million , according to Spotrac , which is a problem since Minnesota has only about $4.4 million in salary cap space available.
It would take some work, but a deal could be done to bring the 27-year-old rusher to Minnesota. He would instantly become the team's starter, allowing Aaron Jones Sr. to recover from a knee injury and use Jordan Mason in a backup role this season.
The Vikings got good play out of their safeties against the Colts last week, but could use a more consistent force in the secondary and a long-term replacement for when Harrison Smith retires after this season.
Cardinals safety Budda Baker would instantly be a starter in Minnesota, but the 30-year-old defender brings salary cap issues to the table. He is under contract through the 2027 NFL season, with salary cap hits of $10.8 million this season and $19.2 million next year.
Baker has made seven consecutive Pro Bowls and can do everything that defensive coordinator Brian Flores would ask him to do. Through seven games this season, he has 44 tackles, five quarterback hits, four pass defenses, four tackles for a loss, 3.5 sacks, and an interception, proving his versatility.
Minnesota missed out on trading for Colts guard Quenton Nelson , who was dealt to the Seahawks. However, landing Eagles guard Landon Dickerson could be the next best thing for the Vikings.
The 28-year-old offensive lineman would immediately fill the starting left guard spot that Joe Huber is holding down after the season-ending injury to Donovan Jackson. Dickerson is struggling in Philadelphia's offense and could use a change of scenery.
Dickerson made the Pro Bowl in 2022 and 2023, so his difficulty this season in Philadelphia seems like an anomaly. However, he is under contract through the 2028 season with cap hits of $9.455 million this year, $13.768 million next year, and $17.79 million in 2028, making money an issue in acquiring him.

title: Patriots Recent Roster Moves Seem to Revolve Around TreVeyon Henderson's Future
full_text:
The New England Patriots spent a second round pick on TreVeyon Henderson last season, and the running back quickly became one of the team's most electric players on offense. More than 1,000 yards of offense and breakaway speed like no other, Henderson appeared to be one of the centerpieces of this new-look Patriots team.
One year later and he hasn't had the same output on the field. An ankle sprain and an illness have held him out of two games this season, and when he's been on the field, he's seeing his workload dwindle down.
Six games into his sophomore campaign, the 24-year-old has just 52 carries, 203 rushing yards and one touchdown. As a receiver, he's caught five passes for 45 yards. He's played just 32% of the Patriots' offensive snaps this year and has been part of a rotation that's seeing Rhamondre Stevenson shine and Corey Kiner get a step up.
So what's happening with Henderson ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline? Is he getting moved? If so, where? Even asking those questions feels a bit too rash right now. Running backs coach Tony Dews laughed at that question last week. However, some of the Patriots' recent moves at the running back position feel a bit curious.
Let's try to work out this Henderson -shaped puzzle and see what might be in the Patriots' plans.
Henderson missed the season opener with an ankle injury he suffered in practice. He would return in Week 2, scamper his way to a long touchdown and then fall back into a little bit of a production rut. In Week 5 against the Las Vegas Raiders, he suffered what was told to him as a high-ankle sprain.
Maybe a bit too quickly, Henderson was practicing and appeared ready to rock and roll. He'd play one week later against the New York Jets and carry the ball seven times for 31 yards in the win. On a short week and some more time to let that ankle heal, Henderson seemed poised for a breakout on Thursday Night Football.
Instead, Henderson was sidelined for more of the first half . He ended that game with just three carries, one less than Kiner, and only 13 total offensive snaps. He ran into contact with 9:12 left in the first quarter and wouldn't get his next touch until there was 7:36 left in the third.
"We had some things for him, packages or personnel groupings," head coach Mike Vrabel said at the time. "TreVeyon will help us. Wanted to see where we were with Corey getting a couple carries too, but TreVeyon will help us plenty here down the stretch. He helped us a little bit tonight."
"To me, it's more just the way the game flows more than anything," Dews said. "There's no other rhyme or reason. ... You're trying to get three guys that are capable of playing, reps. Somebody gets shorted as you also add the situational things that come up, whether it be two-minute drives, and that's what sometimes drives the snap count."
The Patriots, especially with a banged-up offense, could use Henderson's speed as a rusher and a receiver. But whether he's not fully recovered from that injury or just being used more as a situational player, something feels a bit amiss about Henderson's role right now (compared to what it could be in an offense as dynamic as Josh McDaniels').
This week, preparing for a road test against Miami, Henderson wasn't out there the final two days of practice. The Patriots listed him as having an illness and it's why he didn't participate . He was spotted in the locker room on Thursday, walking out with a backpack as reporters shuffled in.
He'd be listed as questionable one day later, and then downgraded to out the day after that. So the Patriots would be heading into their matchup with the Dolphins with just Stevenson and Kiner on the active roster. At that point in time, it was expected that Lan Larison — the practice squad back who was elevated to the roster when Henderson was out in Week 1 — would get the temporary call-up.
Nope. The team announced he'd be signing to the active roster for good , bypassing his two remaining elevations that could have been used. This move would give the Patriots, when fully healthy, four running backs on the 53-man roster. An interesting decision that Vrabel would be asked about a day after the game.
"Well, we just had a spot open and felt like that would give us some flexibility down the road," Vrabel said Monday.
Larison, who's chipped in as a receiving back and on kick returns , has shown signs of promise since arriving as an undrafted free agent in 2025. Now with four running backs competing for time in that cycle mentioned by Dews, could that cut into Henderson's playing time even more?
He's a nice backup option if Henderson's illness bleeds into next week, but it raised some eyebrows that the team decided to sign him rather than elevate for just that game.
With an open spot on the practice squad left by Larison, the Patriots went out and brought in another running back. It's one who's familiar with the system in place, as Terrell Jennings agreed to a deal to return to where his career began in 2024.
Jennings was in line to make the initial 53-man roster out of training camp, but injuries forced him to go on IR and then later released with a settlement. Since then, the team has brought in several players as depth options, and Jennings — who really looked good during his time as the RB3 a year ago — feels like one who can stick.
Again, similar to the situation with Larison's signing, adding another running back to the team feels like a bit of overkill at this point in time. Jennings has special teams value, and he'll be the fifth running back to suit up in practice every day. We'll see soon if it's becoming too many.
Some teams are looking for running backs at the deadline ( the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings is one that remains a top buyer at that spot ), and so maybe Henderson ends up on the move in less than two weeks.
Moving off of Henderson this early into his pro career would feel like a rash decision, considering how impactful he was for this offense just a season ago. However, as you read between these running back lines, it feels like something has to give when it comes to this position.
In a way, Henderson's start to 2026 feels similar to how his 2025 season began. He repped behind Antonio Gibson until the veteran tore his ACL in October. It wasn't until then that Henderson really broke onto the scene. Dews compared the current state of the room to last year's pre-Gibson injury, and it's a fair point to make. Stevenson has looked incredible as the workhouse and Kiner has become a stalwart of late-game drives. They're playing well enough to remain on the field.
Henderson appears to be the odd man out right now heading into Week 9, though, and these running back moves are going to start fanning that trade rumor flame a little more. We'll see if he gets a bigger chance this week.

title: Is Andy Borregales' Kicking Job With Patriots in Jeopardy? Doesn't Seem Like It
full_text:
Despite the New England Patriots' 24-19 win over the Miami Dolphins , there was still plenty to clean up for the defending AFC East champs. One of those things involved a missed field goal from Andy Borregales in the second quarter.
It was Borregales' third missed field goal of 40 yards or less this season . He's 10-for-13 on the year with all of those short misses resulting in every miss he has in his second season. Now, of course, it was raining hard in Miami during the game, but Borregales hasn't had a perfect year in 2026 to this point.
That miss to the right kept the score at 6-3 Miami, and that lead would later balloon up to 13-3 at halftime.
He's 20-for-21 on extra points this year, and has reached 50 yards on a field goal. Could the Patriots potentially make a change (or bring in some competition) at kicker soon? Based on Mike Vrabel's answer when he was asked about it Monday, it doesn't feel like it.
"That needs to get corrected. I've got a lot of confidence in Andy," Vrabel said. "I think when you see the timing and when the approach is in rhythm, it looks really good. We have to make our kicks. Everybody has a job here."
We've seen teams across the league make decisions on a new kicker based on some misses. The Los Angeles Rams moved on from Harrison Mevis after a shaky primetime outing against the Buffalo Bills a few weeks back, and just a week ago, the Kansas City Chiefs signed Justin Tucker to the practice squad in response to a few Harrison Butker misses.
Borregales doesn't seem like he needs to be worried about the state of his job security just yet, but if these misses keep happening, that might need to be a larger conversation. However, Borregales — a sixth-round pick a year ago — has all the leg strength in the world to be an excellent kicker for New England.
In his career, he's 82.2% on field goals and 96.1% on extra points. That's a good clip a year-plus into his NFL tenure.
Other than the miss, Borregales hit a 34-yard field goal to open up the scoring and was perfect on all three extra point attempts. He also tackled Dolphins running back Jaylen Wright on a kickoff return, potentially saving a touchdown-scoring sprint.
For now, the Patriots' special teams trio of Borregales, punter Mitch Wishnowsky and long snapper Julian Ashby remains in tact. But a confident Vrabel wants to make sure that Borregales is accurate on his kicks for the remainder of the year.
"There's no real message. It's, 'Hey, we've got to make them,'" Vrabel said about his message to Borregales. "But I've got a lot of confidence. I thought he did a really nice job on the kickoff with the ball placement. Hopefully, he's making a lot of extra points and not having to kick a lot of field goals."

title: Patriots Don't Have Immediate Update on Hunter Henry's Status
full_text:
The New England Patriots suffered yet another blow to the offensive side of the ball this week, seeing starting tight end Hunter Henry leave Sunday's win over the Miami Dolphins early with a foot injury. Henry, just a few days after restructuring his contract to give the Patriots more cap space , would make a catch in the second quarter and miss the following three snaps on the sideline.
Henry would then go from the blue medical tent to the Patriots locker room. He'd try to return to the field, but would depart again back to the locker room, and the team would rule him out later in the 24-19 win .
The 31-year-old tight end finished the afternoon with three receptions on three targets and 30 receiving yards. After he went down, the Patriots relied a lot more on rookies Eli Raridon and Tanner Arkin to finish out the game. Raridon played a career-high 55 snaps.
"Yeah, it's always tough losing Hunter," Drake Maye said postgame. "Anytime with Hunt and Eli n there, we were kind of down some receivers, those guys were going to be big for us. ... I saw him when he got up from the catch. I was worried about him and probably shouldn't be worried about him, but I'm worried about Hunt. I know he went back in the locker room, but he seems fine in there. He seems like he's walking around fine and he's got a smile on his face. So he's always Hunt."
One day later, at his weekly Monday press conference, head coach Mike Vrabel didn't have any futher updates on Henry or his status.
"I don't have any expectations yet," Vrabel said. "We'll see kind of how he responds here, wasn't able to finish the game, so you know, we'll see where he is. And I know Hunter will do everything that he can to get back to help us, and we'll go from there."
Losing Henry would be another injury this Patriots team would need to work through. Already down several key pieces in that game ( A.J. Brown, TreVeyon Henderson , Alijah Vera-Tucker, Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs), the last thing the Patriots would want is their trusty tight end to also miss time.
"I mean, everybody prepares as a starter and you know, we missed Hunter, certainly that leadership and his understanding in tough, close games, he always seems to come up and make plays for us," Vrabel said postgame. "So again, the guys were ready to go. I though Josh (McDaniels) and the offensive staff did a really nice job of moving guys around and guys being ready to go. It's a tough, tough game on the road in the division. These are never easy."
The Patriots will be on the practice field on Wednesday as they prepare for a Week 9 home matchup with the Green Bay Packers. Henry, along with Hollins and fullback Reggie Gilliam (who are both eligible to be activated off of injured reserve), will be names to watch when that practice kicks off.

title: Kevin Byard Finally Nabs Important First Patriots Interception in Win
full_text:
Last year with the Chicago Bears, Kevin Byard led the NFL with seven interceptions. Through seven games with the New England Patriots, the veteran safety hadn't grabbed one.
He wasn't alone, as the Patriots secondary had struggled to force a lot of turnovers this season. It was a point of emphasis for them all week against the Miami Dolphins, and Byard finally got his name on the board.
Early in the fourth quarter, and the Patriots leading the Dolphins 17-13, a Malik Willis pass intended to push the ball downfield hit the helmet of defensive tackle DaQuan Jones and fluttered up in the air. Byard, along with fellow safety Craig Woodson, were in the area as Dolphins wideout Caleb Douglas reached for the ball.
It fell right into the awaiting arms of Byard, who came down with New England's first takeaway of the day and his 37th career interception. It was a big play in what turned into a 24-19 victory .
"It felt excellent. It's kind of like I finally got the monkey off my back to be able to go get my first one this year," Byard said postgame, also sharing he teased Woodson a bit after dropping a pick of his own earlier. "It was in a big spot too because we were able to go up two scores. ... Hopefully this is just a sign of more to come because they come in bunches."
The Patriots haven't been able to get a lot of takeaways this season. That was just their fifth interception of the season. Part of that might be the injuries that hit the secondary earlier in the year, but now that group — fully healthy for the first time since Week 1 — is looking to cause more of a disruption.
"We have been kind of talking about this secondary being one of the best in the league and to finally have us all back out there, hipefuly we can continue to build upon that," he said. "Some things we definitely need to clean up for sure, but this is a good start."
Nearly 40 seconds later, the Patriots would use that Byard interception to put points on the board . Drake Maye found DeMario Douglas along the sideline, who would sprint his way to a 48-yard touchdown and a much more breathable score.
"We have to tip passes, affect the quarterback, the weather," Mike Vrabel said. "The more than we can turn the football over, that makes a huge difference, especially on the road and in the offense, being able to capitalize and make it some points and touchdowns."
It wasn't the prettiest game for the Patriots in totality, but a strong second half willed them to a third divisional win on the year. And now Byard, former teammates with Willis, can add that first Patriots pick football to his collection .
"Just kind of proud of the guys, the way we just fought back and didn't fold during the first half," Byard said. "Outside of that double move, we basically didn't give up any points in the second half for our defense. We just fought and kept fighting and kept the momentum strong."
