title: Giants Bye Week Watchlist: 8 Players Who Will Decide the Second Half
full_text:
As the New York Giants enjoy their much-needed, well-deserved bye week, they will take stock of their performance through their first seven games of the 2026 NFL season.
Big Blue has defied the odds to earn a 4-2-1 record and sole possession of first place in the NFC East for the first time since 2015.
Despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart and outside linebacker Brian Burns to season-ending injuries, the Giants arrived at their bye week as a battle-tested squad ready to pursue their first playoff berth since 2022.
Though the Giants are undoubtedly pleased with their effort in all three phases, from the coaching prowess of John Harbaugh to the on-field performance of quarterback J.J. McCarthy, New York must keep putting in maximum effort through the season’s 10 remaining games.
With that in mind, here are eight players worth watching as the Giants prepare to return to the field.
While a strong running game and a lockdown defense remain vital to modern NFL success, the league is still quarterback-driven. In that regard, McCarthy tops New York’s watchlist for the second half of the season.
Since taking the starting reins from Jameis Winston in Week 6, the 23-year-old McCarthy has showcased his multifaceted skill set while staying calm, cool, and collected.
McCarthy has completed 63.3% of his passes for 495 yards and one touchdown. Though certain areas of his game still require improvement, the 10th overall selection in the 2024 NFL Draft has seemingly done enough to earn the starting job for the foreseeable future.
Now, the biggest question is whether McCarthy can sustain the level of play and leadership required to keep New York in contention for the division title.
Though he may be best suited to an offense built on zone reads, designed runs, and RPO packages, the former Michigan Wolverine has also shown his prowess in the deep passing game.
Ultimately, the Giants’ playoff hopes may rest on McCarthy’s dual-threat capabilities.
With star receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely almost certain to remain McCarthy’s top pass-catching targets, Fields has emerged as another notable option along the perimeter.
The Giants’ rookie has compiled 16 catches for 248 yards and one touchdown, including a four-catch, 83-yard performance in the team’s Week 7 victory over the Houston Texans.
At 6-foot-4, 222 pounds, Fields is one of the biggest and strongest receivers on New York’s roster. As he continues to improve, he should remain one of the Giants’ most prominent vertical targets in the coming weeks.
After a string of subpar performances to begin the season, most notably a Week 6 loss to the Saints in which he saw just six snaps and zero carries, Skattebo returned to the Giants’ offensive mix with a vengeance .
In their overtime victory over Houston, the Arizona State product had his best game to date, carrying the ball 17 times for 124 yards and a touchdown.
Like McCarthy, however, Skattebo now faces the challenge of maintaining and even exceeding his improved play.
If offensive coordinator Matt Nagy continues to deploy the 24-year-old as the team’s lead back, Skattebo will need to perform consistently on every down while setting the tone for fellow running backs Devin Singletary and Greg DeRosiers.
After starting his rookie season 9-for-9 on field goals (including three makes from 50+ yards out), Zvada’s fortunes have taken a hit in recent weeks.
The Giants’ undrafted rookie out of Michigan missed three field-goal attempts in New York’s Week 5 tie with the Washington Commanders, then missed 44- and 56-yarders in Week 7 against the Texans.
In total, the kicker has connected on 13 of 18 field goal attempts, while going 12-for-12 on extra points.
Harbaugh recently said the Giants have no current plans to change the kicker. Still, they remain hopeful Zvada will use the bye week to work on his plant placement and other fixable mechanics that have caused him difficulty lately.
While the talent is clearly there, New York cannot afford for its kicking game to become a liability in its quest for a postseason bid.
Through the Giants’ first seven games this season, Reese leads the team with 56 total tackles, 1.5 sacks, and 5.5 tackles for loss. Right now, Giants fans are wondering just how good the fifth overall selection in April’s draft can be over the next 10 games.
The 6-foot-4, 243-pounder possesses a triple-threat skill set that lets him stop the run, drop into coverage, and rush the passer. As a result, Reese has found comfort playing all over the field. Though he is unquestionably at his best when aligned inside, he has also been a factor on the edge when called upon to help in the pass rush.
While the case can be made for linebacker Abdul Carter or safety Jevon Holland, Reese has arguably been New York’s best defensive player this season.
As he continues to grow and develop, the team’s front seven is poised to become even more effective in making life difficult for opposing offenses.
One of the best decisions the Giants’ coaches made during the first half of the season was choosing to deploy Banks as a true matchup cornerback. Fortunately for the Giants, he has delivered above expectations.
In five appearances (all starts) this season, the 25-year-old has compiled 20 total tackles, 10 passes defensed, and one interception, which he returned for a 98-yard touchdown against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 4.
Still, Banks’ best showing came during the team’s Week 7 win over the Houston Texans. When directly matched against star receiver Nico Collins, Banks held him to just one catch for four yards on four targets.
If he continues to show the same shut-down capabilities against opposing receivers into the home stretch, New York’s secondary will be a big reason for its success.
After linebacker Tremaine Edmunds’ season-ending shoulder injury, the Giants needed someone to step in at inside linebacker.
Based on his most recent performance, McFadden appears to be their much-needed “next man up.”
The fifth-year veteran delivered 10 tackles, three run stuffs, two tackles for loss, and one quarterback hit against the Texans in Week 7.
With 14 total tackles this season, the 6-foot-2, 232-pounder will remain a key component at inside linebacker.
Given his sideline-to-sideline range at the second level, McFadden should help keep the Giants’ defense at a respectable level for the remainder of the season.
As several NFL pundits continue to weigh the pros and cons of trading him before the Nov. 10 deadline, Thibodeaux’s recent production may ultimately keep him in a Giants uniform through the remainder of the 2026 season.
New York’s first-round pick in 2022 has logged 277 defensive snaps through the Giants’ first seven games, collecting 15 total tackles.
However, Thibodeaux has zero sacks during that span. With Big Blue needing more punch in the pass rush, he will need to step up his production to help offset Burns’ loss.
Despite his struggles along the edge, Thibodeaux has established value as a run defender. Over the last three weeks, the 6-foot-5, 258-pound defender is tied for the second-most run stops in the league among edge rushers with six.
Given New York’s need at the position and his improved run-stopping, Thibodeaux will be worth watching during the Giants’ stretch run.

title: Why Chasing Jonathan Taylor Wouldn't Be a Repeat of the Giants’ 2022 Mistake
full_text:
The New York Giants ’ reported trade interest in big names such as former Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons (now with the Bears) and Colts running back Jonathan Taylor has the fan base and the football world in general abuzz.
But Ted Nguyen of The Athletic views the Giants’ reported push to be big-time buyers in the final days before the Nov. 10 trade deadline as recent Big Blue history repeating itself, and not in a good way.
The film analyst, taking to X , wrote, “Giants going after Jonathan Taylor is a classic team that’s ‘ahead of schedule’ mistake, IMO.
“Harbaugh had (sic) made a difference, and they are competing every week, but do they really think they are an RB away from being a true contender?”
Taylor, the Colts' second-round pick in 2020, has earned first-team All-Pro honors (2021), three Pro Bowl selections (2021, 2024 and 2025), one league rushing yardage title (2021) and two league rushing touchdown titles (2021 and 2025). Indianapolis is now reportedly open to trading him .
The 27-year-old Taylor is signed through 2028, and he represents the type of bell cow running back Giants head coach John Harbaugh wistfully wished for just two weeks ago.
NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported that the Colts rejected a 2027 second-round draft pick plus an additional pick for the running back, suggesting they believe some desperate team looking for a bell cow might do whatever it takes to acquire him.
The crux of Nguyen’s objection seems to be the mistake the Giants made after the 2022 season. Following a 9-7-1 campaign that included a postseason berth, the team went backward because general manager Joe Schoen thought it was further along than it really was.
In retrospect, that 2022 team never really had a clear identity, as the roster-building process felt like the front office was merely slapping pieces together at random.
That hasn’t been the case with the 2026 team, which has a clear identity on both sides of the ball. As a result, it has been easier for the front office to add players who fit Harbaugh’s vision and get rid of those who don’t.
The result has been a Giants team that, while not always pretty, has been competitive. Say what you want about the quality of the NFC East, which has come into focus as the season has gone on.
Harbaugh has still kept the team competitive and within the identity he envisioned, despite losing his starting quarterback and outside linebacker, which speaks to a lack of panic when adversity has hit.
Harbaugh and the Giants have seemingly taken the approach of swapping draft picks for players who not only fit their vision and identity but are also under contract for multiple years.
Those in favor of building through the draft might argue that the approach is akin to cutting corners. What they ignore is that the Giants’ attempts to rebuild via the draft have not exactly been at the top of the league in terms of success, and that Harbaugh isn’t willing to wait until the team is two or three draft classes into his tenure to make a run.
Acquiring Taylor, if the Giants can do so, would fit a major piece of the puzzle into an existing framework rather than trying to reinvent the wheel, as might have been the case in 2022.
The most important thing to remember is that such a move, if it comes to fruition, is less about the short term than the big picture. And while Nguyen also argues that “[Taylor] should be for a contender trying to go over the top,” well, isn’t that what the Giants are trying to do?

title: 4 College Prospects Giants Scouts Should Watch This Weekend
full_text:
As the New York Giants enjoy their much-needed bye week, Giants scouts may be watching closely as college football’s Week 9 slate unfolds.
With the stretch run ahead at 4-2-1, this could be a good time to scout potential targets as prospects make their cases for selection in the 2027 NFL Draft.
Beyond running back, the team’s biggest need remains defensive tackle. Coach John Harbaugh and his staff may also want to keep an eye on late Day 3 or undrafted options in the kicking game, should rookie Dominic Zvada’s struggles continue.
Here are four players the Giants may watch this weekend.
Despite Cam Skattebo’s stellar Week 7 performance against the Houston Texans, New York is still likely to be in the market for a running back this draft season.
Though the position may no longer be Big Blue’s top priority, the team may be wise to take a close look at Florida’s Jadan Baugh, the consensus top running back in this year’s draft class.
The 6-foot-1, 225-pound back is a well-built rusher who can be effective on every down. In addition to his impressive blend of size and speed, Baugh is known for his impeccable ball security.
Aside from one fumble during his freshman season, the Atlanta native has held onto the ball for more than 1,000 collegiate snaps. Given the Giants’ struggles with ball security this season, Baugh would likely put those concerns to rest.
In a marquee matchup against No. 3 Georgia this weekend, Baugh should be well-motivated to add to his 763 rushing yards and 13 rushing touchdowns. He has also caught nine passes for 59 yards out of the backfield.
While the Giants continue to be linked to defensive tackle trade rumors as the NFL’s Nov. 10 deadline approaches, they may find a few college prospects quite intriguing. Washington deserves to be on that list, largely because he can play anywhere along the defensive front.
At 6-foot-3 and 330 pounds, the Detroit native has impressive size and power, with much of that potential still untapped.
Washington is at his best when stacking blockers, while using his frame to anchor and resist opposing double teams. As a run defender, he projects to maintain gap integrity at the pro level.
As the Ducks prepare to face No. 20 Northwestern in Week 9, look for Washington to be a factor in run defense while showcasing his surprisingly quick first step when trying to collapse the pocket.
As a former defensive end, Etta is well-versed in getting after the quarterback off the edge and finishing rushes with sacks. However, his versatility in taking on double teams and stuffing run plays led the Wolverines to move him inside.
Given the Giants’ need for an ominous presence on the interior of their defensive line, Etta could be an intriguing fit. He has developed as a run defender, and he uses both his athleticism and technique to pressure the quarterback.
On that note, the Giants may be wise to keep an eye on SHI Stadium in nearby Piscataway, N.J., as Michigan takes on Rutgers this weekend, especially with Etta determined to add to his 20 tackles and 0.5 sacks for the Wolverines this season.
Although teams rarely invest draft capital in specialists, Carneiro is among the top kicking prospects in this year’s class. With Zvada’s recent struggles, New York might wish to keep its options open heading into 2027.
Since transferring to Ole Miss from Western Kentucky following the 2024 season, Carneiro has become one of the Rebels’ top point-scoring weapons.
The 5-foot-11, 195-pounder is known for his leg strength and clutch kicking. His 48-yard game-winner against Louisville on Sept. 6 earned him co-winner honors for the SEC Special Teams Player of the Week award.
This season, the Cornelius, N.C., native has made 11 of 14 field goals, with his longest coming on a 57-yarder against Charlotte in Week 2. Carneiro has also been perfect on extra-point attempts, going 29-for-29 and earning a total of 62 points.
In what many expect to be a closely contested matchup against Auburn, Carneiro may get a few chances to showcase his kicking prowess this weekend.

title: Jets Rookie & Sophomore Power Rankings: Who's Rising (and Falling) Ahead of Week 9
full_text:
The Jets dropped another winnable game, losing to the Raiders 38-33 at MetLife Stadium. While questionable coaching decisions persist, such as calling a Hail Mary with 14 seconds left, Sunday’s loss was largely a result of the players’ failure to execute.
From a costly special teams touchdown to the defense surrendering 24 points in the second half, nothing went right for Gang Green.
With another humiliating loss in the books, New York drops to 2-6, and head coach Aaron Glenn’s hot seat is sizzling . Despite the defeat, there were some positives, including the offense’s red-hot performance and promising contributions from the young players.
With that said, let’s take a look at where the rookies and sophomores rank heading into the team’s Week 9 meeting with the Chiefs.
Note: Anez Cooper and VJ Payne are currently excluded from the list. Both Cooper and Payne are on injured reserve but are eligible to return after missing the first four games of the season.
With how things are unfolding this season, several players on this list likely won’t be on the team next year. One of them is Arian Smith.
The former Georgia Bulldog hasn’t proven that he can contribute beyond special teams or show any significant progression as a receiver. One thing New York will be looking for this offseason is to strengthen its depth at receiver.
Given Smith’s lack of production, it's safe to assume we’ve seen the last of him in green and white.
While the stats won’t tell the whole story, Geno Smith had one of his best seasons against Las Vegas. Playing against his former team, Smith completed 62.5% of his passes for 290 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception.
He was comfortable in the pocket, took shots downfield, and put the offense in scoring position more often than not. Smith did everything he could to help the team win, leading the offense to a season-high 33 points. The defense just didn’t hold up its end of the bargain.
Even though the loss isn’t on Smith, New York could turn to Cade Klubnik if the team can’t get into the win column over the coming weeks. With head coach Aaron Glenn on the hot seat and the Jets sitting at 2-6, upper management could want to see what they have with Klubnik once they are eliminated from playoff contention.
Once again, Kiko Mauigoa was inactive for Sunday’s matchup against the Raiders, as a lingering quadriceps injury has kept him out of five of the past six games.
Even though Mauigoa wouldn’t have changed the outcome, New York could have given him some reps, given how poorly Demario Davis has been this season .
Outside of his leadership and locker room presence, Davis just hasn’t cut it for the Jets. He’s regressed immensely in coverage and as a run defender, already recording 11 missed tackles so far.
While Mauigoa wasn’t significantly better in his rookie season, the Jets must consider giving him an opportunity if they continue to drop games.
If you told Jets fans a few months back that Malachi Moore played just nine defensive snaps across eight games, they would be surprised.
The former safety from Alabama has seen his starting role reduced to a depth role with the additions of Dane Belton and Minkah Fitzpatrick. Despite this, he’s made the most of his opportunity on special teams.
Although the unit allowed the first kickoff-return touchdown of the season, Moore has been New York’s most productive special teamer, recording eight tackles.
If his production continues and the Jets' losing streak extends, we should expect to see Moore earn reps on defense.
With Jarvis Brownlee Jr. listed as a healthy scratch last week and D’Angelo Ponds playing well in his absence, it felt like the Jets would lean more on their 50th overall selection at nickelback.
That wasn’t the case against the Raiders, however, as Ponds played just one defensive snap. Meanwhile, Brownlee played in 27 snaps and delivered another underwhelming showing, giving up a touchdown and committing two defensive pass-interference penalties (one accepted).
Additionally, his 27.8 coverage grade was the lowest among all Jets defenders , per Pro Football Focus.
With Brownlee underperforming and New York four games under .500, it’s time for Glenn to make a change and give Ponds the starting nickelback job. The team used a second-round pick on him, yet he’s played just 65 defensive snaps over six games.
We already know that, at best, Brownlee is a serviceable contributor. With Ponds, however, we have no clue what he can bring to the table. Now’s the time to start increasing his reps.
Another week, another quiet game for Kenyon Sadiq.
While the former Oregon Duck made a great 22-yard grab that set up Braleon Allen’s touchdown on the next play, Sadiq just hasn’t been involved or utilized since Week 3.
Offensive coordinator Frank Reich designed plays for him in the first four weeks: from jet sweeps to screen passes. Now, we don’t even see the Jets try to use his athleticism.
However, Reich isn’t entirely at fault. Sadiq hasn’t consistently created separation downfield, while Mason Taylor continues to outshine him as a pass catcher and blocker. While Sadiq has improved as a blocker over the last few weeks, it’s evident the team prefers Jeremy Ruckert and Jelani Woods on running downs.
At some point, Reich has to find a way to get him involved, much like the team tried to get Garrett Wilson going against Las Vegas.
Taylor wasn’t nearly as dominant as he was last week versus the Dolphins, but he still managed to haul in three catches for 19 yards on five targets.
It hasn’t been a pretty season for Taylor, but he continues to see an increased role in the offense since returning from a thumb injury, posting 15 receptions (20 targets) for 138 yards and two touchdowns across four games.
The former LSU Tiger has also stood out as a run blocker, earning a 67.5 run-blocking grade , per PFF . With his solid play as a receiver and blocker, Taylor remains the Jets’ TE1.
Omar Cooper Jr. has balled out since his return from the injured reserve. In the past two games, the former Indiana Hoosier has posted two consecutive 100-yard performances, showcasing his speed and playmaking ability.
Heading into Week 8’s matchup against the Raiders, it felt like Cooper would have another terrific game in store, considering how bad their secondary has been. However, Cooper was a complete non-factor, as he didn’t even receive a single target.
Yet, this isn’t a total surprise. With Wilson visibly frustrated by his lack of targets over the past few weeks, Reich and Co. needed to get him involved in every way possible. Additionally, with Mitchell back, he’s taken some of Cooper’s downfield opportunities.
Hopefully, Cooper can bounce back against Kansas City.
If you look solely at the stat sheet, you’d think Darrell Jackson Jr. had a quiet game. That couldn’t be any further from the truth, as the fourth-round selection was one of the few impactful defenders in the loss.
Playing a career-high 42 defensive snaps, he helped New York hold the Raiders to 95 rushing yards and 2.9 yards per carry. With his presence upfront, Jackson did an excellent job clogging running lanes and shutting down the Raiders in short-yardage situations.
His best play came late in the second quarter, when he and Harrison Phillips stopped the Raiders on a sneak attempt to force a turnover on downs. Although he didn’t generate pressure, Jackson continues to showcase that he can be a reliable contributor in the defensive line rotation.
With T’Vondre Sweat sidelined for the foreseeable future, the Jets will need to rely on the former Florida State Seminole.
Azareye’h Thomas started the season strong, emerging as one of the Jets’ breakout players in coverage. Over the past few weeks, however, Thomas’ play has steadily declined.
Against Las Vegas, Thomas allowed five catches (six targets) for 50 yards and a touchdown, earning a 50.4 coverage grade , per PFF . This marks the third straight game Thomas has finished with a coverage grade below 55.

title: Biggest Decision Aaron Glenn Got Wrong vs. Raiders Show What Needs to Change in Week 9
full_text:
Despite getting off to a much quicker start and leading by double digits in the second half, the Jets still found a way to suffer an excruciating 38-33 loss to the Raiders on Sunday at MetLife Stadium.
Even with a 100-yard receiver (Adonai Mitchell), a 100-yard rusher (Braelon Allen), more first downs (26-22) and the advantage in total yards (439-333), red-zone struggles, special teams issues and a poor defensive game plan came back to bite Gang Green in a game they will certainly want back.
Granted, rookie edge rusher David Bailey missed his first game with a groin injury , and the defense was without four of its starters overall on the D-line, but that is still no excuse for New York to drop its third straight game, all of which have been by single digits.
The Jets did feast on a Raiders rushing attack that averages the second-fewest yards per game (77.3 ypg), giving up just 95 total yards in the game. While that may have been the case, head coach Aaron Glenn did a poor job making defensive adjustments coming out of the break to ensure his team protected its lead and remained in control of the game.
From consistently leaving smaller corners on Raiders tight end Brock Bowers and allowing him to shred the middle of the field to costly third-down penalties and allowing three consecutive touchdowns out of the locker room, it was a second-half collapse for Glenn behind some more questionable coaching decisions.
With points on each of their first-half drives, everything appeared to be lining up well for the Jets to have a shot on Sunday. They even answered the Raiders' TD drive to begin the second half with one of their own to stretch the lead back to nine in the third quarter, but that is when the momentum started to shift in favor of Las Vegas.
The Raiders marched down the field on another 10-play, 65-yard drive to get within two and followed up a three-and-out from the Jets offense with a nine-play, 84-yard drive to take the lead early in the fourth quarter. Back-to-back three-and-outs ensued from both sides before the two teams traded field goals on their next two drives and set the stage for one last Jets drive trailing 38-33.
Despite advancing all the way down to the Raiders' 35-yard-line, offensive coordinator Frank Reich made the bizarre decision to go for a Hail Mary with 14 seconds on the clock instead of getting a little closer to the end zone with time to work with. That is when quarterback Geno Smith accounted for the game's only turnover as Jeremy Chinn came down with the toe-tapping interception (h/t The Goal Line Grind ) to end the game.
Jeremy Chinn seals the victory for the Raiders and shows off some toe drag swag for the INT off Geno Smith. pic.twitter.com/Eqd8TQpAH4
Glenn has made it clear that play-calling is his "superpower ," but it was anything but that in this game and has been for most of the season. The blown lead in the second half was one thing, as was the offense's inability to convert in the red zone (2-of-6) and on third down (4-of-11), but the decision to isolate New York's smaller corners on Bowers proved detrimental.
Between Bowers (seven catches, 92 yards, two TDs) and Michael Mayer (five catches, 53 yards), Glenn failed to find an answer for either of them or make the appropriate adjustments to account for the success they were having. That, in turn, allowed QB Kirk Cousins to establish a rhythm and the Raiders offense to stay on the field, even without a go-to wide receiver on the field.
There is no denying that the 95-yard kickoff return from Dylan Laube was the difference in the game for the Raiders in a five-point outcome, but the Jets still did more than enough offensively to come away with the win. The defense, however, could not put a full game together and could not get the timely stops that were needed to secure the victory.
The Jets hit the road again to take on the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, and if they want to avoid another frustrating outcome and pull off the upset, Glenn needs to simplify his defensive approach and be willing to adapt to what is happening on the field.
His superpowers failed against the Raiders and it is important that he can get his unit to eliminate the back-breaking penalties and make it tougher on opposing QBs to establish any rhythm. After all, Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes always keeps opposing defenses guessing with his versatility and ability to evade pressure in the pocket. Running back Kenneth Walker III, meanwhile, has the third-most rush yards in the league (770) and has been an absolute force in his first season with the franchise.
After giving up a combined 92 points over the last three games, when you include the kickoff return from Sunday's game, Glenn needs to become more flexible with his schemes and disguise some of his coverage, especially if the Jets want to create more red-zone stops after allowing the Raiders to convert all four of their attempts.
There were a lot of positives to take from the Week 8 loss, but if Glenn is going to have his bunch ready to face the challenge the Chiefs will present on Sunday, he has to be willing to make defensive adjustments throughout the game.
If he fails to do that and keeps making questionable decisions with his schemes, it could get ugly this week and moving forward as his time in Gotham continues to run out.

title: Omar CooperJr.'s Week 8 Disappearing Act Isn't Really That Concerning for Jets
full_text:
Omar Cooper Jr. was nowhere to be found in the Jets' Week 8 loss to the Raiders . The rookie wideout got zero targets against Las Vegas after back-to-back 100-plus-yard performances, leaving New York fans wondering if the explosive start to his career is almost over.
However, New York shouldn't be too concerned about the rookie's limited usage in the loss.
Cooper has shown what he is capable of early on in his NFL career. That does not mean that he should be expected to be a 100-yard receiver every week. As the Jets continue the season, there will be plenty of opportunities for Omar, but they may not be as plentiful as they were in Weeks 6 and 7.
Cooper is a rookie, no matter what his performances look like. Cooper was drafted as a complementary receiver . not to be the number-one receiver on the team. While he's been great, there was not a lot of opportunity for his skill set against Las Vegas.
Geno Smith only had three pass attempts over the middle against the Raiders, where Cooper has had his most success this season. The Raiders clearly wanted Geno to throw the ball outside, which hurt Cooper's performance.
The rookie ran 26 receiving routes in Week 8; 16 of them were from the slot , according to Pro Football Focus . Weeks like this are bound to happen for Cooper, especially when opposing teams try to take away his main area of success. There's no need for panic as the former Hoosier settles into his role in the Jets' offense.
Week 8 was the first time that the Jets had a fully healthy receiving corps for a full game. That leaves mouths to feed. The Jets clearly have talent all across the board at skill positions. Garrett Wilson is Garrett Wilson ; Adonai Mitchell had seven catches for 142 yards and a touchdown; Kenyon Sadiq has had a 100-yard performance; and Mason Taylor was coming off a two-touchdown game.
An incredible 48-yard catch by Adonai Mitchell! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/a7pOlkJn27
There will be weeks when Cooper doesn't get the majority of targets. The Jets have a lot of talent on the perimeter. Smith has felt comfortable spreading the ball around, and Wilson needs to get his. This doesn't mean Cooper will be iced from the offense; he is just playing his role.
The 22-year-old was drafted as the Jets' slot receiver, making him (for now) the de facto number-three receiver. Wilson and Mitchell will stay on the outside, and Cooper will patrol the middle routes. With a fully healthy receiving group, the slot not getting the most targets every week isn't a concern.
Cooper will have a chance to get back in the box score against Kansas City in Week 9. According to NFL Next Gen Stats , the Chiefs gave up six completions on eight middle-of-the-field attempts against the Broncos in Week 8; that bodes well for the Jets' rookie.
Cooper has 12 receptions this season; seven of those have been over the middle. The game script against the Chiefs should favor the rookie. Not every game will be a breakout game for Cooper, but he does have a chance to continue his stellar season in Week 9.
The Jets will likely look to get the rookie back into the game after his donut against Las Vegas . If Cooper lets the game come to him and keeps performing as he has, he should return to being an integral part of the offense.
The Jets and their fans shouldn't worry about the rookie after a game that didn't favor his talents; they should look for what he does when the game favors him.

title: Potential Isaiah Williams Trade Destination Makes Too Much Sense for Jets to Ignore
full_text:
The walls are closing in on the Jets after Sunday's loss to the Raiders cemented Gang Green's second three-game losing streak of the season. Beginning Week 9 with a 2-6 record all but guarantees the Jets will be sellers ahead of the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 10, making it interesting to see who general manager Darren Mougey will be open to moving.
Third-year wide receiver Isaiah Williams is among the players who could be moved in the coming days. Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, and Omar Cooper Jr. have solidified themselves as the three best wideouts in New York's offense, making Williams expendable—especially as he's scheduled to become a restricted free agent in March.
Based on his usage this season, the Jets may not see Williams having much of a future (or present) left in Gotham. If they attempt to trade him and recoup the best return before the trade deadline, one potential destination stands out as the best first-call option for Mougey & Co.
On Friday, Sports Illustrated' s Albert Breer reported that the Steelers are among the buyers who've "asked around on receivers" leading up to the trade deadline. That might be even truer after Pittsburgh's WR room left much to be desired in Sunday's 27-6 win over Cleveland.
Even though it was a 21-point victory, the Steelers' wideouts didn't make much impact. Only three of their WRs recorded a reception, with none surpassing the 30-yard mark. It's crystal clear that DK Metcalf isn't the WR1 he once was, and with Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson still on Pittsburgh's injured reserve, New York would be foolish not to at least do some due diligence.
A quiet start to the 2026 season (12 catches for 169 receiving yards and two touchdowns) has Williams needing a change of scenery . He won't instantly become the next Hines Ward for the Steelers, but he's a solid enough hand to keep things afloat in the Steel City. Williams's 73-yard performance against the Bears in Week 4 showed he can have the occasional big game, and his 18-yard touchdown against the Raiders on Sunday might have done enough to boost his value at the right time.
Geno Smith hits Isaiah Williams and the Jets take the lead LVvsNYJ on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TDgw4CC6Fb
Williams is also familiar with the AFC North after spending time there with the Bengals in 2024 and 2025, which could further interest the Steelers. He faced Pittsburgh twice, including giving a glimpse of what he could do when he returned four kicks for 133 yards—his second-most in a game—in Week 18 of the 2024 season.
As for how a deal with the Steelers would benefit the Jets, look no further than the Black and Yellow's draft pick stockpile. According to Spotrac , the Steelers have nine selections in each of the next two NFL Drafts , so they might have an easier time walking away from that capital if the Jets can help with one of their most pressing issues.
Even if it's just a pair of 2027 seventh-rounders, two picks would be better than one. That's even truer if the Jets aren't going to re-sign Williams this offseason.
The Steelers (or any team) acquiring Williams would take on a cap hit of $986,928 , according to Spotrac , which isn't bad for someone who can occasionally put up a 70-yard game. His special teams contributions also add to why it's more than fair value. Williams has returned 12 punts for 127 yards and 13 kicks for 343 yards this season, one year after being one of the NFL's best returners.
With just over a week before the trade deadline, the Jets need to stop waiting. The Steelers will address their WR needs one way or another, so it may as well be Gang Green who benefits from a potential deal.

title: Faria's Focus Week 8: 5 Jets Thoughts as Losing Streak Extends to Three With Loss to Raiders
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. —The definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over while expecting different results.
It's obvious that definition should be the centerpiece of the Jets' slogan by now.
New York gave up 24 second-half points after leading by nine at the half, and found a way to lose another one-score game on Sunday. Las Vegas moved to 4-4 with rookie head coach Klint Kubiak, with a 38-33 win.
The Jets' 2-6 record now shows a team that is bad in situational football and still in the early phases of a rebuild. With that said, it's time to break down some of the most important thoughts from the team's loss on Sunday.
Let's get to five of them here.
No one is really surprised by Sunday's loss. Gang Green has seen five of their six defeats come by one score this season, and much of that is due to in-game decision-making mistakes by the coaching staff. It is evident that, after 25 games, they aren't going to learn from their mistakes or get better.
Many of the issues in Sunday's loss to the Raiders came from in-game decisions. New York continuously settled for field goals instead of going for touchdowns on four offensive drives. ESPN 's tracker listed three of those decisions as mistakes, including both field goals kicked in the first half.
When the Jets were kicking field goals, the Raiders were scoring touchdowns.
There's also the reality that the Jets' defense simply isn't good enough. Injuries certainly play a part, but for a head coach who touted that play-calling was his superpower, the results have been simply unacceptable.
Asking the Jets to alter their staff or make changes in the middle of a 2-6 start to the season would not be the correct move. New York currently has the fourth, sixth and 10th overall selections in the 2027 draft, according to Tankathon . The Jets should aim to keep their pick as high as possible.
It would be best for the organization to keep the staff where it is, and allow them to bottom out.
We've already talked about one of the long-term benefits of this season crumbling, as it has for the Jets. They could be the first team in NFL history to have three first-round picks all inside the top 10.
But that isn't the only benefit to what the Jets have shown on taoe.
There is a lot to like about New York's offensive firepower. Last week, Omar Cooper Jr. and Mason Taylor had excellent games. This week, Adonai Mitchell's seven-catch, 147-yard game even overshadowed a bounce-back performance from Garrett Wilson. Add in an offensive line that controlled the line of scrimmage in the run game, and the Jets have a collection of young offensive weapons that the next coaching staff won't be able to overlook.
For as bad as the season has become, the more offensive success the team has, the easier it will be to lure another coach to do the job when they get to that point in January.
New York has been left with no choice here. Braelon Allen, after another incredible performance on Sunday, has snatched the Jets' starting running back role from Breece Hall, who has been out for the last five weeks due to an injury.
On Sunday, Allen recorded 146 yards on 21 carries, including a 21-yard score to give the Jets a two-score lead late in the third quarter. Over his last four games as a starter, Allen has 440 yards rushing combined, including becoming the first running back since Curtis Martin in 2004 to have three straight 100-yard games.
Braelon Allen scores and now has 142 rushing yards on the day! LVvsNYJ on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/aGaC9Th33s
Afterwards, Glenn still commited his loyalty to Hall in making sure he would be 100% before returning to the field.
"Breece is still a part of this team," Glenn said. "I've said it before: We're in the business of keeping good players and he's one of our better players so he'll be here."
But reading between the lines, it's clear that Allen is going to be the team's bellcow moving forward. It wouldn't make sense any other way.
Multiple things can be true about New York's defense.
The last point may not seem fair to the coaching staff or talent, but context must be included. In the Raiders' first two offensive touchdowns of the day, the team targeted All-Pro-caliber tight end Brock Bowers, who found himself matched up against a cornerback.
What defensive coach would want Jarvis Brownlee or Brandon Stephens covering an athletic freak like Bowers, especially in a goal-line situation?
New York's defensive alignment, focusing heavily on four down linemen due to the injuries, also cost the unit. Las Vegas had just 2.9 yards per carry, but the team also had all day to throw. That's because the Jets do not have the pass rushers needed to be consistent on every down. There were limited adjustments, and they didn't have much of a plan when their blitzes weren't working.
Again, injuries have something to do with that, but coaching matters. And for a team that is 5-20 with Glenn as head coach and defensive play-caller, it will only reflect on him.
For yours truly, Sunday was a nightmare. I'm colorblind, so you had a better chance of me kicking a 60-yard field goal than figuring out if Raiders fans had taken over MetLife Stadium at the start of the game. The green and black looked exactly the same.
That said, you didn't need to see Raider fans to know they were there. They DID take over MetLife Stadium. Those fans even had an impact on the game, as the crowd noise pushed Olu Fashanu into a false start late in the contest.
Jets fans aren't exactly shocked by that. After 15 years of no playoffs and soon-to-be 11 years of finishing below .500, MetLife Stadium has normally been overtaken by opposing fans for years now.
And no one should expect that to change until a new coaching staff has been brought in.
Until then, MetLife will repeatedly find opposing fans cheering for their teams, and any home-field advantage the Jets probably wish they had will go by the wayside. It's what happens to a battered fanbase like this.
It's not like the Jets have changed much from their mindset over the years.

title: Most Important Jets Postgame Quotes From Week 8 (And What They Mean Moving Forward)
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — It's getting late for the Aaron Glenn era of the Jets.
After their 38-33 loss to the Raiders , Gang Green fell to 2-6 in the 2026 season and 5-20 in their first 25 games under Glenn. It appears obvious that the future of the head coach is only a matter of when, and not if, they move on from him.
Sunday's loss was more of the same : poor in-game coaching, a lack of adjustments, and failed execution when the team needed it most. And it's left both players and coaches looking for answers.
Here are some of the biggest quotes to keep an eye on after Week 8 and ahead of the final stretch before the NFL trade deadline.
This was the quote of the day. After another defeat, the team's sixth in their last seven contests, All-Pro safety Minkah Fitzpatrick explained why the team's defense struggled as much as it did on Sunday.
Jets being Jets. Same old Jets. The moniker that Glenn has tried repeatedly to end came back at the worst time, from one of his most important leaders.
Now, Jets PR afterward did clarify Fitzpatrick's comments, saying he actually meant Jets "beating" Jets, inferring the fact the team was beating themselves with mental and physical mistakes after the game.
But it doesn't change the fact that players understand what comes with playing for the team. What can go wrong will go wrong. And no one has a plan to stop that.
"It's something different every single week; that's the frustrating part," Fitzpatrick said. "It's not a consistent problem. The only good thing about that is we can fix the thing we struggled last week, but at some point we have to play consistent football."
As usual, Glenn made several mistakes over the course of Sunday's loss . Chief among them, though, was his willingness to take field goals early in the game, including on their first two drives, instead of going for it on fourth down.
The Jets traded field goals for touchdowns with the Raiders. It's no wonder that the team lost by five. On Monday, though, Glenn made it clear he felt he made the right decision with those passive calls, while pointing to other issues as to why the team lost.
Glenn is not the only defensive-minded head coach with a very passive in-game decision-making process. In fact, most head coaches with a defensive background tend to be conservative with their decision-making when it comes to points.
But there's also a reason why those coaches tend to struggle more than offensive guys. It's because they come in with a desire to see their defense play physically and aggressively, but they won't match that with in-game decision-making.
Glenn's defense of his decision-making is expected, but it's also fair to say his mindset from the very beginning was wrong on both counts, as it's been for the first 25 games of his tenure.
No group has been more disappointing this season for the Jets than their special teams roster. Injuries have played a part in the struggles, but they don't excuse the 95-yard return for a score they gave up to the Raiders early in the contest.
FIRST KICKOFF-RETURN TD OF THE SEASON! Dylan Laube takes it 95 yards to the house for a @Raiders touchdown! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/qKvypanZrw
"Special teams, we can’t give up a return," Glenn said. "We’ve got to find a way to get better at what we’re doing."
New York's return game has been non-existent, too. The fact is that the group was the best overall unit in the league last season and has been a major hindrance to them in 2026. Chris Banjo seemed like the coordinator who could do no wrong last year.
Now, like Glenn, he appears to be on the hot seat.
Last week, an uncomfortable conversation . Now, it's reality. Jets running back Braelon Allen has earned the starting job in the offense after another stellar performance on Sunday. The former Wisconsin product had 21 carries for 147 yards and over seven yards per carry.
Braelon Allen takes it to the house to add on another @nyjets TD! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/egbD2UhKZr
He's the first Jets runner since 2004 to record 100 yards rushing in three straight games and is on pace for a 1,200-yard season. There is no way that, following Breece Hall's eventual return from injury, the team will go back to their former star as the starter after these numbers.
Even if it means Hall won't be on the trade block.
"Breece is still a part of this team," Glenn said. "I've said it before: We're in the business of keeping good players, and he's one of our better players, so he'll be here."
Allen has recorded 419 rushing yards over his last four games. It's more than any four-game stretch Hall has had in his entire career.
The changing of the guard has happened. It's not a theory anymore. When Hall returns, he will be the third-down back, but nothing more. Allen has taken over.
By the way, Allen is only 22 years old. There's plenty more to come from him.
At 2-6, it's become clear that the current Jets coaching staff will not be here beyond the 2026 regular season. Eventually, they will go in a different direction.
That doesn't mean the players will sign up for that. Despite the record and coaching struggles throughout the season, New York's roster remains steadfast in their belief in Glenn as both head coach and leader.
As a former player himself, Glenn understands that the NFL is a results business. He won't get many opportunities to prove himself for the remainder of the season. But that isn't going to distract him either as the losses continue to pile up.
"There's so much that I think about when it comes to us improving each week that really doesn't come across my mind, to be honest with you," Glenn said. "It's a bottom-line business, and we have to win, but we still have nine games left, so we still have an opportunity to win nine games."
New York is going to finish below .500 for the 11th straight season and miss the playoffs for the 16th straight year. What appears to be a foregone conclusion will most likely only happen at the end of the year, though.

title: Jets Week 8 Awards: Crowning 5 Winners After Excruciating Loss to Raiders
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — If you've seen one Jets game, you've seen them all.
In Week 8, New York squandered a two-score halftime lead over the Raiders by giving up 24 second-half points en route to a 38-33 loss . The defeat dropped the Jets to a measly 2-6 after breakdowns in key areas, including defense, special teams, and coaching.
After their sixth loss in their last seven games, it's time to hand out five awards. And there's plenty to celebrate and point out.
There isn't much more to say . The Jets have had five of their six losses come by one score. Normally, that's a sign of a team improving in all the right ways. Their offense has talent, and they remain in a good cap situation to improve quickly.
It just doesn't seem like head coach Aaron Glenn is going to be part of those future plans.
It's hard to argue against that notion either. Before the year began, Glenn touted his expertise as a play-caller as he took over the duties for the team's defense. Early in the season, it seemed like the move was paying off. On Sunday, it was anything but.
New York gave up 38 points to a Raiders offense without a true top receiver. They gave up 24 second-half points, including the game-winner early in the fourth. In a game where the Jets held the Raiders to just 2.9 yards per carry, and it didn't remotely matter. The unit got completely outclassed and outcoached.
It's left Glenn searching for more answers.
Through 25 games as a head coach, Glenn is 5-20. His defense has gotten worse each week , and the in-game mistakes continue. It's clear that the 2-6 Jets are not going anywhere this season, and it seems that Glenn won't get the benefit of a third year.
Bad football teams find different ways to lose football games. The Jets are a bad team, and their coach just isn't good enough to keep his job at this point.
Does anyone remember Wally Pipp? He was the Yankees' first baseman who sat out a game in 1925 and never got it back for Hall of Fame legend Lou Gehrig. 100 years later, Breece Hall's injury with the Jets isn't a measly headache, but it's clear his role is never going to be the same again.
That's because Braelon Allen and the Jets' rushing attack have turned into an absolute force. Allen became the first running back since HOF RB Curtis Martin in 2004 to rush for 100 yards in three straight games.
On Sunday, Allen ran the ball 21 times for 147 yards, including a 21-yard touchdown. He's mixed his downhill rushing with quality speed and explosiveness that opponents simply aren't ready to handle, especially in the modern game.
Braelon Allen scores and now has 142 rushing yards on the day! LVvsNYJ on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/aGaC9Th33s
After the game, Glenn made it clear that both Breece and Hall would have a role once the latter's injury was fully healthy.
"He’s an important part of what we’re doing, of what we’re building," Glenn said of Hall's recovery. "We’re going to make sure he’s fully healthy before putting him out there, because what we don’t want is a setback."
But it's very clear that there is one lone feature back in New York now. It won't be Hall, perhaps ever again.
Last week, it was Mason Taylor and Omar Cooper Jr. This week was Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell.
In case anyone didn't know already, the Jets are loaded with offensive talent .
We've already talked about how good New York's rushing attack has been, but their passing attack has shown a level of balance over the last several weeks. It makes Glenn's comments about there being "only one ball" seem hilarious.
Geno Smith threw for 290 yards and was able to spread the ball around. Cooper didn't even record a touch in Sunday's game, but Mitchell had a career day with seven catches, 142 yards, and a touchdown. Wilson, meanwhile, added six catches for 83 yards on the day.
An incredible 48-yard catch by Adonai Mitchell! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/a7pOlkJn27
The Wilson-Mitchell-Cooper trio is going to be really fun to watch with a competent play-calling head coach next season. It's going to be even more powerful when the Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq tight end duo continues to develop.
This is how the group should look every single week going forward. They are too talented to struggle otherwise.
In 2025, the Jets' special teams unit was the best in the league by DVOA. It was one of the best overall years for any special teams unit in years.
What did the group do as an encore? Take a significant step back.
The Jets gave up a 95-yard return for a touchdown, the first of any team this season. New York has been banged up all year on their kickoff coverage. But the loss of Kiko Mauigoa and other special teams players should not be the excuse for so many breakdowns in kick and punt coverage.
Yes, the team should celebrate the fact that Jason Sanders made all four of his kicks, but that's not enough to move forward. 2025 seems like a fluke year for coordinator Chris Banjo and the Jets' special teams roster.
It's a group that must make changes.
New York's offense was a clear positive on Sunday. Despite their troubles in the red zone, the unit provided a clear reason for optimism once the Jets bring in a new coaching staff.
That isn't the only glass half-full mindset to have, though.
New York watched the Colts get blown out by the Jaguars, 42-7. Then, the Dallas Cowboys lost an embarrassing 33-30 overtime game to the two-win Cardinals. The Jets own both the Colts' and Cowboys' first-round picks. If the season ended today, the Jets would own the fourth, sixth and 10th overall selections in the 2027 draft, according to Tankathon.
The Jets have to draft a new quarterback, and must reinforce their defense even more. With three potential picks in the top 10, they should be able to solve those major goals.
It's also a significant treasure trove for any future head coach to work with. This will be an attractive job in January.

title: Jets Week 8 Report Card: Grading Every Position After 2nd-Half Collapse vs. Raiders
full_text:
After blowing an opportunity against the previously winless Dolphins in Week 7, it only got worse for the Jets after getting outscored, 24-10, in the second half and losing a 38-33 shootout to the Raiders on Sunday in the second of back-to-back home games.
It was a much quicker start for the Jets with points on all five of their first-half drives. They even outgained the Raiders, 439-333, and were about as efficient as you could ask for offensively, but the persistent red-zone issues (2-of-6), poor special teams play and the defense's inability to get consistent stops proved costly in a tightly contested game.
Instead of winning a pair of games on home soil at MetLife Stadium, the Jets lost both and head into a trickier part of the schedule riding their second three-game losing streak in just eight games with a disappointing 2-6 record.
Before we get too far ahead to a Week 9 road trip to Arrowhead Stadium to face the Chiefs, let's hand out some grades for each unit following another blown opportunity against the Raiders.
Geno Smith was instrumental in New York's quicker start and efficient offensive performance. He was 20-of-32 for 290 yards with two touchdowns and one interception, averaging a solid 9.1 yards per attempt and pushing the ball downfield effectively as the Jets went on to score on each of the offense's first six possessions.
It was not a perfect performance for Smith against his former team, but he ended the game on a sour note with the game-ending interception on Gang Green's final drive as Jeremy Chinn came down with the toe-tapping pick in the end zone .
Jeremy Chinn seals the victory for the Raiders and shows off some toe drag swag for the INT off Geno Smith. pic.twitter.com/Eqd8TQpAH4
The long-awaited breakout performance finally came from WR Adonai Mitchell, coming off zero catches on three targets in his return from a finger injury. He led the way for the Jets' passing attack with seven catches (on nine targets) for 142 yards and a 12-yard touchdown that gave the game its fourth lead change of the opening half.
Garrett Wilson was finally a bigger part of the offense with six catches (on 12 targets) for 83 yards, while Isaiah Williams scored the first TD of the game for Gang Green after a slow start to the season. Rookie Omar Cooper Jr. was not a factor after back-to-back 100-yard receiving games, but it is clear this is a talented group of wideouts where any of the three starters can go off on any given Sunday.
One week after Mason Taylor exploded for two TDs and had a career outing for himself, the TE group made little impact this week. Rookie Kenyon Sadiq had one reception for 22 yards and Taylor came down with three of his five targets for 19 yards, but it was clear the focus this week was more on the WR unit and distributing the ball on the outside against a Raiders defense that ranks 29th in the league in points allowed (28.1 ppg).
It was still some complementary football from this group alongside the wideouts and they helped stretch the middle of the field, but they did not have an impactful performance this time around. It only made matters worse that Raiders TE Brock Bowers went for 92 yards and two TDs and completely took over the game for his unit.
It was hard to find much to be disappointed with from this group as Braelon Allen went off for 21 carries, 147 yards and one TD, averaging a career-high seven yards per carry in the process. He broke free for this 21-yard TD run to give the Jets a nine-point lead in the third quarter (h/t NFL).
Braelon Allen scores and now has 142 rushing yards on the day! LVvsNYJ on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/aGaC9Th33s
He is the first Jets running back with three straight 100-yard games since Hall of Famer Curtis Martin and continues to do a phenomenal job filling in for the injured Breece Hall. Isaiah Davis only had five carries for 15 yards, but he did not have to do much, as Allen completely dominated the Raiders up front and gave the offense some explosive plays to balance out the pass game.
Although they were not as dominant in the second half, the O-line continues to show glimpses of how effective it can be in the trenches. In addition to affording Smith plenty of time to throw, Allen had his way on the ground and took advantage of some open lanes to make the Raiders pay on numerous occasions.
They did allow two sacks and failed to capitalize late with some penalties and an inability to finish out drives when the end zone was in sight. That said, starting left guard Dylan Parham returned to the lineup and was instrumental in helping the unit up front open up holes for Allen to exploit, and it was clear what potential exists as this unit takes more snaps together.
Despite an uncertain future surrounding Will McDonald IV , he recorded his third sack of the season late in the first quarter (h/t SNY Jets) and provided a bright spot for a D-line that was without four of its starters for Sunday's game.
Will McDonald gets the third-down sack 💪 pic.twitter.com/OatTNNgtsD
That was even followed by a fourth-down stop on the Raiders' next offensive possession, but it was clear this unit was banged up and struggling to contain anything Las Vegas threw at them. Granted, the Raiders only mustered 95 yards on the ground, but the Jets could not find a way to slow down QB Kirk Cousins and could not get off the field on third down, as the problems only seem to be getting worse up front as the injuries keep piling up.
Jamien Sherwood continued his breakout season with a team-high 14 tackles (five solo) while also being active against the run. Demario Davis was not bad, either, with seven tackles (one solo), but this unit was still a mixed bag that failed to provide much relief from the inconsistency up front on the D-line.
Coverage issues were a clear problem, with Bowers going off for a pair of TDs and RB Ashton Jeanty going for 64 yards on just three receptions. The inability to contain the open field and limit Bowers and Jeanty proved costly, as did the critical conversions that were allowed in the second half.
The Jets have utilized a heavy dose of man coverage this season, and this was one of the key matchups entering the weekend to see how the secondary could fare against Bowers. Coverage breakdowns and communication issues were prevalent throughout the game as Bowers had his way, and Cousins completed 19 of 26 passes for 247 yards and three TDs, in addition to a season-best 141.0 passer rating.
The secondary failed to create a game-changing takeaway and, while safety Dane Belton led the group with 12 tackles (nine solo), along with one tackle for loss and one pass defended, it was a struggle for the entire group. That was particularly true for Brandon Stephens, who continues to become an unnecessary Jets headache after being called for a defensive holding penalty on a third-and-goal in the third quarter, which led to a Raiders TD a few plays later.
This has nothing to do with kicker Jason Sanders, who nailed all four of his field goals and each of his three extra points. Punter Austin McNamara was solid with an average of 44 yards per punt, and Williams averaged 33 yards on both kickoff returns, but the 95-yard kickoff-return TD from Dylan Laube (h/t NFL+) was the difference in the game.
✅ 95 yards to the house ✅ Raiders' first kickoff return since 2011 ✅ NFL's first kick return TD of 2026 ✅ Dylan Laube's fastest TD (20.97 MPH via @NextGenStats ) LVvsNYJ on FOX/FOX One Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/xu0hAbc4RK
Simply put, that type of play cannot happen, especially in a game decided by five points. You can point to the D-line's continued struggles and some more coaching miscues from this staff, but that play completely flipped the momentum and had a huge say in the outcome of the game, even if the rest of the special teams unit held up its end of the bargain.
So much for head coach Aaron Glenn's confidence in his play-calling coming into this game . His defense gave…

title: Biggest Jets Studs & Duds in Week 8 Loss to Raiders: Aaron Glenn's Superpowers Fail on Braelon Allen's Big Day
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Where were you when the Jets' offense exploded to one of their most impressive performances over the last decade?
Where were you when the Jets' best offensive performance was squandered by a poor defense and special teams breakdowns?
New York scored on their first six drives of the game to kick off Week 8 , but it wasn't enough. The Las Vegas Raiders, encouraged by a large traveling fanbase, took control of the contest late and held on for the 38-33 win. The loss dropped the Jets to a 2-6 mark in a game where they had over 400 yards of offense and over 166 yards on the ground.
As with any loss, there are studs and duds from Sunday's game. Let's break them all down right now.
We have come to the point now where Braelon Allen's production has far exceeded anything a single Jets running back has done since Hall of Famer Curtis Martin was with the team in 2004. Allen ran for 147 yards on 21 carries, including a 21-yard touchdown run to give New York a two-score lead into the third quarter.
Braelon Allen scores and now has 142 rushing yards on the day! LVvsNYJ on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/aGaC9Th33s
Allen became the first running back in team history to have three straight 100-yard games on the ground since Martin. He has become the bell cow that many Jets fans have hoped to see from Breece Hall.
After the game, head coach Aaron Glenn talked about Allen's performance and focused on not rushing Hall back from his quad injury.
At the end of the day, though, the Jets cannot move Allen away from the starting lineup . He has been too dominant to stop.
New York's offense had its most dominant day of yard production we have seen in quite some time. The unit recorded 424 yards of offense, including 166 on the ground. The problem, though, lay in the fact that the red zone offense was an abysmal 2-for-6 .
Four field goals kicked and only two touchdowns. Unacceptable in the modern age of offense-first football.
There were many issues why the unit struggled. Sometimes, like in the game's opening drive, the team couldn't hook up with their best players. Garrett Wilson couldn't corral a back-shoulder fade. Later in the game, though, penalties and missed throws all played a role.
No team that puts up 33 points should lose a game in the NFL. New York's offense will have a lot they can be happy about today.
But the Jets also could have put the game out of reach multiple times and failed to do so. When their defense eventually broke, they didn't have an answer.
New York's starting quarterback was not perfect on Sunday. He missed several throws early on and threw a pick to end the game instead of giving his offense one more chance to score on a Hail Mary.
But those mistakes aside, Smith was excellent for the Jets all game. He finished 20-for-32 passing for two touchdowns and the late pick. He was sacked twice in the second half but repeatedly pushed the ball downfield against Las Vegas' maligned secondary.
One thing Smith will want back is the team's red zone success; we'll get to that later. But putting up 33 points should be enough to win a game in the NFL. Smith's performance, again, was good enough to win.
Last season, the Jets rostered one of the best special teams units of all time. Before 2026 began, there was major concern about how Jason Sanders would look, but genuine confidence was found in their unit as a whole.
Things have changed drastically since the start of the season, though.
New York gave up a 95-yard touchdown return in the first half that gave Las Vegas the lead, 14-13. For a game that was decided by one score, the special teams breakdown was a game-turning play. It won't matter that Sanders made all four of his field goals today either.
It will be remembered for the breakdown in coverage that gave Las Vegas seven free points.
The second half wasn't as dominant as the first, but the Jets' offensive line continues to play exceptionally well over the last several weeks. New York gave Smith plenty of time to throw and averaged over six yards per carry as a collective unit.
This was also the first game back for starting left guard Dylan Parham. His return brought the group back to a dominant fold. They moved Las Vegas at the line of scrimmage all game and found ways to open holes for whoever was touching the football.
This is a kind of loss that will sting because this group continues to show how good they can be with more snaps together. The future is very bright for New York's offensive line.
New York's defensive line made two nice plays on Sunday.
Throughout the game, though, and particularly in the second half, the Jets' defensive line got tossed around. There's a reason for that, of course. New York was without four starters: David Bailey, David Onyemata, T'Vondre Sweat and Joseph Ossai.
The numbers tell one story. New York gave up just 2.9 yards on the ground in a clear focus of stopping the run, but the team failed to record much pressure at all on Kirk Cousins. That led to 24 points scored in the second half and three straight scoring drives.
The Jets' defensive line is their biggest weakness right now, and it seems like it's only going to get worse.
Fans were waiting to see a breakout performance from AD Mitchell all year. They finally got it on Sunday.
Mitchell caught seven passes for 142 yards and a touchdown. He could have had even more with one drop down the field costing him at least another 42 yards of offense. Mitchell was Smith's most trusted target, as has been the case all season.
An incredible 48-yard catch by Adonai Mitchell! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/a7pOlkJn27
His development is also huge for a Jets offense that seemed to get Garrett Wilson going (team-high 12 targets), and didn't target rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. The Jets have an embarrassment of riches at receiver now, and it makes their offense very fun to watch.
Even after a loss such as this.
Glenn was clear he wanted to call plays this season because play calling was his "superpower."
It was anything but in Week 8.
Glenn's defense gave up three straight touchdown drives to open up the second half, erasing what had been a 10-point halftime lead into a five-point deficit late in the fourth quarter. Now, a lot of things are working against Glenn. His ideal defensive line is hurt, and the team didn't get the kind of quality play they normally saw from their secondary.
But there were many strategic decisions Glenn made that hurt the team as well. Chief among them was keeping cornerbacks on Las Vegas's tight ends for a majority of the game. Both of Brock Bowers's touchdowns came against cornerbacks. Michael Mayer also made four catches for 46 yards as well.
New York needed a better defensive coaching plan. Especially from someone who was brazen enough to call it his superpower at the start of the offseason.

title: Eagles Week 8 Report Card: Grading Every Position After Sunday's Loss vs. Commanders
full_text:
The Eagles' nightmare season continued with a 27-10 loss to the Commanders in Week 8. They have now lost six straight games for the first time since 2012. This also marks the first time the team has started 2-6 since 1999, which was Andy Reid's first year as head coach.
The struggles that have plagued the Eagles for over a month returned on Sunday Night Football. Philly jumped out to a 10-0 lead before stalled offensive possessions and shaky defense allowed Washington to take over. The Eagles were outgained 339-268 and shut out in the second half.
Before looking ahead to a Week 9 clash against the Giants, let's hand out some grades for each unit following another demoralizing defeat.
Quarterback Tanner McKee's outing on Sunday was simply not good enough. The fourth-year pro's third-quarter fumble erased Philly's momentum, and his fourth-quarter interception all but ended the game. He failed to throw a touchdown pass for the first time in his five career starts.
McKee has been heralded as an accurate pocket passer, yet 10 of his 23 completions came behind the line of scrimmage in Week 8. Whether or not play calls are holding him back, he is hesitating to throw into tight windows. Jeff Kerr emphasized just how poorly the offense has performed with McKee.
The #Eagles offense -- in 3 games Tanner McKee has started PPG -- 15.0 (29th in #NFL ) Yards Per Play -- 4.2 (32nd) Passer Rating -- 76.6 (26th) Yards Per Attempt -- 5.6 (31st) Yards Per Game -- 270.3 (30th) Pass % -- 64.9% (2nd) Points Per Possession - 1.4 (28th) 3-and-out % --…
Eagles running backs logged 64 rushing yards on 24 carries on Sunday night. The duo of Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell averaged a lackluster 2.7 yards per carry and did not have a single rush for more than nine yards. Philly is averaging the sixth-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL (88.1).
Now, it's worth pointing out that Barkley is not fully healthy and Mitchell is Philly's RB6. Asking either one to carry an offense missing its stars would be foolish. Barkley isn't helping this squad by playing 32% of the offensive snaps, though. Sitting out in Week 9 would give him nearly three weeks to rest.
DeVonta Smith's hamstring injury and Dontayvion Wicks's ankle injury hindered the Eagles in Week 8. Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, and Hollywood Brown played the majority of the wide receiver snaps with those two sidelined. Cooper and Brown barely made a ripple, totaling 36 yards on four catches.
Lemon flashed his upside for the second straight week, recording 57 yards on six catches (nine targets). The rookie is using crisp routes to get open on passing plays and draw defenders away on running plays. Lemon's increased impact should be a top storyline in the second half of the season.
Philadelphia tight ends put in a solid effort in Week 8. Dallas Goedert finished with 30 yards on four receptions. He has been on the field for at least 69% of the snaps and posted a catch of 15 yards or more in five of his six games played. Those stats should maintain his value in the trade market .
Rookie TE Eli Stowers impressed during his 13 snaps, hauling in three passes for 53 yards. The second-round pick was explosive after the catch and should see more action as the season progresses. This grade is brought down a bit by more blocking struggles from Johnny Mundt and Grant Calcaterra.
Jordan Mailata praising "Jeff Stoutland University" in his Sunday Night Football intro made fans reminisce about what used to be Philly's biggest strength. The offensive line has become the team's biggest weakness in 2026. Running lanes are not opening up, and McKee is not being protected.
Washington generated pressure on 46.5% of dropbacks versus Philly and posted 10 pressures on 12 blitzes (h/t NFL+). It resulted in a whopping five sacks for the Commanders. Free rushers got in McKee's face within seconds as Landon Dickerson and Markel Bell whiffed on crucial blocks.
Washington mixed up looks all night long but what in the world has happened to this Eagles front five. This is unacceptable at the highest level of the sport. pic.twitter.com/RWza2lCVix
There were a few highlight plays from the defensive line on Sunday, with two sacks and four tackles for loss. However, the Eagles gave up 135 rushing yards on 26 carries. They have surrendered over 100 rushing yards in each of their first eight games. That hasn't happened in Philadelphia since 1968.
A failure to stop the run not only tires out Philly's defense, but it also puts pressure on the secondary to be perfect. Every mistake becomes costly. Committing more than $300 million to Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, and Jonathan Greenard has hurt the team more than it has helped so far this season.
Jeremiah Trotter Jr. stepped up in place of the injured Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) on Sunday, leading the Eagles with 10 tackles. It'll be interesting to see if Trotter takes over the ILB2 role moving forward. The former Clemson standout has shown glimpses of improved instincts and technique.
Meanwhile, veteran Zack Baun stayed consistent with seven tackles and a fumble recovery. It's important to hold Baun and Trotter. accountable in run defense. The easiest way to combat open running lanes is by making tackles at the second level. That isn't happening as often as it needs to.
If there's any room to move away from defensive doom and gloom, it's in Philly's secondary. Safety Andrew Makuba forced a first-quarter fumble deep in Washington territory that spurred the Eagles' only touchdown drive of the contest. The Texas product finished with nine tackles and a pass breakup.
FLIPPING THE FIELD pic.twitter.com/hfqKnSxz0C
The Eagles held quarterback Jayden Daniels to a 55.2% completion rate by jumping passing lanes and forcing low throws. Depth issues came into question, though, as cornerback Kenny Moore II was picked on for an eight-yard touchdown pass, a 30-yard completion, and a 20-yard completion.
Braden Mann is the only reason this grade is not an F. The veteran punter landed three of his five punts inside the 20-yard line. Otherwise, the special teams unit was a disaster. Kicker Jake Elliott missed a 41-yard field goal that would've turned a six-point deficit into three during the third quarter.
It has to be mentioned that Philly's kick/punt coverage continues to put the defense in tough spots, too. Washington's Luke McCaffrey's sole kickoff return of the night went to the 50-yard line, and his sole punt return went to the 50-yard line as well.
The Eagles lost the field position battle yet again.

title: 3 Eagles Who Won't Survive the Trade Deadline After Losing Streak Reaches 6 Games
full_text:
Changes are coming for the Eagles after they dropped their sixth consecutive game to the hapless Commanders on Sunday Night Football. With the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline right around the corner, some of those changes will be imminent.
Here's a look at three Eagles players who will likely be continuing their careers elsewhere outside of Philadelphia after the deadline.
It almost feels like the writing is on the wall when it comes to Landon Dickerson's future in Philadelphia. The Eagles are in the midst of a complete overhaul of the offensive line following the retirement of Lane Johnson and the trade of Cam Jurgens, and Dickerson could be the next player on the line to be traded .
Dickerson has spent the bulk of the current campaign on the sideline due to injury, and when he has played, he hasn't been great. He did decently against Dallas in Week 7, but he played poorly against the Commanders in Week 8. He hasn't played enough snaps to qualify for a Pro Football Focus ranking, but his grades at his position are all well below league average.
For the Eagles, it feels like the right time to just pull the bandage off, move on from Dickerson and spend the rest of the season evaluating young players along the offensive line to see if any have a future with the franchise as a potential building block.
During an appearance on 97.5 The Fanatic following Philadelphia's Week 8 loss to Washington, Ryan Fowler of NBC Sports Philadelphia named Dickerson as a player to keep an eye on leading up to the deadline.
"Keep an eye on Landon Dickerson," Fowler said. ". . . I don't think he's healthy still. I think he's a guy who's battling, similar to what Saquon Barkley is doing. He's trying, but at the end of the day you're not going to make excuses for anybody. It's just not good enough right now, and I think Landon Dickerson, along with those guys you just mentioned, is a name to know as we approach the deadline."
At this point, it feels like it would be a surprise if Dickerson were still on Philadelphia's roster after the deadline.
This is almost painful to write, given how integral Dallas Goedert has been to Philadelphia's offensive attack for the past decade, basically.
But it certainly feels like his time with the Eagles could be coming to an end in the near future, and that's not an indictment of Goedert. He'sstill a productive player at his position, and that could make him intriguing for contending teams in a potential trade. He's currently playing on a one-year deal, so it might make sense for the Eagles to try to get something in return for him, as opposed to potentially losing him for nothing in free agency.
Tanner McKee connects with Dallas Goedert for the first down! PHIvsWAS on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/dpHuatfr1Z
Rookie tight end Eli Stowers is finally healthy, and he had his most productive and promising performance of the season against the Commanders in Week 8, as he caught three passes for 53 yards and also showed promise as a blocker. This could provide the Eagles with additional reason to move on from Goedert. In a lost season, it would be beneficial for Stowers to get increased on-field opportunity so that the team can see exactly what they have in him.
There's really no reason for the Eagles to hang on to Riq Woolen at this point.
They're not legitimate contenders in the NFC, so it doesn't really matter who they trot out at cornerback opposite Quinyon Mitchell. And it's not like Woolen has been great anyway. He's been average in coverage , according to PFF, and he leads the team in penalties this season with five. He's been called for a holding penalty in each of Philadelphia's last two losses.
Woolen, who is playing on a one-year contract, doesn't appear to have a real future in Philly, so it would make sense for the Birds to flip him for some draft capital before the deadline.
