title: McMullen: Eagles Might Have a Nick Sirianni Problem After Loss to Commanders
full_text:
LANDOVER, M.D. — With his team in freefall, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni has spent the past several weeks stressing the idea of attention to detail.
The message landed with team leaders like Saquon Barkley and Jordan Mailata, and the trains have run on time from Monday through Saturday if you believe the self-scouting, only to derail on game days.
On Sunday night at Northwest Stadium, the Eagles opened an early 10-0 lead, while trying to halt the only five-game losing streak in the Sirianni era, only to watch the limited Commanders lap Philadelphia with 27 unanswered points the rest of the night, sending Sirianni into “uncharted territory.”
A frustrated Sirianni played what's becoming an all-too-familiar hit, holding himself accountable while shielding his assistant coaches and players.
“Until we coach better, until we have better detail as coaches, until our players play with better detail, then we’re gonna see the same results,” he said. “And that falls on me."
“I feel like with all the detail that’s not happening right now, I got to try a different approach. And so that’s 100% on me. With how many of those issues are happening right now, I’ll do everything I can to try different things to make sure that we’re getting that point across.”
Detail is literally part of Sirianni's coaching mantra of “tough, detailed, together.” The coach is obsessed with “mastering the things that require no talent,” yet in the biggest moment of the game, the Eagles draped themselves in unforced errors.
Trailing 16-10, Philadelphia was moving the football and preparing to go for a fourth-and-four conversion at the Washington 13-yard line with 9:04 left in the game.
The Eagles were late on the play clock as Tanner McKee began imploring for the snap. Feeling the urgency, rookie right tackle Markel Bell moved early, forcing the Eagles into a 36-yard field goal attempt that Jake Elliott drilled.
That successful kick would have made it a 16-13 game with plenty of time to keep pressing, but the attempt was wiped out because Jordan Mailata was not on the line of scrimmage. The illegal formation penalty backed the kick up five yards, and Elliott banged it off the left upright.
DOINK 🚨 PHIvsWAS on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qtlhWoqpGe
The Eagles got nothing out of the drive.
Subsequently, the Commanders responded with an eight-play, 45-yard march, ending with a 42-yard Drew Stevens field goal—his fourth of the night—making it a two-possession game, 19-10 with only 3:43 remaining.
A six-game skid for the Eagles was assured, not to mention being outclassed by two division foes with a combined record of 5-9-1 on national television in less than a week.
Straining for answers, Sirianni mused about messaging.
Mailata was angered by his own miscue, throwing a tablet to the ground after rewatching his mistake on the sideline.
"It sucked the wind out of our momentum," Mailata admitted.
You can blame Bell, McKee, Mailata, Elliott, or all of the above, and that's kind of the point. In the ultimate team game, too many are contributing to the Eagles' poor results.
Sirianni, though, wears the product on his sleeve.
“Every product on that field—Offense, defense, special teams, fundamentals, situational football, player making a mistake, coach making a mistake—that’s my freaking job,” Sirianni said. “And so I’m pissed at myself, and I know I’ll fight like hell to do everything I can to get it fixed.”
When discussing a conservative offensive approach at the end of the first half instead of a bolder approach, Sirianni sounded defeated.
“That’s just kind of a product of what we have been," he admitted.
And that product has now bled over to the other phases.
"I feel like we’re doing a great job in practice and throughout the week,” Barkley said. “And for some reason, it’s not transferring over to the football field when it matters most.”
The Eagles are 2-6 because those details have gone missing when the bright lights are on. Whether that will be corrected or just another routine postmortem against the Giants in Week 9 will be decided on the field, not in lip service.

title: 5 Losers & 2 Winners From Eagles' Loss to Commanders in Week 8
full_text:
Changes are coming to the Eagles. How can they not be after not showing any signs of turning things around in their sixth straight loss —a 27-10 defeat by the Commanders in a game that saw the home team score 27 unanswered points after Philly took an early 10-0 lead?
Those changes could come as soon as their bye week, which kicks in after they host the NFC East-leading Giants in Week 9
Until then, here are some winners and losers. Mostly losers:
Nick Sirianni, HC: The head coach’s seat is very hot, to say the least . If his team loses out, which is a distinct possibility, Sirianni is probably gone. He can still save his job by turning things around, but this team certainly doesn’t give any confidence that a win is anywhere in the near future.
Sean Mannion, OC: The offensive coordinator could only find a way to score 10 points against a team that was giving up 28 per game. Sirianni was asked afterward if he was thinking of making a change with the OC.
“I'm not thinking about any of that stuff right now,” he said. “I got a bunch of guys in that locker room that are hurting—every player, every coach. Right now, I'm getting through this moment with those guys. I'm not thinking about any of that stuff right now. … I got a lot of faith in everybody in that locker room.”
The Eagles’ had just two plays that gained more than 20 yards and the longest one – a 34-yard pass to rookie Eli Stowers came with just two seconds left and the Commanders’ defense not pressing.
Michael Clay, STC: The special teams coordinator has had his hands full filling his units with healthy bodies, but he won’t use that as an excuse, nor should he. The kickoff team gave up a 47-yard return to start the game that would have led to a quick 3-0 lead, except rookie Drew Stevens missed a 55-yard field goal. That wasn’t the case at the end of the first half when a 27-yard punt return put Washington at midfield with 50 seconds to play. That led to a 39-yard field goal with 23 seconds to go, and a 13-10 Commanders lead at halftime.
Riq Woolen, CB: The cornerback keeps giving up too many completions and too many yards. And he had his second straight game with a holding penalty. It might not be
Markel Bell, OT: It was bound to happen sooner or later that the rookie third-round pick would melt in the spotlight. He’s done well for the most part since stepping in at right tackle after the abrupt retirement of Lane Johnson. Sunday night was his worst game yet.
Bell surrendered two sacks and was called for a costly motion penalty to turn fourth-and -three at Washington’s 14 midway through the fourth quarter into fourth-and-eight. The Eagles had been lined up to go for it on fourth down, but the penalty changed Sirianni’s mind, and he opted to send out the field goal team.
Jake Elliott made the 36-yard kick, but Jordan Mailata was called for an illegal formation penalty. The re-kick, from 41 yards, hit the upright.
Saquon Barkley, RB: What a leader he is . Despite battling hamstring and back injuries, Barkley played 22 snaps, got 13 carries and posted 30 yards. He scored the Eagles’ only touchdown and a direct snap, three-yard run in the first quarter. It was his second straight game with a rushing TD. He also made a nifty 24-yard catch off a wheel route to the 2-yard line that set up his TD.
Barkley never sat down the entire game, trying to keep his back from tightening up.
Jeremiah Trotter Jr., LB: Did the Eagles miss injured Jihaad Campbell, who didn’t play? It didn’t look like it. Trotter led the team with 10 tackles while playing 54 snaps (90%).

title: 9 Eagles Observations After Commanders Hand Philly a 6th Straight Loss in Week 8 SNF
full_text:
Move over Andy Reid’s 2012 team. You have company. The Eagles lost their sixth straight game on Sunday night , and that is the first time the organization has lost this many in a row since Reid’s last year, when the losing streak reached eight.
The Eagles went 4-12 and Reid was fired after that dismal season.
The Eagles are now 2-6 after Sunday night’s 27-10 loss to the host Commanders. They went winless in October and started November with another loss. They haven’t tasted victory since Sept. 20, when Jalen Hurts drove the offense for a game-winning touchdown against the Titans in Nashville.
It’s fair to wonder if head coach Nick Sirianni will suffer the same fate as Reid did in 2012. Yes, the Eagles are banged up, but nothing seems to be getting better. Maybe in small snippets they do, but not enough to find a way to win a game.
There are too many mistakes, such as left tackle Jordan Mailata not lining up on the line of scrimmage on a 36-yard field goal made by Jake Elliott. Pushed back five yards, Elliott hit the top of the left upright with about nine minutes to play, keeping the score at 16-10.
The effort seemed better, but again, that didn’t help win a game. The run defense was still not nearly good enough, allowing the Commanders to run for 135 yards, and the offense still cannot find a consistent rhythm.
The Eagles jumped to a 10-0 lead, doing all their scoring in the first quarter, but they couldn’t score a single point over the final three quarters. The Commanders methodically scored 27 unanswered points, getting four field goals from rookie kicker Drew Stevens.
Making his third start, quarterback Tanner McKee was again too inconsistent. He had a costly fumble late in the third quarter just as the Eagles had pulled into a long-range field-goal attempt at minimum. Rookie Markel Bell allowed the strip-sack. McKee, who also threw an interception, was sacked five times.
The Commanders cashed the turnover into a field goal and a 16-10 lead with 1:33 to go in the third quarter.
1. Three-and-outs: The Eagles had fewer of them. After going three-and-out on their first possession, the offense had just one more.
2. Points: The Eagles doubled their first-quarter point output for the season, putting up 10 points. They had been outscored 40-10 coming in and now it’s 43-20 after taking a 10-3 lead into the second quarter.
3. Fumble recovery: The Eagles finally got one. It happened in the first quarter when Drew Mukuba belted tight end Chig Okonkwo after catching the ball. Zack Baun fell on it to set up the offense at the 26, and they turned it into a 3-yard touchdown run by Saquon Barkley.
FUMBLE 🗣️ Zack Baun recovers for the Eagles! PHIvsWAS on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CbAEhq9j0k
The Eagles were the only team in the NFL not to recover a fumble. That streak is over. Still, it was just the fourth turnover the defense has forced all season.
4. First road start: It was McKee's first start on the road,  and he entered the game for the first time not trailing. He led the offense to 10 points before the Commanders got off the deck and started carving up the Eagles’ defense. McKee cooled off, too, and the Eagles didn’t do anything after that.
5. Eli Stowers: Hey, the rookie tight end made his first catch, which went for seven yards on second-and-six in the third quarter. He finished with three catches for 53 yards.
6. Tyler Steen: The offensive line struggled mightily even though Washington was without the injured Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw, but Steen’s play was particularly glaring. And not in a good way.
7. Unblocked pressure: The Eagles allowed a pivotal sack in the first half when it appeared the offensive line slid right, allowing a free rusher to sack McKee. It was Landon Dickerson who stepped right, allowing the rusher to get home. That could either be a bad scheme by line coach Chris Kuper or a miscommunication about what the Commanders were showing. Maybe both.
8. Pass rush: It’s still too inconsistent, though it showed some life. Jalen Carter notched a big sack to force a punt midway through the third quarter. It was his fourth of the season to take over the team lead, one ahead of Nolan Smith.
Jalen Carter and Jonathan Greenard teaming up for the SACK! PHIvsWAS on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QB0jrdQCHq
Smith forged back into a tie with a fourth-quarter sack. The outside linebacker also clobbered Jayden Daniels at the end of the first half on a dropback. Still, the Eagles have 10 sacks this season.
Oh, there was a Jonathan Greenard sighting but only because he jumped offsides to negate an interception from Mukuba in the end zone.
9. Third downs: The worst team in the league at converting third downs at 30.9%, the Commanders converted five of 13 (38.5%).

title: Eagles-Commanders Stock Market: Collapse Continues in DC
full_text:
LANDOVER, MD - After a 2-0 start this season, the Eagles are now 2-6 after losing a sixth straight game in the shadow of the nation's capital against the Washington Commanders.
In a microcosm of the season, Philadelphia got off to a 10-0 start on Sunday night and never scored again en route to an ugly 27-10 setback.
A very limited team due to circumstance that has included everything from significant injury attrition to questionable coaching and the retirement Land Johnson, the once powerful Eagles were outgained for the eights consecutive time this season with the Commanders piling up 339 yards to 268 for Philadelphia, the latter number buoyed by the garbage time of the last drive of the night.
The Eagles are now 0-2 in a key three-game stretch against NFL East foes in what's considered a bad division, a run that will finish against the first place New York Giants (4-2-1), who will be coming off their bye week next Sunday.
With tonight's loss, the Eagles are now at the bottom of the division. Dallas (3-5) is in second despite losing to Arizona in troubling fashion Sunday, and the Commanders leapfrogged the Eagles with their second win (2-4-1).
SAQUON BARKLEY'S HEART - There wasn't much to like in this game but Barkley played despite hamstring and back injuries because he felt he could and that his team needed him. In a Super Bowl-or-bust society, the fact that Barkley didn't embrace the tanking mentality is the kind of culture setter that is meaningful in the NFL.
It wasn't great statistically -- 13 carries for 30 yards and a reception for 24 yards -- but the lone touchdown was all Barkley with the 24-yard catch on a wheel route and a three-yard scoring run after a turnover.
LONG-SUFFERING WASHINGTON FANS - For years, the Commanders fans have had to take it as their Eagles peers would invade Northwest Stadium and take over. While Washington is not exactly lighting the league on fire, its faithful enjoyed serenading the Eagles fans out of the stadium in the waning moments. It felt like a cleansing for a long-suffering fanbase although the suffering looks far from done inside the Beltway.
ATTENTION TO DETAIL - Nick Sirianni has claimed that the detail hasn't always been there during the Eagles' skid. That showed up in the fourth quarter when a promising drive that could have stolen the game was quickly derailed by a series of mistakes that "take no talent."
Trailing 16-10, Philadelphia was preparing to go for a fourth-and-four conversion at the Washington 13-yard line with 9:04 left in the game. The Eagles were late in the play clock, as Tanner McKee began imploring for the snap. Feeling the urgency rookie right tackle Markel Bell moved early, forcing the Eagles into a 36-yard field goal attempt that Jake Elliott made drilled.
That worst-case would have made it 16-13 with plenty of time to keep pressing but the kick was wiped out because Jordan Mailata was not on the line of scrimmage. The illegal formation backed the kick up five yards and Elliott banged it off the left upright.
The Eagles got nothing out of the drive. In turn, the Commanders responed with an eight play, 45-yard marching, ending with a 42-yard Drew Stevens field goal -- his fourth of the night -- that made it a two-possession game, 19-10, with only 3:43 remaining.
PLAY ACTION - Everyone should have someone who believes in them like Sean Mannion believes in play action. No matter how ugly George Halas' creation looks in Philadelphia, Mannion is going to throw out 13 personnel with poor blocking tight ends and watch his quarterbacks turn their backs to heat-seeking missiles on the blitz.
THE PASS RUSH - It’s almost amazing that the Eagles have not been able to generate any real consistent pressure with an interior that includes Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis and Moro Ojomo, and an edge group of Jonathan Greenard, Nolan Smith and Jalyx Hunt .
The front has been the key to their success for a very long time and the organization invested heaving in Carter, Davis and Greenard this offseason. The Eagles had just three pressures in the first halft and nine total with two somewhat emoty sacks. The lone bright spot was one strong rush by Smith that seemed to rattle Jayden Daniels for a stretch.
In a Vic Fangio defense, the four-man rush has to be significantly better to generate the expected success.

title: Emerging Eagles' Defensive Concern Needs an Answer to End Losing Streak in Week 8
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Head coach Nick Sirianni found nothing wrong with the Eagles' effort in Monday night’s loss to the Cowboys . Nothing. Nada. Zip.
He stated it unequivocally, too, during the week: “I did not see an effort issue on Monday night. … There were other things. But effort in no way, shape [or] form was an issue here.”
Two days later, Jordan Davis contradicted his coach.
“It was poor from everybody, and that's just simple and plain about it,” the Eagles defensive tackle said. “It was poor.”
Linebacker Zack Baun pulled no punches when asked if the effort level was up to par. “I do not, no,” he said succinctly.
Sirianni is a player's coach, so hopefully he is just saying publicly that there was no issue with effort, and behind the scenes he is harping on it. It was apparent to those who watched the Cowboys dust the Eagles by 17 points that effort was an issue.
The turnaround has to start on Sunday night when the Eagles visit the Commanders in another primetime game.
Is that even possible at this point?
While key offensive players have been injured at historic levels, the Eagles defense has remained mostly healthy—save for Jonathan Greenard, who can’t seem to shake an ankle injury that has dogged him the last few weeks.
There is talent on the defense. It simply didn’t go away overnight.
“When I first got in the league, they let me know the NFL's not easy to win in,” Jalen Carter said. “It's gonna be hard, day in and day out. And this year's proven that it's hard to win in the NFL and that we just gotta change things now, change things around.”
It should start with effort, and the way to turn that around is through leadership. Who in the Eagles’ locker room has stood up to demand that effort on defense?
There’s no issue on the offensive side, where Jordan Mailata stood in the middle of the Lincoln Financial Field locker room shortly after it opened after a loss to the Panthers, telling reporters he would take their questions right then and there. He was still dressed in full pads and was beginning to unlatch his shoulder pads as he took questions.
Saquon Barkley spoke for more than 15 minutes after the loss to Dallas. Landon Dickerson was on the verge of tears after losing to the Cowboys, saying he played horribly.
Meanwhile, the only players on defense who spoke after losing to Dallas were Cooper DeJean and Jihaad Campbell.
Davis said he thinks players aren’t having fun, that they are approaching things as a “job,” and not enjoying themselves.
“You ask anybody in this locker room, you're not having fun playing the game; it kinda seems like a... That's when it really seems like a job,” Davis said. “When you're having fun, it doesn't seem like a job. It feels like something that you get to do; you have to enjoy this game. It's gonna be wins and losses and everything, and that's in life. You have to find those little moments to enjoy, and right now we're trying to find those little moments, those little wins.”
Nakobe Dean was the player who held everyone accountable. The linebacker made sure his teammates were having fun, whether he was on the sidelines, in practice, in the locker room, or in a game.
This isn’t to relitigate the decision to let Dean walk in free agency to Las Vegas on a three-year, $36 million contract. It's simply to ask: who is the leader of the defense? That is to be determined. Maybe it will be Davis.
“We know what we're capable of,” he said. “We've reached the highest of highs. We've seen the lowest of lows now. We have to do something to fix it, and that's one of the things that we've been a part of in practice this week: fixing the effort. We have to give effort.”

title: Eagles Need Saquon Barkley More Than Ever as Banged-Up RB Room Remains a Week 8 Concern
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — With the Eagles sitting at 2-5 and hamstring and back injuries that cost him two days of practice this week, an average superstar would likely shut things down and live to play another day.
That’s not Saquon Barkley, the pro’s pro who doesn’t even have a game status for Sunday night against the Commanders despite dealing with the kind of nagging issues that will have him on a pitch count.
"One day I'm not gonna be playing football,” Barkley said at his locker on Friday. “Whenever that is, I don't want to look back and be like, 'I could have gave it a chance, and I didn't.'
“That's kind of what I live by. So try my best to just keep recovering, being smart. But I like playing football. So if I have the opportunity to play, I'll try my best to play."
Barkley was able to practice in a limited fashion on Friday after missing the first two days of the week and was removed from the injury report.
The 29-year-old said that he feels “decent” after a week of rehab.
Barkley suffered the hamstring injury early in the Oct. 4 loss to the Rams and missed the next two games. He returned Monday night against the Cowboys on a limited pitch count. Despite that, he performed with remarkable efficiency, rushing seven times for 62 yards and a touchdown, and adding two catches for nine yards before exiting with back tightness.⁠
Barkley said he tweaked the hamstring on his first carry against the Cowboys , a 29-yard run, and later dealt with back issues while trying to compensate.
“Definitely dealing with some stuff, but just working through it,” Barkley said.
He described the recovery as non-linear and said he has stayed focused by “attacking the day, every single day” and remaining “obsessed with my process and my rehab.”⁠
In Landover, Barkley expects to manage the injuries during the game by following the coaches’ plan and keeping his body activated.
“When I was out there, I felt like I was able to provide a spark and make some plays,” he said of his limited action against Dallas.
Through five games this season, Barkley has 244 rushing yards on 43 carries for a 5.7-yard average and one touchdown, plus six receptions for 17 yards. He has been effective when on the field but has had only two or three fourth-quarter carries all season, an area he called a source of frustration.⁠
Barkley understands his value reaches beyond production and into the intangible world of presence.
“That’s one of my best qualities,” he said. “I feel like I have a really good gift of being close with the offense and the defense.”⁠
The Eagles’ running back room has been thinned badly by injuries.
Primary Barkley backups Tank Bigsby (abdomen), Will Shipley (foot) and Dameon Pierce (undisclosed) are on injured reserve. The team also recently reached an injury settlement with Carson Steele and waived him.
Barkley said he has “never seen anything like this” in terms of the attrition at the position and praised the efforts of remaining options expected to help him against the Commanders, veteran practice squad addition Elijah Mitchell and recent 53-man roster promotion Jaydon Blue.
Barkley’s presence could provide a boost for an offense that has ranked near the bottom of the league in several categories as the Eagles try to halt a five-game skid, the worst stretch in the Nick Sirianni era.
“Saquon's an unbelievable player,” quarterback Tanner McKee said. “Obviously, we feel confident with everybody that we have back there. But Saquon's very special, and he makes special plays. He makes a lot of guys miss. He's a vocal leader. He also leads by example and he's an unbelievable player. And so he makes a lot of plays that most people in the NFL can't make.”

title: Eagles-Commanders SNF: Who Wins and Why in Week 8 NFC East Matchup
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – For some reason, Eagles-Commanders round two wasn’t flexed to an afternoon game. The NFL decided to keep this matchup between a par of struggling teams, with three wind combined between them in primetime.
The 2-5 Eagles will try to snap a five-game losing streak, while the Commanders will try to win for just the second time this season. They already lost in the season-opener to the Eagles.
Here’s a closer look at the matchups:
The Eagles coach is 10-3 against Washington, including a stomping in the NFC title game two years ago. Sirianni, however, is mired in a five-game losing streak , the team’s longest in his tenure and the longest since the 2016 season when Carson Went was a rookie quarterback.
A loss on Sunday night would be their first six-game losing streak since 2012, when Andy Reid’s team lost eight in a row to finish 4-12. Reid was fired at the end of that season and replaced by Chip Kelly.
The backfield will be manned by a pair of players who signed only recently—Elijah Mitchell, who was with the Eagles in training camp until he was waived injured on Aug. 11 and brought back on Oct. 20, and Jaydon Blue.
Saquon Barkley might play, but last week his hamstring acted up, which led to a back injury, and he played 10 snaps. He was limited in the only practice he participated in this week.
“Obviously, we've been beat up in that room with injuries,” said head coach Nick Sirianni, “but I feel good about the depth and the guys that we have. I was really excited about Elijah throughout camp, and then he got dinged up in camp. Just really glad to have him back."
“Always have liked Jaydon and the things that he can do, going back to watching him coming out of Texas. Feel good about that room. Obviously, a little beat up in that room and looking forward to when we can get guys back, but I'm excited about these guys that are going to go in there and rip it.”
Britain Covey is third in the league in average yards per punt return at 12.6, but the fifth-year pro is battling a knee injury that will sideline him. Makai Lemon stepped up in a pinch last week when Covey went out in the first quarter, but special teams coordinator Michael Clay said Cooper DeJean and Jaydon Blue could also be options.
The defense has been a sieve, giving up 399 yards or more in four straight games. In last Monday’s loss to the Cowboys , they allowed 416 yards, including 204 on the ground, with Javonte Williams shredding them with a career-high 155 yards on 25 carries.
The run defense has slipped to No. 27 in the league. Washington uses a balanced running game, with Jacorey Croskey-Merrick leading the way, with Rachaad White and recently signed Austin Ekeler in the mix. Quarterback Jayden Daniels is also a threat to take off and run. That foursome has the Commanders’ rushing attack ranked No. 9 in the league.
Philly hasn’t been good at getting them, but the Commanders have. The Eagles are the only team in the league that hasn’t recovered a fumble, and they have just three interceptions.
They have turned the ball over six times, five with interceptions. That puts them at minus-3 in the takeaway/giveaway category, which is tied for 21st in the league. Washington has the second-best turnover differential at plus-6.

title: 3 Realistic Dallas Goedert Trade Destinations as Eagles Deadline Buzz Picks Up
full_text:
The Eagles have had an impressive run of homegrown tight end talent. Brent Celek's toughness stood out through 11 seasons in Philadelphia. Zach Ertz's receiving skills helped the franchise hoist its first Lombardi Trophy. Dallas Goedert's versatility has been a pillar of the offense for over eight years.
The party can't last forever, though. Ertz was traded to the Cardinals prior to the 2021 NFL trade deadline, which allowed Goedert to take on a bigger role moving forward. Could a similar move be made in 2026? Goedert is playing on a one-year deal, and rookie Eli Stowers is waiting in the wings .
The Eagles sport a disappointing 2-5 record and are expected to be at least mild sellers at the upcoming trade deadline on Nov. 10. SI's Albert Breer noted Goedert "could be had," alongside other Philadelphia contract-year pros. Here's a look at three realistic trade destinations for Goedert.
Broncos' tight ends have tallied 186 yards and three touchdowns on 19 receptions through seven games. That yardage total trails just the woeful Tennessee Titans for the lowest in the NFL. The trio of Evan Engram, Adam Trautman, and Nate Adkins is not making an impact in the passing attack.
Goedert has posted 228 yards and two touchdowns on 22 catches in five games in 2026. The 31-year-old has logged more than 500 receiving yards in six of his last seven seasons. Elite body control and an ability to rack up yards after the catch serve as the foundation of Goedert's receiving skills.
Goedert with his second TD of the night 👏 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/ytYh8raEz6
Quarterback Bo Nix could use another reliable target. He is averaging 181.6 passing yards per game, which is nowhere near his 231.2 average last season. Denver is projected to have multiple fourth-round picks in 2027. Offering one to the Eagles could sway Philly general manager Howie Roseman.
The Bears have emerged as a tight end trade destination, but it's not because of Colston Loveland's underwhelming performances. Cole Kmet suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 7. Kmet had played 62% of the offensive snaps, as head coach Ben Johnson regularly utilizes two-tight-end sets.
Kmet's injury leaves Sam Roush as the only healthy tight end behind Loveland. The rookie out of Stanford has been playing over a dozen offensive snaps a game as a run-blocker. It'd be a lot to ask of him to take over Kmet's receiving role. That's where someone like Goedert would come in handy.
Goedert has the pace to run vertical routes and the quickness to run in-breaking routes. That's in addition to his physicality as a run-blocker. Johnson can use that flexibility to his advantage. Chicago has already been aggressive , acquiring defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Goedert could be next.
Cincinnati tight end Mike Gesicki has been a red-zone monster in 2026, scoring a touchdown in five of six games. However, the depth behind him took a hit after Week 7. Erick All Jr. tore his ACL and joined Tanner Hudson on injured reserve. The Bengals suddenly find themselves in the TE market.
Goedert set an Eagles franchise record with 11 touchdowns in 2025. Those scores were highlighted by shovel passes, quick-flip tosses, and crisp short routes. Lining him up alongside Geiscki near the end zone would leave defenses with no easy matchups against an offense stacked with elite talent.
Acquiring Goedert would be a larger move than his expected price of a late-round pick suggests. The Super Bowl champ boasts PFF's second-highest overall grade among 30 qualified tight ends (80.0) in 2026. It'd be an all-in move that shows Cincinnati trusts quarterback Joe Burrow to lead a deep run.

title: T.J. Watt Makes History in Steelers Win Over Browns
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns renewed the hatred in their AFC North rivalry during their Week 8 contest. The Steelers routed their divisional foes, winning by a final score of 27-6.
The win evened the season series between the Steelers and Browns and kept Pittsburgh atop the AFC North standings.
The game was highlighted by the defense's ability to get to the Browns' quarterback. The Steelers sacked Deshaun Watson eight times, led by superstar T.J. Watt with 2.0 sacks on the day. With that performance, Watt now has 19.5 sacks against Cleveland in his career. According to Assistant Director of Communications for the Steelers, Michael Bertsch, that is the most by any individual against the Browns.
"T.J. Watt now has 19.5 career sacks vs. Cleveland," he wrote. "Which is the most by any player against the Browns in League history. He is the ninth player in NFL history to hold sack record vs. multiple teams."
The other team that Watt holds the sacks record against is the Baltimore Ravens. Watt has produced 17.0 sacks against the Ravens in his career.
T.J. Watt now has 19.5 career sacks vs. Cleveland, which is the most by any player against the Browns in League history. He is the ninth player in NFL history to hold sack record vs. multiple teams (Cleveland, 19.5; Baltimore, 17.0). #HereWeGo #CLEvsPIT #BertschyBits
Watt adds yet another accolade to his long list of accomplishments in the NFL. Elected to eight consecutive Pro Bowls and named First-Team All-Pro four times, Watt is now officially the most productive pass rusher the Browns and Ravens have gone up against.
But more importantly for Watt and the Steelers is the fact that this team is cruising as the bye week arrives. Following their fourth consecutive victory, the Steelers are at the top of the AFC North and one of the best teams in the NFL.
With the bye week coming at the perfect time, there is a feeling in Pittsburgh that this team might be a contender.
With the latest two sacks, Watt is trying to renew his campaign for Defensive Player of the Year, a far cry from the hopes of Cleveland's head coach Todd Monken and his offense. They had to suffer through a monstrous performance by Watt, and it should put him back among the best defensive players in the league.
Through the first seven games, he has 17 total tackles, 11 of which have been recorded individually. He also has nine quarterback hits, seven tackles for loss, 5.5 sacks, a forced fumble, a fumble recovery, an interception and two pass batted down at the line of scrimmage.
It's been an All-Pro-caliber season for Watt, and his production is a key reason why the Steelers have a fearsome defense and a 6-2 record.
And the Browns keep learning firsthand just how elite Watt still is.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: 'Stay Tuned': Insider Hints at Steelers' Garrett Wilson Trade Interest
full_text:
An NFL insider seems to think that there's something potentially brewing between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the New York Jets when it comes to star wide receiver Garrett Wilson.
On X, Jason La Canfora responded with, "Stay tuned," after Dave Dameshek wrote, "Color me...INTRIGUED," after the former initially connected Wilson to the Steelers.
Stay tuned https://t.co/xX8jPjFwhB
Pittsburgh is 6-2 as it begins its Week 9 bye after blowing out the Cleveland Browns 27-6 this past weekend. The franchise has been connected to a number of different wide receivers ahead of the November 10 trade deadline, though all signs have pointed to Wilson not being available, which makes La Canfora's report eye-opening.
In an interview on November 2, La Canfora explained why Wilson could intrigue the Steelers as a possible target over the next week.
“I'd keep an eye on the Pittsburgh Steelers. I'm told they're being pretty ambitious behind the scenes and would love to add another playmaker," La Canfora said . "DK Metcalf has some limitations in terms of the route tree he runs, but if you were to add someone like Garrett Wilson to that offense, it starts to get really interesting. With the tight ends they have, a running back like Jaylen Warren who can catch a lot of passes, and Metcalf stretching the field on go routes, adding a receiver like Wilson would give them another dynamic dimension. That could be a very intriguing offense.”
ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on October 31 that a "well-placed source" stated there was "no way" Wilson was moved by New York ahead of the deadline, and he also told reporters last week "no" when asked if he will or has asked for a trade (per SNY's Connor Hughes ).
La Canfora has pushed back on that notion , though, and perhaps the door is still at least a little open for the Steelers and Jets to come together and make a mega deal.
With 527 yards and three touchdowns on 43 receptions over eight games this season, Wilson has proved himself to be a top-10, if not better, receiver in the league.
New York has struggled to the tune of a 2-6 record, but it does own three first-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft and has plenty of assets that could help it turn things around rather quickly.
Because Wilson is a building block piece who signed a four-year extension worth $130 million in July 2025, there aren't a ton of reasons for the Jets to consider moving him unless he makes it abundantly clear that he wants out, which doesn't appear likely to occur at this stage.
Wilson and Aaron Rodgers, who were teammates with New York in 2023 and 2024, don't seem to have much of a relationship either.
In fact, The Athletic's Zach Rosenblatt reported last year that the pair, "weren’t exactly the best of friends," by the time their final season together concluded, and that they, "took subtle shots at each other in press conferences."
Considering it would take at least one first-round pick and then some to acquire Wilson, the Steelers might have some real reservations about parting with a treasure trove of assets in order to bring Wilson in if he and Rodgers won't be on the same page.
For that reason, it's hard to imagine Pittsburgh being a realistic landing spot for Wilson for the time being, even if he were to ever hit the trade block before the deadline arrives.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Can't Trade Patrick Queen Now
full_text:
It wasn’t long ago that trading Patrick Queen felt like the right decision for the Pittsburgh Steelers.
In a contract year, and with all of his struggles for the vast majority of his time with the Steelers, sending Queen elsewhere at the trade deadline this season was firmly in the cards just a matter of weeks ago.
Now, however, Queen has put together his best string of performances in Pittsburgh amidst the team’s four-game win streak and has become incredibly valuable to a defense that is establishing itself as one of the league’s premier units.
Queen was viewed as a bounce-back candidate throughout the offseason once Mike McCarthy was hired as the Steelers’ head coach and brought Patrick Graham with him as his defensive coordinator.
Mike Tomlin’s system never quite seemed to suit Queen, and it showed with how he struggled over his first two years with the black and gold.
Queen’s 32 missed tackles led the NFL in 2025 ( per Pro Football Focus ), and he became a liability in coverage as well.
The 27-year-old wasn’t necessarily a superstar over the first four seasons of his career with the Baltimore Ravens, but he regressed to a noticeable degree upon landing with Pittsburgh.
It has taken Queen some time to acclimate to Graham’s system, and while the first four weeks of the season or so were rough, the former Pro Bowler has finally found his footing with the Steelers.
After showing real signs of turning things around in Week 6’s comeback win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Queen followed that outing up with a fantastic performance in Week 7’s win over the New Orleans Saints, a game in which he sacked Tyler Shough on his last dropback of the day while also playing a huge role in limiting the Saints to 18 yards on 17 carries.
It was more of the same from Queen in Week 8’s blowout victory over the Cleveland Browns , as he recorded a new single-game career high of 1.5 sacks with a pass deflection and a team-high 12 tackles while helping hold Pittsburgh’s AFC North rivals to 34 yards on 15 rushing attempts.
There was palpable trade buzz surrounding Queen in the offseason, with the Dallas Cowboys reportedly pursuing him in March, though those talks didn’t end up leading anywhere.
As previously noted too, Queen was floated as a potential trade candidate just a handful of weeks ago after his underwhelming start to the year.
At the time, the Steelers’ signing of Elandon Roberts to their practice squad on October 12 felt like it could've led to Queen losing snaps to the former.
Roberts has yet to be elevated by Pittsburgh, though, and Queen has since had a much-needed resurgence that's essentially removed any doubt about his viability as a starter.
Not only that, but Queen has played at as high of a level as he has in years over the past two or three weeks as the Steelers have gained sole possession of first place in the AFC North at 6-2 as they begin their Week 9 bye.
As a result, Queen should no longer be available for trade and is a key piece of Pittsburgh's defense at inside linebacker next to Payton Wilson, who has also made some strides this season.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers’ Michael Pittman Jr. Reveals Hopeful Return Date
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers haven't had wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. on the field since their Week 4 contest against the Cleveland Browns.
Without Pittman, the Steelers' wide receiver issues have been exacerbated. Even with the emergence of rookie Germie Bernard, there is a noticeable lack of depth at the position.
The hope is that after the bye week, the team will have a new addition via trade and possibly see some players return from injury. One possibility is the return of Pittman Jr. following the week off. Speaking to the media the day after the team's Week 8 victory, the veteran receiver shared an encouraging update and some more information on his current injury.
He wasn't able to say for sure, but he shared that he would love to return following the bye week.
"It would be great to be back after the bye week, which is what I would like," he told reporters. "But I can't go out there if I'm not effective. So, only time will tell."
As a veteran in the NFL, Pittman Jr. has experienced a lot. But this specific injury has been brand new for the former Indianapolis Colts pass-catcher. Steelers On SI publisher Noah Strackbein spoke with Pittman, who shared some more detail on this injury.
According to Strackbein, Pittman has been dealing with planter fasciitis, at least at first. Since that initial injury, it's "morphed" into something else, something that "surgery wouldn't fix."
"Yeah I mean, I've never dealt with this (injury)," he said. "So, I don't know what it's supposed to feel like or what it's going to feel like. And we got a great team here that's been helping me through it."
For Pittman, it's about doing everything he can to get back on the field and contribute with his teammates.
"Trying to get back out there as fast as possibl and prove to this team that I came to better it and not just sit on the sidelines."
While he hasn't been able to be on the field for the past four games, Pittman has had the chance to get an up-close view of the offense at work. After their latest, he offered some insights when asked for his observations.
The biggest thing Pittman noted was the impact of the team's running backs and tight ends.
"I think the offense is doing good and I think Jaylen Warren and our tight ends are really holding us up," he stated.
When Pittman Jr. returns, hopefully after the bye week, the hope is the passing game can reach that same level.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: DK Metcalf Revives Steelers' Need for WR Trade
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers absolutely dominated their Week 8 matchup, defeating the Cleveland Browns in a familiar fashion.
The 27-6 win was the Steelers' fourth consecutive victory and their sixth of the season. It was a huge win, one that could solidify this team as a contender in the AFC.
The win also solidified this team's wide receiver troubles as the biggest issue once again. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers was once again rendered less effective due to not having enough talent on the outside, and despite the team's stubbornness and defiance, they have to address this glaring hole in the lineup.
Rodgers has had four interceptions this season that came directly off the hands of his receivers. In Week 8, Metcalf dropped an easy pass. Not only that, the ball deflected off his hands and into Cleveland's possession.
When it was rookie Germie Bernard who bobbled a screen pass that resulted in an interception, it was just a moment's lapse for a first-year player. When a pass ricocheted off Roman Wilson's hands for a turnover, it was frustrating, but not a terrible mistake.
When your top pass-catcher does it, it's bad. When the player who is supposed to be your top offensive weapon and top pass-catcher makes such a costly mistake, it's a call for change.
Mistakes happen. Like many other players in Pittsburgh, it's about how you rebound from your failures. Metcalf has the chance to make up for his costly error when the team returns to the gridiron in Week 9 against the Cincinnati Bengals.
But one trend is becoming too big to describe as a one-off or a single mistake. The Steelers have been trying endlessly to make Metcalf the focal point of their red zone offense and it's been an utter disaster. Once again in Week 7, the Steelers dominated on the ground, only to turn into a passing offense when they had the goal line left to gain.
Even head coach Mike McCarthy expressed some regret about how he called a red zone trip in the first half.
"That series there, I would could have those three plays back," he said during his postgame press conference.
And that's a sentiment he probably feels about all of their red zone trips so far in 2026. It's clear that McCarthy wants to let Rodgers run the show, but Metcalf hasn't executed on the plan. The only red zone threat on this team is tight end Darnell Washington, no matter how many goal-line fades they hurl Metcalf's way unsuccessfully.
The Steelers have been involved in trade talks and the subject of many rumors as the NFL trade deadline rapidly nears. The latest rumor has tied them to Indianapolis Colts pass-catcher Josh Downs , while another report claims they're a team to watch for Jacksonville Jaguars' Brian Thomas Jr.
And after another underwhelming outing from their top wideout, it's clear that a player like Downs is essential. Downs is an explosive pass-catcher who can create separation. Those are two traits the Steelers desperately need infused into their wide receiver group immediately.
If not Downs or Thomas, any player who fits that description would upgrade this offense . As Rodgers tries to make his final season one for the history books, they need to give him as many weapons as possible.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: 7 Winners, 2 Losers From Steelers Blowout Win Over Browns
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers left no doubt about how the better team was in Week 8.
After a week filled with trash talk, specifically from Jared Verse , the Steelers dominated the Cleveland Browns in every facet of the game and got revenge for their Week 4 loss to their AFC North rival with a 27-6 blowout victory at Acrisure Stadium this time around.
With that, here are Pittsburgh's winners and losers from the contest as it heads into a Week 9 bye.
Washington continues to make his mark as a real threat in the passing game for the Steelers.
Washington went for a total of 92 yards, which led Pittsburgh on the day and is also a new career high.
The 25-year-old is now on pace for 540 yards, which would eclipse his 364-yard campaign in 2025 by a healthy margin.
It's tough to quantify how brilliant Warren has been for Pittsburgh this season.
Though he didn't log any receiving yards on his one catch for the first time this year, Warren more than made up for it by recording 143 yards and a touchdown across 17 carries.
He has now put up 100 or more yards on the ground in four games this season.
Facing a rookie left tackle in Spencer Fano, Highsmith's veteran expertise was on full display in this one.
Alongside drawing a couple of holding penalties on the first-rounder, Highsmith also posted five tackles, 0.5 sacks and three quarterback hits to go with three pressures (per SumerSports ) as part of a monster day for the Steelers' pass rush.
Pittsburgh didn't need anything from Metcalf in order to rout the Browns, but it felt like he regressed back to the level of play he showcased in the first few weeks of the season.
Metcalf hauled in just one pass from Aaron Rodgers, which went for four yards and marks his lowest single-game total since Week 17 of the 2022 campaign.
Furthermore, Metcalf was wide-open deep down the field and dropped a throw from Rodgers as he adjusted, which ended up in the hands of Denzel Ward for an interception.
Heyward hadn't done much as a pass rusher coming into this week, though that changed vs. Cleveland.
The 37-year-old posted 1.5 sacks, which more than doubled his prior total of 1 on the season, and he also had five total pressures (per SumerSports ).
Heyward was disruptive against the run per usual as well, logging two tackles for loss and being one of the main reasons why the Browns finished with 34 yards on 15 carries.
Queen, after a rough start to the season, has begun to really turn things around in a contract year.
Following what was arguably his best game as a Steeler in the team's Week 7 win over the New Orleans Saints, Queen led the black and gold with 12 total tackles while also recording 1.5 sacks, which is the most he's ever had in a single game.
Despite being under constant pressure, Deshaun Watson was still able to complete 27 of his 39 passing attempts for 324 yards.
Brisker's had an up-and-down season for Pittsburgh after signing a one-year deal with his hometown franchise in March, and he wasn't exactly playing at the top of his game against the Browns.
According to Pro Football Focus , Brisker allowed 55 yards in coverage (his most in a single contest this season) while also missing a tackle.
Watt had started cooling off just a bit after coming out of the gates hot this season, though he was back to his usual ways vs. Cleveland.
The 32-year-old paced the Steelers with two sacks, which pushes his total on the year to 7.5, and he also had a pass deflection.
In their defeat at the hands of the Browns earlier this season, Pittsburgh's offensive line allowed Rodgers to be sacked five times.
The Steelers were far more stout in pass protection in their rematch vs. Cleveland, however, as Rodgers was sacked just once.
With Spencer Anderson back in the mix as part of the team's jumbo package too, the offensive line created plenty of holes for Warren to run through as they got the better of the Browns' defense.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Take Control of AFC North
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers are playing their best football in 2026 and it's putting them on track towards postseason success.
The Steelers dominated the Cleveland Browns 27-6 at Acrisure Stadium in Week 8 and have taken the lead of the AFC North at 6-2.
Cleveland previously held the tiebreaker, after beating Pittsburgh 27-24 in Week 4 at Huntington Bank Field, but this win gives Pittsburgh a game advantage, 6-2 compared to 5-3.
It's a big victory for the Steelers, who have won four in a row since that defeat and head into their bye week as one of the best teams in the NFL.
The Steelers are in the second-most competitive division in football in the AFC North, with only the NFC North having a better combined record.
Perhaps the next team that is most competitive in this division, aside from the Browns, is the Cincinnati Bengals, who are playing some good football too.
Cincinnati has won three straight games, 31-24 over the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium in Week 5, 35-13 over the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium in Week 7 and then a 43-36 victory in overtime against the Tennessee Titans at Paycor Stadium in Week 8.
The Bengals fended off a late comeback from the Dolphins, scored 35 unanswered points in the second half against the Ravens and erased two fourth-quarter deficits against the Titans to win it in overtime.
Pittsburgh and Cincinnati face one more time in 2026, including the first game out of the bye week at Paycor Stadium in Week 10, with Pittsburgh winning the first matchup , 30-27 at Acrisure Stadium in Week 3.
The Browns have lost two of their last four games, and all five of their wins have come within one possession.
Baltimore is in the worst position of all these teams, as they have lost their last three games, including 36-10 to the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium in Week 8.
The Ravens may also have lost quarterback Lamar Jackson for the rest of the season with a thumb injury, which he sustained on the first play from scrimmage in the loss to the Bills.
Philadelphia Phillies (Road)
Jacksonville Jaguars (Road)
The remaining nine games for the Steelers in 2026 feature some tough opponents and a few poorer ones as well.
Pittsburgh facing the Bengals out of the bye week on the road will be tough, as well as their matchups with the Denver Broncos at home in Week 12 and the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars on the road in Week 14.
The Steelers also face the Ravens twice in Week 15 and Week 18, the Philadelphia Eagles without Jalen Hurts in Week 11, the struggling Houston Texans at home in Week 13, the inconsistent Carolina Panthers in Week 16 and the terrible Tennessee Titans in Week 17.
It's a combined record of 31-35, so not the easiest of stretches for the Steelers, but certainly not the hardest.
Six wins from these nine games shouldn't be too surprising from the Steelers, barring serious injuries,  and it should spark them to back-to-back AFC North Titles out of the bye week.

title: Steelers Are Contenders, Not Trash Talkers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are 6-2 heading into the bye week. They just beat a Cleveland Browns team that brought plenty of attention with them because of their AFC North-leading record and trash talk heading into the game. And leaving Acrisure Stadium for the last time until Black Friday, this team is as "real" and they could be.
"He should have kept his mouth shut," Jaquan Brisker said after the game about Jared Verse's trash talk. "All that talk, and then to come out with zero tackles, that’s bad."
That was as bad as it got for the Steelers in response to Verse after the game. For those who missed it, Verse said the Browns would "own" Pittsburgh in this game. He didn't, and neither did the Browns, but the Steelers didn't really care.
For the most part, this team made it simple. "Some talk, some walk," Jaylen Warren summed it up.
That was the vibe in the locker room afterward. This team wasn't focused on revenge or shutting Verse up. They felt more disrespected that Cleveland elected to receive the ball to start the game.
Pittsburgh is focused on the big picture more than the little one. They wanted to win four in a row heading into the bye week and accomplished it. They were determined to get their defense clicking to become the dominant group they could be, and to figure out their offensive line before the midway point of the season.
"We're 6-2 going into the bye, first in the division. We're right where we want to be," Aaron Rodgers said after the game.
It's been a long time since the Steelers felt like a real contender. There have been moments and glimpses of great play, but overall, it's felt largely like Mike Tomlin was carrying them as far as he could drag them, ultimately to be eliminated from the postseason early.
This year, making the postseason isn't the goal. This team doesn't want to "get to the dance"; they want to win it. They want to be serious contenders.
"We didn't discuss it one second, what they were saying about us," T.J. Watt said about the Browns. "We just want to go about business. We have a lot of mature guys who have done it here and done it other places and had a lot of success and a lot of young guys who want to continue to grow and be great. We're just focused about what's in the building right now."
Inside the building, the Steelers have a defense that ranks top 10 in points allowed and takeaways. The team has scored over 20 points in all but one game, and is currently at the top of the division with a chance to increase that lead after the bye against the Cincinnati Bengals.
It's about Super Bowls, not trash talk in Pittsburgh.
A mindset that makes them feel bigger than their opponent. And like a real contender at the break.
"We were motivated because we wanted to get this damn win before we got to the bye," Heyward put it,"so...

title: Steelers' Jaylen Warren Roasts Jared Verse: 'Some Walk, Some Talk'
full_text:
Cleveland Browns EDGE rusher Jared Verse's comments coming into a Week 8 matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers drew plenty of attention, as he previously stated the black and gold were "dirty" and said he wasn't "worried about nobody they got on their team."
During his postgame press conference following a blowout 27-6 win for the Steelers, however, Warren stated that the team was aware of Verse's remarks and didn't pay them much mind when asked if it was a motivator. He did offer more of an opinion on the matter at the end of his answer, though.
"Yea, but we didn't really pay attention to it," Warren said. "Some walk, some talk."
In a contentious game between a pair of AFC North rivals sitting atop the division at 5-2, the Steelers got the better of the Browns at nearly every turn.
Warren, who's emerged as one of the best running backs in the NFL this season, really helped set the tone for Pittsburgh and had yet another explosive outing en route to the black and gold's fourth-straight victory.
The 28-year-old, who celebrated his birthday on the day of the game, was unusually quiet as a receiving option out of the backfield, finishing with zero yards in that regard for the first time in 2026.
That didn't stop Warren from torching the Browns on the ground, however, as he logged 143 yards and a touchdown over 17 carries while the Steelers as a whole rushed for 200 yards on the contest.
Verse, meanwhile, recorded a single tackle and no sacks.
It sure felt like the Steelers were playing with an extra edge vs. Cleveland, which didn't come as a surprise given the gravity of the contest.
Pittsburgh flew around the field on defense and combined for a total of eight sacks with 13 quarterback hits. Additionally, it limited the Browns to 34 yards on 15 carries and recovered two fumbles.
In the locker room after the game, Jaquan Brisker stated that he believed Cleveland's decision to receive the ball after winning the opening coin toss was disrespectful and essentially motivated the Steelers from there on out while also noting that Verse's comments were far from the only reason the team was "hungry" to earn a victory.
"I think them taking the ball was kinda disrespectful," Brisker said. "Especially being at home. So it kinda turned us up, and obviously you seen how the first series went and things like that... I wouldn't say a particular player really amped us up, because I wouldn't say he motivated us. I think we were just motivated overall. Basically we didn't like how the first game went, how the first meeting went. Of course we heard the noise, so that added a little bit to it, but I wouldn't say it was just Verse. We were just hungry to win, and obviously hungry to get a win before the bye week."

title: Steelers vs. Browns Takeaways: Jared Verse Owes an Apology
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are now 23-0 in their last 23 home games against the Cleveland Browns.
The Steelers heard the noise from Cleveland all week, and ignored it. Cam Heyward said early in the week that Jared Verse's comments about Pittsburgh playing "dirty" in their latest game would "be addressed."
It was, in the fashion of a 27-6 win at Acrisure Stadium.
Let's dive into some takeaways.
The Steelers spent all week ignoring the Jared Verse smack talk in front of cameras , but they certainly heard the noise and took it as a challenge.
Before the game, I predicted the Steelers would have five sacks (minimum) in this game. They had four at halftime. They finished with eight, and nearly took Deshaun Watson out of the game on the opening series when he was checked for a concussion.
As for Verse himself, Mason McCormick made sure to let him know they heard him talking...
Jared Verse been talking all week. Mason McCormick did his talking on this play A 15-yard penalty he will gladly take pic.twitter.com/qZT7H0HPmH
It was a welcome to the AFC North game for Cleveland's newest starting edge rusher. Everyone needs one of those games, but when you talk beforehand, it usually makes it a little bit tougher of a day for you during the game.
In this instance, it not only made life rough Verse, but made it especially difficult for his quarterback.
It's a live-and-learn situation for Verse, but one he won't get to make right until either the playoffs or next season. One thing is for certain, though, the Browns did not "own" Pittsburgh after this one.
Another week, another reminder that Jaylen Warren is a top five running back in the National Football League. This week, he finished with 17 rushes for 143 rushing yards and a touchdown.
He had 10 rushes for 102 yards at halftime.
Warren turned 28 on game day and had a little extra burst in his play to celebrate.
For another week in a row, Warren was the best player on the Steelers' roster. He continues to be the driving force for the offense and one of the most explosive players in the entire league.
Yes, he's underrated. Yes, he's arguably top five in the NFL. Yes, chances are he'll be featured in this column again next week.
5️⃣1️⃣ YARDS 🚂 @Nunless2 pic.twitter.com/3d2lNSEUfv
If it's Mike McCarthy, someone needs to tell the head coach to do some self-scouting on his red zone play-calling. If it's Aaron Rodgers, someone needs to tell him to stop trying to pad the stats. But whoever is making these red zone decisions needs to be corrected, because it's bad. Real bad.
The pointless DK Metcalf fades are where it usually begins, but it never seems to get much better from there. Jaylen Warren, who we just got done talking about being a top-five runner, is barely used inside the 20-yard line. Rico Dowdle, the two-time1,000-yard rusher behind him, doesn't get much attention, either.
Correction: the last 6 plays inside the 10. https://t.co/OcbB4Jvvga
Pittsburgh's inability to realize they need to run the ball more near the goal line will continue to hold them back. Luckily, the offense as a whole is good enough to move the ball and produce points. A few more touchdowns compared to field goals would go a long way in tight games, though.
This defense has plenty of excitement surrounding it, but every week, we're reminded that their secondary is the weak link of the entire roster. Even when the pass rush is as elite as it was this week, the corners and safeties struggled, and it made the end result look much different than it should have been.
If the Steelers could cover for just another second on average, there would be several more sacks for this team.
With the trade deadline approaching, general manager Omar Khan should at least be checking on names. Nahshon Wright, Alontae Taylor, Amik Robertson and others have been mentioned as possible trade candidates. Maybe they don't fix the problem, but if they don't cost much to acquire, it's worth taking a shot on someone.
Pittsburgh's entire defense could use the boost.
The Steelers announced an extra offensive lineman during their pregame introductions. To kick things off, they welcomed Spencer Anderson as part of the starting offense. The 200 rushing yards backed that display of appreciation well.
The jumbo package returning to the offense is a great sight to see. There were even a few moments when Riley Nowakowski was in the game at fullback.
This team may have Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy enjoying one last ride together, but this is a running football team. One with six starting offensive linemen.
Over the weekend, Alex Highsmith was mentioned as a potential name to watch at the trade deadline. The Steelers aren't interested in trading him away, but the right offer could spark a conversation.
To this point, they've told every team that has called no. That probably won't change after this game.
Highsmith was a force from start to finish, recording five tackles and a half-sack against the Browns.
His trade value went up in this one. So did the Steelers' desire to keep him for the upcoming playoff run.
The Steelers are paying DK Metcalf over $30 million for the 2026 season and then for the next three seasons afterward. He hasn't shown he's been worth that amount of money one time since he joined the roster, and that deal continues to look worse with each poor performance he has.
Against the Browns, Metcalf had one reception for four yards before Aaron Rodgers found him deep in the middle of the field, wide open. It didn't result in a completion. Instead, Metcalf bobbled the ball, which landed in the hands of Denzel Ward, instead.
So, yeah, the Steelers need to add a WR pic.twitter.com/5nwkki18rY
You could see the defeat in Metcalf as he walked off the field and was surrounded by his teammates. But the boos from the crowd were loud, and as much as this fanbase wants to embrace Metcalf as their star wide receiver, it's very difficult for them to.
The Steelers probably need a wideout at the deadline. They won't get a WR1 to replace Metcalf, but anyone helps. As long as they have options, they can probably make up for the lack of production from their $132 million wide receiver.

title: 3 Observations in Seahawks Loss vs. Bears
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are back in the loss column after their 34-17 loss against the Chicago Bears inside Lumen Field.
The Seahawks gave up a touchdown in the first quarter, forcing them to play from behind all night long. Ultimately, Chicago's offense was too much for them to withstand, as D'Andre Swift ran for three touchdowns in the second half, which doomed Seattle. Here's a look at three observations from the game.
The Seahawks did not get the most out of their running backs in today's game against the Bears. Both rookie Jadarian Price and veteran Zach Charbonnet made their return to the lineup after dealing with injuries over the last several weeks.
For Charbonnet, it was his debut for 2026 after recovering from a torn ACL suffered during the playoffs last season. He ran the ball six times for 23 yards and also caught three passes for six yards. Meanwhile, Price had 10 carries for 29 yards, along with two catches for eight yards.
Given that the Seahawks were trailing for most of the game, the offense shifted from the running game to the passing game, so it's not quite a full reflection of what the ground game can do. That said, now that they've dipped their toes in the water, there should be an expected improvement next week.
For most of the night, third down might as well have been fourth down for the Seahawks. The team converted just one of their 11 third-down plays throughout the game, which makes it very difficult to win in the NFL.
Most of the time, the Seahawks would stuff the running back on first and second down, forcing the team into third and long. The play calling became a bit predictable, and that is ultimately what led to their struggles throughout the evening.
The Seahawks need someone outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba to be able to bail them out of these situations. The team's touchdown drive in the first half was consummated thanks to a long run by JSN, which gave the Seahawks some life going into the locker rooms at halftime. Unfortunately, they didn't have much success outside of that drive during the game.
The more the season progresses, the less Sam Darnold looks like himself from last season. The turnovers continued again tonight, as he threw his ninth interception in the last six games. He simply didn't execute the opportunities that were in front of him.
Sam Darnold consistently has some of the worst awareness in the NFL watch him even after the interception 💀💀 pic.twitter.com/dQyJd3RGUh
Darnold's touch feels a bit off in this game, but it is a pattern of what we have seen throughout the year. If it continues in the playoffs, where they might play a team like the Bears, it's hard to imagine Seattle coming out of that game on top.

title: 3 Winners & 4 Losers From Seahawks Disheartening Week 8 Loss to Bears
full_text:
A win over the Kansas City Chiefs gave the Seattle Seahawks plenty of hope as they entered Week 8 against the Chicago Bears. They also felt the addition of Quenton Nelson could help their offense get on track , but the Bears made a big move of their own.
Chicago added Jeffery Simmons , who helped set the tone for the road team on Monday Night Football. The Bears spent the entire day pushing the pocket as they sacked Sam Darnold three times, with Simmons recording one in his debut.
The Seahawks showed fight and even cut the lead to three points in the fourth quarter, but the Bears proved to be too much as they went on to win 34-17. Let's look back at the action and see which Seahawks stood out as both winners and losers in the frustrating loss.
On the opening punt, Nehemiah Pritchett made a great play that should have forced the Bears to start from their own three-yard line. A gaffe from Rodney Thomas II gave Chicago a touchback, but it was still a great play by Pritchett. He also had another big play near the end of the first half, breaking up a pass intended for Rome Odunze. Had Odunze hauled in the bullet from Caleb Williams, it would have allowed Chicago to kick a field goal before halftime. Instead, the Bears' final drive of the half ended in no points.
Just how good is Jaxon Smith-Njigba? The Seahawks went into the half with 114 yards of offense. 92 of those yards were courtesy of JSN.
The offense struggled in the second half when Chicago put the clamps on Smith-Njigba, but that was a reminder of how much this team needs to find someone who can take some pressure off his shoulders. It was again a one-man show, with Smith-Njigba recording 118 yards and a touchdown on six receptions. The next highest yardage total was Tory Horton, who had 26 yards on three catches.
Chicago had all the momentum following a blocked field goal early in the fourth quarter, but the Dark Side defense got them back in the game. Seattle forced a third-and-long and DeMarcus Lawrence delivered. The veteran defensive end tackled Colston Loveland and forced a fumble in the process. For good measure, Lawrence also recovered the fumble, setting the Seahawks' offense up with a short field.
The Seahawks had an unfortunate three-and-out to start the game, but appeared to have won the field position game early. Michael Dickson perfectly drilled a punt inside the five-yard line and Nehemiah Pritchett made a great play to keep the ball out of the end zone.
As the ball rolled to a stop around the three-yard line, safety Rodney Thomas II touched the ball as he was sliding to the ground. In doing so, he pushed the ball into the end zone for a touchback, giving Chicago the ball at the 20.
Chicago went on to score a touchdown, even converting a fourth-down conversion near midfield on the play. Perhaps that fourth down isn't even attempted with better field position, making this a hige mistake from Thomas.
Mike Morris got his first career sack, which was a win. However, he also made a huge mistake that helped Chicago after Seattle cut the lead to three. Morris was flagged for unnecessary roughness, which allowed the Bears to start at the Seattle 44-yard line, setting them up for a touchdown drive that put the game away.
Chicago just extended their lead to 27-17, and the Seahawks needed to get some momentum back. That didn't happen thanks to Irv Charles, who was guilty of an unnecessary roughness penalty on the ensuing kickoff, their second major penalty on special teams. That forced Seattle to start with the ball at their own 11, which was their worst starting position of the game.
Charles does deserve some praise for blocking a punt earlier in the game, although that might have gone down as the longest blocked punt in NFL history. Despite Charles getting a piece of the ball, the punt traveled 45 yards downfield.
The Chicago defense harassed Sam Darnold all night, and he just never seemed comfortable. Things took an especially bad turn when the Bears found a way to cover JSN in the second half. Everything was difficult for Darnold, who finished 17-of-34 with 188 yards, two touchdown passes, and one interception.

title: Leonard Williams Injury Update: Seahawks Star Defender Leaves Field in Third Quarter
full_text:
The Chicago Bears just put a great drive up on the board for a touchdown to go up 20-9 in the third quarter. During that drive, Leonard Williams left the field with an unknown injury, going to the injury tent without his helmet. He at least was able to walk under his own power, with no help or noticeable limp, but as of this moment we don’t know what his status is.
The injury comes at a suboptimal time for the Seahawks, who are playing tonight without Uchenna Nwosu and Brandon Pili. With no Nwosu, Williams is depended on more to slide out to the edge and provide snaps on the outside. The Seahawks defense has yet to take the field since the touchdown, so there’s not yet any particular way to figure out how bad it is.
Williams's value to this team goes without saying. He may be the best player on this defense, an interior defensive lineman with elite pass rushing skills while maintaining dominance against the run. 'Big Cat', as he is known, had 11 sacks for the 2024 season, getting some votes for Defensive Player of the Year. Last year, he had seven, starring on the best defensive line in the sport.
The Seahawks are going to lean heavily on Byron Murphy II and Jarran Reed for the rest of this game, which might be a reasonable ask given the game only has one quarter left in it. Rylie Mills has played quite a bit tonight and will probably rotate in some, but his shortcomings as a run defender have shown up in a big way. Mike Morris could be considered as well.
Brandon Pili is out tonight, remember so he will not be an option. The early word on Williams is that he has a stinger injury, and is questionable to return. We'll find out soon if he's available as the Seahawks have a lot of work to do to salvage this game. They also have a short week ahead, as they are currently playing on Monday Night Football, so that's another thing to consider here.
On the first defensive drive since the injury has not yet seen Leonard Williams on the field, so the injury is clearly at least significant given he would certainly be out there at a big moment like this. For the moment, the Seahawks just recovered a fumble, so he'll have some time to work on a potential return.

title: Jadarian Price, Zach Charbonnet In, But 7 Seahawks Ruled Inactive vs. Bears
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are taking on the Chicago Bears , but not everyone will suit up for the team.
The Seahawks had some roster changes throughout the week, and rookie Jadarian Price is back in the lineup, along with veteran Zach Charbonnet. However, with the two of them playing, it means others are sitting. Here's a look at the inactive list for the Seahawks against the Bears.
With both Price and Charbonnet back for the Seahawks, the team is ruling Velus Jones Jr. inactive as he deals with a hamstring injury.
The most notable and active player for the Seahawks is Charles Cross, who has been the starter for the entire season. As Cross moves to the sidelines, the team will elevate Josh Jones from the second string to the starting lineup.
"Josh will play left tackle," Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said via the team's website.
"He's done a good job when he's gone in there and played. There was a stretch of time last year where we were missing Charles and Josh came in and played good football for us and that's what we expect. That's why we want him here, that's why he's such an important part of our team. Shoutout to the guys for being able to bring him back because he's a good player."
The most notable inactive for the Bears is running back Kyle Monangai, who is dealing with turf toe and a thumb injury. Monangai last played in Week 4 against the New York Jets, but his absence means D'Andre Swift will lead the backfield. Swift is one of the best running backs in the league, rushing for 476 yards and seven touchdowns across seven games for the Bears.
Kickoff for Monday Night Football between the Bears and Seahawks is scheduled for 5:15 pm PT inside Lumen Field. Fans can watch the game on ESPN or stream it on the ESPN app.
