title: Is Jadarian Price Playing Today? Seahawks RB Gets Injury Update
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are celebrating as they are expected to get running back Jadarian Price back in the lineup for their Week 8 matchup against the Chicago Bears.
Price has been on injured reserve for the past four games due to a chest injury, but the team is officially putting him back on the 53-man roster, making him eligible for Seattle's matchup against Chicago.
Price gives the Seahawks a lot to work with in the backfield. The team selected him with the No. 32 overall pick in the NFL Draft this past spring out of Notre Dame. They were hoping he would be the replacement they needed for Kenneth Walker III, who signed with the Kansas City Chiefs' agency to become the league's highest-paid running back.
Price struggled with fumbling during his first three games, coughing up the football once in Week 2 against the Arizona Cardinals and again in Week 3 against the Washington Commanders. His output took a hit in Week 3 after his fumble, but it also came with his injury that has held him out for four weeks.
The intriguing development about Price returning is that Zach Charbonnet is also making his 2026 debut in the game. Charbonnet has been recovering from his injury that he suffered during the Divisional Round of the playoffs back in January and has been working diligently to get back on the field. Now, his return coincides with Price, who should form a 1-2 punch out of the backfield.
It remains a mystery for the Seahawks on how their carries will be distributed. On top of Price and Charbonnet getting carries, Emanuel Wilson has earned a role moving forward after his 100-yard performance against the Chiefs in Week 7.
The three of them should form a committee that will likely ride the hot hand depending on the week. There is no exact player that should be RB1 because all of them can take on that role in any given game.
Wilson is probably the likeliest candidate to be the lead back in this particular game against the Bears to get Price and Charbonnet back into a rhythm, but moving forward, this is a big boost of depth for the Seahawks.

title: Seahawks' Tory Horton Given Huge Role vs Bears in Week 8
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks (4-3) can capitalize on their dominant Week 7 win over the Kansas City Chiefs and the Quenton Nelson trade on Monday Night Football . The Chicago Bears (5-2) are one of the better teams the Seahawks have faced so far this season, but Seattle is much better than its record indicates. The Seahawks’ Dark Side Defense will have a big battle against one of the most explosive offenses in the league.
​On the other side of the matchup, the Seahawks face a solid Bears defense that got better with the trade for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans. Seattle faces a lot of injury concerns, including wide receiver/return specialist Rashid Shaheed . This leaves a big opportunity for second-year wide receiver Tory Horton to have the biggest role of his career.
​The Seahawks created urgency with their offense by trading for Nelson on a cheap package deal from the Indianapolis Colts. Not only does Nelson’s addition help the rushing offense , but it also helps the passing game. Chicago is one of the most blitz-happy defenses in the league, which means quarterback Sam Darnold needs to quickly find open receivers.
​Horton is a receiver who has been able to get open thanks to his speed and his solid route-running. Through the six games played, Horton caught five receptions on 10 targets for 67 yards and a touchdown. He hasn't had many opportunities this season due to the offense's regression in play-calling, quarterback play, offensive line stability and lack of explosiveness in the run game.
​Horton should get his second start of the season with Shaheed out. It also means he could get more targets as the Bears' defense will look to double-cover wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Horton would be the next target that Darnold turns to if he needed a quick pass-catcher. His speed and great hands could be a great weapon against a Bears' secondary that is among the worst in the league.
​Horton has accounted for 48 receiving yards twice in his professional career. Last season, he had four games where he accounted for a receiving touchdown. This game could be an opportunity for him to account for more than one touchdown since his breakout 38-14 win over the Washington Commanders before his shin injury kept him out for the year.
​With Shaheed out, the Seahawks likely make Horton the leading kickoff and punt returner. He had two kickoffs for 60 yards in Week 7's 20-3 win over the Chiefs. He has experience in making big plays on special teams. Horton returned three punts for 113 yards, including a 95-yard punt return for a touchdown in the 44-13 Week 3 win last season over the New Orleans Saints.
​This game is Horton’s chance to show he deserves to be in the starting lineup full-time as the Seahawks might be facing some questions with their receiver corps. A solid performance from Horton might also suppress the trade talk that the Seahawks should inquire about another wide receiver like Brian Thomas Jr.

title: Seahawks Confidence Meter: Running Game Should Be Much Better
full_text:
A lot has changed for the Seattle Seahawks (4-3) between Week 7 and 8.  The Seahawks dominated the Kansas City Chiefs thanks to their impressive defense. Just a few days after the win over the Chiefs, the Seahawks instantly improved their offense by trading f or eight-time Pro-Bowl guard Quenton Nelson. This should easily be one of the most impactful trades this season.
​ Seattle should also get some much-needed reinforcements in the running game thanks to the return of veteran running back Zach Charbonnet, and possibly rookie running back Jadarian Price. Charbonnet is returning from an ACL injury he suffered in the NFC Divisional Round win last January.
Price is coming off a chest injury that forced him to go to IR for four games. The Seahawks should have a drastically improved running game in Week 8's Monday Night Football game versus the Chicago Bears (5-2).
​The Seahawks' offense has been incredibly unbalanced this season due to the adjustments of new offensive coordinator Brian Fleury, the instability of the offensive line and the numerous turnovers. The Seahawks averaged 129.5 rushing yards in the first two wins, both resulting in wins.
In the next four games, including when Price was put on IR  after Week 3, the Seahawks averaged 96 rushing yards. Seattle is 1-3 in those games, as quarterback Sam Darnold's interceptions are a massive factor in the losses .
Seattle rushed for 153 yards, with a good portion coming from long, sustained scoring drives. Seattle dominated Kansas City 20-3, but could've made it 27-3 due to Darnold's interception in the red zone. It was also the best performance from the offensive line this season. The Seahawks added Nelson and two reliable and more explosive running backs ahead of Emanuel Wilson and George Holani. There is hope for Seattle to have a top-ten or top-five rushing offense .
The Seahawks missed Price’s speed and his ability to quickly find and attack a hole at the line of scrimmage. He should get more chances behind an elite run-blocker in Nelson. Charbonnet doesn’t possess the speed that Price or his previous backfield teammate Kenneth Walker III possess.
What makes him more efficient than Wilson and Holani is his athleticism and aggressiveness to run for more yards after first contact. Charbonnet should be back to playoff form if he isn’t limited by his knee injury.
​There are some reasons that the Seahawks might have a slow start running the ball. Among the reasons is the offensive line movement since the Nelson trade . He is immediately inserted as the starting left guard while second-year guard Grey Zabel is moved to the starting right guard. Anthony Bradford, who had a solid performance in his first game, is moved to the bench. It may take some time for Nelson to adjust to his new team or Zabel to a new position for the first time in nearly two years.
​The Seahawks might also see Charbonnet not as explosive or aggressive as he was before his injury. Price hasn’t been taken off IR late Sunday night for Week 8. If he does play, he might not be 100%. The last game he played, he was benched for his turnover issues.
The Bears, on the other hand, made moves to improve their defense significantly. Chicago traded multiple draft picks to the Tennessee Titans for four-time Pro-Bowl defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. The Bears had the eighth-best rushing defense in the league before the trade for Simmons. Nelson and Simmons should have another huge battle ahead of them on Monday Night Football.

title: 3 Matchups That Will Decide Seahawks’ Week 8 Clash vs. Bears
full_text:
On Monday night at Lumen Field, Mike Macdonald’s Seattle Seahawks look to stay above the .500 mark when they host the 5-2 Chicago Bears. It’s a battle of defending division champions and the third straight prime time contest for the defending Lombardi Trophy holders.
Macdonald’s team owns the league’s top-ranked defense in terms of fewest total yards and fewest passing yards allowed per game. Chicago’s offense has reached the end zone 21 times in seven games, while the Seahawks have allowed only 12 offensive TDs in the same number of contests.
Both teams have been in the news lately for making huge acquisitions. More importantly, both the Bears and Seahawks are looking up in their respective divisions behind a pair of 6-1 clubs. So here’s a look at some key battles that will play a big part in tonight’s result.
Talk about irony? Since 2019 and including a meeting back in Week 6 at Lucas Oil Stadium, eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson of the Indianapolis Colts and four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons of the Tennessee Titans certainly had their share of battles. Last week, both found new homes last week as the former was traded to the Seahawks and the latter was dealt to the Tennessee Titans.
Now due to an amazing set of circumstances, they will renew acquaintances on Monday night in the Pacific Northwest. Nelson is currently Pro Football Focus’ second-ranked player at his position , while Simmons is PFF’s No. 10 interior defender. In seven games this season, the eight-year pro has totaled 38 tackles, four sacks, nine QB sacks, and four passes defensed.
Prepare for another epic battle.
A year ago, the 10th overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft led the Bears in catches (58) and receiving yards (713) and tied for the team lead with six touchdown grabs. Seven games into this season, tight end Colston Loveland and wideout Kalif Raymond both have 26 receptions for 244 yards, tied for the second on the club in both categories.
Loveland has two touchdowns to Raymond’s one. However, exactly half of Loveland catches (13), more than half of those yards (134) and both of those scores have come in Chicago’s last two games.
Eight-year pro Julian Love ranks sixth on the club with 24 tackles despite missing one game. He leads the Seahawks with six passes defensed and is tied for the team lead with a pair of interceptions. Can he cool off the suddenly-hot tight end?
D'Andre Swift bounces it outside for the SCORE. Bears up, 10-0. NEvsCHI on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/R75ldG3SHb
Entering Week 8, Ben Johnson’s club owned the league’s top-ranked ground attack, averaging a brisk 154.3 yards per outing. The Bears’ leading rusher is D’Andre Swift, now in his third season in the Windy City. He’s totaled team highs in carries (116), yards (476), and total touchdowns (7)—all of those scores via the ground. He comes off a season-best 22 attempts, good for 78 yards and one touchdown in Chicago’s Thursday night win over the Patriots.
Seahawks’ linebacker Drake Thomas ranks third on the team with 35 tackles, behind only Ernest Jones IV (68) and Devon Witherspoon (41). While Thomas’s 2026 grade (60.6) via Pro Football Focus is far from awe-inspiring, his number in terms of run defense (70.5) is worth mentioning. And does Aden Durde also use the former undrafted free agent from North Carolina State to spy Caleb Williams?

title: 5 Key Things to Know About Bears vs. Seahawks in Week 8
full_text:
The defending Super Bowl champions have had no choice other than to prove that they are ready for prime time. For the third consecutive week, the Seattle Seahawks will be under the lights and facing a playoff team from 2025. From a Thursday night visit to Denver (overtime loss) to a Sunday evening home game with the Chiefs (win) to this Monday night clash of defending division champions in the form of the Chicago Bears.
Yes, the ‘Hawks they’re already lost as many games as they did all of last season and are just 3-2 in their last five outings. But they sent somewhat of a physical message to Andy Reid’s team last Sunday night at Lumen Field, handing the Chiefs their first loss of 2026 via a 20-3 score.
Bears QB Caleb Williams Week 7 Highlights vs. Patriots 22/33 308 PASS YDS 2 PASS TD 0 INT Bears win 30-24. pic.twitter.com/Tw6Yxc2ioI
Meanwhile, the Bears have had some extra time to prepare for their first appearance in the Pacific Northwest since 2021. They were last seen outlasting the New England Patriots, 30-24, on a Thursday night at Soldier Field thanks to a big evening by quarterback Caleb Williams.
Of course, both of these teams made big noise late last week when it came to acquiring star players. Seahawks’ general manager John Schneider orchestrated a deal to acquire eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts. A day later, Chicago’s Ryan Poles completed a trade with the Tennessee Titans to add four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons—and paid a hefty price to do so.
As far as the rest of the NFC West, the first-place San Francisco 49ers had Week 8 off, while the Los Angeles Rams and Arizona Cardinals both came up with wins on Sunday.
Even though the Bears own a pair of postseason wins in this setting, it’s the Seahawks that have a four-game overall lead (12-8) in a series that dates back to Seattle’s inaugural campaign in 1976.
As for much more recent times, this marks the second time in three years the clubs will battle. Back on a Thursday night (the day after Christmas), the ‘Hawks managed a 6-3 triumph over the Beats in Chicago in one of the uglier games in recent years. As for the Bears’ last appearance in Seattle, the club came up with a 25-24 triumph back in 2021.
SAM DARNOLD IS PICKED IN THE END ZONE BEFORE THE HALF 😱 (via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/QjFAJ7JRGc
Both clubs own a minus-1 turnover differential this season. Chicago has forced 10 turnovers and totaled 11 giveaways. Seattle has 12 takeaways, but has already given up the football 13 times. It's worth noting that Seahawks’ quarterback Sam Darnold has thrown at least one interception in five straight games.
Only five teams in the league, including the Bears (87.6) are allowing fewer rushing yards per game (89.4 average) than Macdonald’s team. But Aden Durde’s defense faces a very stiff challenge in the league’s top-ranked ground attack. Led by D’Andre Swift, Chicago is averaging 154.3 rushing yards per contest.
Dillion Thieneman’s sack was on green dog blitz. Green dog is when the defender has the green light to blitz if their man to man responsibility blocks. Quick recognition here by Thieneman to add on. #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/h2DUSiW57q
He was the 25th overall pick in April’s draft and has come up big in his rookie season. Former University of Oregon defender Dillon Thieneman (who began his college career at Purdue) leads the Bears with 43 defensive tackles, to go along with 1.5 sacks, five passes defensed, one interception, and four special teams’ stops.
Mike Macdonald’s club has proven to be a second-half team this season. The Seahawks have been outscored a combined 72-63 in the first 30 minutes in their seven games. On the other hand, they have nearly doubled up the opposition in the second half and overtime, 105-53—allowing four offensive TDs.

title: Why DeForest Buckner Wanted to Return to the San Francisco 49ers
full_text:
The trade for and return of defensive tackle DeForest Buckner is exactly what the San Francisco 49ers needed ahead of the trade deadline.
It was reported that the Chicago Bears offered multiple picks for Buckner, but there was only one destination the 32-year-old had on his mind: San Francisco.
Speaking with the media for the first time since the trade was made, Buckner stated to reporters : "When everything kind of unfolded and everything, I stated that I wanted to come here. I didn't want to go anywhere else.
"Obviously, the familiarity with being here, being drafted here, all the guys that are still here when I was here, watching them. I've been keeping up with the games over the years and just watching the standard of play that they play at, and the winning football that they play at. This is where I wanted to be.
"I'm really just focused on the new opportunity I have here and just taking it one week at a time," Buckner added. "Like, literally, that's all I've been thinking about. It's been a whirlwind and everything, but my main goal is just continuing each and every week to get better.
"It's just crazy how life work. Coming back full circle, being here, this new opportunity. You all don't understand how excited I am to be back in the red and gold, where it all started, and with a bunch of guys that I have love for, and they have love for me, and I just want to continue to show them what I can do and what I can bring to the table."
Clearly, no bridges were burnt after six years away, which is a more than welcome outcome as the 49ers desperately needed to improve on their pass rush.
Ironically, despite not having played a single snap for San Francisco yet, he is already the team's sack leader. He's recorded four sacks this season and returns at the perfect time, with the 49ers' bye week having just finished. This gives him a full week to reintegrate into the team before returning to action.
Dre Greenlaw returned in free agency, Deebo Samuel followed during training camp, and now Buckner is back in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick. It's becoming clearer than ever that San Francisco wants to stay loyal to some of its former veterans .
This year is the best time to win it all. Acquiring Buckner is shrewd business.

title: Jauan Jennings did the 49ers a Favor by Saying No
full_text:
At first glance, Jauan Jennings turning down a trade back to San Francisco looks like a snub. The 49ers reportedly worked out a framework with Minnesota that depended on Jennings telling the front office he wanted to come back. According to reports, he said no and chose to stay with the Vikings.
My take is that the 49ers got lucky.
BREAKING: The 49ers and Vikings recently had a trade agreement in place for WR Jauan Jennings to return to San Francisco, but Jennings made it clear he didn’t want to go back, and the deal fell through, per Jay Glazer. pic.twitter.com/9vpr0Q4u2s
Look at who the Niners would have been lining up. Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Jennings and George Kittle are all big, physical players who win with strength, hands and yards after the catch. That group has plenty of toughness and plenty of ways to move the chains. The problem is that none of them is a pure burner. Add Jennings and you have a very strong receiver room that would struggle to stretch the field.
I’d argue San Francisco is already short on speed, and I wouldn’t make it worse by adding another receiver who works the same way.
Jennings Would Have Cost Stribling Snaps
The other issue is playing time. De’Zhaun Stribling is a rookie the front office spent a No. 33 pick on, and he needs reps, especially once he’s fully healthy. Jennings would have been a veteran with a long history in this offense and a clear claim on snaps. That kind of crowding would take targets and playing time from the player the team should want to develop, and the coaching staff might have defaulted to the familiar name.
If any WR is being added and would demand snaps and targets away from Stribling, it better be Jets Garrett Wilson or Colts Josh Downs.
Demarcus Robinson showed what the offense is missing in Week 1 against the Rams. He had only two catches, but they went for 50 yards, including a 39-yard touchdown that came on a play where the defense had to respect him downfield. That kind of threat opens up everything else, including the underneath routes and the run game.
Jennings is a very good possession receiver. He caught 210 passes for 2,581 yards and 22 touchdowns in five seasons in San Francisco. But he’s not that type of player, and this season he has just four catches for 43 yards in Minnesota’s offense. That’s no longer a game-changing role.
Since Jennings isn’t coming back, the 49ers can keep looking for a receiver with real separation and speed on his routes. That’s the target I wrote about last Friday with Garrett Wilson, and there may be others who fit better. The Nov. 10 deadline is close, and an idea that was ruled out for the wrong reasons isn’t a loss.
A Jennings, 49ers reunion doesn’t fix the real problem of the lack of speed and route running separation. The fact that Jennings declined takes the injured WR room solution off the table, and that might be the best thing that could happen for the Niners this week.

title: Latest Brandon Aiyuk News Greatly Benefits the 49ers
full_text:
After an incredibly odd summer, Brandon Aiyuk is finally taking the proper steps towards filing for reinstatement,
Aiyuk has hired Drew Rosenhaus as his new agent after being without one for the last half-year. This move signals that Aiyuk is actually serious about playing football again.
It also means that the San Francisco 49ers will need to factor him into their plans. And no, that doesn't mean they will put him on their active 53-man roster.
As desperate as the 49ers are at wide receiver, the bridge with Aiyuk has been burned for a long time. However, his pending return would greatly benefit the 49ers in another way.
Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has hired Drew Rosenhaus for representation, and the agent said that he is “working on getting him back to work and playing again in the NFL.” pic.twitter.com/qFtuAYajOx
Aside from the 49ers, there are countless teams with wide receiver needs. The Kansas City Chiefs, Las Vegas Raiders, and the Pittsburgh Steelers are a few to name.
The 49ers can easily dangle Aiyuk as trade bait for those desperate teams. That's why Aiyuk has decided to hire Rosenhaus to represent him now.
With the NFL trade deadline steadily approaching on Nov. 10, he's aiming to be reinstated quickly and have the 49ers trade him so he can revive his NFL career.
Aiyuk damaged his reputation throughout the offseason with a flurry of social media posts. From trashing the 49ers to acting like he was already signed to the Washington Commanders .
It was incredibly odd and foolish of Aiyuk. He did nothing to help his case against the 49ers or to further his NFL career.
However, now there's a chance for him to rebound. If the NFL reinstates him within the week, assuming he actually files for it, the 49ers can trade him.
Despite damaging his image in the offseason, he has a market again, with several teams needing a receiver. They can easily look past his weird social media posts.
All they will want to know is if he's healthy and in shape to help them win games. The Chiefs would certainly look past any character concerns with Aiyuk. They do it all the time.
Aiyuk looks like a saint compared to their red-flag players they have. The 49ers should reach out to the Chiefs and ask for a sixth-round pick for Aiyuk.
It's not significant draft capital by any means, but getting something for Aiyuk after the offseason he had would be tremendous.
Plus, it's good to get Aiyuk off the team and finally be done with him. Everything hinges on the NFL granting Aiyuk's reinstatement soon, assuming he does.

title: The 49ers Player Who Needs to Step Up After the Bye Week
full_text:
There likely isn't a player under more pressure than San Francisco 49ers kicker Eddy Piñeiro after the bye week.
For him, the week off presented an opportunity to reflect, get in extra practice by taking hundreds or even thousands of kicks, as well as regain his confidence and rhythm heading into the second half of the season.
Piñeiro has missed four PATs and 3 field goals so far this year. That places him tied for 31st and then 32nd, respectively. A massive decline since last year.
At first, it didn't have a direct impact on winning the game, but that changed in his performance against the Atlanta Falcons. San Francisco would have been down by just one score on the final possession if Piñeiro hadn't missed an extra point earlier in the game.
Any continued struggles, particularly in potential game-winning situations, will put the 49ers' front office in a difficult position.
The organization handed him a four-year contract that, at the time, seemed well deserved. However, if his struggles persist, the 49ers could find themselves tied to an expensive contract that becomes increasingly difficult to justify.
His performance this season simply hasn't been good enough, regardless of the limited number of game-winning situations in which the 49ers have needed him this season.
Perhaps equally concerning is Piñeiro's admission that he needs to review the tape to figure out where he's going wrong. His job is, quite literally, to kick a football from various angles and distances, with extra points offering an even more favorable opportunity at just 29 yards. At this stage, Piñeiro needs to find a way to get back on track and deliver.
"We have a lot of belief in Eddy. He has had a tough run early this year, but we extended Eddy for his body of work with us but then throughout the history of his career," shared John Lynch on KNBR recently.
"He's going through a rough patch right now.... We have belief in Eddy, and we're going to ride with him."
The contract Piñeiro signed makes it difficult for the 49ers to consider releasing him, particularly given the significant dead-cap hit they would incur. With so much guaranteed money tied up in his deal, moving on from him would come at a considerable financial cost.
He became a fan favorite last year, but he now faces a lot of pressure. He needs to step up. Plain and simple.

title: 5 49ers Poised for Better Play After Bye Week
full_text:
Now that the San Francisco 49ers are at their bye week, it is a good chance for some players to reset their bodies and minds and get ready for a strong end of the season. Which players on the roster are poised to play better in the second half than they did in the first half?
Watkins started to come along in the two weeks prior to the bye week. He has 184 career snaps in one and a half seasons. Of those, 97 were in the past two weeks. He has eight career catches for 164 yards. He has four catches for 78 yards in the past two weeks.
San Francisco might get healthier at the bye week. That could push Watkins down a bit. However, the team has to find ways to keep him on the field because he is young and talented.
Odighizuwa has two sacks in seven games, so is already pacing toward his career-high of 4.5 sacks. However, with DeForest Buckner in the picture, life should get a lot easier for him. He should play fewer snaps and be more impactful when he does play. Look for at least three more sacks this year.
The rookie made his defensive debut with two snaps in Week 7. Now, the team has cut Jack Jones, leaving a role open for dime snaps. When San Francisco wants to push Deommodore Lenoir in the slot, it likely means Prysock coming in on the outside now. This will be a lot more on his plate.
Williams returned from his ACL injury in Week 5. He went from 23 snaps in his debut to 30 the following week and then 33 the game after that. Now, he gets a bye week to regroup and reassess where he stands.
Williams should come out of the bye week healthy with a better group of players around him. He should finish the year strong.
Mustapha started the season on the bench. The third-year safety has three starts this season. However, he had 22 career starts before that. So, now that he is back in the lineup and playing well, it is going to be hard to pull him. They might bench Ji’Ayir Brown when Marques Sigle is healthy and roll with Sigle.

title: The 49ers Have 5 Trade Targets After Jauan Jennings Snub
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers reportedly called the Minnesota Vikings to make a trade for wide receiver Jauan Jennings. However, Jennings did not want to play for the 49ers, so the deal did not go through. Still, it confirms the 49ers' interest in a wide receiver.
Now that they have shown interest in a wide receiver, who are the best pivots for the 49ers?
Downs requested a trade from his current team, so he is clearly going to be an option available on the trade block. However, he is also 25 years old with an 800-yard season on his resume. So, he is going to cost a bit more than some others on the trade market.
Still, if the 49ers can trade for him and extend him, he could join De’Zhaun Stribling as a young core.
Jeudy is more of a veteran who can put the team over the top this season. The Cleveland Browns' best receivers are rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion. While they are 5-3, their best bet is to let these two develop. Trading Jeudy can open snaps for these two.
Thomas put up 1,282 yards in his rookie season. However, the team changed coaches, and the scheme does not appear to fit the former first-round pick. The Jaguars benched him in Week 6, and while he caught a touchdown in Week 8, it is not going to cool down the trade talks. The issue with Thomas is that the Jaguars are going to look for a return similar to Marvin Harrison Jr. That is a lot to trade for a player who has as many questions as Thomas.
Ridley has five catches for 81 yards this season. He is not 32 years old and has not been fully healthy this season. Still, some of that can be the player; some can be playing for a poor Titans team. Ridley is not going to cost much to acquire in a trade, and the upside is still there. The 49ers can give him a chance.
Johnston might be the best fit when you factor in age, production and cost. The Chargers are now 0-7, and Johnston is likely going to leave in free agency. Their best choice would be to trade him.

title: The 49ers Have 3 Trade Suitors Emerging for Mac Jones
full_text:
As the weeks get closer to the NFL trade deadline , the odds of the team trading quarterback Mac Jones have once again increased. Who are three teams that are now emerging as likely candidates to trade for Mac Jones?
The Vikings are heading into Week 9 at 6-1. However, they are being carried by the best defense in the NFL and a below-average offense. An offense with Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison has enough firepower to win games. So, the issue is Kyler Murray.
The NFC North is tight, and the last-place team is sitting at 5-3. So, the Vikings could go from the last undefeated team to last place in their division in the matter of a few weeks if they do not get things together on offense.
The Vikings have the weapons and the run game for Jones to step in and compete with Murray. It would be the only chance for Minnesota to stay in contention with their elite defense. That could cause an overpay that the 49ers would have to accept.
The Ravens are going to place Lamar Jackson on the IR with a thumb injury. Their backup Tyler Huntley got hurt in Week 8. So, they are onto rookie UDFA Joey Fagano. The Ravens are sitting at 4-4, but now they are in last place in their division. They need to find a way to turn things around quickly.
What makes things interesting for Baltimore is that Jackson only has one year left on his deal and a high cap hit. The Ravens will either be looking to extend him or trade him this offseason. With a brand new coaching staff and his history of injuries, the team might look to use this year to pivot. If Jones keeps them in contention, he could be the Ravens' 2027 starter.
Philadelphia is another team that could be looking to the future. Jalen Hurts suffered blood clots and is out for the year. No one knows when he will play again. We have all seen enough of Tanner McKee to know he is not the Eagles' answer for the future.
They can trade for Jones and give him the rest of the season to prove that he deserves a chance in 2027. The division being weak only makes trading for Jones more sensible.

title: The 49ers Have Multiple Needs to Address Before the Trade Deadline
full_text:
Now that the San Francisco 49ers traded for defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, the team has taken one of their needs off the board. San Francisco made the trade early enough that they still have time to make another move before the trade deadline. If they did make a move, what would be the biggest need?
A lot of people would see this as their biggest need, but the addition of Buckner, combined with Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams starting to get healthy, has the team stronger on the edge. Williams will not slide inside nearly as much with Buckner, giving them a full-time rusher. Bosa should be back soon, and rookie Romello Height has taken steps. With Keion White as the fourth rusher, it is not a pressing need.
The team started the season playing Jack Jones in a dime role. He is now a free agent. Their backup slot option is Ashtyn Davis, who is borderline unplayable. San Francisco is going to try a rookie fifth-round pick, Ephesians Prysock or the injured Nate Hobbs . Both have potential and questions.
The good news is that adding a depth cornerback is not going to cost too much. That is a relatively big need for the 49ers.
Left guard is a big need because it is hard to see the roster getting any better naturally. Connor Colby is in his second NFL season, and his progress appears to have stalled. Carver Willis is a rookie fourth-round pick who played tackle in college. Willis could take over and hit the ground running, but the team might be best served giving him time. At the very least, looking to insert the rookie during a run into the playoffs would be a dangerous move.
Whether it be a one-season rental or someone who could push Willis next season as well, they need to figure it out.
Receiver is the toughest to gauge, but ultimately their biggest need. Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Demarcus Robinson, and De’Zhaun Stribling could all finish the year healthy. However, all four have major injury questions, and aside from Evans, the other three do not have much proven production this season
When adding in that Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing did not take advantage of their snaps with those four out, it is fair to think they can add to the position. This is their biggest need.

title: Latest Report Shows 49ers Made Right Decision Moving On From Jauan Jennings
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers may need to trade for a wide receiver right now to strengthen their Super Bowl hopes this season, but a recent development has reminded them that some of their offseason decisions were spot on.
In the offseason, the 49ers had many decisions to make at wide receiver. They moved on from Kendrick Bourne after a one-year return, and they also parted ways with Jauan Jennings, who ultimately went to the Minnesota Vikings .
Jennings, in particular, was a name that raised some eyebrows. He's an intriguing character with plenty of admirable qualities, including his toughness, but he ultimately showed that he didn't make the most of his opportunity in one of the best offensive systems in the league.
This was demonstrated further after new reports from Jay Glazer revealed the 49ers and the Vikings were exploring a possible trade for Jennings, but he didn't want to hop on a FaceTime call with Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch after an agreement was in place.
Here’s Jay Glazer talking about Jauan Jennings not wanting to get on a FaceTime call with Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch to get traded back to the 49ers https://t.co/JWWNIT0zQQ pic.twitter.com/ceOmmEpLvF
Now, if true, it shows the 49ers made the right call all along with Jennings and their management of him. Don't forget that during the 2025 training camp, he missed time with a calf injury, but it was also reported that he was exploring a new deal.
It made sense for the 49ers to consider rewarding Jennings after he enjoyed a career-best 2024 season, finishing just 25 yards short of a 1,000-yard campaign. That said, handing him a lucrative new deal was understandably something the franchise was hesitant to do. Instead, the two sides eventually agreed to an incentive-based contract that also added an extra year to his deal.
However, Jennings arguably became the architect of his own downfall from that point onwards. After dealing with injuries and the consequences of missing valuable preparation time, he struggled to build on his breakout campaign. He finished the 2025 season with 55 receptions for 643 yards and a career-high nine touchdowns across 15 games. He was playing for some of those games with injuries too.
And then, during the recent offseason, reports stated that the 49ers were willing to offer $17 million a year . He declined. Then things went quiet and he joined the Vikings on a one-year, $13 million contract, with $8 million base. So far, he's only had four receptions all year.
All that can be said is that it's a massive upgrade to have a future Hall of Famer like Mike Evans on the team for less than what they were offering Jennings, despite the unique qualities Jennings brought to the receiver corps.

title: The 49ers and Vikings had a Trade in Place for Jauan Jennings and He Nixed It
full_text:
What a bad look for the 49ers.
They desperately need a wide receiver because their three big additions this offseason -- Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and De'Zhaun Stribling -- are all injured. So, of course, the 49ers called up the Vikings to inquire about trading for Jauan Jennings, who has four catches for 43 yards this season.
And, of course, the Vikings were open to trading Jennings back to the 49ers, where he spent the first five seasons of his career. The two teams even had a deal in place, a ccording to FOX's Jay Glazer.
But Jennings nixed the deal. Apparently, it was contingent upon Jennings having a FaceTime call with Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch, presumably to clear the air after their relationship became rocky during the past couple seasons.
Jennings refused to participate in the call. He wouldn't even talk to Lynch and Shanahan. Which means Brandon Aiyuk isn't the only former 49ers wide receiver who seems to hold a deep, personal grudge against them.
It's unclear why Jennings seems so upset with the 49ers. Maybe he thinks the Vikings are the better team and that he'll get his opportunities soon enough. Or, maybe he's still bitter than the 49ers never gave him the contract extension he wanted. He always saw himself as the best receiver on their roster, even better than Aiyuk, and felt the 49ers didn't appreciate him.
Did Jennings have an inflated opinion of himself? Absolutely. But that's part of what made him good. He truly believed he was the best, even though he's not. And now, the 49ers want him back, and they can't have him because they didn't show him love. Or something.
What's important to the 49ers is that they haven't figured out a solution to their wide receiver problem. Clearly, they're searching the bargain bin for a receiver they can get in exchange for a late-round draft pick, which is disappointing.
They need a true difference-maker to replace Mike Evans if he misses time with Achilles tendinitis. And they'll never draft that wide receiver at the end of Round 1, which is where they pick almost every year. They tried recently and ended up with Ricky Pearsall and Stribling, who aren't exactly as good as Evans.
The 49ers need to get serious and start offering their first-round picks to bad teams that have great wide receivers. They have 10 days to figure it out.

title: Bucs' Baker Mayfield Reveals Why He Didn't Complete a Single Pass
full_text:
It was an interesting game, to say the least, as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' 16-0 Week 8 defeat of the Atlanta Falcons brought them just half a game out of the NFC South lead.
The field and weather conditions made for a sloppy game overall, and ultimately led to both quarterbacks not throwing the ball or not being effective in throwing it.
That led to a huge game on the ground for the Bucs, who set multiple records in the process. However, with Baker Mayfield not completing a single pass on the day, it became the first time a team went on to win a game in that fashion in 52 years (the 1974 Buffalo Bills).
Following the win, Mayfield spoke about not completing a single pass.
“It’s winning – that’s the way I think about it. We won. [It’s] getting our guys lined up, making sure we are running the right run plays," Mayfield said. "Obviously, ball security [is crucial] in these conditions – we had some early ones. We decided to go to the shotgun and pistol sets – it’s just easier to receive the snaps instead of it coming back through your hands under center."
"So, going from there and just trying to manage the game. [It’s] time management and just trying to bleed the clock as much as possible. Just get everybody on the same page and go from there. That’s my job in these conditions and, listen, I will do whatever it takes to win. That’s all that matters to me.”
Mayfield nailed it on the head in his postgame press conference.
It's clear that the game script was going to demand Tampa Bay run the ball, and after doing so effectively against the Carolina Panthers just a week before, the Falcons knew it was coming.
That didn't matter, as the Falcons gave up over 300 yards rushing, with career highs on the ground by both Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell.
It didn't matter to Mayfield whether or not the ball would be put in his hands. It was all about winning, and that is exactly what they did.
Whether the Bucs can continue this type of play and still continue to stack wins remains to be seen, and at some point, Mayfield will have to throw the ball to help.
But for the time being, they should continue to lean on their strengths, which will undoubtedly be tested this upcoming week against a Chicago Bears' defense that ranks fourth in the league against the run.

title: One Big Concern Remains After Buccaneers' Back-to-Back Wins
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are coming off of fantastic wins against the division rival Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons and find themselves only half a game back from first place in the NFC South after a terrible start to the season.
The main boon for this team has been their ability to run the football and play lights-out defense as one of the best units in the league in recent weeks.
One major question is on many Bucs fans' minds, and a growing concern is where the pass game has been in recent weeks this season.
Over the past two weeks, Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield has thrown the ball 14 times for 64 yards and a touchdown, and that includes him throwing just three passes in a monsoon against the Falcons.
The weather is typically attributed as the biggest reason as to why the team ran the ball as much as they did against Atlanta, but there are many who worry that Mayfield isn't fully healthy and the team simply can't throw the football with his thumb injury.
It is important to remember, though, that Todd Bowles and offensive coordinator Zach Robinson want to be a running football team.
"Everything we talked about – controlling time of possession, running the football, getting turnovers on defense, making plays on special teams, the things we had to do to win the ball game – that's what we talked about right before kickoff in the locker room," Bowles said. "So, it came to fruition. I didn't think it would come to fruition that close, but it came pretty close."
Time will tell whether or not the Bucs want to open up the passing attack more going forward with the 2026 offense. However, it is also important to note that right now, the Bucs don't need to pass the football much, considering the great level of success they have running the ball under Zach Robinson.
While it might not be the game plan many wanted the Buccaneers to have on offense to reach success, the plan the team has in place is working well.

title: Todd Bowles Gives Injury Update on Buccaneers Defensive Starter
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are on a bit of a hot streak. They've won three of their last four games, and now, they're just a half game out of the NFC South lead.
They'll want to keep that going, and to do that, they'll need as many starting players as they can to contribute. But one key defensive starter could be out for some time after Sunday's 16-0 win over the Atlanta Falcons — but it might not be too long.
Todd Bowles spoke to media on Monday, and he gave an update on edge rusher Yaya Diaby and whether or not he could miss some time.
Todd Bowles told the media Monday that Diaby sprained his MCL in the win over the Falcons. It corroborates an earlier Monday report by NFL Insider Ian Rapoport. Rapoport reported that it was a Grade 2 sprain and that Diaby could miss a little time, but that he wouldn't miss significant time.
#Bucs outside linebacker YaYa Diaby, who exited Sunday’s win early, is believed to have suffered an MCL sprain, source says. He’ll have an MRI this morning, but the hope is the injury is not one to cause him to miss extended time. pic.twitter.com/r1nJQnwxix
Bowles confirmed on Monday that Diaby has a sprain and that the hope is that he won't be put on injured reserve.
"He has an MCL sprain. Not sure how much he'll miss," Bowles said. We'll see how the week progresses and we'll go from there."
Diaby is in a contract year in 2026, and while he was slow to get going this season, he's made up for lost time in recent weeks.
Diaby had a hat trick of sacks against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7, boosting his total to three. So far this year, he has 11 solo tackles, three sacks and an interception, the latter of which he got against the Dallas Cowboys in a win on Thursday Night Football.
If Diaby misses some time, the Bucs will likely turn to players like David Walker, Al-Quadin Muhammad and Anthony Nelson to fill in for him on his side. Walker has been a standout edge rusher this season for Tampa Bay and is earning more snaps there, while both Muhammad and Nelson have been strong rotational pieces so far this year.
If Diaby does have to miss some time, he has at least one thing going for him. The Bucs will have a bye week in Week 10, so he could use that as a buffer to recover and miss fewer games than he normally would.
The Bucs willl play the Chicago Bears on Sunday night on Nov. 8 at Soldier Field.

title: Every Record the Buccaneers Set in Historic Win Over Falcons
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers beat the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8. With that win, they moved within half a game of the NFC South lead and picked up their second win in a row for the first time in 385 days.
It isn't the fact that Tampa Bay won that has people talking, though — it's how Tampa Bay won. A rainy day brought a big change to the offensive game plan, and it resulted in a historic, record-breaking performance in Tampa Bay's 16-0 win.
Here's every record the Bucs became a part of when they beat the Falcons without completing a single pass:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers — and, by extension, quarterback Baker Mayfield — did not complete a pass against the Atlanta Falcons. That's an astonishing feat in itself, and it created a windfall that led to breaking more records.
The Bucs became the first NFL team since 1974 to win an NFL game without completing a pass. That game was on Sept. 9, 1974, when the Buffalo Bills defeated the New York Jets 16-12 in similarly rainy conditions.
The Falcons also set a new record on Sunday, though it's probably not one they're very proud of. Atlanta got shut out by the Bucs on Sunday, and with that, the Falcons became the first team to be shut out by a team that didn't complete a pass since 1942. Mayfield didn't complete a pass, but his passer rating (39.6) was higher than Falcons quarterback Michael Penix's (12.0).
With the conditions as they were, the Bucs had to run the football a lot, and oh, did they. The Bucs toted the rock to the tune of 324 rushing yards, which broke the franchise record for most rushing yards in a game — that record was previously set in 2015 against the Philadelphia Eagles, when the Bucs had 283 rushing yards that day.
Tampa Bay may not have passed much at all on Sunday, but it didn't last Sunday, either. Over the last two games the Bucs have played, they've completed just seven passes on 14 attempts — despite that, they've won both of those games by a combined 59-13.
The Bucs are set to play the Chicago Bears on Sunday Night Football in Week 9 on Nov. 8. They probably won't be able to win that game by completing fewer than 10 passes, but at this point, we're open to believing.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Buccaneers' 16-0 Shutout Victory Over The Falcons
full_text:
That's how many days had passed since the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last won back-to-back football games.
Thankfully, that dreadful drought has officially reached its conclusion after the Buccaneers secured a much-needed victory on Sunday, defeating the Falcons 16-0 for their second victory in as many weeks. With the win, the Bucs have now improved their overall record on the year to 3-5 while going 2-0 against NFC South teams.
Not only does this victory represent the first time the Bucs have won back-to-back games in well over a year, but it also provides some optimism for a team that was getting dangerously close to eliminating itself from playoff contention before the halfway mark of the 2026 NFL season.
Now, let's break down the good, the bad and the ugly we saw in this crucial Week 8 NFC South showdown between the Buccaneers and Falcons.
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers' rushing attack entered a new tier of domination on Sunday.
Following last week's 258-yard explosion, I don't think anybody expected the Bucs to surpass that mark again this season, let alone the very next week. The Bucs didn't just surpass that mark, though; they absolutely obliterated it by rushing for an absurd 324 total yards on the ground against the Falcons, a top-five rushing defense in the entire league heading into this game.
As has been the case for the majority of this season, Bucky Irving was electric running the football in this contest. When it was all said and done, Irving had ducked and weaved his way to 170 yards on the ground and 1 TD while averaging 6.3 yards per rush on 27 carries. Had he not fumbled the ball through the end zone early in the game, he'd have had another TD added to his resume.
As the game went on, Irving got some rest while Kenneth Gainwell took the majority of snaps, and boy did he take advantage of that opportunity. Gainwell rushed 25 times for a career-high 140 yards, and his relentless and slippery style of running was reminiscent of his partner in crime, Irving.
After a surprisingly disappointing start to the year, the Buccaneers' offensive line has officially re-established itself as one of the league's best. As a group, they deserve a ton of credit for the team's dominant rushing performance over the past two weeks.
The 324 total rushing yards achieved by the Buccaneers today vs. the Falcons is the most in franchise history.
Oh, how things can change quickly in the NFL. Just a few short weeks ago, the fans in Tampa were calling for Todd Bowles' job. Now? They would be wise to praise him for the job he's done with his young defense, which all of a sudden looks like one of the best all-around units in the entire NFL.
The Bucs' defense has been operating on all cylinders over their past four games, and they've produced some pretty astounding numbers in the process. Dating back to their Week 5 win over the Cowboys, the Bucs' defense has come up with 10 sacks, nine interceptions, two forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries with their opponents averaging just 13.8 points per game over that stretch.
For the first time all season, Alex Anzalone made a big impact on this football game. Not only did the veteran linebacker have two interceptions (in the rain) in the first half, but he also did a much better job fitting the run. Anzalone finished the game with six total tackles and, more importantly, appeared to be much quicker at diagnosing plays and reacting accordingly.
The Bucs don't need Anzalone to lead the team in interceptions this season (which he currently is) for him to meet the expectations he had coming into this year — they just need him to play sound, disciplined football without making costly errors. If Anzalone can do that, the Bucs' defense will be much better off.
Jacob Parrish and Zyon McCollum continue to impress. Not only did each player record an interception today, but they've both been incredibly consistent in all phases of coverage while also providing exceptional run support this entire season.
If the Bucs' defense continues to perform as it has been, the play of their two starting corners will be a big reason why. If the Buccaneers continue to churn out victories, don't be surprised to see one, if not both, players named to an All-Pro team by season's end.
Although it didn't matter in the end, Irving fumbled a ball through the end zone in the first quarter. Mistakes happen, sure, but this one was completely avoidable. Irving was far too cavalier carrying the football with a defender in close proximity and pursuit, and he got burned for it.
The play happened right in the middle of a torrential downpour at Raymond James Stadium, which should have been added motivation for Irving to keep the ball high and tight.
The Buccaneers became the first team since the Bills in 1974 to win a game without completing a single pass. It's an impressive feat, really, and a testament to just how dominant the Buccaneers were at running the football. That being said, it's likely not an achievement that Baker Mayfield is very proud of.
The Bucs become the first NFL team since the 1974 Buffalo Bills to win a game without completing a pass 😳 pic.twitter.com/kQQJ3S9fqr
All that matters, though, is that the Buccaneers won this football game, and Mayfield finished the contest without any setbacks to his injured thumb.
It goes without saying that the weather played a big role in the lack of success for both the Falcons and Buccaneers on Sunday. Especially in the first half, the rain was as relentless through the air as Irving and Gainwell were on the ground, and credit to the fans who stuck around to cheer on the home team — if only the grass at Raymond James Stadium were so resilient.
Even though he passed for more yards than Mayfield, there's no question that Michael Penix struggled more than any other player in this football game. Penix was 8/24 and threw for 125 yards and 0 TDs to go along with his four interceptions.
He should have had another interception on the opening drive when a pass intended for Drake London hit Jacob Parrish square in the hands, but the Bucs' talented young corner was caught off guard and couldn't secure it.

title: Grading Each Position Group in Buccaneers' Shutout Win Over Falcons
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers dominated in an absolute monsoon in Week 8 against the Atlanta Falcons. Everything went right for the team on all three sides of the ball, and the Falcons looked like they couldn't play football in certain situations.
Let's go over the grades for each position group in another Buccaneers win.
Baker Mayfield did not complete a pass today, and it really didn't matter. Given the conditions of the pouring rain, Mayfield did a great job of staying on top of the football and handing the football off well.
Yes, there were a couple of fumbled snaps between Mayfield and center Graham Barton, but that was mainly due to the conditions of the game. Mayfield did what he needed to do in this matchup.
When you set a new franchise record for team rushing yards in a game, you get the highest grade possible. Both Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell set career highs in rushing yards today with 170 yards and 140 yards, respectively. We didn't see any of Sean Tucker in this matchup, but overall, Irving and Gainwell were phenomenal in this game.
The receiver's main role was blocking on the day, and they did that job well. Chris Godwin Jr., Tez Johnson and Ted Hurst III did a good job of helping extend runs for the Bucs' backs and contributed in the way they needed to for this matchup.
Cade Otton has really transformed into a great blocking tight end this season. It is also important to note that Bauer Sharp has essentially become this team's second tight end on the roster, and it makes sense due to his great blocking ability in recent weeks.
This group has been one of the top reasons why the Bucs have had rushing success the past two weeks and should have a big role going forward.
This group has dominated in the past two weeks regarding the rushing offense. The Falcons knew that the Bucs' game plan was to run the football all day today, and it didn't matter because the offensive line simply executed at a higher level than the Falcons could handle.
The Bucs have found their identity as a rushing team and the offensive line is the biggest reason as to why.
This unit really did a good job of containing one of the best running backs in the league, Bijan Robinson. The pressure was there on quarterback Michael Penix Jr., especially from rookie Rueben Bain Jr. This defense continues to make plays, and the pass rush looks to finally take form.
Alex Anzalone had two interceptions on the day and was far and away in his best game as a Tampa Bay Buccaneer. Josiah Trotter also did a very good job making tackles today and continues to have a great rookie season for this team. There were some missed opportunities given the rain, but overall this unit seems to be getting better every week.
Starting corners Jacob Parrish and Zyon McCollum both had interceptions today and continue to look like one of the best duos in the entire NFL. The only negative was that Antoine Winfield Jr. took a very bad angle on a Jahan Dotson reception that resulted in a big completion.
However, this has been one of the best surprises of the season so far, and Todd Bowles and cornerbacks coach Rashad Johnson deserve a lot of credit.
Chase McLaughlin led the way with three field goals and helped the Bucs keep the lead throughout the day. Riley Dixon had a great day punting the football given the conditions and put the Falcons in field position that they simply couldn't deal with.

title: Overreactions From Buccaneers' Run-Heavy Win Over Falcons
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have won two games in a row. They've done it off the back of some seriously impressive rushing performances.
Tampa Bay defeated the Atlanta Falcons 16-0 in a game where they did not complete a single pass. They're now 3-5 and just a half-game back of the NFC South lead, and they have an excellent ground game and a chainsaw of a defense to back it up.
Here are our three overreactions to Tampa Bay's crazy win against the Falcons without a passing game to be seen:
This might seem crazy to say, and it doesn't mean that the Bucs are necessarily a good team. But let's look at the facts.
They certainly have the best defense — it's a top-five unit in the league. They definitely have the best running game, too, as it's come alive over the last two weeks behind Bucky Irving. They also have the best kicker in football, and that kicker largely won the game for them on Sunday.
The Buccaneers are just half a game out of the NFC South lead. They might drop some games coming up against teams like the Chicago Bears or Detroit Lions, but even then, they seem to be better than every other team in the NFC South at this point.
That could win them the division and get them in the ballroom.
Running back Bucky Irving had over 100 yards by halftime, and the Bucs put up nine points without completing a pass. This brand of football seems unsustainable, but the Bucs have done it two weeks in a row now.
Zac Robinson's switch to a gap and counter run scheme has opened up the run game in a big way. The Bucs will eventually have to pass at some point, but if the run game is this dominant, Tampa Bay may be able to lean on it in a way that no one thought they would be able to.
Is it entirely sustainable? No, but it's proven that the Bucs can win games solely off the back of the run game.
My goodness, have the Bucs been on a heater on defense this last few weeks.
The Bucs had four interceptions off Michael Penix on Sunday. They continue to take the ball, and the linebacking corps and the secondary continue to swarm. The Bucs defense has been suffocating, and it's clear now that this is legitimately a top defensive unit in the NFL.
Todd Bowles has been calling excellent games over the past few weeks, and his players are executing at every level. This Bucs offense may need some work in a few areas, but this Bucs defense? They're absolutely lethal.

title: Buccaneers Lose Starter to Knee Injury
full_text:
It's football weather in Tampa Bay as the Buccaneers take on the Atlanta Falcons.
Since kickoff, the rain has been coming down nonstop and has led to some sloppy play by both teams.
The Bucs have had a botched snap or fumble four times, while Michael Penix Jr. has thrown three interceptions for Atlanta.
The Buccaneers' running game and defensive ability to take the ball away have been at the forefront of the game
Even with how well those two aspects are playing, the defense took a bullet in this one as outside linebacker Yaya Diaby has been ruled out for the rest of the game with a knee injury.
According to our boots on the ground in Tampa, Falcons tight end Nick Muse fell into Diaby. And despite trying to work through the injury on the side, he will be unable to go the rest of the way.
Diaby is now OUT for the remainder of the game. https://t.co/dSf5RrQhME
Diaby had been extremely underwhelming to begin his contract year, but exploded last week against the Carolina Panthers for three sacks. He also has 11 tackles and one interception.
He finally looked to be turning his own personal season around, and the hope is that nothing serious is going on inside his knee that could cause him to miss an extended period of time.
We will hear from head coach Todd Bowles following the game on Diaby's status, but likely won't have a true understanding of the seriousness of it until further tests are done on Monday.
With Diaby now out for the rest of the game, the Bucs will rotate the likes of Anthony Nelson and David Walker.
Walker has been extremely useful against the pass, but with the weather, Nelson might be better suited to stop the run game led by Bijan Robinson.
The good news is that the Bucs haven't had to generate much pressure due to the weather and field conditions, so being down one player won't necessarily have a huge impact on the game.

title: Buccaneers Reveal Good News Right Before Falcons Matchup
full_text:
Every game is a must-win game for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at this point, but this game on Sunday vs. the Atlanta Falcons could very well make or break Tampa Bay's season.
The Bucs are 1.5 games out of first place in the NFC South. The Carolina Panthers lost their Thursday Night Football game to the Green Bay Packers (and fired a good number of their defensive staff as a result), so if the Bucs beat the Falcons, they'll be just 1.5 games back from the NFC South lead.
Naturally, Tampa Bay will want every starter it can have to try and win this game. And it looks like one questionable key offensive player will indeed play today against the Falcons.
Right tackle Luke Goedeke has been dealing with a calf injury for the last two weeks. He didn't play against the Panthers and did not practice on Wednesday and Thursday this week, but he did practice Friday — and now, he's slated to play.
Goedeke is active against the Falcons today. With no practice squad elevations, he'll almost certainly play against Atlanta, giving the offensive line a big boost against a Falcons front that can get a lot of good pressure with four players.
Swing tackle Ben Chukwuma played in Goedeke's stead last week. He won't have to do so again this week, as Goedeke will anchor down the right side while All-Pro Tristan Wirfs holds down the left side.
Goedeke will be a crucial player. The Bucs may need to establish the run in inclement weather, and Atlanta boasts the fourth-best run defense in the NFL by rushing yards per game. If running back Bucky Irving is going to get going, he'll need Goedeke's help to do it, and that could be the key to controlling the clock and beating an Atlanta team that just knocked off the San Francisco 49ers the week prior.
The Bucs play the Falcons at 1 p.m. at Raymond James Stadium.

title: 2 Position Groups That Need to Step Up for Buccaneers to Beat Falcons
full_text:
After a brutal start to the 2026 NFL season for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , there's all of a sudden a slight glimmer of hope.
After pummeling the Panthers in Carolina last weekend 43-13, the Bucs are now looking to string together back-to-back regular season victories for the first time in over a year. More importantly, with the Atlanta Falcons coming to town on Sunday, the Buccaneers will have a chance to make up even more ground in the division with the Panthers having already lost this week's matchup to the Green Bay Packers on Thursday.
Even though the Falcons and Panthers both sit at 3-4 atop the NFC South standings, the Falcons have a -2 point differential on the season compared to Carolina's -15. Interestingly enough, the Buccaneers, who are looking up at both teams with their 2-5 record, are +11 in the point differential category.
A win against Atlanta this week would be massive for the Buccaneers to close the gap in the NFC South standings. And with four divisional games still to be played, Tampa Bay would all of a sudden have a very realistic path to push for the top seed in the South by season's end.
Conversely, a loss to Atlanta would not only put the Bucs even further behind these teams in the standings, but it could signify the end of their competitive window this year and potentially turn the Bucs into sellers ahead of the Nov. 10th trade deadline.
In other words, even though we aren't quite at the halfway mark, the result of this Sunday's game against the Falcons could very well determine the fate of the 2026 Buccaneers.
Let's take a look at two key position groups that will need to step up in order for the Buccaneers to get a much-needed victory this weekend.
Although Todd Bowles' defense has really established itself as one of the league's better all-around units, there are still flaws to be found.
Most obvious among them is veteran LB Alex Anzalone who, despite signing a substantial contract to become a key leader of this defense in the offseason, has struggled mightily in all facets. Far too often, Anzalone loses his footing, fails to shed blocks, takes poor angles and misses tackles. Even more concerning is that he's been more of a liability in pass coverage than the asset that he was advertised to be coming over from Detroit.
Thankfully, his rookie running mate, Josiah Trotter, has been superb . That being said the Buccaneers have struggled as a unit when it comes to defending opposing tight ends. Meanwhile, Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts, though inconsistent, always seems to be a problem for the Buccaneers.
Trotter needs to keep playing how he has been, but Anzalone must step up in order to contain Pitts, who remains one of the most gifted pass-catching tight ends in the game. Throw in the challenge of defending the best running back in football, Bijan Robinson, and the importance of the Buccaneers' linebacker duo stepping up on Sunday becomes that much more obvious.
Even after Mike Evans surprised everyone by leaving Tampa Bay in the offseason, the Buccaneers remained confident in their WR room because of the quality depth they'd assembled leading up to that moment. Unfortunately, though, the Bucs' talented collection of pass catchers hasn't come close to producing the results everyone expected.
Although Chris Godwin has proven in the past to be a game changer, we've yet to see that version of the Bucs' veteran this season. The team's supposed number one WR, Emeka Egbuka, is unlikely to suit up in this game due to a foot injury and Jalen McMillan remains without a timetable for return.
Young receivers like Tez Johnson and Ted Hurst have both performed well in limited opportunities, but they'll need to be targeted more in this game in order to take the top off the defense and open up other opportunities for Zac Robinson's offense .
Although the Buccaneers managed to dominate the Panthers last weekend while passing for just 64 yards in the game, that's unlikely to be replicated against the Falcons, who present a much stouter run defense. As a result, the Bucs will need to attack the Falcons through the air in order to keep them honest. With Mayfield still nursing a thumb injury on his throwing hand, even more of that responsibility will fall on the Bucs' pass catchers.
In order for the Bucs to be effective through the air against Atlanta, they'll need to take some shots downfield to both Johnson and Hurst while utilizing Chris Godwin at all levels of the field. If those players are able to create separation against the Falcons' defensive backs, it will make life that much easier on Mayfield and significantly increase the Bucs' chances of winning this critical game.

title: Titans' Snap Count Winners and Losers: Tony Pollard Dominates, Backfield Reserves Unseen in Week 8
full_text:
On Sunday, the Tennessee Titans lost to the Bengals in a 43-36 overtime shootout in Cincinnati. Following the loss, the Titans fall to a 1-7 record. For the second straight week, Tennessee has fallen despite possessing a two-score lead in the first quarter.
While another close loss hurts, there have been positives for the Titans that were unforeseen in the beginning of the season. It marked the Titans' highest-scoring game in five years.
Let's take a look at the winners and losers for the Titans' hotly contested matchup with Cincinnati.
Over the past two weeks, RB Tony Pollard has seen an uptick in snaps and delivered with monster performances. Against Cincinnati, Pollard rushed for 117 yards on 21 carries for two touchdowns.
In the first quarter, Pollard ripped a 41-yard rush where he broke through numerous Bengals defenders to score his first touchdown of the game. Through the first six weeks of the season, Pollard was averaging 31 snaps per game, according to Fantasy Pros .
Against the Bengals, he recorded a season-high 63 snaps. After playing 47 snaps the week prior against Cleveland, where he scored three touchdowns, he recorded more than 150 yards from scrimmage.
Prior to playing the Browns, Pollard only had one touchdown all season. Now, his total is up to six with more playing time. With the NFL trade deadline nearing on November 10, Pollard's breakout performances may lead the Titans to deal him to a contender.
After another poor performance against the Houston Texans, head coach Robert Saleh decided to bench CB Alontae Taylor against the Browns. However, Taylor redeemed himself with his best performance of the season against Cincinnati.
Ahead of the game, Saleh announced Taylor would be moved from an outside back to nickel corner, specializing in the slot.
In his new role Taylor played 51 snaps against the Bengals, and he was everywhere on the field for Tennessee. He recorded five tackles, two quarterback pressures, a tackle for loss and a forced fumble.
Taylor stepped up for the Titans' secondary, with CB Marcus Harris exiting the contest with an ankle injury.
Tennessee had high hopes for the former second-round pick, inking him to one of their most expensive contracts of the offseason with a three-year deal worth up to $58 million. Taylor may have found a good fit in a new position for the Titans moving forward.
There was real concern for the Titans' passing game heading into Cincinnati after the team announced rookie WR Carnell Tate would be out with a shoulder injury, but WR Chimere Dike stepped up with a breakout performance.
After only playing 13 snaps the week prior, Dike made the most of his 63 snaps against the Bengals. The second-year pro caught five passes for 71 yards and a touchdown, including the Titans' longest reception of 28 yards.
This season Dike has primarily served as a kick returner with limited offensive reps. In the previous two games, Dike had zero catches on a lone target.
Against the Bengals, Dike surpassed his season total of 53 receiving yards with an elevated role in Tate's absence. It was his first 70-plus receiving performance since Week 8 against the Colts last season.
For the second straight week RB Tyjae Spears and rookie RB Nick Singleton were healthy scratches. The pairing entered the season as the Titans' second- and third-string running backs, but they have completely fallen out of the rotation.
Pollard consumed 63 of 78 snaps of the Titans' backfield. The other backfield snaps went to RB Michael Carter and RB Julius Chestnut with 13 and two snaps, respectively. Carter and Chestnut only served as blocking backs; neither back received any touches.
Spears has zero touchdowns, 23 touches and 141 yards from scrimmage this season. Singleton has four carries for 12 yards and zero touchdowns, and he hasn't seen any offensive snaps since Week 4 against the Ravens.
It may take Pollard getting traded before Spears and Singleton return to action.
